children.translated_text: First chapter (<s>vilāsa</s>)
<s>Camatkāracandrikā</s> (Moonlight of Wonder), composed by <s>Viśveśvara Kavicandra</s>. First chapter.

children.text: vāgdevī vadane mama sphuratu yā dhvanyātmanollāsinī varṇavyaktimupāgatā ca tadanu sthānaprayatnādibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: May the Goddess of Speech shine forth in my mouth—she who gleams in the form of suggestive meaning (<s>dhvani</s>), who then manifests through distinct phonemes (<s>varṇa</s>) by means of place of articulation, effort, and so on,

children.text: bhāvānāṃ padasaṃjñayā vidadhatī tredhā samullekhanāny ānandānanusaṃdadhāti viduṣāṃ prāptā mahāvākyatām // Ckc_1.1 //
children.translated_text: who produces, through what are called words (<s>pada</s>), three kinds of delineation of emotions, and who, having attained the status of a great statement (<s>mahāvākya</s>), bestows bliss upon the learned. // Ckc_1.1 //

children.text: ramyockayarthatanūjjvalā rasamayaprāṇā guṇollāsinī cetorajjakarītivṛttikalitā pākaṃ vayo bibhratī /
children.translated_text: Radiant with beautiful diction and meaning, having <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic flavor) as its life-breath, shimmering with <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), fashioned with behavior that captivates the mind like a rutting elephant, bearing maturity in age,

children.text: nānālaṅkaraṇojjvalā rasavatī sarvatra nirdeṣatāṃ śayyāmañcati kāminīva kavitā kasyāpi puṇyātmanaḥ // Ckc_1.2 //
children.translated_text: resplendent with various ornaments, full of <s>rasa</s>—may poetry (<s>kavitā</s>) everywhere enter the bed-chamber of someone fortunate, like a beloved woman! // Ckc_1.2 //
If a composition is skillful in desired themes, elevated with the virtues of a noble hero,
then I compose this jewel among treatises on poetics as an illustration of the virtues of King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>. // Ckc_1.3 //

children.text:
loke rāghavapāṇḍavādbhutakathāgandhānusaṃdhāyinau tau granthāviba tanmunipraṇihitau śrīsiṅgabhūpāśrayaḥ /
yāyādādaraṇīyatāṃ kṛtadhiyāṃ grantho 'yamasmatkṛto nāhaṃ yadyapi tādṛśo 'smyayamasau rājā hi tādṛgguṇaḥ // Ckc_1.4 //
children.translated_text: In the world, those two texts composed by those sages, tracing the wondrous stories of <s>Rāghava</s> and the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>—under the patronage of King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>, may this text composed by us attain reverence among the learned; for though I am not such a one (as those sages), this king is indeed one of such virtues. // Ckc_1.4 //

children.text: nṛṇāṃ vidhau ca nāthe ca śikṣā kāvyaprayojanam /
children.translated_text: Instruction in duty and lordship for men—that is the purpose of poetry;

children.text: śikṣa ca sacamatkāraṃ bodhitā sthiratāṃ bhajet // Ckc_1.5 //
children.translated_text: and instruction, when conveyed with <s>camatkāra</s> (wonder/aesthetic delight), attains permanence. // Ckc_1.5 //
<s>Camatkāra</s> (wonder) is that which creates an overflow of bliss in the learned;

children.text: guṇaṃ rītiṃ rasaṃ vṛttiṃ pākaṃ śayyāmalaṅkṛtīm // Ckc_1.6 //
children.translated_text: <s>guṇa</s> (quality), <s>rīti</s> (style), <s>rasa</s> (flavor), <s>vṛtti</s> (mode), <s>pāka</s> (maturity), <s>śayyā</s> (verbal arrangement), and <s>alaṅkṛti</s> (ornamentation)— // Ckc_1.6 //
these seven the wise call the causes of <s>camatkāra</s> (wonder);
by reason of their shared capacity to produce beauty in sentences, // Ckc_1.7 //
they have been declared by <s>Kubja</s> and others as each being a single limb of poetry;
elsewhere, King <s>Bhoja</s> speaks of three limbs: <s>guṇa</s>, <s>bhūṣā</s> (ornament), and <s>rasa</s>. // Ckc_1.8 //

children.text:
saptāṅgasaṅgataṃ kāvyaṃ sāmrājyamiva bhāsate /
lakṣyate taditaṃ sāṅgaṃ mayā kṛtadhiyāṃ mude // Ckc_1.9 //
children.translated_text: Poetry endowed with all seven limbs shines like an empire; this seven-limbed poetry is examined by me for the delight of the learned. // Ckc_1.9 //

children.text: atrālaṅkaraṇe bhavantu sudhiyaḥ snigdhā iti prārthanā vyarthā yadbharatādibhaktiṣu matiryeṣāṃ talasparśinī /
children.translated_text: The prayer 'may the wise be favorably disposed toward this work on ornamentation' is futile for those whose understanding in devotion to <s>Bharata</s> and others barely touches the surface;

children.text: te sārajñatayaiva bibhrati mudaṃ ye saṃśayenāsphuṭā- ste sandehanivṛttaye hṛdi dhaiyaṃ kartuṃ yatante svayam // Ckc_1.10 //
children.translated_text: those connoisseurs take delight precisely through their expertise; those who are unclear due to doubt should themselves strive to create certainty in their hearts. // Ckc_1.10 //
Word and meaning accompanied by <s>camatkāra</s> (wonder)—knowers of poetry know this to be <s>kāvya</s> (poetry);

children.text: vākchabda iti paryāyau vāgbhirarthaḥ śivaḥ smṛtaḥ // Ckc_1.11 //
children.translated_text: <s>vāk</s> (speech) and <s>śabda</s> (word) are synonyms; the meaning conveyed by words is remembered as <s>Śiva</s> (auspicious/the ultimate). // Ckc_1.11 //

children.text: sā vāka tredhā smṛtā varṇāḥ padaṃ vākyamiti kramāt /
children.translated_text: That speech is said to be threefold: <s>varṇa</s> (phonemes), <s>pada</s> (words), and <s>vākya</s> (sentences), in order;
the <s>varṇas</s>, from 'a' to 'ha,' are called <s>mātṛkā</s> (the mother-letters). // Ckc_1.12 //

children.text: alpaprāṇā mahāprāṇā iti te ddevidhā matāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Alpaprāṇa</s> (unaspirated) and <s>mahāprāṇa</s> (aspirated)—thus they are considered twofold;
the wise call the four sibilants (<s>ūṣma-catuṣṭaya</s>) aspirated among them. // Ckc_1.13 //
Some say that identical consonants within a class are called <s>savarṇa</s> (homogeneous);

children.text: alpaprāṇāstu śeṣāḥsyuḥ śasāvapi paraiḥ smṛtau // Ckc_1.14 //
children.translated_text: the remaining ones are unaspirated; 'śa' and 'sa' are also considered so by others. // Ckc_1.14 //

children.text: ubhayo te 'pi kathitā snigdhā rūkṣā iti dbidhā /
children.translated_text: Both types are also described as twofold: <s>snigdha</s> (smooth) and <s>rūkṣa</s> (rough);

children.text: alpaprāṇāḥ sajātī yairyuktāḥ snigdhā iti smṛtāḥ // Ckc_1.15 //
children.translated_text: unaspirated consonants joined with those of their own class are considered smooth. // Ckc_1.15 //

children.text: svai ranyairvā mahāprāṇā yuktā rūkṣāḥ paraiḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Aspirated consonants joined with their own or others are called rough by others;
unaspirated consonants too are said to be rough when joined with ya, ra, la, and va. // Ckc_1.16 //

children.text: sānusvāratayā snaigdhyaṃ yānti rūkṣā api kvacit /
children.translated_text: Through the addition of <s>anusvāra</s> (nasal mark), even rough ones sometimes become smooth;
the distinction should be known by the wise through the number-examples such as <s>vandya</s> and <s>vandhya</s>. // Ckc_1.17 //
These <s>varṇas</s> are useful for <s>rasa</s> and other purposes as is fitting;
<s>varṇas</s> placed at the opening of a poem are embodiments of their presiding deities, // Ckc_1.18 //
and produce auspicious or inauspicious effects for the author, patron, and listener;

children.text: akāraḥ prītidāyī syānniṣedhe tu viparyayaḥ // Ckc_1.19 //
children.translated_text: the letter 'a' bestows joy, but in negation it is the opposite. // Ckc_1.19 //
The long 'ā' gives delight, but it too is inappropriate in anger, suffering, etc.;
the four letters beginning with 'i' produce satisfaction and wish-fulfillment. // Ckc_1.20 //
The four beginning with 'ṛ' cause continuity and stupefaction;
and the four beginning with 'e' bestow desire, eloquence, liberation, and prosperity. // Ckc_1.21 //
The <s>ka-varga</s> (ka-class) bestows <s>Lakṣmī</s> (fortune); the letter 'ca' destroys fame;

children.text: chajakārau raugaharau jhajau tu maraṇapradau // Ckc_1.22 //
children.translated_text: 'cha' and 'ja' remove disease; 'jha' and 'jau' cause death. // Ckc_1.22 //
'ṭa' and 'ṭha' cause distress; 'ḍa' is auspicious; 'ḍha' destroys beauty;
'ṇa' brings acquisition of things; 'ta' destroys obstacles. // Ckc_1.23 //
'tha' is a war-maker; 'da' and 'dha' bestow steadfastness;
'na' causes torment in some contexts, but in non-negation is considered auspicious. // Ckc_1.24 //
'pa' bestows protection; 'pha' bestows timidity;
'ba' produces health; 'bha' produces memory and fortune. // Ckc_1.25 //
'ma' causes agitation; 'ya' bestows prosperity; 'ra' causes burning;
'la' causes sluggishness; 'va' is a mine of speech, health, and longevity. // Ckc_1.26 //
The <s>ūṣman</s> (sibilant) consonants in order are repositories of happiness, distinction, fortune, and <s>nirvāṇa</s>;

children.text: kṣaṃ vinā krūrasaṃyuktaḥ saumyastyājyo viṣānnavat // Ckc_1.27 //
children.translated_text: except for 'kṣa,' a gentle one joined with a harsh one should be avoided like poisoned food. // Ckc_1.27 //
A conjunct of two auspicious ones is better, like giving of fortune and leisure;

children.text: guruḥ punar laghuśceti varṇāḥ punaramī dvidhā // Ckc_1.28 //
children.translated_text: furthermore, these <s>varṇas</s> are again twofold: <s>guru</s> (heavy) and <s>laghu</s> (light). // Ckc_1.28 //
Those ending in <s>anusvāra</s> or <s>visarga</s>, long vowels, those followed by a conjunct, and <s>pluta</s> (protracted) vowels

children.text: guravo laghavastvanye smṛtāste tu trayo gaṇāḥ // Ckc_1.29 //
children.translated_text: are heavy; the rest are considered light; and these form three <s>gaṇas</s> (metrical groups). // Ckc_1.29 //
The <s>gaṇas</s> named <s>ma</s>, <s>ya</s>, <s>ra</s>, <s>sa</s>, <s>ta</s>, <s>ja</s>, <s>bha</s>, and <s>na</s> are produced, each subsequent one from the preceding;

children.text: janyo 'tra janakanikaṭe sutavadvitanoti nāśubhaṃ karma // Ckc_1.30 //
children.translated_text: the generated one here, placed near its generator, like a son, does not produce inauspicious effects. // Ckc_1.30 //

children.text: sarvamūlaṃ tu magaṇaṃ prāpya sarvagaṇaḥ śubhaḥ /
children.translated_text: But the <s>ma-gaṇa</s>, being the root of all, makes every <s>gaṇa</s> auspicious when it is present;

children.text: pūrvācāryoditaṃ teṣāṃ lakṣma daivaṃ phalaṃ bruve // Ckc_1.31 //
children.translated_text: I shall state the characteristics, the presiding deity, and the fruit of each, as taught by earlier masters. // Ckc_1.31 //
The <s>ma-gaṇa</s> (all heavy), with Earth as its deity, gives welfare;
the <s>ya-gaṇa</s> (light at beginning), with Water as its deity, produces wealth. // Ckc_1.32 //
The <s>ra-gaṇa</s> (light in middle), with Fire as its deity, gives fear;
the <s>sa-gaṇa</s> (heavy at end), with Wind as its deity, causes destruction. // Ckc_1.33 //
The <s>ta-gaṇa</s> (heavy at beginning), with Space as its deity, gives lordship;
the <s>ja-gaṇa</s> (heavy in middle), with Sun as its deity, causes suffering. // Ckc_1.34 //
The <s>bha-gaṇa</s> (heavy at beginning), with Moon as its deity, gives happiness;
the <s>na-gaṇa</s> (all light), with Sacrifice as its deity, produces wealth. // Ckc_1.35 //

children.text: aṣṭau jātiṣvamī proktā mātrāyāṃ tu trayaḥ smṛtāḥ // Ckc_1.36 //
children.translated_text: These eight are stated for <s>jāti</s> (syllabic) meters; for <s>mātrā</s> (moraic) meters, three are mentioned. // Ckc_1.36 //

children.text: gaṇa ihatu laghucatuṣkaṃ dve vā guruṇī laghudvayaṃ caikaguru /
children.translated_text: The <s>gaṇa</s> here is a set of four light syllables, or two heavies, or a light pair with one heavy;
the presiding deities and fruits of all-light, all-heavy, and one-heavy are as stated before. // Ckc_1.37 //

children.text: śubhaṃ kāvyamukhe nyasyaidgaṇaṃ varṇa ca nāsubham // Ckc_1.38 //
children.translated_text: One should place an auspicious <s>gaṇa</s> and <s>varṇa</s> at the opening of a poem, not an inauspicious one. // Ckc_1.38 //
"In the north there are word and meaning..."—the example "some beloved one" is cited;
in the three works of <s>Kālidāsa</s>, auspicious <s>gaṇas</s> and <s>varṇas</s> should be recognized. // Ckc_1.39 //
In "<s>śriyaḥ kurūṇām</s>" (glory of the Kurus) and "<s>śriyaḥ patiḥ</s>" (Lord of <s>Śrī</s>),
the mention of <s>Śrī</s> and <s>Śrīpati</s> is for the purpose of concealing the flaw of the <s>ja-gaṇa</s>. // Ckc_1.40 //
Alternatively, due to proximity with a <s>ta-gaṇa</s>, a <s>ja-gaṇa</s> born from it is auspicious;
this is the teaching for poets; and here again, through conjunction with a <s>ma-gaṇa</s>— // Ckc_1.41 //
when used for an auspicious purpose, or in naming, or in marking a deity's name,

children.text: gaṇo na dūpyo varṇaśva devatādhiṣṭitāśmavat // Ckc_1.42 //
children.translated_text: a <s>gaṇa</s> is not to be censured, nor a <s>varṇa</s>—like a stone presided over by a deity. // Ckc_1.42 //
In "<s>caturmukha</s>" and such, the letter 'ca' and the <s>ja-gaṇa</s> too,
being marked with <s>Brahmā's</s> name, are auspicious even at the beginning of a poem. // Ckc_1.43 //
In "<s>śṛṅgāra-vīra-sauhārda</s>" and such, at the opening of this treatise,
the letter 'ṛ' and the letter 'śa' too are distinguished as auspicious. // Ckc_1.44 //
At the beginning of praise, by the expression of the worthy, of continuity, and such,

children.text: pakāro rephayukto 'pi sphuṭaṃ kāvyamukhe śubhaḥ // Ckc_1.45 //
children.translated_text: even 'pa' joined with 'ra' is clearly auspicious at the opening of a poem. // Ckc_1.45 //
At the opening of earlier poems, one who establishes their authority—

children.text: duṣṭe varṇe gaṇe dhīmān kuryādevaṃ vicāraṇām // Ckc_1.46 //
children.translated_text: when there is an inauspicious <s>varṇa</s> or <s>gaṇa</s>, the wise should make such a justification. // Ckc_1.46 //
The utterances of the ancients are generally profound;
by the moderns, through mere citation of those examples, the established rules should not be transgressed. // Ckc_1.47 //
This rule pertains to the praise of a present-day hero;

children.text: na bhūtapurvaviṣaya iti kecana manvate // Ckc_1.48 //
children.translated_text: it does not apply to past subjects—so some think. // Ckc_1.48 //
That should be considered, or else abandoned with courtesy—why such things?
Even in a narrative poem, former events are selected for the treatise. // Ckc_1.49 //
From the impulse of desired fruit for the author, patron, and listener,
and from the power of a composition free from faults to produce instruction— // Ckc_1.50 //
due to the absence of proper bounds, there arises the occasion for speaking as one pleases;
in the alternative of hearing of faults, this is never the view of the wise. // Ckc_1.51 //

children.text: ekasminnapi naṣṭaṃ syād dṛṣṭe doṣe vratāyutam /
children.translated_text: Even in a single instance, when a fault is perceived, merit equal to ten thousand vows would be destroyed;

children.text: doṣasyaitādṛśī śaktiḥ sahajā kiṃ nu kurmahe // Ckc_1.52 //
children.translated_text: such is the innate power of a fault—what can we do? // Ckc_1.52 //
Therefore, with every effort, by a poet who desires <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, and the rest,

children.text: kavinā doṣaleśo 'pi tyājya eveti niścayaḥ // Ckc_1.53 //
children.translated_text: even the slightest trace of a fault must be abandoned—this is certain. // Ckc_1.53 //
<s>Guṇa</s> (quality) is sweetness of sound; <s>varṇadoṣa</s> (phonemic fault) is the opposite. // Ckc_1.54 //
Thus ends the analysis of <s>varṇa</s> (phonemes).

children.text: vibhaktyantaṃ pataṃ tacca vācakaṃ lakṣakaṃ dvidhā /
children.translated_text: A <s>pada</s> (word) ends with a case-suffix, and it is twofold: <s>vācaka</s> (denotative) and <s>lakṣaka</s> (indicative);
a third, <s>vyañjaka</s> (suggestive), is stated by knowers of the <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion) school. // Ckc_1.55 //
A word that conveys meaning according to convention is considered <s>vācaka</s> (denotative);

children.text: yaugikaṃ rūḍhamityetad dvidhā syāttatra yaugikam // Ckc_1.56 //
children.translated_text: it is twofold: <s>yaugika</s> (derivative/etymological) and <s>rūḍha</s> (conventional); among these, the derivative one— // Ckc_1.56 //
is that which reveals its own meaning in dependence on the derivation of its constituent parts. // Ckc_1.57 //
For example:
In the case of the moon, sandalwood juice, and King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>,
the sense-organs of people, which grasp form, have their purposes fulfilled. // Ckc_1.*1 //
Here, the words <s>candra</s>, <s>candanasarasa</s>, etc. convey their meaning only through etymological derivation such as 'that which delights'—hence their derivative character.
The <s>rū���ha</s> (conventional) type, on the other hand, is independent of the derivation of its constituent parts. // Ckc_1.58 //
For example:

children.text: dānena karṇo dayayā dilīpo nayena kāvyo vinayena rāmaḥ /
children.translated_text: In generosity he is <s>Karṇa</s>, in compassion <s>Dilīpa</s>, in statecraft <s>Kāvya</s> (Śukra), in humility <s>Rāma</s>;

children.text: yadi prasiddhiṃ dadhatāmamībhiḥ śrīsiṅgabhūpo nikhilaiḥ prasiddhaḥ // Ckc_1.*2 //
children.translated_text: while these attained fame through individual qualities, King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s> is famous through all of them. // Ckc_1.*2 //
Here, the words <s>Karṇa</s> and others have the character of being conventional (<s>rūḍha</s>) because they convey meaning even without etymological derivation of their parts.
When the conventionally designated meaning is blocked, and the word operates upon a related object,

children.text: vyāpṛtaṃ lakṣakaṃ tacca dvidhā rūḍheḥ prayojanāt // Ckc_1.59 //
children.translated_text: that is the <s>lakṣaka</s> (indicative) word, which is twofold: due to established usage or due to purpose. // Ckc_1.59 //
Here, the established type of indication—for example:

children.text: śrīsiṅgakṣitipāla pālanakalāniṣṇāta sevāvatāṃ saṃśikṣākuśalapratītamanasāṃ prāptau pravīṇaśriyām /
children.translated_text: O King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>, protector, skilled in the art of governance, of those who serve—whose minds are gained through trust in proper training, who have attained accomplished prosperity—
enemy kings worship the sun of your feet with rubies from the crests of their crowns, which humble the pride of the beauty of a fresh <s>Indragopakas</s> (red insect). // Ckc_1.*3 //

children.text:
atra niṣṇātakuśalapravīṇaśakragopaśabdānāṃ nitarāṃ snātaḥ, kuśān lāti, prakṛṣṭā vīṇāsya, śakraṃ gopāyatīti mukhyārthānamavivakṣayā cāturyendragopakīṭalakṣaṇāyā rūḍhireva mūlam, nānyatsahṛdayā hlādakāraṇaṃ kiṃciditi rūḍhalakṣakatvam /
saprayojanalakṣakaṃ yathā
children.translated_text: Here, the words <s>niṣṇāta</s>, <s>kuśala</s>, <s>pravīṇa</s>, <s>śakragopa</s>, etc.—without intending their primary meanings ('well-bathed,' 'one who takes kuśa grass,' 'one who has an excellent lute,' 'one who protects Indra')—their root is conventional usage alone (meaning 'skilled,' 'adept,' 'expert,' 'the indragopa insect'), and nothing else gives delight to the connoisseur—hence their character as conventional-indicative. The purposive type of indication—for example:

children.text: śrīsiṅgabhūpa samaye samaye bhavantam āsthānamaṇṭapagataṃ janarañjanāya /
children.translated_text: O King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>, at the proper time, when you have gone to the audience hall for the delight of the people,

children.text: kalyāṇahemakalaśaiḥ samamātapatrair āndolikāḥ sapadi sevitumāpatanti // Ckc_1.*4 //
children.translated_text: palanquins rush at once to attend upon you, along with golden auspicious finials and parasols. // Ckc_1.*4 //

children.text:
atrācetanānāṃ hemakalaśāṅkitachatrāṇāmāndolikānāñca sevārthamāgamanamasaṃbhāvitamiti chatrādhārāḥ puruṣāḥ, āndolikādheyā rājāno vidvāṃso vā saṃlakṣyante /
anena cāsthānamaṇṭapāṅgaṇe chatrāntolikānāmatibāhulyaṃ prayojanatayā vivakṣitam /
tena ca nāyakamāśritānāmāndolikādyavadhayo vibhūtaya iti ca /
tadidaṃ prayojanalabhakam /
children.translated_text: Here, the coming of inanimate golden-finialed parasols and palanquins for the purpose of attending is impossible—therefore what is indicated is that persons bearing parasols, and kings or scholars seated in the palanquins, are implied. And by this, what is intended as the purpose is the great abundance of parasols and palanquins in the courtyard of the audience hall; and thereby, the palanquins and other accouterments of those who have resorted to the hero represent his opulence. This is purposive indication.
When the meaning is conveyed through a non-primary or primary <s>vṛtti</s> (verbal function),

children.text: utkarṣāya yadanyārthadyotakaṃ vyañjakaṃ hi tat // Ckc_1.60 //
children.translated_text: that which illuminates another meaning for the sake of heightening is indeed called <s>vyañjaka</s> (the suggestive element). // Ckc_1.60 //
For example:
Oh, what literary fortune of King <s>Śrīsiṅga</s>!

children.text: ślāghāyai yasya sannaddhā vāco viśveśvarasya me // Ckc_1.*5 //
children.translated_text: For whose praise the words of me, <s>Viśveśvara</s>, stand arrayed. // Ckc_1.*5 //

children.text: atra sarasasāhityacāturīviśrāmabhūmirahamiti viśiṣṭo 'smadarthor'thāntarasaṃkramitena mameti padena lakṣyate /
children.translated_text: Here, the special meaning 'I am the resting-ground of refined literary skill' is indicated through the word 'mama' (me), which transfers the sense of 'asmat' (first person) to another meaning by <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (indication).

children.text: anena sāhityasahajasairabhaṃ vinā nānyasmai camatkārakāriteti vyajyate /
children.translated_text: By this, it is suggested (<s>vyajyate</s>) that without the innate boldness born of literary mastery, no one else could produce <s>camatkāra</s> (aesthetic wonder).

children.text: saṃnaddhā iti padenātyantatiraskṛtavācye (na?) tatparatayā grathitā iti lakṣyate /
children.translated_text: By the word 'saṃnaddhā' (arrayed), the <s>vācya</s> (denoted meaning) being entirely set aside, it is indicated that [the words] are strung together with that as their purpose.

children.text: atrānena ca nāyakasāhityasya sarvasājātyātiśāyitvaṃ dyotyata iti padavyañjakametat //
children.translated_text: And here, by this, the surpassing of all peers by the patron's literary [excellence] is illuminated — thus this is an instance of <s>pada-vyañjaka</s> (word-level suggestion). //
An example through primary [verbal function]:
King <s>Siṅga</s> is an <s>alaṃkārī</s> (one who adorns / master of figures), while <s>Rāvaṇa</s> was a <s>laṅkārī</s> (lord of Laṅkā);
The difference of a single letter between the two is heard [and] universally acknowledged. // Ckc_1.*6 //

children.text: varṇenākṣareṇāntaraṃ bhedo yayostacvamiti mukhyayā vṛcyā vācye pratiṣṭhite varṇāṃ vaiśyajātirantaraṃ nāyakaraghunāyakayoriti parasparavyatirekāraṅkāro varṇāntaramiti padena vyajyata iti padavyañjakametat //
children.translated_text: The compound 'varṇāntaratva' means 'the state of having a difference (antara) of a letter (varṇa = akṣara)' — thus, with the <s>vācya</s> (denoted meaning) established through the primary <s>vṛtti</s>, through the word 'varṇāntara' it is suggested that 'varṇa' means the <s>Vaiśya</s> caste and 'antara' means difference between the patron and <s>Raghu</s>'s hero [<s>Rāma</s>] — [establishing] the figure of mutual distinction (<s>vyatireka-alaṃkāra</s>). Thus this is an instance of <s>pada-vyañjaka</s> (word-level suggestion). //
Or for example:
He who broke through the iron pillar, who nourished the devotee <s>Prahlāda</s>,
This <s>Narasiṃha</s>, lord of <s>Śrī</s>, shines as the crest-jewel among kings. // Ckc_1.*7 //

children.text:
kṛto racita ayastambhasya śubhāvahavidhijāḍyasya nirbhedo nivāraṇaṃ yena saḥ kṛtāyastambhanirbhedaḥ /
daivānukūlyasaṃpādanacatura ityarthaḥ /
bhaktapraṅlādapoṣakaḥ sevakasantoṣavardhanaḥ rājaśekharo bhūpālamauliḥ narasiṃhaḥ śrīsiṅgabhūpālo rājata ityasiddhayā prākaraṇiker'the pratipādite ye 'yaṃ kṛtalohastambhabhedanasya prahlādābhidhānabhaktapoṣakasya candrakalādhāriṇo bhagavataḥ śrīnṛsiṃhasya pratītistayā śabdaśaktimūlayā nāyakakaṇṭhīravakapaṭakaṇṭhīravayorupamālaṅkāradhvaniranusandhīyata iti vyañjakamidam /
children.translated_text: 'Kṛtāyastambhanirbheda' means: one by whom the breaking (nirbheda) of the iron pillar (ayastambha) — [i.e.,] the removal of the rigidity of inauspicious ritual fate — was accomplished (kṛta); the meaning is: one skilled in securing divine favor. 'Bhaktaprahlādapoṣaka' means: one who increases the joy of servants. 'Rājaśekhara' means: the crest-jewel of kings. '<s>Narasiṃha</s>' [here refers to] King <s>Śrīsiṅga</s>, who shines — thus, when the contextual meaning is established through the non-established [secondary] sense, the recognition of the blessed Lord <s>Nṛsiṃha</s> — who broke the iron pillar, who nourished the devotee named <s>Prahlāda</s>, and who bears the crescent moon — arises through that word-power, and thereby the <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion) of the figure of <s>upamā</s> (simile) between the patron-lion and the divine lion is discerned. Thus this is a <s>vyañjaka</s> (suggestive element).
Now, <s>pada-doṣas</s> (word-faults):
A word is faulty [when it is]: <s>apabhraṣṭa</s> (grammatically corrupt), <s>aprayukta</s> (disused by good authors), <s>nirarthaka</s> (meaningless),
<s>viruddhārtha</s> (contradictory in meaning), <s>apuṣṭārtha</s> (weak in meaning), <s>apratīta</s> (unfamiliar), <s>aniścita</s> (ambiguous), // Ckc_1.61 //

children.text:
kliṣṭaṃ deśyaṃ saneyārthaṃ pratihastamavācakam /
jugupsitamakalyāṇaṃ vrīḍākaramitīritam // Ckc_1.62 //
children.translated_text: <s>kliṣṭa</s> (tortured/strained), <s>deśya</s> (provincial), having a low meaning, <s>pratihasta</s> (clashing), <s>avācaka</s> (non-expressive), <s>jugupsita</s> (repulsive), <s>akalyāṇa</s> (inauspicious), and <s>vrīḍākara</s> (shame-inducing) — so it is declared. // Ckc_1.62 //
Among these, <s>apabhraṣṭa</s> means [a word] not sanctioned by the learned.
For example:

children.text: vāgdevyāḥ prabhaviṣyatā prabhavatā gāḍhaṃ prabhutena ca śreyaḥpākabhareṇa siṅganṛpate bhāvajñacūḍhāmaṇim /
children.translated_text: O King <s>Siṅga</s>, by the potency of the goddess of speech, by [your] prevailing power, by [your] mighty lordship, and by the full ripening of [your] auspicious merit — the crest-jewel of connoisseurs —

children.text: tvāṃ jetāramajījanat prasavitā sargasya nocediyaṃ satye vā viphalāyuṣāṃ kṛtadhiyāṃ śāpe na jīveta vim // Ckc_1.*8 //
children.translated_text: the creatrix of the world gave birth to you as a conqueror; otherwise, she would not live in truth, or in the curse of those whose lives are fruitless though wise. // Ckc_1.*8 //
Here, 'jīveta' employs the <s>ātmanepada</s> (middle voice) ending, which is contrary to grammatical rule (<s>anuśāsana</s>).
Therefore, 'jīvet katham' (how could she live?) is the better reading. //
Yet even this [fault] becomes a <s>guṇa</s> (quality) in <s>anukṛti</s> (imitation/mimicry). // Ckc_1.63 //

children.text: rājā saṃskṛtavādiṣu praṇayavānityāśayā guṇbhitaṃ tadbhṛtyatra bhavāmahe padarajairedhema maulisthitaiḥ //
children.translated_text: 'The king is fond of those who speak Sanskrit' — with this intention, [this verse is] made a quality: 'We are his servants here; may we prosper by the dust of his feet placed upon our heads.'

children.text: itthaṃ paṇḍitamānināṃ kṣitibhujāṃ dussaṃskutaṃ vācināṃ taiḥ sākaṃ supadīkaroti kṛpayā śrīsiṅganārāyaṇaḥ // Ckc_1.*9 //
children.translated_text: Thus, <s>Śrīsiṅga-Nārāyaṇa</s> graciously corrects the ill-formed speech of those kings who fancy themselves scholars but speak poorly, together with them. // Ckc_1.*9 //

children.text: atra bhṛtyatnetyasarvanāmno bhṛtyaśabdāt tralpratyayaḥ, bhavāmahe ityātmanepadam padarajairityakārāntatvam edhemetyedhateḥ parasmaipaditvaṃ cāpabhraṃśāḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, 'bhṛtyatra' — the suffix 'tra' is applied to the word 'bhṛtya' (servant) which is not a pronoun; 'bhavāmahe' uses the <s>ātmanepada</s> (middle voice); 'padarajaiḥ' has the non-standard 'a'-ending; 'edhema' uses <s>parasmaipada</s> (active voice) for the root 'edhate' — these are all grammatical corruptions (<s>apabhraṃśa</s>).
Nevertheless, since this is an imitation of the speech of the unlearned, it is not a fault.
<s>Aprayukta</s> (disused) is that which, though grammatically correct, is not employed by poets. // Ckc_1.64 //
For example:
O King, <s>Padmā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) has been abandoned by <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune) who has the lotus-face,
Were it not so, [she] who has lost her fortune would not laugh together with the night-lotuses (<s>kumuda</s>). // Ckc_1.*10 //

children.text: atra "vā puṃsi padmaṃ nalinaṃ'; ityanuśāsane 'pi kavibhiḥ puṃliṅge prāyeṇa na prayujyata iti padmā ityaprayuktamidam /
children.translated_text: Here, although the grammatical rule states 'padma and nalina are also used in the masculine,' poets generally do not use it in the masculine — thus 'padmā' [in feminine] is an instance of <s>aprayukta</s> (disused form).

children.text: padmaṃ tyaktamiti prathamārdhe, na cedasya gataśrīkairiti dvitīyārghe ca pāṭho ramaṇīyaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'Padmaṃ tyaktam' in the first half, and 'na ced asya gataśrīkaiḥ' in the second half — this would be the better reading. //
Even this [fault] is considered a <s>guṇa</s> (quality) by the learned in contexts such as <s>yamaka</s> (paronomasia) and the like. // Ckc_1.65 //
For example:
The assembly of chief <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> desires all the deities (<s>sarvadaivatāḥ</s>);
O King <s>Śrīsiṅga</s>, may they hold [you as] all the deities (<s>sarvadaivatāḥ</s>). // Ckc_1.*11 //

children.text: atra daivataśabdasya puṃliṅge kavibhiranādṛtasyāpi heyatvād āvṛttiyamake prayogo na duṣṭaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, although the word 'daivata' in the masculine gender is not employed by poets, since it is to be avoided [normally], its use in a <s>yamaka</s> (repetition figure) with recurrence is not faulty.
That which is mere <s>pādapūraṇa</s> (verse-padding) and which adds no distinction,
that is called <s>nirarthaka</s> (meaningless) by those who understand word-embellishment. // Ckc_1.66 //
For example:
<s>Kamalā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), fearing the loss of lotuses in winter and such seasons,

children.text: adhyāste sarvavandyā vai mukhaṃ śrī siṅgabhūpateḥ // Ckc_1.*12 //
children.translated_text: she who is worshipped by all, indeed (vai), resides upon the face of King <s>Śrīsiṅga</s>. // Ckc_1.*12 //

children.text:
atra vai iti pādapūraṇamātramā /
kṣiyaḥ sarvavandyeti viśeṣaṇaṃ saśaṅkāyāmadhyāsanakriyāyāṃ viśeṣaṃ nopapādayatīti taddvayaṃ nirarthakam /
"adhyāste sarvadā ramyam'; iti dvitīyārghapāṭho ramaṇīyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, 'vai' is mere <s>pādapūraṇa</s> (verse-padding). And the qualifier 'sarvavandyā' (worshipped by all) does not contribute any distinction to the act of residing [on his face] motivated by fear — thus both [words] are <s>nirarthaka</s> (meaningless). 'Adhyāste sarvadā ramyam' (she always resides beautifully) — this would be the better reading for the second half.
The learned declare that even this [fault] has purposefulness in <s>yamaka</s> and similar [figures]. // Ckc_1.67 //

children.text:
yathā yā praṅktirbrāhnaṇendrāṇāmāśāsta iti pūrvodāhṛtam /
atra nirarthakatvādevakārasya pādapūraṇamātratve 'pi yamakanirvāhakatvādeva sārthatvam /
viruddhārthatvam /
children.translated_text: For example, the verse previously cited: 'yā praṅktir brāhmaṇendrāṇām āśāste' etc. Here, although the particle 'eva' is meaningless and serves as mere <s>pādapūraṇa</s> (verse-padding), it has purposefulness precisely because it enables the completion of the <s>yamaka</s> (repetition figure). [Now follows] <s>viruddhārthatva</s> (contradictory meaning):

children.text: viruddhārtha hi tadyatra viruddhārthaḥ pratīyate // Ckc_1.68 //
children.translated_text: That is called <s>viruddhārtha</s> (contradictory in meaning) where a contradictory sense is apprehended. // Ckc_1.68 //
This lord of <s>Indrāṇī</s>, with the splendor of [one whose] enjoyment [rivals] <s>Guhyakeśa</s> (<s>Śiva</s>),
the <s>Pāṇḍya</s> king shines with glory equal to <s>Gopāla</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>). // Ckc_1.*13 //

children.text: purātanakaviproktaḥ so 'pi doṣāya no bhavet // Ckc_1.69 //
children.translated_text: Even this [fault], when used by ancient poets, does not constitute a defect. // Ckc_1.69 //
For example:
By King <s>Siṅga</s>, who possesses the prowess of the hero of <s>Janaka</s>'s daughter, who shattered the laws of his enemies with his bow,

with matted locks wearing hides and bark-garments made [as if] born of the earth, a likeness to the Lord of <s>Ambikā</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) was attained [that was acknowledged even] by enemy kings. // Ckc_1.*14 //

children.text:
atra janakaputrīnāyako raghurāma iti vivakṣāyāmapi pitṛsutāpatiriti yadyapi viruddhārthaḥ; ambikānātha ityatra ca pārvatīpatiriti vivakṣāyāṃ jananīpatiriti pratīyate tathāpi na virodhaḥ /
nanu-viruddhārthapratītisādhāraṇye ambikānāthādīnāṃ guṇatvaṃ, indrāṇīnāthādīnāṃ doṣatvamitikathaṃ vyavastheti cet; ucyate-prāyikaprayogarūpeṇa śiṣṭānāṃ parigraheṇaiva /
kaipunaratra siṣṭāḥ? yatra prathamaṃ mārgamupadiśanti tatra ta eva siṣṭā iti sthitirarocakinaḥ /
children.translated_text: And who are these 'learned' here? Where they first establish the path, there they themselves are the authorities — this is the position for those of discerning taste.

children.text: purātanāḥ kavīndrā eva śiṣṭāḥ na punaḥ satṛṇābhyavahāriṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: The great ancient poets alone are the authorities, not those who consume grass [i.e., cattle-like imitators].

children.text: ataḥ "dinakarakularatnaṃ jānakīcānireṣaḥ'; iti; "taditijanakaputrī śikṣitā ca'; iti; "janakatanayāsnānapuṇyodakeṣu'; iti; "pāyādvaḥ so 'mbikāramaṇaḥ'; iti; "ambikānitambavimbasparśalampaṭakarāmbujā'; iti; "tāmapāyayata pānamambikām'; iti ca mahākavibhiraṅgīkṛtā guṇaprayogāḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore: 'the jewel of the solar dynasty, the lord of <s>Jānakī</s>'; 'thus <s>Janaka</s>'s daughter was instructed'; 'in the waters sanctified by the bathing of <s>Janaka</s>'s daughter'; 'may that lover of <s>Ambikā</s> protect you'; 'with lotus-hands eager to touch the buttock-region of <s>Ambikā</s>'; 'he made <s>Ambikā</s> drink the drink' — thus these usages are accepted as qualities by the great poets.

children.text: janakaputrīnāyakāmbikāramaṇādīnāṃ guṇatvaṃ svakapolakalpitānāṃ punarindraṇīnāthādīnāmārūḍherasundaratvamiti so 'yaṃ sarasasāhityatīrthakarasaṃmato ghaṇṭāpathaḥ //
children.translated_text: The quality-status of '<s>Janakaputrī-nāyaka</s>', '<s>Ambikā-ramaṇa</s>' and such is [established by great poets], while the ungraceful nature of self-invented compounds like '<s>Indrāṇīnātha</s>' etc. [is evident] — this is the well-trodden path (<s>ghaṇṭāpatha</s>) approved by the authorities of refined literary criticism. //

Here, when the intended meaning is that '<s>Janakaputrī-nāyaka</s>' refers to <s>Raghurāma</s>, the compound literally yields 'husband of the father's daughter' — which is contradictory in meaning. And in '<s>Ambikānātha</s>' (Lord of <s>Ambikā</s>), though the intended meaning is 'husband of <s>Pārvatī</s>,' the literal sense 'husband of the mother' is apprehended — yet there is no fault. Now, if one objects: given that contradictory meaning is common to both, how is it that '<s>Ambikānātha</s>' etc. count as qualities while '<s>Indrāṇīnātha</s>' etc. count as faults? The answer is: precisely through the acceptance by the learned in the form of prevalent usage.
That which conveys a trivial meaning with excessive verbosity is called <s>apuṣṭārtha</s> (weak in meaning). // Ckc_1.69(a) //
For example:
The enemy kings attain a fitness for lordship that is the opposite of the lordship
equal to the majesty of <s>Īśāna</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) — O King <s>Śrīsiṅga</s>. // Ckc_1.*15 //

Here, where one could simply say 'lāghava-yogyatām' (fitness for lightness/insignificance), the verbal heaviness of 'garimaiśvarya-pratīpaiśvarya' (lordship opposite to the lordship of majesty) [is a fault]. //
Even this [fault] sometimes becomes a <s>guṇa</s> (quality) when the intention is to convey heightening or the like. // Ckc_1.70 //
For example, in [describing] the patron's own lineage:
From the lotus-feet of that one was born a <s>varṇa</s> (lineage/stream) free from impurity,
which attained brotherhood with the fruit of <s>Bhagīratha</s>'s penance. // Ckc_1.*16 //

children.text:
atra gaṅgetyarthe kanīyasi bhagīrathatapaḥphalamiti padādhikyam /
tathāpi tasya sagarakutapābanakriyāsūcakatvena gaṅgāśabdādatyutkarṣāpādakatvamiti guṇatvam /
children.translated_text: Here, where the meaning is simply '<s>Gaṅgā</s>' (the Ganges), the elaborate expression '<s>Bhagīratha</s>-tapaḥ-phala' (the fruit of <s>Bhagīratha</s>'s penance) involves verbal excess. Nevertheless, because it indicates the act of bringing down [the Ganges] for the redemption of the sons of <s>Sagara</s>, and thus conveys a heightening beyond what the word '<s>Gaṅgā</s>' alone would, it has the status of a quality.
That which is known only in the <s>Vedas</s> and <s>śāstras</s> is here called <s>apratīta</s> (unfamiliar). // Ckc_1.71 //
For example: O King <s>Śrīsiṅga</s>, by your <s>sphya</s> (sword/sacrificial post) [the realm] flourishes;
the glory of [your] ally <s>Śrīrāma</s>, by [your] <s>manu</s> (mantra/counsel), has grown in the pride-destruction of enemies. // Ckc_1.*17 //

children.text: atra sphyasya khaḍgākāravastuvācakatvaṃ veda eva; manormantravācakatvamāgama eva; vṛddhinirāsakatvaṃ śabdaśāstra eva prasiddhamiti tadapratītam //
children.translated_text: Here, the meaning of 'sphya' as a sword-shaped implement is known only in the <s>Veda</s>; the meaning of 'manu' as mantra is known only in the <s>Āgamas</s>; and the meaning of 'vṛddhi' as removal is known only in the grammatical <s>śāstra</s> — thus these are <s>apratīta</s> (unfamiliar). //
When employed in the course of expounding that very discipline, this [unfamiliar usage] becomes a <s>guṇa</s> (quality). // Ckc_1.72 //
For example:

children.text: īḍāpiṅgalayoḥ pidhāya vadanaṃ baddhvā triśṭaṅgāṭikāṃ sauṣumnopari saṃkramayya sarutaḥ ṣaḍgranthigandhacchidaḥ /
children.translated_text: Closing the openings of <s>Iḍā</s> and <s>Piṅgalā</s>, binding the <s>triśṛṅgāṭikā</s> (triple junction), causing [the breath] to ascend above the <s>Suṣumnā</s> with sound, piercing the six knots (<s>ṣaḍ-granthi</s>),

children.text: prātyagjyotiṣarociṣā prasaratā saṃdrāvya cāṃdrīṃkalāṃ tanniṣṭhyūtaparāmṛtaiḥ paricito yogī ciraṃ jīvati // Ckc_1.*18 //
children.translated_text: melting the lunar digit (<s>cāndrī kalā</s>) with the spreading light of the inward-facing radiance, and nourished by the supreme nectar (<s>parāmṛta</s>) flowing from that — the <s>yogī</s> lives long. // Ckc_1.*18 //

Here, although <s>Iḍā</s>, <s>Piṅgalā</s> and such terms are known only in <s>yogaśāstra</s> and thus would be <s>apratīta</s> (unfamiliar), since the description of the practice of <s>abhyāsa-yoga</s> is coherent throughout, it has the status of a quality.
That is called <s>aniścita</s> (ambiguous) where there is a doubt that does not contribute to heightening. // Ckc_1.73 //
For example:
The lineage of vassal kings, proud of the sole serpent-like devotion to the lotus-feet of King <s>Śrīsiṅga</s>,
is a tree of destiny (<s>kalpakṛt</s>) for the enjoyment of the earth (<s>dhātrī</s>). // Ckc_1.*19 //

children.text:
atropamātā dhātrī dharitrī vā dhātrīti saṃśayapratīteridamaniścitam /
bhūmibhogāyeti pāṭho ramaṇīyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the doubt arises whether '<s>dhātrī</s>' means 'nurse' or 'earth' (<s>dharitrī</s>) — this is <s>aniścita</s> (ambiguous). 'Bhūmibhogāya' (for the enjoyment of the earth) would be the better reading.
This [fault], when the specific meaning is ascertainable from context and the like,

children.text: utkarṣe vāviroghe ca doṣakakṣyāṃ na gāhate // Ckc_1.74 //
children.translated_text: or when it serves heightening or is non-contradictory, does not fall into the category of a fault. // Ckc_1.74 //
For example:

children.text: recarlānvayamaulimaṇḍanamaṇe śrīsiṅgabhūpālaka tvatkhaḍgasya ghanadyuteḥ sa mahimā loke kathaṃ varṇyate /
children.translated_text: O jewel adorning the crown of the <s>Recarlā</s> lineage, King <s>Śrīsiṅga</s>, how can that greatness of your sword, [brilliant] as a dense cloud's radiance, be described in the world?

children.text: yasmin kampitamātra eva samitikṣoṇībhṛtāṃ maṇḍalaṃ sāntatyena vimānavartanakathāmāpnoti mitraissamam // Ckc_1.*20 //
children.translated_text: When merely brandished, the circle of battlefield-kings continuously attains the tale of aerial-chariot-journeying, together with [their] allies. // Ckc_1.*20 //

children.text: atra ghanadyuterityasya ghanā sāndrā dyutirasyeti, ghanasya meghasyeva dyutirasyeti vā saṃśaye 'pyavirodhānna duṣṭatvam /
children.translated_text: Here, 'ghanadyuteḥ' may mean either 'one whose radiance is dense (ghanā)' or 'one whose radiance is like a cloud's (ghanasya)' — yet since both readings are non-contradictory, it is not faulty.

children.text: vimānavarta nakathāmityatra vigatābhimānavartanasya vā vyomayānavartanasya veti saṃśayepyatyantotkarṣānna doṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: In 'vimānavartanakathām,' whether it means 'the tale of the turning away of pride' or 'the tale of journeying in aerial chariots' — even with this doubt, because of the extreme heightening [of meaning], it is not a fault.

children.text: kṣoṇībhṛtāmityatra rājñāṃ girīṇāṃ vetisaṃśaye nāyakakhaḍgavarṇanaprakaraṇāt pratirājalakṣaṇaviśeṣāvagamānna doṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: In 'kṣoṇībhṛtām,' whether it means 'of kings' or 'of mountains' — since from the context of describing the patron's sword, the specific meaning of 'rival kings' is ascertainable, it is not a fault.
In this way, even through conjunction, separation, and other [contextual factors], when a specific meaning is ascertainable, the same [principle] should be observed. //
That is called <s>kliṣṭa</s> (tortured/strained) from which the meaning is very far removed. // Ckc_1.75 //
For example:
Of the enemy kings' women — whose eyes are like the vehicle of the livelihood-giver of the armlets of the companion of the one born from the progenitor of the friend of the ocean —
O King <s>Śrīsiṅga</s>, your own capital became [like] a forest-land. // Ckc_1.*21 //

children.text: atra vārāsimitraṃ mainākaḥ, tasya janko himavān, tatprabhavā pārvatī, tatsahāyo maheśvaraḥ, tatkeyūrāṇi sarpāḥ, teṣāṃ vetanakaṃ jīvanakāraṇaṃ vāyuḥ, tasya yānaṃ vāhanaṃ mṛgaḥ tasya locane iva locane yāsāṃ tāḥ, ityativyavahitārthatvāt kliṣṭamidam //
children.translated_text: Here: the 'friend of the ocean' (vārāśimitra) is <s>Maināka</s>; his progenitor (janaka) is <s>Himavān</s>; born from him (tatprabhavā) is <s>Pārvatī</s>; her companion (sahāya) is <s>Maheśvara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>); his armlets (keyūra) are serpents; their livelihood-source (vetanaka) is wind (<s>Vāyu</s>); its vehicle (yāna) is a deer; [eyes] like that deer's eyes — because the meaning is arrived at through such extremely remote connections, this is <s>kliṣṭa</s> (tortured). //
In completing an [elaborate] compositional scheme, or in indicating the defeat of mighty [foes],

children.text: prayuktasya vkacit kāvye kliṣṭasya guṇathā bhavet // Ckc_1.76 //
children.translated_text: sometimes in poetry, the use of <s>kliṣṭa</s> (strained expression) may attain the status of a <s>guṇa</s> (quality). // Ckc_1.76 //
An example of the completion of sequence (<s>prakramanirvāha</s>) —

children.text: śrīsiṅganṛpo vibhave dhanuṣi naye vapuṣi rañjane jiṣṇum /
children.translated_text: The glorious King <s>Siṅga</s> surpasses <s>Jiṣṇu</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>/Indra) in wealth, in the bow, in statecraft, in body, and in delighting (others);

children.text: tatputraṃ tanmitraṃ tatputraṃ jayati tanmitram // Ckc_1.*22 //
children.translated_text: he surpasses his (Jiṣṇu's) son, his (Jiṣṇu's) friend, his (friend's) son, and his (son's) friend. // Ckc_1.*22 //

children.text: vibhave jiṇuṃ devendraṃ, dhanuṣi tatputraṃ devendraputramarjunaṃ, naye devendraputramitraṃ vāsudevaṃ, vapuṣi devendraputramitraputraṃ pradyumnaṃ, rañjane devendraputramitramitraputramitraṃ candramiti vyavadhānāda durvitarkapratyayamapi tacchabdaprakramanirvāhād guṇatvam //
children.translated_text: In wealth, <s>Jiṣṇu</s> is <s>Devendra</s> (Indra); in the bow, his (<s>Devendra</s>'s) son is <s>Arjuna</s>; in statecraft, <s>Devendra</s>'s son's friend is <s>Vāsudeva</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>); in body, <s>Devendra</s>'s son's friend's son is <s>Pradyumna</s>; in delighting, <s>Devendra</s>'s son's friend's son's friend is <s>Candra</s> (the Moon) — thus, though the referent is difficult to discern due to intervening (terms), the quality arises from the completion of the sequence of the 'tad' (that) pronoun.
An example of indicating the great person's boar-form (<s>hainya</s>) —

O glorious <s>Siṅgabhūpa</s>, long-armed one, guardian of the city's bolt — the portions of the form of the lord (<s>Bhartṛ</s>) with elongated golden hands: those enemies of his have elongated golden hands,

children.text: śrī siṅgabhūpa nagarārgaladīrgabāho tacve 'pyanāyatasuvarṇakaro 'si citram // Ckc_1.*23 //
children.translated_text: yet even regarding that, you (alone) do not have elongated golden hands — how wonderful! // Ckc_1.*23 //

children.text:
atra āyato dīrghabhūtaḥ suvarṇaḥ sukāro yasyeti āyatasuvarṇaḥ tādṛśaḥ karaśabdo yasya saḥ āyatasuvarṇakaraḥ sūkara ityarthaḥ /
āyatasuvarṇakarākṛtiḥ sūkarākṛtiriti viṣṇostiryaktvakathanabhayena vaktrā dūrārthapratyayaḥ śabdaḥ prayukta iti guṇatvam /
children.translated_text: Here, 'elongated' means 'long'; '<s>suvarṇa</s>' means 'good' and '<s>kara</s>' means 'hand' — thus '<s>āyatasuvarṇakara</s>' (one with elongated golden hands). The word '<s>kara</s>' (hand/tusk) yields '<s>sūkara</s>' (boar). '<s>Āyatasuvarṇakarākṛti</s>' means 'one having the form of a boar' — the speaker has used a word with a far-fetched meaning out of fear of mentioning <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s animal incarnation (directly), hence the literary quality.
An example of forceful meaning (<s>haṭhārthapratīti</s>) —

children.text: śaṃbhoḥ sthitā bhūṣaṇapeṭikāyāṃ śriyaḥ sapatnīmabhitaḥ sphurantī /
children.translated_text: Established in <s>Śambhu</s>'s (<s>Śiva</s>'s) ornament-box, surrounding <s>Śrī</s>'s (<s>Lakṣmī</s>'s) co-wife on all sides, radiating brilliantly,

children.text: viṣṇoḥ padaṃ madhyamamāviśantī virājate siṅganṛpālakīrtiḥ // Ckc_1.*24 //
children.translated_text: entering the middle abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s> — the fame of King <s>Siṅga</s> shines forth. // Ckc_1.*24 //

children.text: atra śaṃbhubhūṣaṇapeṭikā pātālam, śrīsapatnī bhūmiḥ, madhyamaviṣṇupadamākāśamiti nātidurbodhatvādakleśakaramiti guṇatvam /
children.translated_text: Here, <s>Śambhu</s>'s ornament-box is the netherworld (<s>pātāla</s>); <s>Śrī</s>'s co-wife is the Earth (<s>Bhūmi</s>); the middle abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s> is the sky (<s>ākāśa</s>) — since (the meanings) are not too difficult to understand and cause no strain, it possesses literary quality.
That which is well-known in a region but lacks (standard) etymological derivation is called <s>deśya</s> (provincial/dialectal). // Ckc_1.77 //
For example —
With beautiful rounded hips wrapped in a <s>pekā</s> (traveling garment), cheeks reddened twofold by the intoxication of <s>hālā</s> (liquor),

children.text: śrīsiṅgabhūpa bhavato mṛgayāvihāre kā vānuyāti yavanī paricārikeva // Ckc_1.*25 //
children.translated_text: O King <s>Siṅgabhūpa</s>, in your hunting sport, what <s>Yavanī</s> (Greek/foreign) woman follows (you) like a maidservant? // Ckc_1.*25 //

children.text: atra pekā paridhānabhastrā, halā madirā, ime deśye /
children.translated_text: Here, '<s>pekā</s>' means a travel-bag (garment), '<s>halā</s>' means liquor — these are provincial words (<s>deśya</s>).
Now (an objection) —
Due to the similarity of '<s>bhastrā</s>' (bag) and '<s>peṭikā</s>' (box), '<s>peṭikā</s>' with elision of the middle (becomes '<s>pekā</s>');

children.text: pekā halā ca halinaḥ priyā deśyā na hīti cet // Ckc_1.78 //
children.translated_text: and '<s>halā</s>' is the beloved of '<s>halin</s>' (<s>Balarāma</s>) — (if so) these are not provincial, (one might say). // Ckc_1.78 //
(Reply:) From the root '<s>kanda</s>' comes '<s>uṭṭīkaṭa</s>' — from '<s>kandāṭṭa</s>' and the like (being) non-provincial (is shown).
Thus, the convention that is supported by etymological resolution is commendable. // Ckc_1.79 //

children.text:
tadidaṃ mārgasaṃkṣobhaprajñākaṇḍūtirujjhyām /
aṅkopālambanāmādau na deśyaṃ dūṣaṇaṃ bhavet // Ckc_1.80 //
children.translated_text: This (provincial usage), in the abandonment of the itch of intellect that disturbs the (correct) path, being first a support for titles (<s>aṅka</s>) — the provincial (word) would not be a fault. // Ckc_1.80 //
'<s>Aṅka</s>' means a title (<s>biruda</s>).
An example of that —
The king, titled <s>Calamartigaṇḍa</s>, who is a <s>Pratigaṇḍabhairava</s> (terrifier of adversaries), is victorious;
<s>Gopāla</s> too was celebrated, the <s>Somakulaparaśurāma</s>, the <s>Pāṇḍayavibhāla</s>. // Ckc_1.*26 //
Here, though '<s>Calamartigaṇḍa</s>' and the like are provincial, their being titles (<s>biruda</s>) makes them a quality.
An example in the context of censure (<s>upārambha</s>) —

children.text: kiṃ dāruṇā koṃkaravaṃkareṇa kiṃ vāsasā cīṃgirimāṃgireṇa /
children.translated_text: What use is a terrible <s>koṃkaravaṃkara</s> (palanquin)? What use is a <s>cīṃgirimāṃgira</s> (variegated) garment?
For beholding the glorious King <s>Siṅgabhūpa</s>, learning alone is the companion of the wise. // Ckc_1.*27 //

children.text:
atra koṅkaravaṃkareṇeti dūṣaṇaṃ padaṃ deśyam /
tādṛśena dāruṇā āndolikayetyarthaḥ /

children.translated_text: '<s>Cīṃgirimāṃgireṇa</s>' — 'variegated with various colors' — the word is provincial;
its meaning is: 'what use is such a garment, i.e., a silk cloth (<s>paṭṭāṃśuka</s>)?'

children.text: atra kaścidāndolikāpaṭṭāṃbarādyāḍaybara mativyayena sampādya nānādiganteṣu rājāsthānāni vigāhya tadvyayamātramapyalabhamātaḥ ṛṇādhikatayā klisyannāḍhambaraṃ vināpi nāyakamālokya tatkaruṇākaṭākṣasamagrībhūta nānāvaibavassana kasmaicidāḍambararahitena bhavatā kathaṃ sampadīdṛśī sampāditeti pṛcchete janāya kevalaṃ vyayakāriṇāndolikāpaṭṭapaṭādibāhyāḍambaravihmbanāpuraḥsaramuttaraṃ vadati /
children.translated_text: Here, a certain person, having acquired palanquins, silk garments, and other pomp with wasteful expenditure of intellect, having entered the courts of kings in various directions, not obtaining even the amount of that expenditure, suffering from excess of debt — without such pomp, merely by seeing the hero (king), having obtained various riches complete through his compassionate side-glance — (he says to) people asking 'how did you acquire such prosperity without any external pomp?' — to those who merely incur expenditure through the deception of external pomp such as palanquins and silk garments, he gives the answer.
Thus here, since '<s>koṃkaravaṃkara</s>' and the like serve as the basis of censure (of ostentation), even though provincial, there is beauty.
Here, '<s>koṅkaravaṃkareṇa</s>' is a fault — the word is provincial; its meaning is: 'with such a terrible palanquin (<s>āndolikā</s>).'
An example in names — in the genealogy of the hero himself —
From those two were born three sons, wish-fulfilling trees of the earth, heroes who terrified enemies:
<s>Siṅgaprabhu</s>, <s>Vennamanāyaka</s>, and the foremost warrior, King <s>Reca</s>. // Ckc_1.*28 //

children.text: atra siṅgama, vennama, recaya śabdānāmavyutpattimacvāddeśyatve 'pi nāmapadatvādaduṣṭapadatvam //
children.translated_text: Here, the words '<s>Siṅgama</s>', '<s>Vennama</s>', '<s>Reca</s>' — though provincial due to lacking (standard) etymology — being proper name words, they are not faulty.
A meaning deliberately contrived by the author (through coded language) is called <s>neya</s> (to be inferred). // Ckc_1.81 //
For example —
The enemies of the king, deprived of reversed vessels (<s>vyatyastapātra</s>, i.e., shame),
are destroyed in the forest swarming with reversed <s>pika</s>s (cuckoos, i.e., monkeys). // Ckc_1.*29 //
Here, the word '<s>pātra</s>' (vessel), by reversal of its letters, indicates '<s>trapā</s>' (shame).
Likewise, '<s>vyāvṛtta</s>' (reversed)
'<s>pika</s>' (cuckoo) becomes '<s>kapi</s>' (monkey) — since it is based on the author's own convention, it is <s>neya</s> (inferential).
In riddles (<s>prahelikā</s>) and the like, this is approved by the learned. // Ckc_1.82 //
For example —

children.text: yogināṃ bhogināṃ kiṃ syādiṣṭametanna vetti yaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'What would be dear to <s>yogin</s>s (ascetics) and <s>bhogin</s>s (enjoyers)? — he who does not know this,

children.text: viparīto harastena na jñāto medinīpate // Ckc_1.*30 //
children.translated_text: the reverse of <s>hara</s> (Śiva) is not known by him, O lord of the earth.' // Ckc_1.*30 //

children.text: atra yogināṃ bhogināñca kiṃ priyamiti praśne raha ityuttare vaktavye viparīto hara ityuktam /
children.translated_text: Here, to the question 'what is dear to ascetics and enjoyers?', the answer should be '<s>raha</s>' (solitude/lovemaking), but '<s>viparīto hara</s>' (the reverse of '<s>hara</s>') is stated (instead).
Though it is based on the author's own convention, since it is a riddle (<s>prahelikā</s>), there is no fault.
<s>Pratihastaka</s> (counter-hand/synonym-indicator) is a device for conveying knowledge of one's own synonym. // Ckc_1.83 //
For example —
'With a sword dark-fanged and terrible,
you, O King <s>Siṅgabhūpa</s>, have cut down your adversaries — (you who are like) camphor.' // Ckc_1.*31 //
From that, <s>Yama</s> (the god of death, associated with <s>kāla</s>) (is understood).
And the word '<s>karpūra</s>' (camphor) indicates its own synonym '<s>ghanasāra</s>' (essence of clouds/camphor).
From that, '<s>adhisāra</s>' (great leader/campaign) is obtained.
Thus, since the words '<s>śyāma</s>' and '<s>karpūra</s>' merely indicate their respective synonyms '<s>kāla</s>' and '<s>ghanasāra</s>', this is <s>pratihastaka</s>.
Here, the word '<s>śyāma</s>' (dark) indicates its own synonym '<s>kāla</s>' (time/death).
In secret letters (<s>gūḍhalekhā</s>) and the like, this (device) generally does not abandon elegance. // Ckc_1.84 //
For example —

On the night (<s>haridrā</s> = <s>niśā</s> = night) when the directions are concealed by the spreading of <s>Rāhu</s> (darkness), having marshalled the army (<s>sārkā</s> = <s>camū</s>), having prepared for adornment (attack) upon the fortress-city (<s>kujarī</s> = <s>nagarī</s>) of the enemies deprived of wings (troops),

children.text: vayaṃ sārkānvītāḥ prahara iti senāpatikṛtā- namātyebhyo lekhān prathayati ca siṅgakṣitipatiḥ // Ckc_1.*32 //
children.translated_text: 'We, accompanied by the army — strike!' — thus King <s>Siṅga</s> dispatches letters, composed by the generals, to the ministers. // Ckc_1.*32 //

children.text:
atra haridrā niśā rātririti yāvat /
rāhustamaḥ dhvāntamiti yāvat /
icchā āśā dik /
prayuktālaṅkṛtiriti prahāraḥ /
viyutagarutāṃ vipakṣāṇām /

children.translated_text: '<s>Kujarī</s>' means 'city' (<s>nagarī</s>).
'<s>Sārkā</s>' means 'army' (<s>senā</s>, <s>camū</s>).
'<s>Prahara</s>' means '<s>yāma</s>' (a watch of the night) / 'let us go.'

children.text: evaṃ haridrādīnāṃ svaparyāyamātrabodhakatvena pratihastatve 'pi senāpatibhirabhiyāti durgocchittaye gataiḥ tadālocitakārya vayaṃ senānvitāḥ timirapihitadaśadiśi niśāyāṃ prahārāya vipakṣāṇāṃ durganagarīṃ yāma ityevaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ mantrabhedabhayād gūḍhalekhamukhena rājñi preṣitamiti na duṣṭatvam //
children.translated_text: Thus, though '<s>haridrā</s>' and the like are <s>pratihastaka</s> (indicating meanings only through their synonyms), since the generals who have gone to cut down the enemy fortress have deliberated upon the plan — 'we, accompanied by the army, in the night when all ten directions are concealed by darkness, go to attack the enemy fortress-city' — this was sent to the king through a coded letter (<s>gūḍhalekhā</s>) out of fear of the secret plan being exposed, hence there is no fault.

Here, '<s>haridrā</s>' means '<s>niśā</s>' (turmeric/night); '<s>Rāhu</s>' means '<s>tamas</s>' (darkness); '<s>icchā</s>' means '<s>āśā</s>' (desire/direction); '<s>prayuktālaṅkṛti</s>' means 'attack' (<s>prahāra</s>); '<s>viyutagarutā</s>' refers to the enemies;
<s>Avācaka</s> (non-expressive) is that which is incapable, employed merely through grammatical formation (without actual expressive power). // Ckc_1.85 //
For example —
In the courtyard of the king's court, the resident horses
neigh sweetly (<s>mañjuvāśante</s>), and the excellent elephants trumpet (<s>śiñjanate</s>). // Ckc_1.*33 //

children.text:
atra tiraśvāṃ rutaṃ vāsitam /
bhūṣaṇaśabdaḥ siñijitamiti maryādāyāṃ "vāśṭa śabdakutsāyām', "śija avyakte śabde'; iti ca yogamātreṇa prayuktau vāśitaśiñjitaśabdau heṣābṛṃhitayoravācakau /
children.translated_text: Here, the sound of animals is '<s>vāsita</s>'; the word for ornament-tinkling is '<s>siñjita</s>' — within the convention that '<s>vāś</s>' is used for sound combined with blame, and '<s>śij</s>' for indistinct sound — the words '<s>vāśita</s>' and '<s>śiñjita</s>', employed merely through (verbal) formation, are non-expressive of neighing and trumpeting.
Even this should be accepted as a quality when it is adopted by authorities in their treatises and the like. // Ckc_1.86 //
For example —

children.text: śrī siṅgabhūmiramaṇe bharitapratāpe nānye sphuranti raṇasīmani rājalokāḥ /
children.translated_text: O beloved of the earth, King <s>Siṅga</s>, filled with might — no other kings flash forth on the battlefield;

children.text: kiṃ vā sphuranti raṭitaspṛśi pāñcajanye līlānukāri taruṇījanakūjitāni // Ckc_1.*34 //
children.translated_text: or do the cooing sounds (<s>kūjita</s>) of young women, which mimic sport, flash forth when the <s>Pāñcajanya</s> (conch of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) resounds? // Ckc_1.*34 //

children.text: atra kāminīnāṃ ratāntareṣu kāmasāstrakāraiḥ haṃsatittirilāvakādirutavikārāmnānāt pakṣiṇo rutādanyatrāvācakasyāpi kūjitasya samarthatvam //
children.translated_text: Here, since the erotic treatise authors (<s>kāmaśāstrakāra</s>s) have enumerated, among the variations of sounds during lovemaking, the sounds of swans, partridges, quails, and the like — '<s>kūjita</s>' (cooing), though non-expressive for birds' sounds in other contexts, becomes competent (in this context).
That from which the mind recoils in disgust is called <s>jugupsita</s> (disgusting), and it is of three kinds:

having a repulsive meaning (<s>heyārtha</s>), having another meaning that is repulsive (<s>heyārthāntara</s>), and being a cause of recollection of a repulsive meaning (<s>heyārthasmṛtihetuka</s>). // Ckc_1.87 //
An example of repulsive meaning (<s>heyārtha</s>) —
With uncouth faces, with great pus oozing from the caverns of their eyes, with the experiencing of burden of putrid belching, with initiation into the desire for flesh,

children.text: heyādantaradantanaiṣṭhikatayā sīdanti durgāṅgaṇe kalyāṇakṣitipapratīpa saraṇī saṃcāriṇo vairiṇaḥ // Ckc_1.*35 //
children.translated_text: suffering from the finality of teeth upon teeth (clenching in agony) in the fortress-courtyard, the enemies who travel the path opposing King <s>Kalyāṇa</s> (suffer thus). // Ckc_1.*35 //
Here, words like 'pus' (<s>dūṣikā</s>), 'putrid' (<s>pūti</s>), and the like — since they directly have a disgusting meaning — constitute <s>heyārtha</s> (repulsive meaning).
An example of having another meaning that is repulsive (<s>heyārthāntara</s>) —
Of those whose splendor is hidden until the end of the appointed time (<s>āsānta</s>), caressed by the hand (of the king),
the sword of King <s>Kalyāṇa</s> is for the enemies an untimely <s>Rāhu</s> (eclipse). // Ckc_1.*36 //

Here, the words '<s>viṭ</s>' and '<s>gūḍhavarcas</s>' — though their intended meaning is 'shining splendor' (of warriors), they also denote excrement (<s>mala</s>) — hence the repulsive alternative meaning.
An example of causing recollection of a repulsive meaning (<s>heyasmṛtihetuka</s>) —
The adversaries, their bodies colored by the dust raised in battle,
are purified (<s>pūyante</s>) by immersion (<s>majjana</s>) in the stream of King <s>Kalyāṇa</s>'s sword. // Ckc_1.*37 //

children.text: atra pūyante majjanenetyanayorvarṇasārūpya brameṇa pūyamajjārthe sarṇejapatvājjugupsārthasmārakatvam /
children.translated_text: Here, '<s>pūyante</s>' and '<s>majjana</s>' — through the resemblance of their syllables — cause the recollection of '<s>pūya</s>' (pus) and '<s>majjā</s>' (marrow), (which are) disgusting in meaning.
The quality-status of these (disgusting expressions) should be accepted (sometimes), as in cases where they are adopted (by great poets) and the like. // Ckc_1.88 //
For example —
Of those women with tender sprout-like palms, with elevated fleshy (<s>māṃsala</s>) breasts,
with the highest pride (<s>māna</s>) among proud women — they are most passionately attached (<s>rakta</s>) to you, O King <s>Siṅga</s>. // Ckc_1.*38 //

Here, though the words '<s>māṃsa</s>' (flesh), '<s>rakta</s>' (blood/passion), '<s>komala</s>' (tender) have disgusting primary meanings or suggest them or remind of them — since they have been accepted by great poets, they possess literary quality.
An example of inauspicious meaning (<s>amaṅgala</s>) —
By the thundering sounds of the war-drums at the occasion of King <s>Siṅgabhūpa</s>'s victory-march,
the enemy kings, their joints suddenly burst open, perish (<s>parimriyante</s>). // Ckc_1.*39 //

children.text:
atra parimriyanta iti sākṣādamaṅgalam /
"nidrānti dīrghaṃ paripanthibhūpāḥ'; iti pāṭho ramaṇīyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, '<s>parimriyante</s>' (they perish) is directly inauspicious. The reading '<s>nidrānti dīrgham</s>' ('they sleep long') is more elegant.
An example of having another meaning that is inauspicious (<s>amaṅgalārthāntara</s>) —
Of the enemies who are in commotion at the preparation of the assembled army of King <s>Siṅgabhūpa</s>,

children.text: saṃtiṣṭhamānaiḥ pūrato ripūṇāṃ kṛtānnibodhaiḥ svavikatthanāni // Ckc_1.*40 //
children.translated_text: the boasts that were made — understand them (as made) by those standing (<s>saṃtiṣṭhamāna</s>) before the enemies! // Ckc_1.*40 //

children.text:
atra santiṣṭhamānairityanena samyak sthitiriva maraṇamapi pratīyate /
uttiṣṭhamānairiti pāṭho ramaṇīyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, by '<s>saṃtiṣṭhamānaiḥ</s>' (those standing firmly), death too is suggested along with firm standing. The reading '<s>uttiṣṭhamānaiḥ</s>' (those rising up) is more elegant.
An example of causing the recollection of something inauspicious (<s>amaṅgalasmaraṇahetu</s>) —
The kings who are protected in their territories by the offerings dedicated to the son of <s>Kātyāyanī</s> (<s>Skanda</s>)
become those who bow down (in submission) to the lord of the earth. // Ckc_1.*41 //
Here, in the word '<s>kukṣayaḥ</s>', the last two syllables cause the recollection of an inauspicious meaning ('<s>kṣaya</s>' = destruction).

children.text: eṣāṃ guptādiṣu prāyo guṇabhāvo 'pi gaṇyate // Ckc_1.89 //
children.translated_text: The quality-status of these is generally recognized when they are concealed (<s>gupta</s>) (by context) and the like. // Ckc_1.89 //

children.text: yo niryasya druhiṇacaraṇo janmabhūmyāṃ nṛpāṇāṃ brahmāṇḍeśe bhagavati paraṃ keśave bhaktibhājām /
children.translated_text: He who, issuing forth from the foot of <s>Druhiṇa</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>), in the birthplace of kings, possessing supreme devotion to <s>Keśava</s>, the lord of the universe,

children.text: kṛtyākṛtyasphuraṇaharaṇe rakṣite yena śo 'yaṃ śatruchedavyasanakuśalo bhāti recarlavaṃśyaḥ // Ckc_1.*42 //
children.translated_text: by whom the discernment of what should and should not be done is protected — he, this descendant of the <s>Recarla</s> lineage, skilled in the pursuit of cutting down enemies, shines forth. // Ckc_1.*42 //

children.text:
atrocchedasya sākṣādamaṅgalārthatve 'pi śatrupadena guptatvādguṇatvam /
kṛtyetyasyāmaṅgalāthatve 'pi kṛtyākṛtye kāryākārye iti sāhacaryeṇa guptatvam /
keśava ityasyāntyavarṇadvayenāmaṅgalārthasmaraṇahetutve 'pi bhagavanmāhātmyena guptatvam /
keśava ityasyāntyavarṇadvayenāmaṅgalārthasmaraṇahetutve 'pi bhagavanmāhātmyena guptatvamityamīṣāṃ guptatvam /
children.translated_text: Here, though '<s>uccheda</s>' (cutting/destruction) has a directly inauspicious meaning, it is concealed by the word '<s>śatru</s>' (enemy), hence it has quality. Though '<s>kṛtya</s>' (sorcery/what should be done) has an inauspicious meaning, it is concealed by the companionship of '<s>kṛtyākṛtya</s>' (what should and should not be done). Though '<s>Keśava</s>' has its last two syllables causing recollection of an inauspicious meaning ('<s>va</s>' = death?), it is concealed by the majesty of the Lord — thus these are concealed.
That which causes shame and is unfit for an assembly — like the previous (categories), it too is of three kinds. // Ckc_1.90 //
Though there are a thousand other lineages devoted to the belly and the private parts,
this one <s>Recarla</s> lineage is devoted to the protection of the virtuous. // Ckc_1.*43 //

children.text:
atra śipūrvaśnaṃ sākṣādasabhyārtham /
nijodareti pāṭho ramaṇīyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here the word beginning with 'śi' followed by 'śna' is directly an <s>asabhyārtha</s> (obscene meaning). The reading 'nijodarā' is the preferable one.
An example of <s>asabhyārthāntara</s> (indirect obscene meaning):
The enemies of <s>Siṅgabhūvara</s> (King <s>Siṅga</s>), their foundations shattered by the force of his army's river-flood,

children.text: yānti ke 'pi yamapālitāṃ dviṣo guhyakeśakalitāṃ diśāṃ pare // Ckc_1.*44 //
children.translated_text: some go to the realm guarded by <s>Yama</s>, while others flee to the direction adorned by <s>Guhyakeśa</s> (<s>Kubera</s>). [Ckc 1.44]

children.text:
atra guhyakeśaśabdaḥ kuberamivakutsitakeśārthamapi vyanaktītyasyāsabhyārthāntaratvam /
yakṣarājakalitāmiti pāṭho ramaṇīyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here the word <s>Guhyakeśa</s> also suggests the meaning 'one with despicable hair,' like <s>Kubera</s>, and thus this is a case of <s>asabhyārthāntara</s> (indirect obscene meaning). The reading '<s>Yakṣarāja</s>-kalitām' is the preferable one.
An example of <s>asabhyatvasmaraka</s> (reminiscent of obscenity):
The feudatory kings, having obtained royal enjoyments through the grace of service to the lotus feet of the glorious <s>Siṅgabhūpāla</s>,
sport in the garden groves among the fluttering bees hovering over the <s>śephālikā</s> (Night Jasmine) flowers. [Ckc 1.45]
Here the first pair of syllables of the word <s>śephālikā</s> causes the recollection of an obscene meaning. The reading '<s>vāsantikā</s>-cañcala' is the preferable one.
And the becoming-a-merit of these [apparent faults] is observed in the examples cited and others. [Ckc 1.91]
For example, in the previous illustration: '<s>yonir</s> of whom is <s>Druhiṇa</s>'s foot' —

children.text: yonirityasabhyārthatve 'pi yoniriva yoniriti gauṇavṛcyā na duṣṭatvam /
children.translated_text: even though '<s>yoni</s>' has an obscene meaning, since it is used in the figurative sense (<s>gauṇavṛtti</s>) meaning 'like a <s>yoni</s> (source/origin),' there is no fault.
Even though the words '<s>janmabhūmi</s>' (birthplace) and '<s>bhagavat</s>' have indirect obscene meanings, their being commonly accepted in ordinary usage makes them a merit (<s>guṇa</s>).

And even though the latter pair of syllables in '<s>Brahmāṇḍa</s>' causes the recollection of an obscene meaning, since it is concealed through the figurative usage (<s>gauṇavṛtti</s>) meaning 'like an <s>aṇḍa</s> (egg/cosmic egg),' it is a merit.
One should not say that all of these have the quality of being a merit or a non-merit simply on the basis of their similarity in having objectionable meanings,
by those who are harsh with logic alone. [Ckc 1.92]
The same thing has attained the status of being either a fault or a merit for different people,
in accordance with those fit for the direct realization of the <s>Brahman</s> (supreme essence) of literature that produces <s>camatkāra</s> (aesthetic wonder). [Ckc 1.93]
Some learned authorities have permitted words like '<s>kumārī</s>,' '<s>kamala</s>,' and the like;
but never before [have they permitted] words like '<s>śraviṣṭhā</s>,' '<s>saṃsthāna</s>,' or those beginning with 'śi' followed by 'śna.' [Ckc 1.94]

children.text: yaiḥ kaiśvitprāktanī sīmā na laṅghyā kovidairapi /
children.translated_text: By some [scholars], the boundary set by the ancients should not be transgressed even by the learned.
Following only the path laid down by them, examining merits and faults — [Ckc 1.95]
one should compose poetry that endures through the end of a <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic age), free from calamity. [Ckc 1.96]
<s>Śrīḥ</s> (Auspiciousness).

children.text: iti sarasasāhityacāturīdhurīṇaśrīviśveśvarakavicandrapraṇītāyāṃ śrīsiṅgabhūpālasudhāsāraśītalāyāṃ camatkāracandrikāyāṃ varṇapadaviveko nāma prathamo vilāsaḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the first <s>vilāsa</s> (chapter) named '<s>Varṇapadaviveka</s>' (Discernment of Letters and Words) in the <s>Camatkāracandrikā</s> — cool as the essence of nectar of the glorious <s>Siṅgabhūpāla</s> — composed by the illustrious <s>Viśveśvara Kavicandra</s>, who excels in the art of graceful literary composition.
Second <s>Vilāsa</s> (Chapter).
<s>Camatkāracandrikā</s> composed by <s>Viśveśvara Kavicandra</s>, Second <s>Vilāsa</s>.

children.text: samanvitapadaṃ vākyaṃ lakṣakaṃ vyañjakañca tat // Ckc_2.1 //
children.translated_text: A <s>vākya</s> (sentence) is that which has syntactically connected words (<s>samanvitapada</s>), and it can be <s>lakṣaka</s> (indicative) or <s>vyañjaka</s> (suggestive). [Ckc 2.1]
Now, <s>vākya</s> (the sentence).
An example of a <s>lakṣaka</s> (indicative) sentence:
O lord <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>, ruler of the earth! That you are sung as one who shelters those devoted to the exalted, who speaks no falsehood — this has now been fully proven by you.

children.text: madbhāgyāni pacelimāni nitarāmevaṃ sapatnījane- ṣvārūḍhāsmi cirāya tāvakakṛpāsaṃbhāvanāyā padam // Ckc_2.*1 //
children.translated_text: These are the fruits of my fortune indeed! Thus among my co-wives I have long ascended to the station of being favored by your grace. [Ckc 2.1*]

children.text: atra mānavatyāḥ kṛtāparādhe dayite cāṭuvākyasyāsaṃbaddhatvād vipralambhako 'sītyādi vācyaviruddhor'tho lakṣyate /
children.translated_text: Here, the flattering speech of the offended heroine (<s>mānavatī</s>) to her erring beloved, being incoherent, indicates a meaning contrary to what is literally said — namely 'you are a deceiver' and so forth. This is <s>lakṣaṇā</s> (indication).
An example of a <s>vyañjaka</s> (suggestive) sentence:
The king, with feet lovely as those fashioned by the cool season, with hands that caress like dark sapphire, with limbs pleasing to the eye,

children.text: rājācale sumahasā mudayānukūle rājā virājati satāmuparañjanāya // Ckc_2.*2 //
children.translated_text: shines with great splendor on the royal mountain (<s>Rājācala</s>), in a manner favorable to joy, for the delight of the virtuous. [Ckc 2.2*]

children.text: atra śabdaśaktimūlo nāyakatārakānāyakayorupamārūpo 'nuraṇanadhvaniḥ sarveṇaivavākyena pratīyata iti vyañjakamidam /
children.translated_text: Here, the <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion) of <s>anuraṇana</s> (sympathetic resonance) in the form of a comparison (<s>upamā</s>) between the hero-star (<s>Nāyakatāraka</s>) and the hero (<s>Nāyaka</s>), rooted in the power of words (<s>śabdaśakti</s>), is apprehended through the entire sentence — hence this is <s>vyañjaka</s> (suggestive).
Now, <s>vākyadoṣāḥ</s> (faults of the sentence):
<s>Apaprayukta</s> (misapplication), <s>duḥsandhi</s> (bad juncture), <s>vyutkrama</s> (disordered sequence), <s>punaruktimat</s> (redundant),
<s>duranvaya</s> (difficult construal), <s>vākyāṅgasaṅkīrṇa</s> (confused sentence-parts), <s>vākyagarbhita</s> (sentence within a sentence), [Ckc 2.2]
two kinds of <s>bhinnaliṅgavacana</s> (inconsistent gender and number), two kinds of <s>nyūnādikopama</s> (deficient or excessive simile),
<s>vikala</s> (defective), and <s>kevala</s> (isolated) — thus faulty sentences are described here. [Ckc 2.3]
<s>Apaprayukta</s> (misapplication) is where there is an incorrect usage (<s>apaśabdana</s>) in the combination of words. [Ckc 2.4]
For example:

children.text: rājānyo hi dhanānyalaṃ janapadāna viṣpīḍyatānyanvahaṃ paṇyastrīviṭaceṭapātraṭhanaṭastomāya saṃyacchate /
children.translated_text: Other kings indeed, squeezing their territories daily, bestow wealth to the retinue of courtesans, rakes, servants, actors, and buffoons.

children.text: śrīsiṅgakṣitipālakaḥ punarayaṃ nyāyakramairarjitānyurvīdevajanāya vedaviduṣe vittāni dattetarām // Ckc_2.*3 //
children.translated_text: But this king <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>, the protector of the earth, gives wealth earned through righteous means abundantly to the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and the learned in the <s>Vedas</s>. [Ckc 2.3*]
Here, in the expression '<s>stomāya</s>,' since the usage is unrefined, a third case-ending (instrumental) should have been used for the meaning of the fourth case (dative).
Nevertheless, the use of the dative case — this is the <s>apaprayoga</s> (misapplication), a sentence fault.
The discerners of merits and faults declare that even this [fault] becomes a merit in some cases, depending on the speaker's intention,
by virtue of its natural beauty. [Ckc 2.5]
For example:

children.text: asmatkalpalatādalāni gilati tvatkāmagaurvāryatāṃ maccintāmaṇivedibhiḥ pariṇamed dūrānnayoccairgajam /
children.translated_text: Your <s>Kāmagaurī</s> (wish-granting cow) swallows the leaves of our wish-fulfilling creeper; may our <s>Cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling gem) platforms transform from afar; drive the lordly elephant far away!

children.text: ityārūḍhavitardikāḥ pratipataṃ jalpanti bhūdevatāḥ siṅgakṣmābhuji kalpavṛkṣasurabhīhastyādidānodyate // Ckc_2.*4 //
children.translated_text: Thus the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> (<s>Bhūdevatāḥ</s>), having climbed the platforms, exclaim one after another, when King <s>Siṅga</s> sets out to give elephants, wish-fulfilling trees, and other gifts. [Ckc 2.4*]

children.text: atra kāmagavīti vaktavye kāmagauriti yaduktaṃ tadidaṃ "gorataddhitaluki'; iti ṭapratyayasya samāsāntavidhiranitya ityanityatvādarthaprasādavivakṣayā nāpaprayuktam /

children.translated_text: And thus is the usage of the great poet, in the <s>Mahākāvya</s> (great poem) named <s>Tīrthakarakramottaṃsa</s> —

children.text: śubhrābhraṅkaṣaśekhareṣu viduṣāṃ vāseśu vāgbhāsināṃ bhavyatvatkaruṇā kaṭākṣakaṇikāsparśena darśeśvara /
children.translated_text: O <s>Darśeśvara</s>! In the abodes of the learned whose speech shines, [abodes] with peaks touching the bright clouds, through the touch of a drop of your auspicious compassionate side-glance,

children.text: kālaṃ vaijananaṃ vinā phalavatī stalpanti kalpadrumāḥ paṅktiḥ kāmagavāñca nirbharataraṃ prasnoti vatsān vinā // Ckc_2.*5 //
children.translated_text: without seasonal limitation, the rows of wish-fulfilling trees (<s>Kalpadruma</s>) bear fruit, and the wish-granting cows (<s>Kāmagavā</s>) overflow with milk even without calves. [Ckc 2.5*]

Here, where one should say '<s>Kāmagavī</s>,' the expression '<s>Kāmagaurī</s>' was used. This is because the rule '<s>gorataddhitaluki</s>' prescribes the <s>ṭap</s> suffix as a <s>samāsānta</s> (compound-final) element, but this rule is optional (<s>anitya</s>), and so with the intention of clarity of meaning (<s>arthaprasāda</s>), it is not a misapplication.
For those whose minds are lazy in perceiving the greatness of the <s>śāstras</s> (treatises) and such,
it [such usage] may seem like incorrect speech, but it does not abandon its beauty. [Ckc 2.6]
Thus.
Thus. And the <s>ācāryas</s> (teachers) have said:
<s>Duḥsandhi</s> (bad juncture) is declared to be that which has unjoined (<s>aśliṣṭa</s>), harsh (<s>kaṣṭa</s>), or vulgar (<s>aślīla</s>) juncture and the like. [Ckc 2.7]
An example of <s>aśliṣṭa</s> (unjoined) and <s>kaṣṭa</s> (harsh) juncture:

children.text: kalyāṇasya inendutulyamahaso avyājaśauryaśriyo vidviḍḍhrībharaḍhogdhra sidyutiyujo dhṛtyā atanvyā uroḥ /
children.translated_text: Of the auspicious one, equal in splendor to the moon, of genuine heroic glory, endowed with the lustre of crushing enemy pride, with a broad chest of unfailing courage,

children.text: śrotre ūrjitakuṇḍale ururuciṃ ādyāṃ kaviprakriyāṃ nāśrāvyāṃ sahataḥ susandhilalite dussandhisambandhinīm // Ckc_2.*6 //
children.translated_text: with ears adorned with large earrings, the foremost poetic art of great beauty — one should not make heard, in a composition lovely with good juncture, that which is associated with bad juncture. [Ckc 2.6*]

children.text:
atra saṃhitā vivakṣiteti prathamapāde padānāmaśliṣṭasandhitvād duḥsandhitvam /
vidviḍḍhrībharetyādi pade śrutikaṭurūpakaṣṭa sandhitvād duḥsandhitvam /
dhṛtyā atanvyā urorityatra luptavisargaprāyakaṣṭasandhitvād duḥsandhitvam /
children.translated_text: Here, since <s>saṃhitā</s> (connected recitation) is intended, the unjoined juncture (<s>aśliṣṭasandhi</s>) of the words in the first quarter constitutes <s>duḥsandhi</s> (bad juncture). In the word '<s>vidviḍḍhrībhara</s>' etc., the harsh-sounding juncture (<s>kaṣṭasandhi</s>) constitutes <s>duḥsandhi</s>. In '<s>dhṛtyā atanvyā uroḥ</s>,' the predominantly elided-<s>visarga</s> harsh juncture constitutes <s>duḥsandhi</s>.
In the third quarter, the predominantly <s>pragṛhya</s> (non-combining vowel) harsh juncture constitutes <s>duḥsandhi</s>.
An example of <s>aślīlasandhi</s> (vulgar juncture):
Look, dear one! Frightened within by the fall of the sword-blades of the noble king,

children.text: saromayā sītkṛtasindhupūraṃ vigāḍhamārtasya kuto vivekaḥ // Ckc_2.*7 //
children.translated_text: with hair standing on end, hissing with the flood of the river — when one is deeply plunged in distress, whence comes discernment? [Ckc 2.7*]
In a remarkable [composition], a single <s>pragṛhya</s> [vowel] at the beginning provides the ground for [being considered] a merit. [Ckc 2.8]
For example:

The ocean, that treasure-house, produces the prosperity of <s>Śrī</s> and of the lotus for King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>, the protector of the earth. He, whose arms have frightened and alarmed the mountain-kings,

children.text: madāndhadve ṣistrīkucakalaśakāśmīramakarī- nirāsavyāsaktiṃ śiva śiva caritrāṇi mahatām // Ckc_2.*8 //
children.translated_text: intoxicated with the saffron paste from the pitcher-like breasts of the enemy's women — O <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Śiva</s>! Such are the deeds of the great! [Ckc 2.8*]

children.text: atra kamalardherityasya kaṣṭasandhitve 'pi kamalāyāḥ kamalasya ca ṛddheriti śleṣanivahiphalatvāt sakṛdeveti guṇatvam /
children.translated_text: Here, even though '<s>kamalardheḥ</s>' has a harsh juncture, because it yields the double meaning (<s>śleṣa</s>) — 'the prosperity of <s>Kamalā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>)' and 'the prosperity of the lotus' — it is a merit, being only a single instance.
An example of a single <s>pragṛhya</s> [serving as merit]:
Your wisdom too, like your eyes, grasps subtle meanings.
Like the expedition of <s>Śrī Siṅgabhūpa</s>, your fame transgresses the boundaries of kings. [Ckc 2.9*]

children.text: atra locane iveti kaṣṭasandhitve 'pi pragṛhyatvāt sakṛdeveti guṇatvam /
children.translated_text: Here, even though '<s>locane iva</s>' has a harsh juncture, because it is a <s>pragṛhya</s> (non-combining dual ending), it is only a single instance and thus a merit.
Vulgar juncture (<s>sandhyaślīla</s>) should everywhere be avoided, like a wicked person.

children.text: asyāpi ca gṛṇībhāve na grāhyaṃ nagnadarśanam // Ckc_2.9 //
children.translated_text: And even in the case of this [fault] becoming a merit, one should not accept blatant exposure (<s>nagnadarśana</s>). [Ckc 2.9]

children.text:
yathā yogyaṃ prayojyasya śabdasyārthasya vā kramaḥ /
