Here, 'mango blossoms in autumn' is a contradiction of time. 'Lotus in a furnace-belly' is a contradiction of reasoning. 'Stones laughing' is a contradiction of popular convention. Despite their faultiness, these serve as the four portents foretelling the calamity about to befall the enemy kingdoms through the hero's anger, hence they possess literary quality.

Here, though the presence of musk deer and camphor trees in the <s>Āndhra</s> region is a contradiction of place, since the intention is to describe the hero's extraordinary power — able to receive tribute-gifts from rulers of various islands — it possesses literary quality.
Poetry, consisting of word and meaning, is declared by those learned in word and meaning
to produce <s>camatkāra</s> (aesthetic wonder) in three degrees — <s>camatkārī</s> (wonder-producing), <s>camatkāritara</s> (more wonder-producing), // Ckc_3.36 //

children.text:
camatkāritamaṃ ceti pravivicya nidarśitam /
śabdacārutvatātparye camatkārīti kathyate // Ckc_3.37 //
children.translated_text: and <s>camatkāritama</s> (most wonder-producing) — these are distinguished and demonstrated. When the emphasis is on verbal beauty, it is called <s>camatkārī</s>. // Ckc_3.37 //
For example —
With drinking-cups fashioned from rows of lotus buds, from the soft humming bee-garland arrangement and the like,

children.text: sarasi sarasatīre sārasārāpasāre viharati bharitaughe rājaśailādhirājaḥ // Ckc_3.*49 //
children.translated_text: on the lake and its lovely banks, amid the departing cranes, in the flood-filled waters, the sovereign of the royal mountain disports. // Ckc_3.*49 //

children.text: atrānuprāsanirvahaṇamātre kaviprayatnasya viśrānteḥ śabdamātracārutvādidaṃ kāvyaṃ camatkārītyucyate /
children.translated_text: Here, since the poet's effort rests merely in the execution of <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration), this poem is called <s>camatkārī</s> (wonder-producing) due to its beauty being purely verbal.
When the emphasis is on beauty of expressed meaning, it is considered <s>camatkāritara</s> (more wonder-producing). // Ckc_3.38 //
For example —

children.text: śrīsiṅgakṣitipāla tāvakacamūdhāṭībhayāṭīkitān ākārairapi śābarairapihitān ghorāṅgaṇe phakkaṇe /
children.translated_text: O King <s>Śrīsiṅga</s>, in the dreadful <s>Phakkaṇa</s> (tribal) territory, your army's march has terrified them — though disguised even in <s>Śabara</s> (tribal) appearances, and concealed —

children.text: ātmīyaiva hi paśyatāṃ piśunayatyābālagaupālakaṃ bhūpālātkuliśātapatra kalaśīcihnā padānāṃ tatiḥ // Ckc_3.*50 //
children.translated_text: yet their own trail of footprints marked with the signs of thunderbolt, parasol, and water-vessel betrays them to the very cowherds and children, O king. // Ckc_3.*50 //

children.text:
atra kaitavakirātānāṃ pratināyakānāṃ kulisādirājalakṣaṇalakṣitapadāvalīparijñānena yadime rājāna ityabhyūhanaṃ so 'yamanumānāmaṅkāraḥ /
tatraiva kaviprayatnasya viśrāntiriti vācakākṣaramullaṅghya vācyacārutvatātparyāditaṃ camatkāritaramityucyate /
children.translated_text: Here, the inference — that the trail of footprints bearing royal insignia such as thunderbolt reveals that these deceitful <s>Kirāta</s> (tribal) adversaries are actually kings — constitutes the figure <s>anumānālaṃkāra</s> (inference as ornament). Since the poet's effort rests there precisely, transcending the mere verbal expression to emphasize the beauty of expressed meaning, this is called <s>camatkāritara</s> (more wonder-producing).
When the suggested meaning becomes the dominant element, the learned call that very same (poetry)
the most wonder-producing; here, the suggested meaning, subordinated (to various degrees), is said to be of eight kinds. // Ckc_3.39 //
<s>Agūḍha</s> (unconcealed), <s>aparasyāṅga</s> (subordinate to another), <s>vācyasiddhyaṅga</s> (auxiliary to establishing the expressed), <s>asphuṭa</s> (indistinct),
<s>sandigdha</s> (doubtful), <s>tulyaprādhānya</s> (of equal prominence), <s>kāvyākṣipta</s> (superseded by irony), and <s>asundara</s> (unbeautiful). // Ckc_3.40 //
Thus.
And thus they state —
An example of <s>agūḍha vyaṅgya</s> (unconcealed suggestion) —
Seeing the gardens on the royal mountain, now rendered unlovely, with their grounds frequented by herds of musk deer and their rows of camphor trees,

children.text: vismerā hṛdi pañcavarṇakaśukādākarṇya karṇotsavaṃ śrīsiṅgakṣitipālavikramakalāṃ nandantyapūrve janāḥ // Ckc_3.*51 //
children.translated_text: amazed at heart upon hearing the delightful sounds of the five-colored parrots, the people marvel at the unprecedented prowess of King <s>Śrīsiṅga</s>. // Ckc_3.*51 //

children.text: atra vikramakalāmityarthaśaktimūlasya nānādvīpādhipaprahitasyopāyanaviśeṣarūpasya vyaṅgyasyoparyeva prabhāvādidamagūḍhaṃ vyaṅgyaṃ nāma camatkāritaraṃ kāvyam /
children.translated_text: Here, the suggested meaning — the special tribute-gifts sent by rulers of various islands, rooted in the semantic power of the word '<s>vikramakalā</s>' (prowess-art) — being openly displayed above (the expressed meaning), this is called <s>agūḍha vyaṅgya</s> (unconcealed suggestion), and the poem is <s>camatkāritara</s> (more wonder-producing).
An example of <s>aparāṅga vyaṅgya</s> (suggestion subordinate to another sentiment) —

children.text: cūtālokabhiyā nimīlitadṛśo rañjanti bhāgāntaraṃ bandhūnāṃ ca kuhūbhiyā śrutirudho nākarṇayantyo giraḥ /
children.translated_text: With eyes shut from fear of seeing mango trees, coloring other regions, the kinswomen with ears stopped not hearing speech from fear of the cuckoo's call,

children.text: pāndhairbhūtabhiyā palāyanaparairnāveditādhvakramāḥ khidyanti tvadaristriyo vanabhuvi śrīsiṅgapṛthvīpate // Ckc_3.*52 //
children.translated_text: the routes unreported by frightened travellers fleeing in terror of ghosts — the wives of your enemies, O King <s>Śrīsiṅga</s>, suffer in the forest. // Ckc_3.*52 //
An example of <s>vācyasiddhyaṅga</s> (suggestion auxiliary to establishing the expressed meaning) —
By the six and the previous sixteen, one <s>gaurī</s> (fair queen) was made a chief queen;
that very one was shattered by the elephant of King <s>Śrīsiṅgabhūpāla</s>. // Ckc_3.*53 //
Here, the <s>vipralambha</s> (love-in-separation) of the enemy's wives is subordinate to the <s>karuṇa</s> (pathos) sentiment.

children.text: atra vaśeti gajakāntālakṣaṇaṃ vyaṅgyaṃ bhūpālakuñjareṇetyatropamārūpakasandehe rūpakasiddhimupapādayatīti vācyasiddhyaṅgamidam /
children.translated_text: Here, '<s>vaśa</s>' suggests the characteristics of an elephant in rut (<s>gajakāntā</s>); in the doubt between simile and metaphor at 'elephant of the king,' it supports the establishment of the metaphor — hence this is <s>vācyasiddhyaṅga</s> (suggestion auxiliary to the expressed).
An example of <s>asphuṭa</s> (indistinct suggestion) —
Wonderful! King <s>Śrīsiṅgabhūpāla</s>, having churned the enemy army,
pours forth <s>amṛta</s> (nectar) that causes delight to the ears of all. // Ckc_3.*54 //

children.text:
atra mandaraḥ samudraṃ vimathya keṣāṃcideva rasanānandakāraṇa mamṛtamutpādayāmāsa /
nāyakastu vāhinīṃ vimathya sarvalokaśravaṇānandakāraṇaṃ kīrtirūpamamṛtaṃ dikṣupūrayatīti mandarānnāyakasyādhikyapratipādanāt pratīyamānasya vyatirekasya nātisphuṭatvam /
children.translated_text: Here, <s>Mandara</s> (the churning mountain), having churned the ocean, produced <s>amṛta</s> that delighted the palate of only some. But the hero, having churned the army, fills all directions with nectar in the form of fame that delights the ears of all. Since the suggested <s>vyatireka</s> (distinction showing the hero's superiority over <s>Mandara</s>) is not very distinct, this is <s>asphuṭa</s> (indistinct suggestion).
An example of <s>sandigdha vyaṅgya</s> (doubtful suggestion) —
The generals of King <s>Śrīsiṅgabhūpa</s>'s army, seated upon the jeweled arches and pavilions of the court hall,

children.text: ālokanena haridāgatarāja rājir- dṛṣṭā kapolatalakandalitasmitena // Ckc_3.*55 //
children.translated_text: were seen with a smile blooming on their cheeks, gazing upon the procession of kings arriving from all directions. // Ckc_3.*55 //

children.text: atra nānādigantāgatarājakagocaraṃ senāpatīnāṃ sasmitānalokanaṃ saṃbhāvanābhiprāyeṇa vā raṇeṣu prabhūtatadīyakātaradaśāsmaraṇena veti sandehaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, is the smiling gaze of the commanders toward the kings arriving from various quarters out of respect and welcome, or from the recollection of the abundant terror they caused those very kings in battles? — this is the doubt.
An example of <s>tulyaprādhānya vyaṅgya</s> (suggestion of equal prominence) —
O King <s>Śrīsiṅgabhūpāla</s>, the rise of the sun of your <s>pratāpa</s> (valour)
continually scorches the kings who bear parasols. // Ckc_3.*56 //

children.text: atra sātapatrān śatrūn pratāpatapanaḥ santāpayatīti vācyasya nirātapatrān naḥ santāpayatīti vyaṅgyasya ca prādhānyaṃ samameva pratīyate /
children.translated_text: Here, the expressed meaning — 'the sun of valour scorches the parasol-bearing enemies' — and the suggested meaning — 'it scorches us who are without parasols (unprotected)' — are perceived with equal prominence.
An example of <s>kākvākṣipta</s> (superseded by irony) —

children.text: bhadrebhādaśanabhatakṣitidharagrāvaśriyo 'gre sthitāḥ rājirvā javanirjitārkahayatā vibhrājināṃ vājinām /
children.translated_text: Before whom stand noble elephants rivalling mountain boulders in their tusk-lustre, and rows of horses whose speed defeats the sun's steeds and who shine splendidly —

children.text: uddaṇḍapratigaṇḍabhairavavibhuṃ prāṇeśa śuddhāṅgaṇe hantādyāpi didṛkṣase na suhṛdaḥ prāṇā na cāhaṃ hitāḥ // Ckc_3.*57 //
children.translated_text: O dear one, even today you do not wish to see the fierce lord <s>Uddaṇḍapratigaṇḍabhairava</s> in the open courtyard? Your life is not dear to you, nor am I cherished! // Ckc_3.*57 //

children.text: atra pratināyakamuddiśya taddevīvākye gandhagajā vājino vā tavāgre na sthitā prāṇāsva priyā evāhaṃ ca tava hitaiveti vyaṅgyaṃ pratīyamānamapi kuñjarādayo 'gre sthitā vā ityādi kākusahakāriṇā vācakaśabdenaivākṣipyata ityupasarjanībhūtatvam /
children.translated_text: Here, in the speech of the enemy king's queen addressed to the rival king, the suggestion perceived — that 'war elephants and horses do not stand before you, your own life is not dear, and I too am not cherished by you' — though perceptible, is superseded by the ironic word-force of the verbal expression 'are they not standing?' etc.; hence the suggestion is subordinated.
An example of <s>asundara</s> (unbeautiful suggestion) —
Transgressing the abode of the Creator (<s>Brahmā</s>), flashing forth, causing the serpent-worlds to tremble,

children.text: śrīsiṅgabhūpāla tava prabhāvāt ślāghyā hi kīrtiḥ sumanogṛheṣu // Ckc_3.*58 //
children.translated_text: O King <s>Śrīsiṅgabhūpāla</s>, by your might, your fame is indeed praiseworthy in the abodes of the gods. // Ckc_3.*58 //

children.text: atra kīrteḥ dhūrtastriyā sāmyaṃ śabdaśaktipratītamapi vācyādanatiśāyīti na sundaram /
children.translated_text: Here, the similarity of fame (<s>kīrti</s>) to a loose woman — perceived through the semantic power of the words — since it does not surpass the expressed meaning, is not beautiful.
When the beauty lies in the suggested meaning, it is considered <s>camatkāritama</s> (most wonder-producing). // 40 //
For example —
King <s>Siṅga</s> is an adorner (<s>alaṅkārī</s>); <s>Rāghava</s> (<s>Rāma</s>) was a destroyer of <s>Laṅkā</s> (<s>Laṅkārī</s>);
the difference of a single letter (<s>varṇāntara</s>) between the two is heard and universally acknowledged. // Ckc_3.*59 //

children.text:
atra varṇenākṣareṇāntaraṃ bhedo yayostacvamiti vācye pratiṣṭhite varṇo vaiśyajātirantaraṃ nāyakaraghunāyakayoriti parasparavyatirekālahkāro vyaṅgyaḥ /
tasyaiva kavitātparyaviśrāntidhāmatvāccārutvamiti camatkāritamatvam /
children.translated_text: Here, with the expressed meaning established — that the difference between them is one of a letter (syllable) — the suggested meaning is the figure <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast): by <s>varṇa</s> meaning 'caste,' the difference is that King <s>Siṅga</s> and <s>Raghu</s>'s hero belong to different castes (one adorns, the other destroys). Since this suggestion is the resting-place of the poet's ultimate intention, it possesses beauty — hence it is <s>camatkāritama</s> (most wonder-producing).
Or, for example —
Having broken through iron pillars, nourisher of the devoted <s>Prahlāda</s>,
this <s>Narasiṃha</s> (<s>Śrīpatinaṃra</s>), bowing to <s>Śrīpati</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), shines as the crest-jewel of kings. // Ckc_3.*60 //

children.text:
atra śabdaśaktimūlo nāyakavaikuṇṭhakaṇṭhīravayorupamālaṅkāro vyajyate /
anena ca kṣaṇādiva nāyako nikhilavirodhividāraṇakriyāpariṇati samarthanirvakraparākrama iti vidhirupaṃ vastu vyajyate /
etena ca nāyakena saha virodho na karaṇīya iti niṣedharūpaṃ vastu, amunā ca nāyakapratibhaṭībhūtā mahīpālā nirbuddhaya ityutprekṣā vyajyate /
anayā ca nāyakavirodhino naranāyakā daivaparāhatā ityutprekṣāparā vyajyate /
evaṃ pratiśatrupratibhāviśeṣapratyayārthaparaṃparāsamunmeṣasaṃpannatayā bāḍhamacintyamahimaviśrāntidhāmatāṃ nītaṃ tadidaṃ camatkāritamamityucyate /
atra bhedaprapañco dhvanilocanādigrantheṣu draṣṭavyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, based on the power of words, the figure of comparison (<s>upamā</s>) between the hero and the lion of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) is suggested. By this, the real object (<s>vastu</s>) in the form of a positive statement is suggested — that the hero is capable of the culmination of the action of tearing apart all opposition, with irresistible valor in an instant. And by this, the real object in the form of a prohibition is suggested — that one should not oppose such a hero. Moreover, by this, the imaginative identification (<s>utprekṣā</s>) is suggested — that the kings who stood against the hero were fools. And by this, yet another <s>utprekṣā</s> is suggested — that the hero's rivals among kings were struck down by fate. Thus, through the flourishing of successive layers of meaning arising from the particular apprehension corresponding to each enemy — it is endowed with the nature of being a resting-place of inconceivable and abundant grandeur, and this is called the most wondrous. The detailed elaboration of this classification should be seen in texts such as the <s>Dhvanyāloka</s> and the like.

children.text: gadyaṃ padyaṃ ca miśraṃ cetyetat sarvaṃ tridhā smṛtam /
children.translated_text: Prose (<s>gadya</s>), verse (<s>padya</s>), and mixed (<s>miśra</s>) — all this is known to be of three kinds.

children.text: apādaḥ padasandarbho gadyaṃ hṛdyaṃ manīṣiṇām // Ckc_3.41 //
children.translated_text: A composition of words without metrical feet (<s>pāda</s>) is prose (<s>gadya</s>), pleasing to the learned. // Ckc_3.41 //
In the assembly of the jewels of fame, some (show) skill in prose;
a poem composed entirely of prose is like <s>Śrīharṣacarita</s> (the <s>Harṣacarita</s>) and the like. // Ckc_3.42 //
Verse (<s>padya</s>), possessing four feet (<s>pāda</s>), is of two types: that beginning with 'ca' (metrical) and that based purely on <s>mātrā</s> (morae).
The details of both should be known from the lexicons of metrical varieties (<s>chandoviciti</s>). // Ckc_3.43 //
Poetry composed of verse is of two kinds: minor (<s>kṣudra</s>) and major (<s>akṣudra</s>). // Ckc_3.44 //
The minor is standalone verse poetry (<s>muktakakāvya</s>), elaborated by <s>Bhāmaha</s> and others.
The major is a composition in cantos (<s>sargabandha</s>) and the like, with praiseworthy and exalted subject matter, // Ckc_3.45 //
brilliant with the wealth of descriptions including place, time, characters, and the like,
yielding the fruits of the three goals (<s>trivarga</s>: dharma, artha, kāma) — such as the <s>Raghuvaṃśa</s> and the like. // Ckc_3.46 //
Mixed (<s>miśra</s>), composed of both prose and verse, is of two kinds: dramatic (<s>prekṣya</s>, to be seen) and narrative (<s>śrāvya</s>, to be heard).
The dramatic is also of two types: <s>rūpaka</s> (major drama) and <s>uparūpaka</s> (minor drama). // Ckc_3.47 //
<s>Rūpaka</s> is declared to be of ten kinds, based on the distinctions of <s>Nāṭaka</s> and the like.
This (genre) is capable of ruling the empire of the <s>mahāprabandha</s> (great literary composition). // Ckc_3.48 //
In the <s>Rasārṇavasudhākara</s> composed by King <s>Siṅgabhūpa</s>,

children.text: asya prapañco vijñeyaḥ ke tathā vaktumīśate // Ckc_3.49 //
children.translated_text: the elaboration of this should be understood — who else is able to speak thus? // Ckc_3.49 //
The <s>uparūpaka</s> (minor drama) is so called; it includes the <s>Śrīgadita</s> and the like.
Its definition should be examined in the <s>Bhāvaprakāśikā</s> and other (works). // Ckc_3.50 //
The narrative (<s>śrāvya</s>) form is said to be of two kinds: <s>campū</s> and <s>upacampū</s>.
Of these, the <s>campū</s> literary composition has descriptions of the eighteen (types of) heroines. // Ckc_3.51 //
That composition (<s>prabandha</s>) is praiseworthy — such as the <s>Bhojarāmāyaṇa</s> and the like.
Who can state the extent of <s>upacampū</s> compositions? // Ckc_3.52 //
In this (genre) too, through the poet's skill, by mixing vernacular languages (<s>bhāṣā</s>), <s>tāla</s> (rhythm), and the like,
through the variations of <s>kalikā</s> (rhythmic prose), <s>utkalikā</s> (crescendo), and the like, // Ckc_3.53 //
they are accomplished fittingly according to the distinctions of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment), <s>bhāva</s> (emotion), and the like.
Nevertheless, for those who touch upon <s>prabhuvandya</s> (praise of the lord), <s>harṣaṇa</s> (rejoicing), <s>ārabhaṭī</s> (energetic style), and the like, // Ckc_3.54 //

children.text: vakṣye ca caturbhadrādīnāṃ keṣāṃcidiha lakṣaṇam // Ckc_3.55 //
children.translated_text: I shall state the definition of some such as <s>caturbhadra</s> (four-fold auspicious composition) and others. // Ckc_3.55 //
The regulation of a definite number of prose passages bound after verses,
with uniformity according to taste, is called <s>bhadra</s> (auspicious unit). // Ckc_3.56 //
Where there are four such (units), that is called <s>caturbhadra</s> (four-fold auspicious). // Ckc_3.57 //

children.text:
bhadraṃ ca satālamatālaṃ miśraṃ ceti trividham /
yatra (padyānantaraṃ tricatura) padyāntatantrī caturamātrādi niyame kevalakalikotkalikānibandhaḥ tatsatālabhadram /
tadidamudāharaṇādiṣu /
yatra padyānantaraṃ gadyāni kalikāśva tanmiśrabhadram /
tadidaṃ caturbhadrādiviṣayam /
caturbhadranibandhanāprakārastu yatkiñcidārabhaṭīvṛttiyogyamāśīrvādabhūṣitaṃ saṃbuddhivibhaktisaṃbhaktanāyakanāmāṅkitaṃ padyamādau nibadhnīyāt /
tato deva dhīra śūretyādi padopakramāṇi gadyānyantānuprāsavanti samasaṃkhyayā vaktavyāni /
paśvād gadyasaṃkhyātikrameṇa dvayordvayorādyantānuprāsasundaramākalanīyāḥ kalikā itīdaṃ samuccitya bhadramityabhidhīyate /
evaṃ caturṇāṃ bhadrāṇāṃ nibandhe caturbhadraḥ /
evamaṣṭabhadrādayo 'pi tasyaivā vṛttito bhavantīti na pṛthagucyante /
children.translated_text: <s>Bhadra</s> is of three kinds: with rhythm (<s>satāla</s>), without rhythm (<s>atāla</s>), and mixed. Where, after a verse, (a composition of) only <s>kalikā</s> and <s>utkalikā</s> is bound in the regulation of three-four verse-end notes of four <s>mātrā</s>s and the like — that is <s>satālabhadra</s>. This appears in the illustrative examples. Where prose passages and <s>kalikā</s>s follow a verse — that is <s>miśrabhadra</s> (mixed). This is the domain of <s>caturbhadra</s> and the like. The method of composing <s>caturbhadra</s> is: first one should compose a verse adorned with a benediction, suitable for the <s>ārabhaṭī</s> style, marked with the hero's name in the vocative case. Then prose passages beginning with words like 'O god', 'O brave one', 'O hero', etc., ending with terminal alliteration, should be stated in equal number. After that, exceeding the number of prose passages, <s>kalikā</s>s adorned with initial and terminal alliteration in pairs should be arranged — this, combined, is called one <s>bhadra</s>. Thus, in the composition of four <s>bhadra</s>s, it is <s>caturbhadra</s>. Likewise, <s>aṣṭabhadra</s> (eight-fold) and others arise by the same procedure, so they are not described separately.
If one desires even a <s>dvibhadra</s> (two-fold) and the languages are of more than one kind,

children.text: khyātaṃ hi raktaṃ kalyāṇaṃ yogassaṃskṛtadeśyayoḥ // Ckc_3.58 //
children.translated_text: the well-known (name) is <s>raktam</s> (colorful) or <s>kalyāṇam</s> (auspicious), the combination of Sanskrit and the regional language. // Ckc_3.58 //

children.text: evaṃ bhāṣādvayīyoge yogyaṃ nāma prakalpayet // Ckc_3.59 //
children.translated_text: Thus, in the combination of two languages, one should devise an appropriate name. // Ckc_3.59 //
That same (composition), marked with various titles (<s>biruda</s>), is a <s>birudāvalī</s> (garland of titles).
Its purpose is to indicate the duties to be performed at each particular occasion, and the like. // Ckc_3.60 //
A <s>bhogāvalī</s> (garland of enjoyment) is considered to be one that possesses the eminence of qualities to be described.
In each <s>bhadra</s>, the exertion of conquest in all directions fully awakened — // Ckc_3.61 //
that <s>caturbhadra</s> is called by the knowledgeable a <s>vijayāvalī</s> (garland of victory).
That which is a <s>satālabhadra</s> (rhythmic bhadra) — that is considered the illustrative example. // Ckc_3.62 //
In the introductory verse, shining with the opening 'jayati' (is victorious), in the verse named <s>Mālinī</s> and the like,
the seven case-endings in order, with the vocative as the eighth, should appear here. // Ckc_3.63 //
In each <s>bhadra</s>, at the end of the verse, one should compose a set of eight <s>kalikā</s>s.
Then, seventeen <s>utkalikā</s>s arranged alternately, each half the size of the <s>kalikā</s>s, // Ckc_3.64 //
ending with the semblance of the respective case-ending, should be composed;
the arrangement of initial and terminal alliteration should be devised in pairs. // Ckc_3.65 //
With the regulation of case-ending semblances, with short endings, and with rhythmic beat (<s>tālika</s>),
one should recite at the end of all case-endings a verse with meaningful case-endings. // Ckc_3.66 //
Accompanied by a benediction — such is the procedure of illustration.
Where there is a set of eight languages in order, with illustrative examples as the basis — // Ckc_3.67 //
a sequence of two, three, or more syllables at the end of one's own preceding word
that forms the beginning of the following word without interruption — // Ckc_3.68 //
this, from the joining of <s>bhadra</s>s, like a wheel, is called <s>cakravāla</s> (wheel-circle).
A row of prose interspersed (with verse), having verse at beginning and end — // Ckc_3.69 //
this is stated by others with (different) terms; the alternation of prose and verse
and the connection of the preceding with the following is considered universally (applicable). // Ckc_3.70 //
At the end of minor compositions, with <s>Āryā</s> or <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> meters,
for making known the name of the author and the hero, and of the composition itself — // Ckc_3.71 //
a single vocative throughout is considered (sufficient), excluding the illustrative (verses).
Thus, other (forms) too should be understood as arising from this same class. // Ckc_3.72 //

children.text:
dvipatīpramukhānāṃ tu kṣudreṣvantargatirmatā /
yeṣāṃ lakṣyaṃ budhairūhyaṃ vayaṃ vistarabhīravaḥ // Ckc_3.73 //
children.translated_text: And the inclusion of <s>dvipadī</s> (couplet) and other (forms) within the minor compositions is accepted. Those whose characteristics should be inferred by the learned — we are afraid of prolixity. // Ckc_3.73 //

children.text: iti śrī sarasasāhityacāturīdhurīṇaviśveśvarakavicandrapraṇītāyāṃ śrīsiṅgabhūpālakīrtisudhāsāraśītalāyāṃ camatkāracandrikāyā marthaguṇadoṣaprabandhaviśeṣaviveko nāma tṛtīyo vilāsaḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the third <s>vilāsa</s> (chapter), named 'The Discrimination of Meaning, Quality, Fault, and Types of Composition,' in the <s>Camatkāracandrikā</s>, composed by <s>Viśveśvara Kavicandra</s>, endowed with the skill of elegant literary art, cooled by the nectar-essence of the fame of King <s>Siṅgabhūpa</s>.
The <s>Camatkāracandrikā</s>, composed by <s>Viśveśvara Kavicandra</s> — Fourth <s>Vilāsa</s> (Chapter).
Just as form and the like are causes of the excellence of the intrinsic nature of the body,
so too do those who discriminate qualities recognize these as the qualities (<s>guṇa</s>) of poetry. // Ckc_4.1 //
<s>Śleṣa</s> (cohesion), <s>prasāda</s> (lucidity), <s>samatā</s> (evenness), <s>mādhurī</s> (sweetness), <s>sukumāratā</s> (delicacy),
<s>arthavyakti</s> (clarity of meaning), <s>udāratva</s> (grandeur), <s>ojas</s> (vigor), <s>kānti</s> (charm), <s>udāttatā</s> (sublimity), // Ckc_4.2 //

children.text:
preyān samādhiraurjiṃtyaṃ saumyaṃ gāmbhīryavistarau /
saṃkṣepaḥ śabdasaṃskāro bhāvikatvaṃ ca sammitaḥ // Ckc_4.3 //
children.translated_text: <s>preyas</s> (appeal), <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), <s>aurjitya</s> (robustness), <s>saumya</s> (gentleness), <s>gāmbhīrya</s> (profundity), <s>vistara</s> (ampleness), <s>saṃkṣepa</s> (conciseness), <s>śabdasaṃskāra</s> (verbal refinement), <s>bhāvikatva</s> (suggestiveness), and <s>sammita</s> (proportion) — // Ckc_4.3 //
the courses of style (<s>gatyuktirīti</s>) in poetry — those are considered to be twenty-three.
The quality of smooth, well-joined words is called <s>śleṣa</s> (cohesion). // Ckc_4.4 //
Of these, <s>śleṣa</s> (cohesion) —
For example —
Effortlessly handsome, of blameless and excellent essence, with arms reaching to the knees, with eyes expansive as lotus petals —

children.text: śrīsiṅgabhūpamavalokayatāṃ janānā- mānanditāni nayanāni sudhāmbuneva // Ckc_4.*1 //
children.translated_text: the eyes of the people who behold King <s>Siṅgabhūpa</s> are delighted, as if by nectar-water. // Ckc_4.*1 //
Here, the perception at the time of recitation that even distinct words (flow) as if they were a single word — that is <s>śleṣa</s> (cohesion).
Where there is swift comprehension of meaning — that is called <s>prasāda</s> (lucidity). // Ckc_4.5 //

children.text: yathā saugandhike ca ghanasāriṇi candane ca bimbādhare ca sudṛśāṃ vadane ca tāsām /
children.translated_text: For example — in the fragrant camphor-scented sandalwood, and in the bimba-fruit-like lips and the faces of the lovely-eyed women,

children.text: śrīsiṅgabhūparacite ca girāṃ kadambeṃ ko vā na nandati jano jagadekasāre // Ckc_4.*2 //
children.translated_text: and in the cluster of words composed by King <s>Siṅgabhūpa</s> — who in the world, which has a single essence, would not delight? // Ckc_4.*2 //
Here, because the feet (lines) convey their meaning simultaneously — that is <s>prasāda</s> (lucidity).
The maintenance throughout — from root to crown — of the composition

children.text: āmūlacūḍaṃ nirvāhaḥ samatā dhīmatāṃ matā // Ckc_4.6 //
children.translated_text: of soft, clear, and mixed syllables is considered <s>samatā</s> (evenness) by the wise. // Ckc_4.6 //
Here, an example of the maintenance of clear syllables —
In battles, raised high by the destruction of the chosen horses of the opposing side, even those trained by your <s>Kaukṣeya</s> (stirrup-skill), O <s>Siṅga</s>, protector of the earth —

children.text: saptāśve pratibhedamātramaribhiḥ prāyeṇa saṃdhāryate kaṣṭaṃ kliṣṭadhiyāṃ gurorapi vṛthā sarvaiva vidyā bhavet // Ckc_4.*3 //
children.translated_text: against the seven-horsed (sun-chariot), only a mere challenge is generally maintained by the enemies. Alas! For those of troubled intellect, all learning even of a <s>guru</s> is in vain. // Ckc_4.*3 //
Here, in all four lines, due to the maintenance of predominantly sonorous (<s>ghoṣa</s>) and semi-vowel syllables — this is <s>samatā</s> (evenness) of clear syllables.
An example of the maintenance of mixed syllable composition —

children.text: ākṣepoktividhāyināṃ kṣitibhujāmātmāvarodhāntike yuddhāgre tu nirīkṣya sādhvasavatāṃ tvāṃ khaḍganārāyaṇa /
children.translated_text: O <s>Khaḍganārāyaṇa</s> (Sword-<s>Viṣṇu</s>)! Seeing the kings who uttered taunts — near their own inner chambers now, and trembling at the forefront of battle —

children.text: rūkṣodagra tṛṇāṅkuragrasanatā jihvāgravicchedanaṃ daṇḍo 'bhūdata eva te hi bhavatā sve sve pade sthāpitāḥ // Ckc_4.*4 //
children.translated_text: the punishment for the harsh, lofty biting of grass-tips by (their) tongue-tips was severing. By you indeed they have been established in their respective places. // Ckc_4.*4 //

children.text: atra pādacatuṣṭaye 'pi nātivarṇamṛduprāyatā nātirūkṣākṣaraprāyatā ceti miśrabandhasamatā /
children.translated_text: Here, in all four lines, neither predominantly soft syllables nor predominantly harsh syllables — this is <s>samatā</s> (evenness) of mixed composition.

children.text: agranthilā pṛdhagbhūtiḥ patānāṃ mādhurī matā // Ckc_4.7 //
children.translated_text: The unentangled, distinct existence of words is considered <s>mādhurī</s> (sweetness). // Ckc_4.7 //
For example —
[Verse in Prakrit/vernacular, partially corrupt/illegible:]

children.text: bommo kāpūṇa sommaṃ tvihuvaṇa raaṇaṃ kaṇṇaaṃ kitti saṇṇaṃ dvihā uṃtie ṇāhaṃ kuṇa iva rauṇaṃ maṃgalaṃ siṃgabhūvam // Ckc_4.*5 //
children.translated_text: ...<s>Siṃgabhūva</s>, (this verse praises the king in a vernacular language) — I do not know how to praise, as if to <s>Rauṇa</s> (Arjuna?), the auspiciousness of <s>Siṃgabhūva</s>, the ornament of the three worlds. // Ckc_4.*5 //

children.text: atra pāṭhasamaya eva padavibhāgaḥ pratibhātīti mādhuryam /
children.translated_text: Here, even at the time of recitation, the word-division is intuitively perceived — that is <s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness).
Pleasantness of sound even in the presence of conjunct consonants (<s>saṃyuktākṣara</s>) is <s>sukumāratā</s> (delicacy). // Ckc_4.8 //
For example —

children.text: yuṣmābhiḥ pratigaṇḍabhairavaraṇe prāṇāḥ kathaṃ rakṣitā ityantaḥ purapṛcchayā yadariṣu prāpteṣu cājñāvaśam /
children.translated_text: 'How did you save your lives in the battle against <s>Pratigaṇḍabhairava</s>?' — when asked thus by the women of the inner chambers, and when the enemies have come under (the king's) command,
the skill in the activity of exchanging elevated glances proclaims (the answer) — the sprouts of color from the sapphire of the ear-ornaments swaying on the cheeks. // Ckc_4.*6 //
Here, despite the predominance of conjunct consonants, the ear is not offended — hence <s>saukumārya</s> (delicacy).
Independence from needing additional explanation is called <s>arthavyakti</s> (clarity of meaning). // Ckc_4.9 //
For example —
The kings skilled in statecraft bow to King <s>Siṅgabhūpa</s>,
who is compassionate to those who seek refuge, for the establishment of their own kingdoms. // Ckc_4.*7 //
Here, the completeness of the sentence is self-evident.
Composition with formidable syllables is called <s>audārya</s> (grandeur) by the wise. // Ckc_4.10 //
For example —
To the splitter of the mountain of roaring <s>Gūrjara</s> pride, the foe of the darkness of the <s>Nepāla</s> king's darkness, the enemy of the harshly rattling <s>Saurāṣṭra</s> kingdom,

children.text: dṛpyatkeralamaulimoṭanakṛte śrīsiṅgapṛthvīṃpate bhūyāsurbhuvanābhayavratabhṛte śreyāṃsi bhūyāṃsi te // Ckc_4.*8 //
children.translated_text: the breaker of the crown of the arrogant <s>Kerala</s> lord — O King <s>Siṅga</s>, lord of the earth, upholder of the vow of fearlessness for the world, may abundant blessings be yours! // Ckc_4.*8 //

children.text: atra vikaṭākṣaratayā nṛtyadbhiriva padairyā bandharacanā tadaudāryam /
children.translated_text: Here, the composition fashioned with formidable syllables, as if the words were dancing — that is <s>audārya</s> (grandeur).
<s>Ojas</s> (vigor) is declared to be of two kinds: an abundance of compounds.
The first type arises from the profusion of compounds that are not too long. // Ckc_4.11 //

children.text:
idaṃ komalamārgānusāriṇāṃ prāṇasaṃmitam /
samāsasyātidīrghatvād dvitīyaṃ gauḍasammatam // Ckc_4.12 //
children.translated_text: This (first type) is considered the lifeblood of those who follow the <s>Vaidarbha</s> (tender) style. The second type, due to the excessive length of compounds, is approved by the <s>Gauḍa</s> (vigorous) school. // Ckc_4.12 //
An example of profusion of short compounds, regarding the hero himself —
With hair-tresses disheveled by drops of perspiration, with half-closed pair of eyes, embracing a state of being overcome,
With other emotions concealed by sprouting bliss — we long for a certain indescribable gesture of the long-eyed one. // Ckc_4.*9 //
And as follows:
<s>Saṅgīta</s>-procession-promenading dear companion, life-giving elixir of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment), avenue of the tree of noble conduct, throne of the empire of cleverness,

The bell-path of the sportive play of <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>, the crest-jewel among kings — the speech (<s>vaikharī</s>) of flattering utterance (<s>cāṭu-vyāhṛti</s>) triumphs, being the ultimate limit of literary art! // Ckc_4.*10 //
Here the quality of having few compounds (<s>svalpasamāsatva</s>) is evident --- --- --- The quality of having long compounds (<s>dīrghasamāsatva</s>) is as follows:

children.text: piśācāḥ saha sahacaṭaiḥ hastatālānukūlaṃ (?) krīḍanti kreṃkriyābhiḥ kahakahaninadāḍambarālambinībhiḥ // Ckc_4.*11 //
children.translated_text: <s>Piśācas</s> (demons) together with <s>sahacaṭas</s> (attendant goblins) play in rhythm with hand-clapping, with <s>kreṃkriyā</s> sounds accompanied by roaring <s>kahakaha</s> laughter. // Ckc_4.*11 //
Here the quality of having long compounds (<s>dīrghasamāsatva</s>) is evident.

children.text: kāntiśchāyā hi bandhasya kathitā bandhakovidaiḥ // Ckc_4.13 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kānti</s> (lustre) or <s>chāyā</s> (radiance) of composition has been described by those skilled in composition. // Ckc_4.13 //
As follows:

children.text: ākṛṣṭā mūrdhni kṛṣṇā gahanamaṇigatā maithilī pūrvamūrvoś channā parṇairaparṇā kila nalamahiṣī kalpitā śitpinīti /
children.translated_text: <s>Maithilī</s> (<s>Sītā</s>) was formerly drawn onto the head, dark-complexioned, gone into the depths of jewels, concealed by leaves on her former thighs — the queen of <s>Nala</s> was indeed fashioned as an ascetic woman, they say.

children.text: āstāṃ tattaddaśāyāmapi dadhati śucaṃ yāvadākṣeparūpair ākhyātaiḥ siṅgabhūpa tvadarimṛgadṛśāṃ sthairyavatyo jaratyaḥ // Ckc_4.*12 //
children.translated_text: Let that be — even in those respective conditions they bore grief; as long as, O <s>Siṅgabhūpa</s>, the aged wives of your enemy-doe-eyed women possess steadfastness through reproachful verbal forms. // Ckc_4.*12 //
Or as follows:
One who spreads the sweet-meaning speech (<s>Bhāratī</s>) enriched by the arrangement and elaboration of charming <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic flavor), in [the court of] <s>Siṅgabhūpa</s>,

children.text: garanigaraṇarūkṣairakṣarair vāvadūko viṣadharakulamūrdhā na sphuṭī yaḥ sphuṭīti // Ckc_4.*13 //
children.translated_text: A chatterbox with harsh syllables fit for swallowing poison — the crest of the serpent-family — does not shine forth as one who truly shines. // Ckc_4.*13 //
Here the extreme brilliance (<s>atyujjvalatva</s>) of the composition is the <s>chāyā</s> (radiance), and that itself is <s>kānti</s> (lustre).
The learned know <s>udāttatā</s> (elevation) as the employment of laudatory qualifiers. // Ckc_4.14 //
As follows:
With an arm that bears the distinction of ornaments from birth, marked with the line of the thunderbolt,
O <s>Śrī Siṅgabhūpāla</s>, by your extended [arm], this ocean-girdled [earth] is protected. // Ckc_4.*14 //
Here the qualifiers of the arm are supremely praiseworthy because they convey extraordinary fortune.
The arrangement of speech sweeter than the beloved's words is the life-breath of <s>cāṭu</s> (flattery) in literature. // Ckc_4.15 //
As follows:
O repository of beauty and fortune, stealer of the hearts of young women, estimable in courtesy, <s>Pārijāta</s> tree of the earth's surface,

children.text: śṛṅgārabhāva karuṇākara siṅgabhūpa gāṃ rakṣa rakṣa tava rakṣaṇameva dharmaḥ // Ckc_4.*15 //
children.translated_text: O embodiment of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment), O ocean of compassion, O <s>Siṅgabhūpa</s> — protect the earth, protect it! Your protection alone is <s>dharma</s>. // Ckc_4.*15 //

children.text: atra nāyakaṃ prati dūtyāḥ priyoktiḥ spaṣṭaiva /
children.translated_text: Here the flattering speech of the female messenger (<s>dūtī</s>) toward the hero is evident.
<s>Samādhi</s> (figurative usage) here refers to the figurative (<s>aupacārikī</s>) function of a word. // Ckc_4.16 //
As follows:
He sits upon the couch spread over the hoods of the chief of serpent-lords, he oversteps the splendor of the girdle-ornaments of the ocean-girdled [earth] at every shore,
He kisses the pride that scratches the matted locks of wonder-shaken <s>Dhūrjaṭi</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) — the dawn of the full glory of the fame of <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>, the lord of the earth. // Ckc_4.*16 //
Here the sitting, overstepping, and kissing are used figuratively (<s>upacāra</s>) because fame (<s>kīrti</s>) is non-sentient.
That which is extreme intensity of composition is called <s>aurjitya</s> (forcefulness). // Ckc_4.17 //
As follows:
The sword, terrible-cornered, taking hold of the firm frontal globes of the lord of elephants .... ....

children.text: tava racayati dhanuradhvaṃsanaṃ siṅgabhūpa pradanakadanagandhapraṅvaṇabvān piśācān // Ckc_4.*17 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Siṅgabhūpa</s>, your bow accomplishes destruction, [creating] <s>piśācas</s> (demons) inclined to the smell of slaughter and carnage. // Ckc_4.*17 //

children.text: atra hrasvākṣarāṇāṃ saṃyuktapūrvatayā gurutve yadgāḍhatvaṃ tadaurjityaṃ nāma /
children.translated_text: Here the heaviness produced by short syllables being preceded by conjunct consonants — that intensity is what is called <s>aurjitya</s> (forcefulness).
The capacity for internal dialogue within words is called <s>saukṣmya</s> (subtlety). // Ckc_4.18 //
As follows:

children.text: bhūdhātuṃ kartṛbhāvādanugatamanunā mānayatyātmamāne paryāye saṃpadāṃ syādabhiparisahitaṃ vidviṣāṃ karmabhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: The root <s>bhū</s> in the agent sense honors self-respect following <s>Manu</s>; in the succession of prosperity, the object-sense of enemies would be accompanied by <s>abhi</s> (i.e., overpowering);

children.text: puṃliṅge tvanmano 'bjaṃ spṛśati śivapadaṃ tvadgṛhālī na puṃsi strīliṅge śātravāṇāṃ nikhilamapi puraṃ siṅgabhūpālacandra // Ckc_4.*18 //
children.translated_text: In the masculine gender, your mind-lotus touches the abode of <s>Śiva</s>; your household woman is not in a man [i.e., devoted only to you]; in the feminine gender, the entire city of enemies, O <s>Siṅgabhūpālacandra</s>. // Ckc_4.*18 //

children.text: atra nāyakaḥ sampado 'nubhavatīti, dviṣaḥ paribhavati, nāyakasya mānasaṃ śivo mahādevaḥ spṛśati, tadvirodhinagaraṃ śivā jambūkaḥ spṛśatīti padānāṃ bhūdhātuṃ kartubhāvādityādiṣu garbhitatvādantaḥ saṃjalpanaśaktiḥpratīyata iti saukṣmyamidam /
children.translated_text: Here, the hero enjoys prosperity, humiliates his enemies, the hero's mind is touched by <s>Śiva</s> (the great lord), and his enemy's city is touched by <s>śivā</s> (the jackal) — since these meanings are embedded within the words through the root <s>bhū</s> in the agent sense and so forth, the power of internal dialogue is perceived. This is <s>saukṣmya</s> (subtlety).
<s>Gāmbhīrya</s> (profundity) is the quality of being rich in <s>dhvani</s> (suggestion).
As follows:

children.text: ekenaiva turaṅgameṇa kakubho vyākramya saumyakramā- naṅgīkṛtya karān kadācidagataḥ kāṃcittamograstatām /
children.translated_text: Having traversed the quarters with a single steed in gentle course, having once accepted the rays, having gone to a certain state of fierce eclipse,

children.text: ullāsāya satāmanantamudayaṃ dhatte tathāpi sphuṭaṃ tvaṃ prājñairnanu siṅgabhūpatilaka jñāto 'si bhāsāṃ nidhiḥ // Ckc_4.*19 //
children.translated_text: For the delight of the good, he assumes an infinite rising — yet clearly, O <s>Siṅgabhūpatilaka</s>, you are known by the wise as a treasury of splendors. // Ckc_4.*19 //

children.text:
atra sūryastu diśasturaṅgamaissaptabhirākramati, tīvrān kiraṇānaṅgīkaroti, rahugrastatāṃ gacchati nakṣatrāṇāmanullāsāya sāntamudayaṃ dhatta iti dhvanirvidyate /
tasmādgambhīratvam /
children.translated_text: Here the suggested meaning (<s>dhvani</s>) is perceived: the sun traverses the quarters with seven steeds, accepts intense rays, goes to the state of eclipse by <s>Rāhu</s>, and assumes a rising for the non-delight of the stars with its culmination. Therefore it has profundity.
Elaborate expression is <s>vistara</s> (elaboration). // Ckc_4.19 //

children.text: puṇyaiḥ pūrvamupārjitaistanumato janmāstu sanmānuṣaṃ janmāpyasya tadāndhradeśatilake rājācale saṃbhavet /
children.translated_text: May there first be a noble human birth through previously acquired merits; may that birth occur on the <s>Rājācala</s>, the ornament of the <s>Āndhra</s> land;

children.text: tatrāpyeṣa dadhātu tāṃ pariṇatiṃ bhāgyasya yogyāṃ tathā gatvā nandati siṅgabhūvara giraṃ tvatkāṃ camatkāriṇīm // Ckc_4.*20 //
children.translated_text: May fortune there too bestow that fitting ripeness, so that having gone, one delights in your wondrous speech, O best of kings <s>Siṅgabhūvara</s>. // Ckc_4.*20 //

children.text: atra nāyakasya sannidhau sarvadā sthātumicchāmīti vivakṣitārthasyātivivṛtya karaṇādvistaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Here the intended meaning 'I wish to always remain in the hero's presence' is expressed through elaborate expansion — this is <s>vistara</s> (elaboration).
<s>Saṃkṣepa</s> (conciseness) is the compressed expression of even a vast subject matter. // Ckc_4.20 //
As follows:
By six and by sixteen kings, one supreme queen was made;
She was brought under control by <s>Śrī Siṅgabhūpāla</s>, the [mighty] elephant. // Ckc_4.*21 //
Here, by 'six' is meant:
"<s>Hariścandra</s>, <s>Nala</s>, King <s>Purukutsa</s>, <s>Purūravas</s>,
<s>Sagara</s>, and <s>Kārtavīrya</s> — these six are universal sovereigns (<s>cakravartins</s>)."
Thus the meaning of that verse; and by 'sixteen kings' is meant:
"<s>Gaya</s>, <s>Ambarīṣa</s>, <s>Śaśibindu</s>, <s>Aṅga</s>, <s>Pṛthu</s>, <s>Marutta</s>, <s>Bharata</s>, <s>Suhotra</s>,
<s>Rāma</s>, <s>Dilīpa</s>, <s>Śibi</s>, <s>Antideva</s>, <s>Yayāti</s>, <s>Māndhātṛ</s>, and <s>Bhagīratha</s>."

children.text:
iti ślokārthasya ca prapañcakathanaprasiddhasyātrātisaṅkocena kathanāccamatkārātiśayakārī saṃkṣepo nāma guṇaḥ ayam --- "sa mārutasutānītamahauṣadhidhṛtavyathaḥ" /
ityādau kavibhiraṅgīkṛto lakṣaṇīyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, the well-known elaborate narratives of those verses are here told with extreme compression — this quality called <s>saṃkṣepa</s> (conciseness) produces extraordinary wonder. --- This [quality] is recognized by poets in passages such as "he, with the pain sustained by the great herb brought by the son of <s>Māruta</s>" and should be so understood.

children.text: supāṃ tiṅāṃ ca vyatpattiśśabdasaṃskāra ucyate // Ckc_4.21 //
children.translated_text: The etymological derivation of nominal (<s>sup</s>) and verbal (<s>tiṅ</s>) endings is called <s>śabdasaṃskāra</s> (verbal refinement). // Ckc_4.21 //
As follows:

The glories of the fame of <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>, the lord of the earth, whose magnificence touches the horizon, whose spread through the sky-paths is lovingly expansive, hanging level with <s>Śambhu</s> (<s>Śiva</s>),

children.text: gāmadhyāsitumīśate pragupate paryāptamāryotsavān kalpānte tava kalpitāṃ vivṛṇute dhāmrā mahimrāṃ śriyam // Ckc_4.*22 //
children.translated_text: Are able to occupy the earth, O master; they sufficiently produce noble festivities; at the end of the age, they reveal the vast wealth of splendor you have ordained. // Ckc_4.*22 //

children.text: atra dikkūlaṃkaṣeti priyaṃbhāvuketi gāmadhyāsitumityādau subantānāmīśata ityādiṣu tiṅntānāṃ ca digvyāpino 'ntarikṣavyāpino gavi tiṣṭhantyādibhi rviśeṣapratibhānācchabdasaṃskāra ityucyate /
children.translated_text: Here in expressions like <s>dikkūlaṃkaṣa</s>, <s>priyaṃbhāvukā</s>, <s>gāmadhyāsitum</s>, etc. — for nominal forms, and in <s>īśate</s> etc. — for verbal forms, since special meanings like 'pervading the quarters,' 'pervading the atmosphere,' 'dwelling on the earth' are discerned, this is called <s>śabdasaṃskāra</s> (verbal refinement).
Speech arising from emotional states such as joy is considered <s>bhāvika</s> (emotional speech). // Ckc_4.22 //
As follows:

children.text: vidyādaivata tāta tāvakaguro sarvajñacūḍāmaṇe stotavyo 'si manīṣiṇāṃ tvamathavā vandyo javākairalam /
children.translated_text: O deity of learning, O father, O guru of yours, O crest-jewel of omniscience — you are to be praised by the learned! Or rather, you are to be honored — enough with <s>javā</s> flowers!

children.text: itthaṃ siṅgamahīpatiṃ gurujano 'pyābhāṣate toṣavān tattatpaddhatidharmamarmaṇi paricchedāni saṃvādinam // Ckc_4.*23 //
children.translated_text: Thus even the assembly of elders, filled with satisfaction, addresses King <s>Siṅga</s>, who accords with the essential principles of each respective tradition. // Ckc_4.*23 //
Since it proceeds from the satisfaction born of discernment, it has the quality of <s>bhāvikatva</s> (emotional expression).
Proportionality (<s>samitatva</s>) is said to be the restraint of words and meaning within proper bounds. // Ckc_4.23 //
As follows:

children.text: vikrame na krame kecitkrame kecinna vikrame /
children.translated_text: Some are [skilled] in valor but not in order; some in order but not in valor;

children.text: vikrame ca krame cāyaṃ dakṣaḥ śrīsiṅgabhūpatiḥ // Ckc_4.*24 //
children.translated_text: This <s>Śrī Siṅgabhūpati</s> is adept in both valor and order. // Ckc_4.*24 //
Here the use of exactly as many words as the meaning requires is <s>samitatva</s> (proportionality).
The ascending and descending movement of tones is called <s>svaragati</s> (tonal movement). // Ckc_4.24 //
As follows:
When <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>, the lord of the earth, bears the earth with the yoke of excellence,
He intoxicates the families of <s>Phaṇipati</s> (the serpent-lord), <s>Hari</s>'s elephant (<s>Airāvata</s>), the mountain, and the deceptive tortoise. // Ckc_4.*25 //

In the first half, there is an ascending (<s>āroha</s>) of tones due to the predominance of long syllables. In the second half, there is a descending (<s>avaroha</s>) due to the predominance of short syllables — this is the <s>gati</s> (tonal movement).
<s>Ukti</s> (suggestion) is said to be the expression of the intended meaning through a different turn of phrase. // Ckc_4.25 //

children.text: yathā tasyāḥ kiṃ guṇajīvitasya kuśalaṃ rājan satī jīvati praśnastatkuśalakramo hi kathitaṃ sā jīvatīti sphuṭam /
children.translated_text: As follows: 'Is all well with her whose life is [sustained by] virtues?' O king, 'The virtuous one lives' — the question about her well-being has been answered thus, namely 'She lives' is made clear.

children.text: bhadre dūti punastadeva kimidaṃ mugdheva saṃbhāṣase śvāse tiṣṭhati sā mṛteti gadituṃ śrīsiṅga kiṃ yujyate // Ckc_4.*26 //
children.translated_text: O good messenger, but then what is this again — do you speak as if confused? Is it fitting to say, O <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>, that she in whom only breath remains is dead? // Ckc_4.*26 //

children.text: atra tasyāḥ kiṃ kuśalamiti nāyakapraśne dūtyā kuśalamakuśalaṃ veti prativaktavyajīvatītyādiyuktibhaṅgyā yo 'yaṃ tvadvirahe jīvitamātraśeṣeti sūcanāprakārasso 'yamuktirnāma guṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, in response to the hero's question 'Is all well with her?', the messenger, through the artful turn of saying 'She lives' — rather than stating whether things are well or not — suggests that in separation from you, only bare life remains. This mode of suggestion is the quality called <s>ukti</s>.
<s>Rīti</s> (fulfillment/style) is defined as the carrying through of what was begun. // Ckc_4.26 //

children.text: ekaṃ yācitamarthinā dbiguṇitaṃ citte tvadīye punar- vākye tantriguṇaṃ caturguṇayutaṃ haste tatastvarthinaḥ /
children.translated_text: One thing was asked by the supplicant; in your mind it was doubled; in your speech, tripled; in your hand, quadrupled; then in the supplicant's palm, quintupled.

children.text: pāṇau pañjaguṇaṃ prakalpitamaho ṣāḍguṇyadīkṣāguro- raudārye tava siṅgabhūpa nitarāmāścaryamācāryakam // Ckc_4.*27 //
children.translated_text: Ah, O guru of the initiation into the six-fold diplomacy, O <s>Siṅgabhūpa</s>, in your generosity there is truly astonishing mastery! // Ckc_4.*27 //
The sequential fulfillment from the first to the sixth is <s>rīti</s> (fulfillment/style).
Thus concludes the analysis of poetic virtues (<s>guṇaviveka</s>).
The arrangement of words is called <s>rīti</s> (style) by those versed in <s>rīti</s>.
From the root <s>rīṅ</s> meaning 'to go,' this [term] <s>rīti</s> is so derived. // Ckc_4.27 //

children.text:
asamāsā samāsena madhyameva vibhūṣitā /
atidīrghasamāsā camiśrā ceti caturvidhā // Ckc_4.28 //
children.translated_text: It is fourfold: uncompounded (<s>asamāsā</s>), adorned with compounds (<s>samāsena</s>), mixed (<s>miśrā</s>), and with excessively long compounds (<s>atidīrghasamāsā</s>). // Ckc_4.28 //
The uncompounded style is as follows:

children.text: rājānaḥ santu loke dinarajanikṛtoratra vaṃśāvataṃsā viṣṇoraitihyasiddhānabhidadhati guṇān kīrtigandhāḥ pravandhāḥ /
children.translated_text: Let there be kings in the world, crest-ornaments of the lineage of the makers of day and night; let chronicles fragrant with fame declare the traditionally established virtues of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: adya kṣoṇī kṛtārthā nṛpatikulagurū cakṣuṣī yasya sau'yaṃ devo recarlavaṃśo viharati bhagavān siṅgabhūpālamūrtiḥ // Ckc_4.*28 //
children.translated_text: Today the earth is fulfilled — he whose two eyes are the preceptors of the royal lineage, this lord of the <s>Recarla</s> dynasty, the blessed one, sports in the form of <s>Siṅgabhūpāla</s>. // Ckc_4.*28 //

children.text:
nanvatra samāsaḥ śrūyate kathamasamāseti cet śrūyatām /
atra nañā samāsasvarūpaniṣedho nābhidhīyate /
kintu tasya tīrgatvaṃ drāghīyastvaṃ ca /
yathā-anudareyaṃ kanyā; nissāraḥ pumān; iti /
tasmād dvayoḥ trayāṇāṃ vā (na) padānāṃ samāse rīteḥ sahṛdayahṛdayānāmanudvegadāyināmasamāsatvameva /
yathā ca dṛṣṭamasamāsamārgānusāriṇāṃ mahākavīnāṃ prabandharatneṣu /
children.translated_text: Now, if one objects: 'Compounds are heard here, so how can it be called uncompounded?' — hear the answer. Here the prefix <s>a</s> does not negate the essential nature of compounds, but rather [negates] their length and excessive extension. Just as [in the expressions] 'this girl is not big-bellied (<s>anudarā</s>)' or 'this man is without substance (<s>nissāra</s>).' Therefore, when a compound of two or three words does not cause discomfort to the hearts of the sensitive, it is indeed [classified as] uncompounded. And this is seen in the gem-like compositions of great poets who follow the uncompounded path:
"Slender, dark-complexioned, with sharp teeth, with lower lip like a ripe <s>bimba</s> fruit" // Ckc_4.*29 //
Thus in the <s>Meghasandeśa</s> (Cloud Messenger [of <s>Kālidāsa</s>]).
"By the hand of the king, with its fragrant nails that arranged the beautiful tresses of the slender-bodied one,
Even this creeper, whose flowers had been plucked, became one with bees clinging to its stalks." // Ckc_4.*30 //
Thus in the <s>Karṇāmṛta</s>.
"With both cheeks blooming, with a wondrous gentle smile, with overflowing passion, having mastered the art of <s>Kāma</s> (love),

children.text: hastena hastamavalambya kadā nu seve sallāparūpamamṛtaṃ sarasīruhākṣyāḥ // Ckc_4.*31 //
children.translated_text: When shall I partake of the nectar in the form of conversation with the lotus-eyed one, clasping hand in hand? // Ckc_4.*31 //
Thus in the <s>Siṅgabhūpālīya</s>.
"With face-first embraces preceded by clinging, with throat-grasps that pressed the limbs,

children.text: nakhapracārai śśithilopagūḍhairlabdhaiḥ priyāyā mumude mukundaḥ // Ckc_4.*32 //
children.translated_text: With nail-marks and loosened embraces — <s>Mukunda</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) delighted in those obtained from his beloved. // Ckc_4.*32 //
Thus in the <s>Kandarpasaṃbhava</s>.

children.text:
evanamyeṣvapi vaidarbhamārgānusāriṇāṃ prabandheṣu tatra tatra ca tunnapadasamāsasyāsamāsatvakīrtanānupraveśākāro 'vagantavyaḥ /
aparañca nyūnānāmadaśādhikānāṃ padānāṃ samāso madhyamaḥ tadvatī madhyamasamāsā
children.translated_text: Thus, in other compositions following the <s>Vaidarbha</s> style as well, the manner of the occasional introduction of compounds, proclaimed as non-compound [style], should be understood. Furthermore, a compound of fewer than or up to ten words is 'medium' — [a style] having such [compounds] is called <s>madhyamasamāsā</s> (medium-compound).
For example:
O <s>Śrīsiṅgabhūpa</s>, from experiencing the sweetness of the nectar-stream of the playful charm of your speech,
the wise become [those] from whose half-closed lotus-like pairs of eyes trickle droplets of bliss-tears. // Ckc_4.*33 //
A compound of more than ten words is an exceedingly long compound (<s>atidīrghasamāsā</s>).
For example:

In the darkness bound upon the shoulder-region of the tawny [elephant] <s>Hari</s> (or <s>Viṣṇu</s>), whose companion-luster is obscured by the canopy of dust raised by the powerful army of <s>Śrīsiṅgakṣoṇipāla</s>,

in the sky, immeasurable by a fathom, the <s>Siddhas</s> (perfected beings), their minds delighted at the cessation of the obstacles to the sport of embracing the breasts of young women, praise him. // Ckc_4.*34 //
From the combination of non-compound and other styles, [they become] mixed. In the mixture of non-compound and exceedingly long compound:
For example:
Of the crest-jewel King <s>Siṅgabhūpa</s>, the waves of fame that flood the three worlds without break, purifying [all] —
competing with the celestial river whose foam, having ripened and burst, slips from the cluster of crests of the matted locks of the uneven-eyed one [<s>Śiva</s>] — // Ckc_4.*35 //
Here, in the first half there is a non-compound [style], and in the second half an exceedingly long compound. In the combination of non-compound and medium compound:
For example:
The sword-edge, hostile to the attendant service of applying beautiful <s>pāṭīra</s> (sandalwood paste) on the enemy kings' wives,

children.text: jayati vijayalakṣmyā veṇikāśreṇikāntī raṇabhuvi tava bāhāsaṅginī siṅgabhūpa // Ckc_4.*36 //
children.translated_text: triumphs — companion of your arm on the battlefield, O <s>Siṅgabhūpa</s>, with the splendor of the braid of the goddess of victory! // Ckc_4.*36 //
Here, in the first half there is a medium compound, and in the second half a non-compound [style]. In the combination of exceedingly long and medium compounds:
For example:

O <s>Siṅgakṣmāpāla</s>, in battle, [drinking] the blood gushing and swelling from the playful creeper-ornaments of the crests of the crowns of the multitude of chariot-lords of the opposing army, filled with fresh fat and the <s>hālāhala</s> [of gore] —

children.text: pāyaṃ pāyaṃ piśācāḥ saha saha carīhastatālānukūlaṃ krīḍanti kreṃkriyābhiḥ kahakahaninadāḍambarālambinībhiḥ // Ckc_4.*37 //
children.translated_text: the <s>piśācas</s> (ghouls), drinking and drinking, sport with cries of '<s>kreṃ kreṃ</s>,' accompanied by the clapping of their companion <s>carī</s>-hands, resonating with the din of '<s>kaha kaha</s>' laughter. // Ckc_4.*37 //

children.text:
atra prathamārdhe 'tidīrghasamāsottarārdhe madhyamasamāsā /
evamanyadapyetajjātīyaṃ draṣṭavyam /
iti rītivivekaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, in the first half there is an exceedingly long compound, and in the second half a medium compound. Thus other examples of this type should be observed. This concludes the analysis of <s>rīti</s> (style).

children.text: yā vikāse ca vikṣepe vikṣobhe vistare tathā /
children.translated_text: That which operates in the expansion, agitation,

children.text: (cetaso vartayitrī syātsā vṛttiḥ sāpi ṣaḍvidhā) // Ckc_4.29 //
children.translated_text: disturbance, and elaboration of the mind — that is <s>vṛtti</s> (mode), and it too is of six kinds: // Ckc_4.29 //
<s>Kaiśikī</s> (graceful) and <s>ārabhaṭī</s> (violent), <s>bhāratī</s> (verbal), <s>sātvatī</s> (grand),
<s>madhyamārabhaṭī</s> (moderate-violent), and <s>madhyamakaiśikī</s> (moderate-graceful). // Ckc_4.30 //
The gentle [rasas are] <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic) and <s>karuṇa</s> (pathetic); the mild ones are <s>hāsya</s> (comic) and <s>adbhuta</s> (marvelous);
the vehement ones are <s>raudra</s> (furious) and <s>bībhatsa</s> (disgusting); somewhat [vehement are] <s>vīra</s> (heroic) and <s>bhayānaka</s> (terrifying). // Ckc_4.31 //
By the gentleness of both word and meaning, the <s>kaiśikī vṛtti</s> (graceful mode) is desired. // Ckc_4.32 //
For example: with unmoving [glances] from majesty, accompanied by the fragrance of undisturbed modesty, swelling with delight, in the company of startled-doe gazes,
generous from eagerness, revealing the secrets of the waves of affection — with such side-glances, the young woman gazed upon <s>Siṅgakṣmāramaṇa</s>. // Ckc_4.*38 //
The <s>ārabhaṭī vṛtti</s> (violent mode) is described as [arising] from the vehemence of meaning and words. // Ckc_4.33 //

children.text: yathā sāvaṣṭambha sadambhajambhagirisadvyālambhanottambhita prārambhādbhūtajambhabhedibhiduratviṅgena khaḍgena te /
children.translated_text: For example: with steadfast pride, with the support of the mountain of arrogant yawning, with a lifted beginning, with a sword that through its terrifying, wonder-striking, yawning-splitting, fierce swing —

children.text: śrīsiṅgakṣitirakṣaka pratimṛdhaṃ siddhyedari kṣmābhṛtāṃ sā rambhākucakumbhasambhramaparī rambhādisambhāvanā // Ckc_4.*39 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Śrīsiṅgakṣitirakṣaka</s>, may the conquest against enemy kings succeed — that expectation of the embrace of the pitcher-like breasts of <s>Rambhā</s> and others, arising from the tumult! // Ckc_4.*39 //

children.text:
atra snigdhaprāṇavarṇaprāyatvaṃ sandarbhasya mṛdutvam /
śruṅgāratvādarthasta mṛdutvam /
atra rūkṣamahāprāṇavarṇapramāyatvena saṃdarbhasya gāḍhatvam /
pratibhaṭadhvaṃsanarupatvādarthasyagāḍhatvam /
children.translated_text: Here, the predominance of smooth, voiced consonants constitutes the softness of the composition. The softness of meaning comes from the erotic theme. Here, the predominance of rough, aspirated consonants constitutes the harshness of the composition. The harshness of meaning comes from the destruction of enemies.
The <s>bhāratī vṛtti</s> (verbal mode) is desired when the meaning is gentle but the composition is vehement. // Ckc_4.34 //

children.text: yathā tajjitvā parirambhaṇaprabhṛtikaṃ dyūte sakhīnāṃ puraḥ śāryāropaṇasūcite paṇavidhau śrīśiṅgapṛthvīkṣitā /
children.translated_text: For example: having won that [wager] beginning with an embrace in a game of dice before her friends, in the betting procedure indicated by the placing of chess pieces, [at the court of] <s>Śrīśiṅgapṛthvīkṣit</s>,

children.text: hāsotphullakapolakāntilaharīsaṃkrāntavakrekṣaṇā sā svinnāṅguli śārikāparikaraṃ sajjīkaroti priyā // Ckc_4.*40 //
children.translated_text: she — with the wave of beauty from cheeks blossoming with laughter spreading to the sidelong glances — the beloved, with perspiring fingers, prepares the set of chess pieces. // Ckc_4.*40 //

children.text:
atra śṛṅgāratvādarthasya mṛdutvam /
bandhasya mahāpraṇarūkṣavarṇaprāyatvaṃ prauḍhatvam /
children.translated_text: Here, the softness of meaning is due to the erotic theme. The vehemence of the composition is due to the predominance of rough, aspirated consonants.
The <s>sātvatī vṛtti</s> (grand mode) is desired when the meaning is vehement but the composition is gentle. // Ckc_4.35 //
For example:
Pearls fallen and glistening on all sides from the crowns of the enemies [slain by] the sword-plough of <s>Śrīsiṅgabhūpa</s> —

children.text: kīlālamāṃsakalitāsu raṇasthalīṣu bījāṅkurāṇi yaśasāmiva nirmalāni // Ckc_4.*41 //
children.translated_text: on the battlefields soaked with blood and flesh, [they appear] like pure sprouts of seeds of fame. // Ckc_4.*41 //

children.text:
atra ripuhiṃsanarūpatvā darthasya prauḍhatvam /
alpaprāṇavarṇaprāyatvātsaṃdarbhasya mṛdutvam /
children.translated_text: Here, the vehemence of meaning is due to the theme of destroying enemies. The softness of the composition is due to the predominance of unaspirated consonants.
The <s>madhyamakaiśikī</s> (moderate-graceful mode) has gentle meaning and slightly vehement composition. // Ckc_4.36 //
For example:

children.text: tvāmāśriteṣvavasaro 'pi na hi kraśimnāṃ taccitamāśrayati ca tvayi sā natabhrūḥ /
children.translated_text: "In those who have taken refuge in you, there is no occasion for thinness; yet that bent-browed one takes refuge in thinness because of you;

children.text: ākhyāti hanta tanimānamiti prasaṅge kasyāyaśo vimṛśa cetasi siṅgabhūpa // Ckc_4.*42 //
children.translated_text: alas, she proclaims thinness at this juncture — consider in your heart whose disgrace this is, O <s>Siṅgabhūpa</s>." // Ckc_4.*42 //

Here, the softness of meaning is due to the theme of love-in-separation. The slight harshness of the composition is due to the predominance of conjunct consonants and short syllables, giving it intensity.
The <s>madhyamārabhaṭī</s> (moderate-violent) has vehement meaning but not excessively gentle arrangement. // Ckc_4.37 //
For example:

children.text: saṃvartapāvakaśikhā kimu kiṃ nu jihvā mṛtyoriyaṃ kimu yugāntakṛtāntadaṃṣṭrā /
children.translated_text: "Is this a flame of the fire of cosmic dissolution? Is this a tongue of Death? Is this the fang of the Destroyer at the end of the age?" —
thus it is speculated in the region frequented in the boundary of battle — the sword-line trembling in the hand of <s>Śrīsiṅgabhūpa</s>. // Ckc_4.*43 //

children.text:
atra samarakriyārūpatvādarthasya prauḍhatvam /
miśravarṇārabdhatvātsaṃdarbhasya nātimṛdutvam /
iti vṛttivivekaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the vehemence of meaning is due to the theme of battle-action. The moderate softness of the composition is due to the beginning with mixed consonants. This concludes the analysis of <s>vṛtti</s> (mode).
<s>Pāka</s> (maturation) of words — they call the ripening of expression that which is rich in relish;

children.text: so 'yaṃ mṛduḥ kharaśceti samāsena dvidhā bhavet // Ckc_4.38 //
children.translated_text: this, in brief, is of two kinds: <s>mṛdu</s> (soft/gentle) and <s>khara</s> (harsh/hard). // Ckc_4.38 //
Here, the <s>mṛdupāka</s> (soft maturation) is as follows:

children.text: kiṃ kāmena kimindunā surabhiṇā kiṃ vā jayantena vā madbāgyādanavotasiṅganṛpate rūpaṃ mayā vīkṣitam /
children.translated_text: "What use is <s>Kāma</s>? What use is the moon? What use is the spring? What use is <s>Jayanta</s>? By my good fortune, I have seen the form of King <s>Anavotasiṅga</s>!"

children.text: dhanyāstatparicaryayaiva sudṛśau hanteti romāñcitā svidyadgaṇḍatalaṃ sagadgadapadaṃ sākhyāti sakhyāḥ puraḥ // Ckc_4.*44 //
children.translated_text: "Blessed are those [who serve] through attending upon him alone!" — saying this with horripilation, perspiring cheeks, faltering words, the beautiful-eyed one declares before her friends. // Ckc_4.*44 //

children.text: atra drākṣāpāka ivākleśena samāsvādadāyī śabdapariṇāmo mṛdupāka ityucyate /
children.translated_text: Here, just as the grape's ripening yields flavor without effort, the transformation of words that yields easy relish is called <s>mṛdupāka</s> (soft maturation).

children.text: so 'yaṃ prāyeṇa sahajasāhityarekhāsamullekhānāṃ sarasakavīśvarāṇāmānandaniṣyandaphale prabandheṣu dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: This is generally seen in the compositions of talented poetic masters whose innate literary instinct is well-etched — compositions that are the overflow of bliss.
For instance, of <s>Kālidāsa</s>:
"The mountain's daughter too, revealing her feelings through her limbs" — and so on, in the <s>Kumārasambhava</s>. // Ckc_4.*45 //
And likewise of <s>Śrīharṣadeva</s>:
"The blossom has opened, the young bees' hum [has grown], modesty is heavy, the other is a stranger,

children.text: piasahi visamaṃ pemmaṃ maraṇaṃ saraṇaṃ ca carama ettaṃ'; // Ckc_4.*46 //
children.translated_text: O dear one, love is unequal; death and refuge — this is the final [resort]." // Ckc_4.*46 //
And likewise my own [verse]:
<s>Lakṣmī</s> cast [perspiration] on [his] forehead with her nail-tips, as if repelling the heat of sweat;

children.text: jugopa devo 'pi sa romaharṣaṃ javābdhi vātāhatikaitavena // Ckc_4.*47 //
children.translated_text: the god too protected his horripilation, with the pretext of the wind striking from the ocean of speed. // Ckc_4.*47 //
Thus in the <s>Kandarpasambhava</s>. Likewise, it should be observed in other [works] too.
<s>Kharapāka</s> (hard maturation) is as follows:

children.text: kalyāṇekṣaṇa heṣayā prakaṭitastambhapratiṣṭhākrame mandākṣacchavi sundare lalitadṛkkoṇakriyātoraṇe /
children.translated_text: "Auspicious-eyed one, in the procedure of establishing pillars displayed by neighing, in the beautiful one with gentle eyes, in the gateway of the action of graceful sidelong glances,

children.text: bhāvollāsavilāsake varatanorasyā manomaṇṭape śrīsiṅgakṣitipālamūrtirayate sāmrājyasiṃhāsanam // Ckc_4.*48 //
children.translated_text: in the pavilion of joy-blossoming-coquetry of her excellent body — the form of <s>Śrīsiṅgakṣitipāla</s> ascends the throne of sovereignty as the mind's temple." // Ckc_4.*48 //

children.text:
atra nārikelapāka iva vimarśakleśena vilaṃbyāsvādadāyī śabdapariṇāmaḥ kharapāka ityucyate /
so 'yamabhyastakavibhūmikānāṃ vakroktivāsanāvāsitāntaḥ karaṇānāṃ vidagdhānāṃ vyutpattimātraphaleṣu lakṣyate /
children.translated_text: Here, just as the coconut's ripening yields flavor only after the effort of deliberation, the transformation of words that yields delayed relish is called <s>kharapāka</s> (hard maturation). This is observed in the compositions of accomplished poet-masters, whose inner faculty is perfumed by the inclination toward indirect expression (<s>vakrokti</s>), bearing fruit only in [the reader's] erudition.
For instance, of <s>Murāri</s>:

children.text: tadātvapronmīlanmradimaramaṇīyāḥ kaṭhinatāṃ vicintya pratyaṅgādiva taruṇabhāvena namitau /
children.translated_text: "The softness that was then just blooming, delightful — thinking about [its imminent] hardness from each limb, as if bowed by youthfulness,

children.text: stanau saṃbibhrāṇāḥ kṣaṇavinayavaiyātyamasṛṇa- smaronmeṣāḥ keṣāmupari sarasānāṃ yuvatayaḥ // Ckc_4.*49 //
children.translated_text: bearing breasts, with the smoothness of momentary modesty-coquetry, love's awakening — upon which spirited persons do the young women [dwell]?" // Ckc_4.*49 //
Likewise, of the author of the <s>Naiṣadha</s> (<s>Śrīharṣa</s>):
"All the hairs too, from childlike eagerness to see the chosen bride,
appeared on her body-stalk in bud-form, as if performing neck-stretching exercises." // Ckc_4.*50 //
Also of the same [author]:

children.text: sādhu tvayā tarkitametadeva svenānalaṃ yatkila saṃśrayiṣye /
children.translated_text: "Well have you reasoned this very point — that you will take refuge in your own fire;

children.text: vināmunā svātmani tu prahartuṃ mṛṣā giraṃ tvāṃ nṛpatau na kartum // Ckc_4.*51 //
children.translated_text: but to strike at your own self without this [fire] is [possible], while to speak falsely to you about the king is not." // Ckc_4.*51 //
Thus it should be investigated in other [works] as well. This concludes the analysis of <s>pāka</s> (maturation).
<s>Śayyā</s> (word-placement) is the mutual friendship of words — unable to bear exchange;

children.text: sa evāsya parākāṣṭhā śayyā deśavibhedanaḥ // Ckc_4.39 //
children.translated_text: that itself at its highest point is <s>śayyā</s>, [the principle of] regional distinction. // Ckc_4.39 //

children.text: loke prasiddhamityeṣā prājñaiḥ śayyeti kīrtitā // Ckc_4.40 //
children.translated_text: What is well-known in the world — that is proclaimed by the learned as <s>śayyā</s>. // Ckc_4.40 //
In the impetuous assault-campaign of King <s>Anavotasiṅga</s>, when the drums resound with 'dhaṇaṃ dhaṇaṃ dhaṇam,'

children.text: modante hi raṇaṃ raṇaṃ raṇamiti prauḍhā stadīyā bhaṭāḥ bhrāntiṃ yānti tṛṇaṃ tṛṇaṃ tṛṇamiti pratyarthipṛthvībhujaḥ // Ckc_4.*52 //
children.translated_text: his valiant warriors rejoice [saying] 'battle, battle, battle!' while the enemy kings become confused [thinking] 'grass, grass, grass!' [i.e. worthless]. // Ckc_4.*52 //
For example:

children.text: līlālokanalolupaṃ mṛgakulaṃ gantā guhāntānimāṃ- statkravyagrasana vratīha bhavitā dvīpī ruṣoddīpitaḥ /
children.translated_text: "A herd of deer, eager to gaze playfully, is going to these cave interiors; there will be a leopard here, vowed to seize prey in its jaws, enraged and inflamed;

children.text: yātā tanmṛgayāratervanamidaṃ śrīsiṅgabhūpodayā- dityādirbhayamādiśantyarinṛpāḥ strīṇāmanīkṣāvratam // Ckc_4.*53 //
children.translated_text: this forest has gone to hunt those deer" — thus, from the rise of <s>Śrīsiṅgabhūpa</s>, enemy kings teach the vow of not-looking [=fearful avoidance] to the women through fear. // Ckc_4.*53 //

children.text:
atra padānāṃ paryāyapadasadbhāve 'pi parivṛcyasahiṣṇutvādanyonyamaitrīrūpā śayyā /
atra rasasya pṛthakprakaraṇe prapañcanavivakṣayā vyutkramya vṛttipākaśayyānāṃ svarūpaṃ nirūpitam /
children.translated_text: Here, even though synonyms exist for the words, the <s>śayyā</s> (word-placement) in the form of mutual friendship is due to their intolerance of being exchanged. Here, with the intention of not elaborating in the separate chapter on <s>rasa</s>, the nature of <s>vṛtti</s>, <s>pāka</s>, and <s>śayyā</s> has been examined in reverse order.
This concludes the analysis of <s>śayyā</s> (word-placement).

children.text: iti sarasasāhityacāturīdhurīṇaviśveśvarakavicandrapraṇītāyāṃ śrīsiṅgabhūpālakīrtisudhāsāra śītalāyāṃ camatkāracandrikāyāṃ guṇaviveko nāma caturtho vilāsaḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth <s>vilāsa</s> (chapter), named 'Analysis of Poetic Qualities' (<s>guṇaviveka</s>), in the <s>Camatkāracandrikā</s>, cooled by the nectar-essence of the fame of <s>Śrīsiṅgabhūpāla</s>, composed by <s>Viśveśvarakavicandra</s>, master of the art of flowing literary composition.
The Fifth <s>Vilāsa</s> (Chapter).
<s>Camatkāracandrikā</s> composed by <s>Viśveśvarakavicandra</s>, Fifth Chapter.
That which, through the skill of composition, as if directly manifest,

children.text: alaukikassa cākhādo yassyātso 'tra raso mataḥ // Ckc_5.1 //
children.translated_text: has an unworldly relish — that here is considered <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic emotion). // Ckc_5.1 //
Through its connection, the beauty of poetry attains loveliness;
the poet creates fame lasting from one cosmic cycle to the end of another. // Ckc_5.2 //

children.text: sa vai rasa iti śrutyā brahmaṇaḥ samakakṣyayā /
children.translated_text: By the Vedic utterance '<s>sa vai rasaḥ</s>' ('He indeed is <s>rasa</s>'), equal in rank to <s>Brahman</s>,
<s>rasa</s> is proclaimed; only some, by fortune, experience it. // Ckc_5.3 //

children.text: śivo rasa iti proktaḥ satyaṃ bhāvakasattamaiḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Śiva</s> (auspicious) is <s>rasa</s> — thus is truly stated by the best of connoisseurs (<s>bhāvakas</s>);
otherwise, how could its eight-formed nature (<s>aṣṭamūrtitā</s>) serve the welfare of the world? // Ckc_5.4 //
It is eightfold: <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic) and <s>hāsya</s> (comic), <s>vīra</s> (heroic) and <s>adbhuta</s> (marvelous) are established;
in pairs: <s>raudra</s> (furious) and <s>karuṇa</s> (pathetic), then <s>bībhatsa</s> (disgusting) and <s>bhayānaka</s> (terrifying). // Ckc_5.5 //
By universal agreement, just as the sweet [taste] among the bitter and other tastes,
among the <s>hāsya</s> and other [rasas], <s>śṛṅgāra</s> deserves the sovereignty of <s>rasa</s>. // Ckc_5.6 //
In that, the poet should exert effort, with the desire to have it savored —
[that rasa] experiencing which, the steadfast do not despise themselves. // Ckc_5.7 //
For that poetry is [great] which is pervaded by it; where the poet has extreme devotion,

children.text: vāsanā mānasī vāpi sphuratīti purā vacaḥ // Ckc_5.8 //
children.translated_text: or where a mental impression shines forth — thus is the ancient saying. // Ckc_5.8 //
"Long live <s>vakrokti</s> (indirect expression)! And let <s>svabhāvokti</s> (natural expression) endure!
It is through <s>rasokti</s> (expression of <s>rasa</s>) alone that poems are captivating" — such is my view. // Ckc_5.9 //
Even though possessed of <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) and the rest, who would enjoy words and meanings that are devoid of <s>rasa</s>?
like a married couple devoid of mutual affection. // Ckc_5.10 //
Even a small statement about <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic flavor) in poetry suffices to create beauty;
just as even a trace of camphor perfumes a substance greatly. // Ckc_5.11 //
<s>Sattā</s> (existence), <s>sphurattā</s> (manifestation), <s>anubandha</s> (continuity), <s>niṣpatti</s> (fruition), <s>puṣṭi</s> (nourishment), <s>saṅkara</s> (mixture),

children.text: hrāsābhāsau śamaḥ śeṣa ityuktā hi rasoktayaḥ // Ckc_5.12 //
children.translated_text: <s>hrāsa</s> (diminution), <s>ābhāsa</s> (semblance), <s>śama</s> (quiescence), and <s>śeṣa</s> (remainder) — these are indeed called the <s>rasoktis</s> (statements of rasa). // Ckc_5.12 //

children.text:
nijāśraye samunmeṣo vibhāvaguṇasaṃpadā /
rasasya sattā ratyādisthāyībhāvā ratiśca sā // Ckc_5.13 //
children.translated_text: The dawning of <s>rasa</s> in its proper locus, through the fullness of <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants) and <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) — that is <s>sattā</s> (existence). And <s>rati</s> (love) and the other <s>sthāyibhāvas</s> (permanent emotions) are that: <s>rati</s> itself is that. // Ckc_5.13 //

children.text:
āśrayo viṣayaḥ, protsāhaḥ sahakārīṇi ceti trirūpavibhāva samagratayā kevalayā rasasya svāśraye yadunmeṣamātraṃ seha sattā /
saiva ratyādīnāṃ kevalānāmākāreṇā vatiṣṭhate /
ratyādayaśca -- ratirhāsotsāhavismayakrodhaśokajugupsābhayāni kramoditaśṛṅgārādirasādhiṣṭhānabhūmayo vāsanāpravāheṇāvatiṣṭhamānā sthāyina ityucyante /
children.translated_text: The locus (<s>āśraya</s>), the object (<s>viṣaya</s>), the excitants (<s>protsāha</s>), and the co-operant causes (<s>sahakārin</s>) — these are the three forms of <s>vibhāva</s> (determinant). When rasa dawns merely through their completeness, in its own locus — this is <s>sattā</s> (existence). It subsists in the form of <s>rati</s> and other basic emotions alone. And <s>rati</s> and the others — <s>rati</s> (love), <s>hāsa</s> (laughter), <s>utsāha</s> (enthusiasm), <s>vismaya</s> (wonder), <s>krodha</s> (anger), <s>śoka</s> (grief), <s>jugupsā</s> (disgust), and <s>bhaya</s> (fear) — these, being the foundational grounds of the sequentially stated <s>rasas</s> beginning with <s>śṛṅgāra</s>, subsisting through the flow of latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), are called <s>sthāyins</s> (permanent emotions).
<s>Sattā</s> in the form of <s>rati</s> (love), for example:
While charming bee-couples hum, while the male cuckoo sings, at the beginning of the worship of <s>Smara's</s> (Love's) sandals at the base of the mango tree,

children.text: śyāmāyā madurādhare mṛgadṛśi vyālola nīlālake dūrādānanapaṅkaje kṣitibhujā vyāpārite locane // Ckc_5.*1 //
children.translated_text: the king fixed his gaze from afar upon the lotus-face of a dark-lipped, deer-eyed woman with flowing blue tresses. // Ckc_5.*1 //

children.text: atra kevalaṃ vibhāvasāmagrīkathanena nāyakasyābhilāṣāmatraṃ pratīyata iti seyaṃ rasasya sattā /
children.translated_text: Here, merely through the description of the aggregate of <s>vibhāvas</s> (determinants), only the hero's longing is perceived — hence this is <s>sattā</s> (the mere existence) of <s>rasa</s>.
When there is the manifestation of even a single <s>anubhāva</s> (consequent) or a <s>sāttvika</s> (involuntary physical response),
through an elaborate process of impression-cultivation — that is called <s>sphurattā</s> (manifestation). // Ckc_5.14 //

children.text:
anubhāvāḥ saṃkṣopato dvividhāhyuktāḥ kāyikā vācikāśceti /
anubhāvatve 'pi stambhapralayaromā ñcasvedavaivarṇyavepathugadgadikāśrulakṣaṇānāṃ sācvikānāṃ pṛthagabhidhānaṃ viśeṣadyotanāya /
children.translated_text: The <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents) are said to be briefly of two kinds: bodily (<s>kāyika</s>) and verbal (<s>vācika</s>). Although they too are consequents, the <s>sāttvika bhāvas</s> — characterized by stupefaction (<s>stambha</s>), dissolution (<s>pralaya</s>), horripilation (<s>romāñca</s>), perspiration (<s>sveda</s>), change of color (<s>vaivarṇya</s>), trembling (<s>vepathu</s>), choking of voice (<s>gadgadikā</s>), and tears (<s>aśru</s>) — are mentioned separately to highlight their distinctive nature.

children.text: ratirūpeṇa rasasya sphurattā yathā keyūraratnamupalālayatā nṛpeṇa yatprārthitaṃ nijasakhaīcana sannidhāne /
children.translated_text: <s>Sphurattā</s> (manifestation) of rasa in the form of <s>rati</s>, for example: The king, who was caressing the jewel of his armlet, when he made a certain request in the presence of his close friend—

children.text: śyāmāpayodharataṭī paramādareṇa tasyottaraṃ kṛtavatī pulakaprarohān // Ckc_5.*2 //
children.translated_text: the dark woman's breast-slope, with supreme regard, responded by producing an eruption of horripilation. // Ckc_5.*2 //

children.text:
atra nāyake keyūranāyakaratnapratibimbatanāyikāpayodharalālanalakṣaṇanāyikānubhāvetpādanarūpā rasasya sphulattā /
nāyikāyāṃ ca pulakalakṣaṇaikasācvikasampādakatayā sphurattaiva /
children.translated_text: Here, through the consequent of the hero — caressing the armlet-jewel that reflects the heroine's breast (as a way of touching her by proxy) — the manifestation of rasa takes the form of the enactment of the hero's consequent. And in the heroine, through the production of a single <s>sāttvika</s> (involuntary response) in the form of horripilation, it is <s>sphurattā</s> (manifestation) itself.
And for example:

children.text: sparśotsavena nṛpateḥ pramadākucābhyāṃ rāgāṅkurā iva dhṛtāḥ pulakaprarohāḥ /
children.translated_text: From the joy of the king's touch, on the young woman's breasts, eruptions of horripilation were held as if they were sprouts of passion;
and his palm-sprout-like hand, as if to water them, displays droplets of perspiration. // Ckc_5.*3 //

children.text: atra kramāt pulakasvedalakṣaṇasācvikābhyāṃ rasasya sphurattā sūcyate /
children.translated_text: Here, through the two <s>sāttvika</s> responses — horripilation and perspiration, in sequence — the manifestation of <s>rasa</s> is indicated.
Through the catalyzing <s>vibhāvas</s> and other excitants, with an increasingly powerful process of cultivation,
here there is the repeated occurrence of a single <s>anubhāva</s>. // Ckc_5.15 //
Whether of a single <s>vyabhicārin</s> (transient emotion) with several <s>anubhāvas</s>, or a single occurrence—
this is called <s>anubandha</s> (continuity) by those who understand the succession of <s>rasa</s>. // Ckc_5.16 //

An example of <s>anubandha</s> characterized by the repetition of a single <s>anubhāva</s>: At the end of a spring festival entertainment scented with camphor, as the beautiful women were departing to their own homes,
King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s> was summoned repeatedly by their sidelong glances turned with difficulty. // Ckc_5.*4 //
