children.translated_text: Here, starting from the rim at the third interval, '<s>Camatkāra-jyotsnā</s>' reveals the title of the work; at the seventh, '<s>Viśvapati-kavi</s>' reveals the author's name; and at the ninth, the hero's name is revealed. From the word '<s>ādi</s>' (etc.), lotus-patterns and others [are included].
Here, a <s>padmabandha</s> (lotus-pattern) is as follows:
"She who has dispelled the demonic temperament through [noble] disposition, she whose feet are comprehended through syllables,

children.text: sārasā dayatu siṅgayaṃ rasā sārayaṃ gajavatī kṣaṇā ca sā // Ckc_6.*22 //
children.translated_text: may she, the crane-like one, the essence, delight King <s>Siṅga</s> — she who possesses elephants, that <s>Lakṣmī</s>, even for a moment!" // Ckc_6.*22 //

children.text:
atra kṣapitāḥ bhāvena rākṣasāḥ krūrajanāḥ yayā sā kṣapitabhāvarākṣasā daridrīkṛtakrūrajanetyarthaḥ /
sākṣarāvagatapādasārasā vidvaddhyātapādapadmā mā lakṣmīḥ rasāsāraṃ bhūvi śreṣṭhaṃ vastu yāti prāpnoti iti rasāsārayaḥ /
taṃ siṅgayaṃ siṅgabhūpālaṃ sārasādāvāsapadmādayatu bhajatu /
tathā gajavatī svādhāradiggajavatītyarthaḥ /
sā kṣamā bhūmiśca /
anyadevaṃ vidhamanusandheyam /
children.translated_text: Here, 'she by whom cruel people have been impoverished through [noble] character' is <s>kṣapitabhāvarākṣasā</s>. '<s>Sākṣarāvagatapādasārasā</s>' means 'she whose lotus feet are meditated upon by the learned.' '<s>Mā</s>' means <s>Lakṣmī</s>. '<s>Rasāsāra</s>' means 'the best thing on earth'; '<s>siṅgayam</s>' means King <s>Siṅgabhūpāla</s>. '<s>Sārasā</s>' means 'from the lotus-dwelling.' '<s>Dayatu</s>' means 'may she favor.' And '<s>gajavatī</s>' means 'possessing the directional elephants that are her supports.' '<s>Sā kṣamā</s>' means that Earth too [is intended]. Other [readings] of this kind should be investigated.
<s>Yamaka</s> (repetition with different meanings) is a re-hearing, inseparable from a group of harsh consonants,
with distinct meanings — occurring at the beginning, middle, end, etc. — it is of three kinds. // Ckc_6.13 //
<s>Ādiyamaka</s> (initial-position repetition) is as follows, of the hero himself:
"Compassionate, compassionate is my intellect; with the presence of [your] incarnation,
sweet, sweet, O Lord — may there be respect from you!" // Ckc_6.*23 //

children.text:
atra caturṇāmapi pādānāmādau pradhamākṣarasahitaṃ varṇatritayamāntaratamavyavthānena punaḥśrutamiti sarvapādādiyamakamidam /
evamanyepi dvipādādiyamakadalayorvyavahitāvyavahitabhedāḥ svayamavagantavyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, in all four quarters, three syllables including the first syllable are heard again with intervening material — hence this is <s>sarvapādādi-yamaka</s> (alliterative repetition at the beginning of all quarters). Likewise, other types such as two-quarter-initial <s>yamaka</s>, with contiguous and non-contiguous varieties of the pair-divisions, should be understood by oneself.
An example of <s>madhya-yamaka</s> (middle alliterative repetition):
In the battle adorned with dense fame, which foremost warrior can endure?

children.text: bhavadasiṃ vada siṅgamahīpate paramayā ramayā bharitadyute // Ckc_6.*24 //
children.translated_text: Speak, O King <s>Siṅga</s>, your sword, filled with supreme delight! // Ckc_6.*24 //

children.text:
atra caturṣvapi pādeṣu prathamākṣaraṃ vihāya madhyākṣarayamakamāntaramavya vadhānena punaḥśrutamiti sarvapādamadhyayamakamidam /
evamanye 'pi pūrvapadasya bhedā nirūpaṇīyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, in all four quarters, leaving aside the first syllable, the middle syllable <s>yamaka</s> is heard again with intervening material — hence this is <s>sarvapāda-madhya-yamaka</s> (middle alliterative repetition in all quarters). Likewise, other subdivisions of this type should be examined.
An example of <s>antya-yamaka</s> (final alliterative repetition):
O King <s>Siṅga</s>, steadfast as <s>Meru</s>, you who are fragrant with fame—
may <s>Vasudeva</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), who has fulfilled his purpose through good deeds, who has distributed abundant wealth, protect you always! // Ckc_6.*25 //

children.text:
he merudhīra siṅgamahīpāla yaśasā saurabhavantaṃ yaśassurabhiṃ bhavantaṃ sukṛtīkṛtavasudevaḥ svajanmanā kṛtārthīkṛtānakadundubhiḥ devaḥ śrīkṛṣṇaḥ vitīrṇaghanavasu yathā tathā pāyādityantyākṣara sahitamakṣaracatuṣṭayam pādadvaye punaḥśrutamiti dvipādāntayamakamidam /
evamanye 'pi bhedāḥ svayamūhyāḥ /
children.translated_text: O 'steadfast as <s>Meru</s>,' O King <s>Siṅga</s>, you who are fragrant with fame — 'he whose good deeds have fulfilled the purpose of <s>Vasudeva</s>' means: he by whose birth <s>Anakadundubhi</s> (Vasudeva, Kṛṣṇa's father) was made fulfilled — Lord <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, distributing abundant wealth — may he protect you! Four syllables including the final syllable are heard again in two quarters — hence this is <s>dvipādāntya-yamaka</s> (final alliterative repetition in two quarters). Likewise, other types should be inferred by oneself.
The further subdivisions of these are many and difficult;
since they conflict with the gentle style (<s>mṛdu-mārga</s>), they have not been elaborated by us. // Ckc_6.14 //
A sentence consisting of speech and counter-speech is called <s>vākovākya</s> (dialogue). // Ckc_6.15 //
For example:

children.text: rambhe kiṃ sakhi menake na sulabhāḥ kalpadrumāṇāṃ srajaḥ te svarge na hi santi kutra dharaṇībhāge kutaḥ kāraṇāt /
children.translated_text: "<s>Rambhā</s>, dear friend <s>Menakā</s>, are not the garlands of wish-fulfilling trees easily available?" "They do not exist in heaven." "Where then?" "On the earth." "For what reason?"

children.text: dātuḥ śrīanavotasiṅganṛpatestairdattahastāṅgulīr brahmā nirmitanānato nu dhanikāḥ sarve 'pi dhātrīsurāḥ // Ckc_6.*26 //
children.translated_text: "The Creator <s>Brahmā</s> made them all, bowing, with hands joined, touching the fingers of the generous King <s>Śrī Anavota Siṅga</s> — are not all the gods of the earth indeed wealthy?" // Ckc_6.*26 //
Here, the dialogue between <s>Rambhā</s> and <s>Menakā</s> is evident.
That in which the connection of action, agent, and relationship is concealed is called <s>gūḍha</s> (hidden). // Ckc_6.16 //
An example of concealed action (<s>kriyā-gūḍha</s>):
He whose circle of lordship over enemy territories is severed by the sword,
O King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>, protector of the earth — <s>vibhava</s> — prospers in abundance! // Ckc_6.*27 //

children.text: atra he vibho samṛddhatāmehīti kriyāpadasya vibhava iti saptamyā gopitatvamiti gūḍhakriyāpadatvāt kriyāgūḍham /
children.translated_text: Here, 'O Lord, come to prosperity!' — the verbal root (the imperative 'come') is concealed by the locative form '<s>vibhava</s>.' Since the action-word is concealed, this is <s>kriyā-gūḍha</s> (concealed action).
And for example:
The form of King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>, lord of the earth, resembling <s>Kandarpa</s> (the god of Love),
on the city street — the unmoving corner-glances of the women. // Ckc_6.*28 //

children.text: atrāpuriti kriyāpadaṃ purandhrīṇāmiti padena gopitamiti kriyāgūḍham /
children.translated_text: Here, the action-word '<s>apu</s>' (they did not drink, i.e., they were absorbed) is concealed by the word '<s>purandhrīṇām</s>' (of the women) — hence this is <s>kriyā-gūḍha</s> (concealed action).
An example of concealed agent (<s>kāraka-gūḍha</s>):
Due to the panic and alarm caused by the military raid of King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>'s plough(-like army),

children.text: kva darī kva darītyadreḥ kāntāre raṭati sphuṭam // Ckc_6.*29 //
children.translated_text: 'Where is a cave? Where is a cave?' — in the mountain wilderness, it cries out loudly. // Ckc_6.*29 //

children.text:
atra raṭatikriyāyāḥ kartṛkārakabhūtā areḥ kāntāḥ kāntāra iti saptamyā gopitamiti kārakagūḍheṣu kartṛgūḍhamidam /
evaṃ karmagūḍhādayo draṣṭavyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the agent of the action 'cries out' — the 'beloved of the enemy' — is concealed by the locative '<s>kāntāre</s>' (in the wilderness, which also hides '<s>kāntā</s> + <s>areḥ</s>' = beloved of the enemy). Hence, among concealed agents, this is an example of concealed subject-agent. Likewise, concealed object-agent and others should be observed.
An example of concealed relational word (<s>saṃbandha-pada-gūḍha</s>):
The beauty of sidelong glances does not merely approach arrows, O king,
and through the graceful play of the eyebrow-creeper, a bow — your service is that of beautiful women too. // Ckc_6.*30 //

children.text:
atra eḥ kāmasyeti sambandhapadaṃ lalitairvilāsairiti tṛtīyā vā (tṛtīyayā?) gopitamiti saṃbandhagūḍhamidam /
paṣṭhayāḥ kārakatvābhāvāt sambhandhagūḍhasyātra pṛthaṅnirdeśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the relational word 'of <s>Kāma</s> (the god of Love)' is concealed by the instrumental '<s>lalitaiḥ</s>' (by the graceful ones) or by the instrumental case — hence this is concealed relationship. Since the genitive case is not a <s>kāraka</s> (syntactic role), the concealed relationship is mentioned separately here.

children.text: yatrottararya nirmedaḥ praśne praśnottaraṃ hi tat /
children.translated_text: Where the answer is contained within the question, that is called <s>praśnottara</s> (question-and-answer);
it is threefold: <s>antaḥpraśna</s> (internal question), <s>bahiḥpraśna</s> (external question), and <s>ubhayapraśna</s> (both). // Ckc_6.17 //
"Whom does the bodiless <s>Manobhū</s> (god of Love) arouse? Does the abode of kings shine with treasures?

children.text: kāmadhurā kathaya saśe tvayaiva kathitaṃ hi siṅgabhūpāla // Ckc_6.*31 //
children.translated_text: Is <s>Kāma</s> sweet? Tell me" — "You have yourself already told it, O King <s>Siṅga</s>!" // Ckc_6.*31 //

children.text:
atra manobhūḥ kamalobhayaditi praśne kaṃ brahmāṇam /
narapativeśma kiṃmiti praśne kinnarapativeśma, kuberagṛhamiti /
madhurā keti praśne kāmadhurā kāmabhāra iti cottarāṇi praśnāvayasyāntara itīdamantaḥpraśnam /
children.translated_text: Here, in the question 'whom does <s>Manobhū</s> agitate?', the answer is '<s>ka</s>' = <s>Brahmā</s>. In the question 'does the king's abode shine?', the answer is 'yes, the abode of <s>Kinnara</s> (a celestial musician) — <s>Kubera's</s> house.' In the question 'is <s>Kāma</s> sweet?', the answer is '<s>kāmadhurā</s>' = the burden of desire. Since the answers are within the interstitial parts of the questions, this is <s>antaḥpraśna</s> (internal question).
"A face opposing faces, with cheeks adorned in the middle, terrifying — is this the head of <s>Bhairava</s>?

children.text: tvayā naceduttaramapradattaṃ rājan na jānāti bhavān bhavantam // Ckc_6.*32 //
children.translated_text: If you do not give the answer, O king, you do not know yourself!" // Ckc_6.*32 //

children.text: atra pratigaṇḍabhairava ityuttarasya praśnavākyāntare pratīyamānatvādidañcāntaḥ praśnam /
children.translated_text: Here, since the answer '<s>pratigaṇḍa-Bhairava</s>' (the title of the king, meaning 'one whose cheeks rival Bhairava') is perceived within the question-sentence, this too is <s>antaḥpraśna</s> (internal question).
An example of <s>bahiḥpraśna</s> (external question):
"Of what kind is the army? And what is the proper address of the Lord of Gods, the Pure One? And what is the circle of your enemies?
O King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>, give the answers — through the augmentation by fear of the previously stated syllables!" // Ckc_6.*33 //

children.text:
atra indrabalaṃ saphali śucisaṃbuddhiḥ pavitreti tvadvipumaṇḍalaṃ vitrapaṃ vitrasaditi vā trīṇyuttarāṇi praśnād bahireva mṛgyāṇi /
bahiḥ praśnamidam /
children.translated_text: Here, the army of <s>Indra</s> is 'successful'; the form of address for the Pure One is '<s>pavitra</s>' (pure); your enemy-circle is '<s>vitrapa</s>' (trembling with fear) — these three answers must be sought entirely outside the question. This is <s>bahiḥpraśna</s> (external question).
An example of <s>ubhayapraśna</s> (both-type question):

children.text: yogināṃ bhogināṃ rājan ka iṣṭastaṃ na vetti yaḥ /
children.translated_text: "O king, who is dear to <s>yogins</s> and enjoyers? He who does not know him—

children.text: viparīto harastena na jñāto hi sahāmbaraḥ // Ckc_6.*34 //
children.translated_text: the reverse of '<s>hara</s>' — by him, indeed, even the sky-clad one (<s>Śiva</s>) is not known." // Ckc_6.*34 //

children.text:
atra rahovāsa ityuttarasya pūrvabhāgo rahaśśabdo viparītaharaśabdena praśnavākyasyāntaḥ pratīyate /
uttarāvayavo vāsa ityayaṃ bahireva mṛgyata iti bahirantaḥpraśnottarasya sthitatvādidamubhayapraśnam /
children.translated_text: Here, in the answer '<s>rahovāsa</s>' (dwelling in solitude/secret), the first part '<s>raha</s>' is perceived within the question-sentence through the reverse of the word '<s>hara</s>' — hence it is internal. The remaining part of the answer, '<s>vāsa</s>,' must be sought entirely outside — hence it is external. Since the answer has both internal and external parts, this is <s>ubhayapraśna</s> (both-type question).
Thus have been properly examined the varieties of <s>śabdālaṅkāra</s> (verbal ornaments);
a poet should adorn his poetry with these so that it is not laughed at by others. // Ckc_6.18 //

children.text: iti sarasasāhityacāturīdhurīṇaviśveśvarakavicandrapraṇītāyāṃ camatkāracandrikāyāṃ śabdālaṅkāraviveko nāma ṣaṣṭho vilāsaḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the sixth chapter, called 'Analysis of Verbal Ornaments,' in the <s>Camatkāracandrikā</s> composed by <s>Viśveśvara Kavicandra</s>, who is pre-eminent in the skill of eloquent literary composition.
Seventh chapter (<s>vilāsa</s>).
<s>Camatkāracandrikā</s>, composed by <s>Viśveśvara Kavicandra</s>. Seventh chapter.
Those which are capable of adorning meanings, which shine in dependence on that (meaning),

children.text: ye tu jātyādayaḥ prājñaiḥ ter'thālaṅkārasaṃjñayā // Ckc_7.1 //
children.translated_text: those beginning with <s>jāti</s> (natural description) are designated by the wise as <s>arthālaṅkāra</s> (sense-ornaments). // Ckc_7.1 //
<s>Jāti</s> (natural description), <s>vibhāvanā</s> (fancy), <s>hetu</s> (reason), <s>ahetu</s> (unreason), <s>sūkṣma</s> (subtle), <s>uttara</s> (reply),
<s>virodha</s> (contradiction), <s>sambhava</s> (possibility), <s>anyonya</s> (mutual), <s>parivṛtti</s> (exchange), <s>nidarśanā</s> (illustration), // Ckc_7.2 //

children.text:
bhedaḥ samāhitaṃ bhrāntiḥ vitarko mīlitaṃ smṛtiḥ /
bhāvo 'numānārthāpattī iti te viṃśatirmatāḥ // Ckc_7.3 //
children.translated_text: <s>bheda</s> (distinction), <s>samāhita</s> (combination), <s>bhrānti</s> (error), <s>vitarka</s> (conjecture), <s>mīlita</s> (blending), <s>smṛti</s> (recollection), <s>bhāva</s> (emotion), <s>anumāna</s> (inference), <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption) — these twenty are considered. // Ckc_7.3 //
The established forms of an object in its various states,
when directly presented — that is called <s>jāti</s> (natural description). // Ckc_7.4 //
Among these, <s>jāti</s> (natural description):
It is twofold, based on the distinction between inherent nature and momentary state.
The first type (inherent nature), for example:
Repeatedly shaking their dust-covered manes, continually tossing their faces and necks,
King <s>Siṅga</s> inspects the horses offered as tribute by enemy kings. // Ckc_7.*1 //
Here, the natural behavior of the horses ... [text damaged] ...
The momentary type (<s>tātkālikī</s>), for example:

children.text: pūrvāṅgaṃ lalitaṃ nidhāya mṛdule siṃhāsanopāśraye paśyan bāṇamṛjūkṛtaṃ savayasā smerairapāṅgekṣaṇaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Placing his graceful front body on the soft seat-rest of the throne, watching an arrow being straightened by a companion with smiling sidelong glances,

children.text: kurvan karṇapuṭīṃ sudhārasamayīṃ vācaṃ parīkṣāvatā- māsthānyāmanavotasiṅganṛpatiḥ puṣṇāti netrotsavam // Ckc_7.*2 //
children.translated_text: making his ear-cavity nectar-sweet with the speech of one who is testing — King <s>Anavota Siṅga</s> nourishes a feast for the eyes at the court-assembly. // Ckc_7.*2 //
Here, since it describes the momentary state and posture of the king, this is <s>tātkālikī jāti</s> (momentary natural description).
When, by excluding a well-known cause, some other cause

children.text: vibhāvyate khabhāvo vā vijñeyā sā vibhāvanā // Ckc_7.5 //
children.translated_text: is fancied, or the absence of cause — that should be known as <s>vibhāvanā</s> (fancy). // Ckc_7.5 //
Here, the imagining of an alternative cause, for example:

children.text: tanvanna bhāravinatiṃ phaṇirājamūdhrnāṃ kurvanna dhautaśucitāṃ haraśāṭikānām /
children.translated_text: Not causing the bending of the serpent-kings' heads with weight, not producing the washed whiteness of <s>Hara's</s> (<s>Śiva's</s>) garments,

children.text: badhrannanambara vitānamajāṇḍabhāge śrīsiṅgabhūpa tava bhāti yaśovilāsaḥ // Ckc_7.*3 //
children.translated_text: not forming a canopy on the surface of the cosmic egg — O King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>, the splendor of your fame shines forth! // Ckc_7.*3 //

children.text: atra vinatiśucitvavitānānāṃ bhāradhāvanāṃśukāni hetutayā prasiddhāni tāni nirvartya yaśaso dhāvalyanairmalyabāhulyānyanyāni kāraṇāni vibhāvyanta itīyaṃ kāraṇāntaravibhāvanā /
children.translated_text: Here, weight, washing, and cloth are the well-known causes of bending, whiteness, and canopy respectively; having set those aside, the whiteness, purity, and abundance of fame are fancied as alternative causes — hence this is <s>kāraṇāntara-vibhāvanā</s> (fancy of an alternative cause).
An example of <s>svabhāva-vibhāvanā</s> (fancy of inherent nature):
O King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>, your wisdom, with its sharp edge never having been whetted,
and your fame, never having been perfumed yet fragrant, are constant. // Ckc_7.*4 //

children.text: atra tīkṣṇatvasugandhitvayorloke ullekhanavāsane prasiddhabhūte iti nirvartya prajñāyaśasoḥ svabhāvo 'pi vibhāvyata itīyaṃ svabhāvavibhāvanā /
children.translated_text: Here, sharpness and fragrance in the world have whetting and perfuming as their well-known causes; having set those aside, the inherent nature of wisdom and fame is fancied — hence this is <s>svabhāva-vibhāvanā</s> (fancy of inherent nature).

children.text: kriyāyāḥ kāraṇaṃ hetuḥ mukhyo gauṇa iti dvidhā /
children.translated_text: The cause of an action is <s>hetu</s> (reason); it is twofold: primary (<s>mukhya</s>) and secondary (<s>gauṇa</s>);
the primary <s>hetu</s> is again twofold: through the <s>kāraka</s> (syntactic agent) and through the indicator (<s>jñāpaka</s>). // Ckc_7.6 //
And the first is threefold: of instigation (<s>pravṛtti</s>), of cessation (<s>nivṛtti</s>), and of causation (<s>prayukta</s>). // Ckc_7.7 //
Here, an example of the <s>kāraka-hetu</s> characterized by instigating action:
Skilled in cutting through the dense mass of sinful deeds, filling again with the utterance of meritorious deeds—

children.text: saṃpādayanti satataṃ pramadaṃ janānāṃ śrīsiṅgabhūpacaritāni mahādbhutāni // Ckc_7.*5 //
children.translated_text: the wondrous deeds of King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s> constantly produce great delight among the people. // Ckc_7.*5 //

children.text: atra nāyakacaritānyevaṃ bhūtāni pracānāṃ prāgasataḥ santoṣasya pravartanakriyāyāmāviṣṭānīti kriyāviṣṭo 'yaṃ pravartakaḥ kārakahetuḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the hero's deeds, being of such nature, are immersed in the instigating action of producing the previously non-existent satisfaction of the people — hence this is an action-immersed instigating <s>kāraka-hetu</s>.
The same, when not immersed in action, for example:
The fame of King <s>Siṅga</s>, whose crown is never broken, has accomplished even the three worlds,

with waves of glory-rivers that rival the <s>Gaṅgā</s> with their foam produced by the slipping of jeweled crests from the twisted matted locks of <s>Viṣama-viṣama-cakṣu</s> (<s>Śiva</s>). // Ckc_7.*6 //

children.text:
atra bhuvanaviśadabhāve kīrtāvanāviṣṭāṃ hetau tṛtīyāṃ prayojayati /
na tu kartarīti kriyānāviṣṭo 'yaṃ pravartakaḥ kārakahetuḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, in the whiteness of the world, fame — not immersed in the action as cause — employs the instrumental case (of cause). It is not the subject-agent — hence this is an action-non-immersed instigating <s>kāraka-hetu</s>.
An example of a cessation-type action-immersed <s>kāraka-hetu</s>:
Excelling greatly in the destruction, at the forefront of fierce battle's delight, of the invincible forces of the enemy army's circle,

children.text: siṅgakṣoṇīpatirabhivahan ghoradaṃbholipālī- jṛmbārambhaprakaṭanadhurā bandhurāṃ khaḍgadhārām // Ckc_7.*7 //
children.translated_text: King <s>Siṅga</s>, wielder of a beautiful sword-edge that serves as the vehicle for the display of the gaping of terrible arrow-rows. // Ckc_7.*7 //
Here, the hero, with only a sword as companion, is immersed as the subject-agent in the action of destroying the enemy's valor — hence this is an action-immersed cessation-type <s>kāraka-hetu</s>.
The same, when not immersed in action, likewise:
From the bow of King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>, due to the excessively risen sound of the bowstring,
the necklace-grounds on the throats of the enemy women attain the state of being without strings (<s>nirguṇa</s>). // Ckc_7.*8 //

children.text: atra vairikulapālikākaṇṭhasūtranivartanakriyāmanāviśan nāyakakodaṇḍadaṇḍo hetau pañcamīṃ prayojayatīti kriyānāviṣṭo 'yam nivartakaḥ kārakahetuḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the hero's bow-staff, without being immersed in the cessation-action of severing the throat-strings of enemy clan-women, employs the ablative case (of cause) — hence this is an action-non-immersed cessation-type <s>kāraka-hetu</s>.
An example of a causative-type action-immersed <s>hetu</s>:

children.text: kumāre śrīsiṅge jaladhiraśanāṃ śāsati mahī- mamaryādādhvastāḥ patanapariṇāhapratibhuvaḥ /
children.translated_text: When Prince <s>Śrī Siṅga</s> rules the ocean-girt earth — the boundaries of transgression, destined for the catastrophe of falling,

children.text: adharmā nirmūlā narakaparipākapraṇidhayo vinaṣṭā duśceṣṭāḥ kali kaluṣapeśīparidhayaḥ // Ckc_7.*9 //
children.translated_text: are uprooted; unrighteous ones, intent on the ripening of hellish fruits, are destroyed; evil deeds, with the coverings of the <s>Kali</s> age's impurities— // Ckc_7.*9 //

children.text: atra maryādādhvaṃsādiṣu kriyāsu saptamīvācyanaimittikādhikaraṇakārakabhāvena nāyako 'yamāviśan prayojako bhavatīti yathoktaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, in the actions of destroying boundaries and such, the hero, by entering as the locative-case conditional-ground <s>kāraka</s>, becomes the causative agent — hence it is as stated.
The same, when not immersed in action, for example:

children.text: śrīsiṅgakṣitināthapārśvamayatāmajñātapūrvaṃ hi naḥ tatsevābhyasanaṃ vidheyamiti te pratyarthipṛthvībhūjaḥ /
children.translated_text: "We must go to the side of King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>; the practice of serving him is indeed unknown to us previously;

children.text: vṛddhāmātyajanānupāṃśu vinayātsiṃhāsane sthāpitān saṃbaddhāñjalayo bhajanti mahitā stotraikacitroktayaḥ // Ckc_7.*10 //
children.translated_text: it must be learned" — thus the enemy kings, with folded palms, approach the elderly ministers privately established on the throne with humility, honored, with speeches of praise as their only ornament. // Ckc_7.*10 //

children.text: atra nīcairavasthānāñjalibandhanastotrakaraṇādirūpāyāṃ sevābhyasanakriyāyāmātmanyevātmanaḥ samāveśo na saṃbhavatīti kriyānāviṣṭo 'yamiti śabdābidheyaprayojako nāma kārakahetuḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, in the practice of service characterized by humble standing, joining of palms, and composing of praises, since self-immersion of oneself in oneself is impossible, this is action-non-immersed — a <s>kāraka-hetu</s> called the expressible causative.

children.text: dvitīyā ca tṛtīyā ca caturthaī saptamī ca yam /
children.translated_text: The second (accusative), third (instrumental), fourth (dative), and seventh (locative) cases—
declares what is not involved in the action — he is the <s>lakṣaka</s> (indicator) and <s>jñāpaka</s> (informer). // Ckc_7.8 //
Of these, the <s>lakṣaka-hetu</s> (indicator-cause) expressed by the second case-ending is as follows:
Toward <s>Śrī Siṅgabhūpati</s>, who cuts down enemies with the sword of cool rays,

children.text: saṅgarasīmani vividhāḥ kātaraceṣṭā bhavanti vimatānām // Ckc_7.*11 //
children.translated_text: at the boundary of battle, the opponents display various gestures of cowardice. // Ckc_7.*11 //

children.text:
atra kriyānāviṣṭenaiva nāyakenana vimatānāṃ bhayajanakakātaraceṣṭā labhyante viśeṣyanta iti so 'yaṃ lakṣaṇahetuḥ /
pratinā yoge dvitīyāmutpādayatīti dvitīyāvācyo 'yam /
children.translated_text: Here, merely through the hero who is not involved in the action, the fear-producing gestures of cowardice of the opponents are obtained and specified — thus this is the <s>lakṣaṇa-hetu</s> (indicator-cause). Since with the word 'prati' (toward) it generates the second case-ending, it is called 'expressed by the second case-ending.'
Similarly, the one expressed by the third case-ending is as follows:
Resorting to kinship allied with a common refuge, in battle the citizens behold the king of the royal mountain-capital,
the king, with a crest of blooming <s>saugandhika</s> flowers, through obedience born of his command. // Ckc_7.*12 //

children.text: atra saugandhikaśekharaṃ darśanakriyāyāmanāviśadeva rājānaṃ jñāpayatītītthaṃbhāvalakṣaṇatṛtīyayā vājyo 'yaṃ jñāpakahetuḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the <s>saugandhika</s> flower-crest, without being involved in the action of seeing, indicates the king — thus this <s>jñāpaka-hetu</s> (informer-cause) is expressed by the third case-ending denoting such a state.
The one expressed by the fourth case-ending is as follows:
<s>Śrī Siṅgadharaṇīpāla's</s> foot-service — one who turns away from it,

children.text: akāṇḍe śemuṣī rājñāṃ rājyabhraṃśāya vairiṇām // Ckc_7.*13 //
children.translated_text: untimely, the intellect of enemy kings leads to the loss of their kingdom. // Ckc_7.*13 //

children.text:
atrotpātabhūtayā rājñāmakāṇḍato nāyakasevāparāṅmukhībhāvabuddhyā teṣāṃ rājyabhraṃśo jñāpyate /
tenāyamutpātena jñāpyamāna iti caturthyā vācyo jñāpakahetuḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, through the intelligence of turning away from the hero's service, which is like an omen, the loss of kingdom of the kings is indicated untimely. Therefore, since this is indicated by the omen, the <s>jñāpaka-hetu</s> (informer-cause) is expressed by the fourth case-ending.
The one expressed by the seventh case-ending is as follows:

children.text: mā bhūta pratirājakātpratimukhāḥ kīrti vihāyādhunā prāṇebhyaḥ kva nuyāta dhūtamatayo bhoḥ paśyatāsmāniti /
children.translated_text: 'Let there be no confrontation with rival kings! Abandoning glory now, O confused ones, where would you go from your very lives? Behold us!' —

children.text: śāsatsu svapatākinī radhikṛteṣvārūḍhamandasmitaḥ śrīsiṅgakṣitipo ripūnabhimukho badhnāti dossampadaḥ // Ckc_7.*14 //
children.translated_text: When the commanders thus discipline their own armies, <s>Śrī Siṅgakṣitipa</s> (King Siṅga), with a gentle smile, faces the enemies and binds them with the splendor of his arms. // Ckc_7.*14 //

children.text: atra senādhipatīnāṃ balānuśāsanakriyayā nāyakasya prakāśanakriyā lakṣyate /
children.translated_text: Here, through the action of the generals disciplining the army, the hero's action of manifestation is indicated.
<s>Hetu</s> (cause) is called <s>gauṇa</s> (secondary) because it depends on figurative usage;
it is also honored as <s>citrahetu</s> (variegated cause) because it produces wonder. // Ckc_7.9 //

children.text:
samakālo viparyasto yuktāyuktāvasaṃgataḥ /
iti tasya samāsena pañca bhedāḥ prakīrtitāḥ // Ckc_7.10 //
children.translated_text: <s>Samakāla</s> (simultaneous), <s>viparyasta</s> (reversed), <s>yukta</s> (fitting), <s>ayukta</s> (unfitting), and <s>asaṅgata</s> (incongruous) — in brief, five varieties of it are proclaimed. // Ckc_7.10 //
Of these, a cause that arises simultaneously with its effect is <s>samakāla</s> (simultaneous).
For example:
<s>Śrī Siṅgabhūpa</s>, devoted to poetry, teacher of heroes on the battlefield, from his quiver

children.text: bāṇān samākarṣati śātakoṇān prāṇairarīṇāṃ samakālameva // Ckc_7.*15 //
children.translated_text: draws arrows with sharp points — simultaneously with the very lives of his enemies. // Ckc_7.*15 //

children.text:
atra kāryapūrvakṣaṇa varti kāraṇamityetadullaṅdhya kāraṇabhūtasya bāṇākarṣaṇasya tatkāryabhūtasya vimataprāṇākarṣaṇasya ca samakālamevotpattikathanāt samakālo nāmāyaṃ gauṇahetuḥ /
kāryādanantaramutpanno heturviparyastaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, transgressing the principle that a cause precedes its effect by one moment, by stating that the drawing of arrows (which is the cause) and the drawing away of the enemies' lives (which is the effect) arise simultaneously — this is the <s>gauṇa-hetu</s> (secondary cause) called <s>samakāla</s> (simultaneous). A cause that arises after its effect is <s>viparyasta</s> (reversed).
For example:
Later does <s>Siṅga</s> release the sword from its sheath, O <s>Śrī Siṅgabhūpate</s>,

children.text: kośaṃ muñcanti paurastyāḥ purastādeva bhūbhujaḥ // Ckc_7.*16 //
children.translated_text: but the eastern kings release their treasuries even beforehand. // Ckc_7.*16 //

children.text:
atra pūrvadikpārthivabhāṇḍāgāratyāgalakṣaṇasya kāryasyotpatteranantaratvāt kāraṇabhūtasya nāyakakhaḍgamokṣasyotpattikathanādiyaṃ viparyasto nāma citrahetuḥ /
yuktakāryakārī heturyuktaḥ /
tadviparīto henurayuktaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, since the effect — namely the abandoning of treasuries by the kings of the eastern direction — arises first, and the cause — namely the hero's releasing of the sword — is stated as arising after it, this is the <s>citrahetu</s> (variegated cause) called <s>viparyasta</s> (reversed). A cause that produces a fitting effect is <s>yukta</s> (fitting). Its opposite is <s>ayukta</s> (unfitting).
Both are illustrated as follows:
May the serpent of your sword, O <s>Siṅgabhūpate</s>, perform the wind-feast upon the life-breath of enemies;
how does the darkness of sorrow of your adversaries increase through the splendor of the heat of your valor? // Ckc_7.*17 //

children.text:
atra prathamārdhe yatsarpāṇāmucitaṃ pavanapāraṇakāryaṃ tadeva kṛtamityayaṃ yukto nāma gauṇahetuḥ /
uttarārdhe tejaso yaduktaṃ tamovardhanaṃ tadevakṛtamityatyukto 'yaṃ gauṇahetuḥ /
adhikaraṇaheturasaṅgataḥ /

children.translated_text: For example:

children.text: bhūbhārastava dakṣa bāhuśikhare mūdhrnā natāḥ pārthivāḥ prāgalbhyaṃ tvayi siṅgabhūvara paraṃ vītatrapā vairiṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: The burden of the earth rests on your capable shoulder-peak — kings bow their heads; boldness in you, O best of kings <s>Siṅgabhūvara</s> — enemies are shameless;

children.text: aunnatyaṃ tvayi garvitāḥ pratibhaṭa vyāptāntarikṣāntarāś citraṃ kāraṇamekataḥ parigataḥ kāryodayastvanyataḥ // Ckc_7.*18 //
children.translated_text: loftiness in you — proud rival warriors have pervaded the interior of the sky. Wonderful! The cause is in one place, the arising of the effect is in another. // Ckc_7.*18 //

Here, in the first half, what is appropriate for serpents — the wind-feast — is performed, thus this is the <s>gauṇa-hetu</s> (secondary cause) called <s>yukta</s> (fitting). In the second half, the very thing said of radiance — namely the increase of darkness — is performed, thus this is the <s>gauṇa-hetu</s> called <s>ayukta</s> (unfitting). The cause based on a different substratum is <s>asaṅgata</s> (incongruous).

children.text: atra nāyakagatānāṃ bhūbharaṇādikāraṇānāṃ pratināyakagatānāṃ namratvādikāryāṇāṃ vaiyadhikaraṇyenāsaṃbaddhatvādasaṅgato nāmāyaṃ gauṇahetuḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, because the causes such as bearing the earth, which reside in the hero, and the effects such as bowing, which reside in the antagonists, are unconnected due to being in different substrata — this is the <s>gauṇa-hetu</s> (secondary cause) called <s>asaṅgata</s> (incongruous).
Thus has been shown this course of the varieties of <s>hetu</s> (cause);
the causes of non-existence (<s>abhāva-hetu</s>) too should similarly be inferred by the discerning. // Ckc_7.11 //

children.text:
vastusvabhāvādanyena hetunā vā parāhataḥ /
notpādayati yaḥ kāryaṃ so 'heturiti gīyate // Ckc_7.12 //
children.translated_text: That which, being overcome by the nature of things or by another cause, does not produce its effect — that is called <s>ahetu</s> (non-cause). // Ckc_7.12 //
<s>Ahetu</s> (non-cause) overcome by the nature of things (<s>vastusvabhāvaparāhata</s>) is as follows:

children.text: rūkṣāhaṃkṛtayo na santi lalite bhedaṃ gate na bhruvau dṛkkoṇo 'pi na rāgameti hasitaṃ mandaṃ ca nāntarhitam /
children.translated_text: There are no harsh expressions of ego, O graceful one; the eyebrows have not parted; the corner of the eye does not assume passion; the gentle smile too has not been concealed;

children.text: dṛṣṭvāpi pratigarjatāṃ kṣitibhujāṃ saṃraṃbhagarbhakriyā mūrtirdāruṇaceṣṭayāpyavikṛtā śrīsiṅgapṛthvīpate // Ckc_7.*19 //
children.translated_text: even upon seeing the roaring enemy kings, the form with its wrathful gestures remains unaltered despite their fierce actions, O <s>Śrī Siṅgapṛthvīpate</s> (King Siṅga, lord of the earth). // Ckc_7.*19 //

children.text: atrātisaṃraṃbhapratināyakaceṣṭāvikaraṇa samarthasyāpi satatākārya (?) nāyaka mūrtisvabhāvaprabhāvaparāhatā huṃkārādikāluṣyarūpaṃ kāryaṃ notpādayatīti so 'yaṃ tathoktaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the actions of the fiercely agitated antagonists, though capable of causing disturbance, being overcome by the power of the hero's ever-composed (?) bodily nature, do not produce the effect of harshness such as roaring — thus it is called as stated.
The second type is as follows:

children.text: dossāraṃ samareṣu siṅganṛpateḥ prāyeṇa jānannapi kṣmāpāleṣu bhavādṛśeṣvapi cirāt tatpādasaṃseviṣu /
children.translated_text: Knowing well the strength of arms of King <s>Siṅga</s> in battles, even among kings like yourself who have long served his feet,

children.text: śruṇvannāptajanoddhatāṃ giramapi prāṇeśa dhīmān bhavān tatsevāṃ na cikīrṣatīti yadidaṃ tahaiva duśceṣṭitāt // Ckc_7.*20 //
children.translated_text: hearing even the bold words of trusted people, O lord of life, your wise self does not desire to serve him — this is indeed due to evil fate. // Ckc_7.*20 //

children.text: atra nāyakadossārajñānādikāraṇānāṃ pratināyakagirā lakṣaṇakāryakaraṇasāmarthye 'pi bhavitavyatāparāhataśaktitvakathanāt kāraṇāntaraparāhato 'yamahetuḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, since the causes such as knowledge of the hero's arm-strength, though having the capacity to produce their effects indicated by the rival's words, are stated as having their power overcome by fate (<s>bhavitavyatā</s>) — this is <s>ahetu</s> (non-cause) overcome by another cause.

children.text: nirūḍhe sāhitye sarasahṛdayānandasadane vadānye śrīsiṅgakṣitipatilake tiṣṭhati puraḥ /
children.translated_text: When in well-established literature, in the abode of joy for sensitive connoisseurs, the generous <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>, the crest-jewel of kings, stands before one,

children.text: kṛtārthaḥ sarvārthe bhavati bhuvi yaḥ kaścana na cel lalāṭe durlaṃghā duritalipirasyaiva mahatī // Ckc_7.*21 //
children.translated_text: whoever in this world is not fulfilled in all purposes — great indeed is the insurmountable inscription of misfortune on his forehead. // Ckc_7.*21 //

children.text: atra vidyāpakṣapātavrata nāyakaudāryasya sakalārthi kṛtārthīkaraṇasāmarthye 'pi yatra kutra cit kāryasyānutpādakatve tadarthilālāṭika durlipiparāhatatvakathanādanyaparāhato 'yamahetuḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, though the hero's generosity, devoted to learning, has the capacity to fulfill all supplicants, wherever the effect fails to arise, by stating that it is overcome by the evil inscription on that supplicant's forehead — this is <s>ahetu</s> (non-cause) overcome by another.
That which is called a chain of causes (<s>kāraṇamālā</s>) is termed <s>hetusantāna</s> (causal continuum);
since individually they lack efficacy, in my view it too is <s>ahetu</s> (non-cause). // Ckc_7.13 //
For example:

children.text: prājñaiḥ prāktanavāsanāparikarairvidvajjavopāsanaṃ tenāpi pratibhā tathā madhurayā sāhityasākṣātkriyā /
children.translated_text: By the wise, through the equipment of prior impressions, there is attendance upon learned persons; through that too arises poetic genius, and through that sweet genius, the direct realization of literature;

children.text: tatproḍhīranavotasiṅganṛpatessmerāḥ kaṭābhakramāḥ te lakṣmīradhikāṃ tathā kṛtadhiyāṃ siddhyet trivargodayaḥ // Ckc_7.*22 //
children.translated_text: through that accomplishment, the beautiful glances from the smiling eyes of <s>Siṅga</s>, the king of fresh boldness; through those, prosperity; and thus for the accomplished, the attainment of the three goals of life would be achieved. // Ckc_7.*22 //

children.text: atra vidvajjanopāsanādīnāmuttarottarahetubhūtānāmapi trivargodaye pūrvapūrvavyapekṣayā samucitanāmeva kāraṇatvamiti pṛthak pṛthagasāmarthyāt kāraṇamālāpyahetureva /
children.translated_text: Here, attendance upon learned persons and the subsequent causes, though each being a cause of the next leading to the attainment of the three goals of life, individually require the preceding one — thus lacking independent efficacy, the <s>kāraṇamālā</s> (causal chain) too is indeed <s>ahetu</s> (non-cause).
<s>Sūkṣma</s> (subtle) has its meaning discerned by the clever, and is twofold: by way of <s>ākāra</s> (gesture) and <s>iṅgita</s> (hint). // Ckc_7.14 //
For example:
When the king, caressing the gem on his armlet in the presence of her own female companions, made his request,

children.text: śyāmā payodharayuge paramādareṇa tasyottaraṃ kṛtavatī pulakaprarohān // Ckc_7.*23 //
children.translated_text: the dark-complexioned lady responded to him on her pair of breasts with supreme affection — by the sprouting of goosebumps. // Ckc_7.*23 //

children.text:
atra keyūranāyakaratnasaṃkrāntanāyikāpratibimbapayodharopalālanakaraṇamiṅgitam /
tena nāyakasya manoratho vidagdhayā nāyikayā lakṣyate sma /
nāyikāyāśca romāñca ākāraḥ /
tenāṅgīkaraṇarūpā svābhilaṣitacikīrṣā nāyikāyā vidagdhena nāyakena jñāyata itīdamubhayavidhaṃ sūkṣamam /
children.translated_text: Here, the hero's caressing of the reflection of the heroine on the breast-like surface of the gem in the armlet is the <s>iṅgita</s> (hint). Through that, the hero's desire is discerned by the clever heroine. And the heroine's goosebumps constitute the <s>ākāra</s> (gesture). Through that, the heroine's wish to fulfill his desire is known by the clever hero — thus this is <s>sūkṣma</s> (subtle) of both kinds.
After that, <s>uttara</s> (climax) is the great excellence that is successively greater among things. // Ckc_7.15 //
For example:

children.text: jambūdvīpe lasati nitarāmandhradeśo viśeṣaḥ śreyastasmin bhavati nagaraṃ rājaśailābhidhānam /
children.translated_text: <s>Jambūdvīpa</s> shines exceedingly; within it, <s>Āndhradeśa</s> is especially distinguished; within that, the city called <s>Rājaśaila</s> is most auspicious;

children.text: tatrotkarṣaṃ kalayati sabhā siṅgabhūpālamaule- ssārātsāraṃ vacanaracanaṃ tatra tasyāpi rājñaḥ // Ckc_7.*24 //
children.translated_text: within that, the court of <s>Siṅgabhūpāla</s>, the crown-jewel of kings, attains preeminence; and the very essence of essences is the verbal composition of that king himself. // Ckc_7.*24 //
Here, because <s>Āndhradeśa</s> and the rest are described with successively increasing excellence, this is <s>uttara</s> (climax).
<s>Virodha</s> (contradiction) is the mutual incompatibility of things;
it has the varieties of <s>asaṅgata</s> (incongruous), <s>pratyanīka</s> (opposed), <s>viṣama</s> (unequal), and <s>adhīra</s> (unsteady). // Ckc_7.16 //

children.text:
so 'yaṃ dvidhā budhairuktaratācvikābhāsa bhedataḥ /
tācviko 'pi dvidhā śuddho grathitaśceti gīyate // Ckc_7.17 //
children.translated_text: This is said by the learned to be twofold: by the division into <s>tācvika</s> (real) and <s>ābhāsa</s> (apparent). The <s>tācvika</s> (real) too is twofold: <s>śuddha</s> (pure) and <s>grathita</s> (braided) — so it is declared. // Ckc_7.17 //
Here, the pure real contradiction (<s>śuddha tācvika virodha</s>) is as follows:

children.text: dhanapradānaṃ dvaviṇārjanaṃ ca sāmrājyakṣmīrbhuvi bhāratī ca /
children.translated_text: Giving away of wealth and earning of wealth, sovereignty over the earth and <s>Bhāratī</s> (goddess of learning),

children.text: dhīvṛddhasevā navayauvanaṃ ca śrīsiṅgabhūpe vilasanti nityam // Ckc_7.*25 //
children.translated_text: attendance upon the wise elders and fresh youth — in <s>Śrī Siṅgabhūpa</s> these always shine forth. // Ckc_7.*25 //

children.text: atra dhanapradānārjanayoḥ takṣmīsarasvatyoḥ vṛddhasevānavayauvanayośca virodhastācviko viviktaśceti yathoktaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the contradiction between giving and earning of wealth, between <s>Lakṣmī</s> (sovereignty) and <s>Sarasvatī</s> (learning), and between service to elders and fresh youth — is real and distinct, thus it is as stated.
The braided real contradiction (<s>grathita tācvika virodha</s>) is as follows:

children.text: kiṃ nirdveṣakathasya daityahananaṃ tatrāpi kiṃ nidrayā nidrālorurasi striyā kimatha sā nissaṃbhavā syātkatham /
children.translated_text: How can the slayer of <s>Daityas</s> (demons) be without enmity? And how, in that case, can he sleep? How can a woman be on the chest of one who sleeps? And how could she be without birth?

children.text: daityāreriti tatpurāṇasamaye goṣṭhīṣu vidvajjana- prauḍhokttīrniśamayya siṅganṛpatiḥ smerānano jāyate // Ckc_7.*26 //
children.translated_text: Hearing such bold utterances of learned people in assemblies regarding <s>Daityāri</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) in the <s>Purāṇic</s> age, King <s>Siṅga</s> breaks into a smile. // Ckc_7.*26 //
Here, because the contradictions are braided one into the next successively, this is the real contradiction (<s>tatva-virodha</s>) called <s>grathita</s> (braided).
Where, through the power of <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia) and the like, contradiction merely appears,
having charm only in apprehension — this <s>ābhāsa</s> (apparent type) is said to be twofold. // Ckc_7.18 //
The pure apparent contradiction (<s>śuddha ābhāsa virodha</s>) is as follows:
We declare King <s>Siṅgabhūpāla</s> to be learned in <s>saujanya</s> (gentility);

children.text: kāmaṃ vadati vīrāliḥ tamasaujanya paṇḍitam // Ckc_7.*27 //
children.translated_text: indeed, the <s>vīrāli</s> (row of heroes) declares him learned in <s>asaujanya</s> (ungentility). // Ckc_7.*27 //

children.text:
atra rājanyasaujanyayogarūpo virodhaḥ śabdaśloṣamātreṇa pratīyate /
tacvatastu vīrapaṅktirasaujanyapaṇḍitaṃ raṇakuśalaṃ vadatīti parihāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the contradiction in the form of the conjunction of royalty and gentility is perceived only through verbal paronomasia (<s>śleṣa</s>). In reality, the row of heroes declares him 'learned in ungentility' meaning 'skilled in battle' — thus is the resolution.
The same in braided form is as follows:

children.text: rājñaste gurutā kathaṃ bada guroḥ padmāttatā syātkatham padmāttasya ca jiṣṇutā kathamaho jiṣṇoḥ kathaṃ saumyatā /
children.translated_text: How can your kingship have heaviness, tell me? How can one who is heavy be born of a lotus? How can one born of a lotus be victorious? How, pray, can a victorious one be gentle?

children.text: saumyasya kṣitinandanatvamucitaṃ loke kathaṃ bhūpateḥ śrīsiṅgakṣitinandantvamapi tallakṣṇīśvarollāsitam // Ckc_7.*28 //
children.translated_text: Is it fitting that a gentle one be a 'joy of the earth' in this world? How can a king, O <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>, be a 'joy of the earth' — yet that too is graced by <s>Lakṣmīśvara</s> (the Lord of Lakṣmī). // Ckc_7.*28 //

children.text:
atrottarottarasaṃkalanayā grathitasya śleṣamūlatvādābhāsatvaṃ spaṣṭameva /
kiṃ bhūpatitvaṃ kutaḥ śrīsiṅgakṣitinandanasya tadidaṃ lakṣmīśvarollāsitamiti /
children.translated_text: Here, through the successive linking, since the braided form is rooted in <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia), its apparent nature is quite clear. 'What is this kingship? Whence is it for <s>Śrī Siṅgakṣitinandana</s>? It is graced by <s>Lakṣmīśvara</s>' — thus.
Of <s>asaṅgati</s> (incongruity) beginning with <s>jāti</s> (class), many varieties of both are acknowledged. // Ckc_7.19 //
Of these, the incongruity of <s>jāti</s> (class) with class, action, quality, and substance is as follows:
<s>Śrī Siṅgabhūpāla</s>, your mind too is a mountain; though a mine of lotuses, it is one whose mud has been dried up;

children.text: khyāto 'si bhogījanavatsalo 'pi bhūmau suparvo 'pi ca sārvabhaumaḥ // Ckc_7.*29 //
children.translated_text: though celebrated as one fond of serpent-people, you are a sovereign emperor on earth; though a <s>suparva</s> (one of auspicious joints / a god), you are a universal sovereign. // Ckc_7.*29 //

children.text: atra prathame pāde meghaparvatajātyoḥ dvitīye padmākarapaṅkaśoṣaṇakriyayoḥ tṛtīye sarvajātivatsalatpaguṇayoḥ caturthe devajāteḥ sārvabhaumanānro diggajalakṣaṇasya dravyasya cāsaṃhatiriti catvāro jātivirodhāḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, in the first quarter there is incongruity between the classes of cloud and mountain; in the second, between the lotus-lake and the action of drying up mud; in the third, between the quality of being fond of all classes and serpents; in the fourth, between the class of gods (<s>deva-jāti</s>) and the substance of directional elephants denoted by <s>sārvabhauma</s> — thus there are four class-contradictions.
The contradiction of action with action, quality, and substance:

children.text: yathā kaviprītiṃ kurvan tirayasi kaviṃ nītinigame tava prajñā tīkṣṇā racayati na bhedaṃ kṛtadhiyām /
children.translated_text: While delighting poets you conceal the poet in treatises on polity; your intellect though sharp does not cause division among the wise;

children.text: kalānātho 'pi tvaṃ tyajasi nanu nabhatrapadavīṃ vicitraṃ śrīsiṅgakṣitivara caritraṃ tava param // Ckc_7.*30 //
children.translated_text: though a lord of arts you forsake the path of the stars — wonderful indeed, O <s>Śrī Siṅgakṣitivara</s>, is your surpassing conduct! // Ckc_7.*30 //

children.text:
atra kaviprītikaraṇa kavitiraskaraṇakriyayoḥ prathamapāde dvitīye tīkṣṇatvaguṇabhedakriyayoḥ tṛtīye kalānāthanāmnaḥ candralakṣaṇadravyasya nakṣatramārgatyajanekriyāyāśca saṅgatiriti trayaḥ kriyāvirodhāḥ /
guṇasya guṇadravyābhyāṃ virodhe dvau bhedau /
children.translated_text: Here, in the first half-verse, there is the joining of the actions of pleasing the poet and scorning the poet; in the second, of sharpness and quality-distinction; in the third, the substance named the moon (<s>Kalānātha</s>, lord of digits) with the action of abandoning the path of the stars — thus three contradictions of action. For the contradiction of quality with quality and quality with substance, there are two varieties.
Of these, the contradiction of two qualities —
O King <s>Siṅgabhūpa</s>, both southerliness and northerliness cannot exist in one tree at the same time;

children.text: dākṣiṇyamuttaratvaṃ bhavati tu nirṛtyapekṣayā bhavati // Ckc_7.*31 //
children.translated_text: yet (they do) exist with reference to the southwest (<s>Nirṛti</s>) direction. // Ckc_7.*31 //
Here, there is contradiction between two qualities: southerliness and northerliness.
An example of the contradiction of quality and substance —
Wonderful, O King <s>Siṅgabhūpa</s> — even by your warriors who are <s>Arjuna</s>s (white/brave),
hosts of fame are increased, (those warriors) who are tender toward <s>Mitra</s>'s (the sun's/a friend's) sons (<s>Nandana</s>). // Ckc_7.*32 //

children.text:
atrārjunalakṣaṇadravyasya karṇa vātsalyaguṇasya virodhaḥ /
dravyasya dravyeṇa virodhe eka eva bhedaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, there is contradiction between the substance named <s>Arjuna</s> (whose enemy was <s>Karṇa</s>) and the quality of tenderness toward <s>Karṇa</s> (= <s>Mitra</s>'s son). For the contradiction of substance with substance, there is a single variety.
For example —
In the sweet (city of <s>Madhurā</s>), in the great and ever-expansive (land/kingdom) yielding (royal) minerals,

children.text: śrī siṅganṛpo dharaṇīṃ māṃdhātāpi praśāsti kṛtavīryaḥ // Ckc_7.*33 //
children.translated_text: King <s>Siṅga</s> rules the earth — even <s>Māndhātā</s>, (who is also) <s>Kṛtavīrya</s>. // Ckc_7.*33 //

children.text: atra prathamārdhe madhurāyā viśalānagaratvaṃ dvitīye māṃdhātuḥ kṛtavīryatvamiti dravyavirodhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, in the first half, the city <s>Madhurā</s> being identified with the city <s>Viśālā</s> (i.e., two different cities); in the second half, <s>Māndhātā</s> being identified with <s>Kṛtavīrya</s> (two different kings) — this is contradiction of substance.
Thus, ten varieties of apparent contradiction (<s>ābhāsavirodha</s>) have been delineated.

children.text: evaṃ tācvika bhedāstu khayamūhyā vicakṣaṇaiḥ // Ckc_7.20 //
children.translated_text: Likewise, the real (tāttvika) varieties should be inferred independently by the discerning. // Ckc_7.20 //
An example of <s>asaṅgata</s> (incongruity) among the varieties of contradiction —
A certain lion among kings shines on the royal mountain, as the fortune of the middle world,
at whose outskirts the intoxication-excess of the enemy-creepers has dissolved — (the intoxication) of the proud elephants who approached (him). // Ckc_7.*34 //

children.text: atra siṃhāntikamāptānāṃ kuñjarāṇāṃ madaśoṣo nasaṃgacchata ityasaṃgato nāmāyaṃ virodhabhedaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the drying up of the rut-fluid of elephants that have approached the lion — this does not accord (with reality, since elephants in rut are more fierce), hence this variety of contradiction is called <s>asaṅgata</s> (incongruity).
An example of <s>pratyanīka</s> (counter-opposition) —

children.text: śrotuṃ raṃbhāracanāṃ nirbharānandagarbhāṃ (?) prāsādeṣu pratidiśataṭinīṃ vīkṣituṃ jālamārgeḥ /
children.translated_text: To hear the most joyful performance of <s>Rambhā</s> in the palaces, to see (her beauty like) a river in every direction through the lattice-windows —

children.text: citraṃ siṅgakṣitipa bhavataḥ khaḍgadhārā nimagnā nidrāmudrāṃ niravadhikathāmāśrayanti dviṣantaḥ // Ckc_7.*35 //
children.translated_text: wonder! O King <s>Siṅga</s>, your enemies, plunged in the stream of your sword, resort to the posture of endless sleep (death). // Ckc_7.*35 //

children.text: atra vacanaśravaṇanirīkṣaṇārthināṃ niravadhinidrāśrayaṇaṃ pratikūlatvenāsaṅgatamiti pratyanīkamapi virodha eva /
children.translated_text: Here, for those who desire to hear and see (performances), resorting to endless sleep is contrary (to their purpose) — since it is incongruous by being counterproductive, <s>pratyanīka</s> too is indeed a form of contradiction.
An example of <s>viṣama</s> (asymmetry/inequality) —

children.text: diśāṃ dukūlaṃ hasitaṃ jayaśriyā yaśo vilāsastava siṅgabhūpate /
children.translated_text: The silk garment of the directions, the laughter of the goddess of victory, the sport of your fame, O King <s>Siṅga</s> —

children.text: svabhāvaśuddho 'pi muśe virodhināṃ karoti mālinyataraṅgitāṃ diśām // Ckc_7.*36 //
children.translated_text: though pure by nature, in the faces of your adversaries, it produces waves of darkness (blemish) upon the directions. // Ckc_7.*36 //

children.text:
atra dhavalasya yaśaso virodhimukheṣu yadatimālinyakaraṇaṃ tasya ca yādṛśo 'pyupajāyate tādṛgeva tadbhavatīti prasiddhivaiṣamyāt parasparāsaṅgaterayaṃ viṣamaṃ nāma virodhaḥ /
athavā diṅmukheṣu viśadīkaraṇaṃ virodhimukheṣu malinīkaraṇañca samavartanaprakāro na bhavatīti vaiṣamyādviṣam virodhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the fact that white fame produces extreme blackening in the faces of enemies — and whatever kind of effect arises, that very kind it becomes — since this asymmetry of established fact results in mutual incongruity, this is the contradiction called <s>viṣama</s> (asymmetric). Alternatively, brightening in the faces of the directions and darkening in the faces of enemies — this mode of operating simultaneously cannot occur, hence, due to inequality, this is <s>viṣama</s> contradiction.
An example of <s>adhika</s> (exceeding) —

children.text: śrī siṅgakṣitipo vahanniśitadhī rākarṇakṛṣṭaṃ dhanuḥ pratyaśvaṃ pratikuñjaraṃ pratinaraṃ muñcannamoghān śarān /
children.translated_text: The glorious King <s>Siṅga</s>, bearing sharp intelligence, a bow drawn to the ear, releasing unerring arrows against every horse, every elephant, every man —

children.text: yāvanti dviṣatāṃ balāni balavatyāścaryameko 'pyasau tāvadvā samameva tairabhimukhairadhyakṣamālabhyate // Ckc_7.*37 //
children.translated_text: against however many forces the enemies possess, though mighty — wonder! — even he alone is perceived equally with all those who face him, as if he were their overseer. // Ckc_7.*37 //

children.text: atraikasyāpi nāyakasyānekairapi sainyai ranekadhā dṛśyamānatve naikatvasaṃkhyāviruddhasaṃkhyādhikyaṃ pratīyata ityadhikaṃ nāma virodhabhedaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the hero, though one, being perceived in many forms simultaneously even by many soldiers — since a multiplicity contradicting the number of oneness is apprehended — this variety of contradiction is called <s>adhika</s> (exceeding).
Where, from the observation of abundant causes, the occurrence of something is expected,

children.text: niṣedho vā viśeṣajñaissa saṃbhava itīritaḥ // Ckc_7.21 //
children.translated_text: or its negation — that is called <s>saṃbhava</s> (possibility) by the experts in distinctions. // Ckc_7.21 //
Here, an example of positive possibility (<s>vidhisaṃbhava</s>) —
O lord of the <s>Recarla</s> earth, when the expanse of the sky is enveloped by the dust of the earth-surface pounded by millions of your terrifying <s>Nāsīra</s> war-horses,

children.text: syātsaṃbhāvyaṃ tanuyavanikāthannadīpopamānaṃ paryantodyatparivṛḍha śikhā padmarāgopalānāma // Ckc_7.*38 //
children.translated_text: it would be plausible to imagine a comparison to a thin curtain, with the brilliantly rising, full-crested ruby-stones of the chieftains (barely visible through it). // Ckc_7.*38 //

children.text: atraivaṃvidhe rajasi sāmantaśikhāmaṇīnāṃ tādṛśī daśā saṃbhāvyeti vidhessaṃbhāvyamānatvādayaṃ vidhisaṃbhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, in such dust, such a condition of the chieftains' crest-jewels is deemed plausible — since a positive occurrence is being imagined as possible, this is positive possibility (<s>vidhisaṃbhava</s>).
An example of negative possibility (<s>niṣedhasaṃbhava</s>) —

children.text: somollāsini pāraśīkanṛpatau saṃdhānusaṃdhāyake kanyāratnasamarpaṇād gajapatau saṃbandhagandhaspṛśi /
children.translated_text: When the <s>Soma</s>-exalted (Muslim/Pāraśīka) king is proceeding with treaty-negotiations, when the <s>Gajapatī</s> (king of Orissa) bears a mere whiff of alliance through offering a jewel-princess,

children.text: raicarlānvayaśārṅiṇaṃ narapatiṃ draṣṭuṃ raṇe sāhasaṃ saṃbhāvyaṃ na hi gautamīparisarakṣudrakṣamābhṛdgaṇe // Ckc_7.*39 //
children.translated_text: the daring to face in battle the king of the <s>Recarla</s> lineage who bears the bow of <s>Śārṅgin</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) — that is not to be imagined among the small kings (<s>kṣudrakṣamābhṛt</s>) in the vicinity of the <s>Gautamī</s> (Godavari). // Ckc_7.*39 //
The daring to withstand such a hero's fury is not to be imagined among the petty kings — since there is negation, this is negative possibility (<s>niṣedhasaṃbhava</s>).

children.text: anyonyaṃ pratīkāro yastadanyonyaṃ mataṃ mama // Ckc_7.22 //
children.translated_text: That which is mutual assistance between two parties — that is my view of <s>anyonya</s> (reciprocal). // Ckc_7.22 //
For example —

O King <s>Siṅgabhūpa</s>, crown-jewel, treasury of snow-mountain-like glory — by the cool, virtuous flow of your gift-waters, purified by the touch of hands that have arrested the submarine fire and sanctified the celestial sages,

children.text: bhāṇḍāgārānyanarghairanudinamavate pūrayatyaiṣa ratnair ityanyonyopakāraprasṛmaravibhavau tvaṃ ca vārāṃ nidhiśca // Ckc_7.*40 //
children.translated_text: this one (the ocean) fills his treasuries daily with priceless gems — thus, through mutual assistance, your powers spread: you and the lord of waters (the ocean) (help each other). // Ckc_7.*40 //
Here, between the hero and the ocean, there is mutual assistance — through the flow of gift-waters and the collection of excellent gems — hence this is <s>anyonya</s> (reciprocal).
<s>Ekatā</s> (unity), <s>cūlikā</s> (pinnacle), and <s>bhrānti</s> (confusion) are variants of <s>anyonya</s> itself. // Ckc_7.23 //
Here, an example of <s>anyonya-ekatā</s> (reciprocal unity) —
Your fame, with its brilliance as clear as arrays of upraised white lotuses, and your valor, lovely in form like gleaming <s>Campaka</s> (golden flowers) —

children.text: pratyathikṣitipālamandirabhuvi śrīsiṅgabhūpojjvalā- nyanyonya dyutimelanena bhavatarḥ sakīrṇavarṇā iva // Ckc_7.*41 //
children.translated_text: O resplendent King <s>Siṅgabhūpa</s>, in the palaces of rival kings, by the merging of each other's radiance, your (fame and valor) appear as if of mingled colors. // Ckc_7.*41 //

children.text: atra kīrtipratāpayor anyonyaṃ vikāryavikā rakabhāvāt pratīkārapratīteranyonyaikyatāpyanyonya eva /
children.translated_text: Here, since fame and valor are in a relationship of mutual cause and effect, and since the perception of mutual assimilation arises, the unity of <s>anyonya</s> too is a variety of <s>anyonya</s> itself.
An example of <s>anyonya-cūlikā</s> (reciprocal pinnacle) —

children.text: vidyāśriyā rājati vidyayā śrīḥ śrīsiṅgabhūpo vacasā śriyā ca /
children.translated_text: King <s>Siṅgabhūpa</s> shines through learning graced with prosperity, through prosperity graced with learning, through speech (graced) with prosperity,

children.text: nayo 'pi sattvena nayena sattvaṃ nayena sattvena yathā sa eva // Ckc_7.*42 //
children.translated_text: through statecraft with courage, through courage with statecraft — through statecraft and courage alike, he is himself. // Ckc_7.*42 //

children.text: atra vidyāśriyorvirājane parasparamupakāryopakārakatayā vartamānayordvayornāyakavirājamānakriyāyā apakārakatvaṃ yat seyaṃ cūlikopari vardhata ityanyonyacūlikeyamanyonyabheda eva /
children.translated_text: Here, learning and prosperity mutually assist each other in their shining forth as both cause and effect; their being the cause of the hero's shining action (while also functioning as effects) — this pinnacle grows upon (itself), hence this <s>anyonya-cūlikā</s> is a variety of <s>anyonya</s> itself.
An example of <s>anyonya-bhrānti</s> (reciprocal confusion) —

children.text: līyante gahatnāntareṣu śanakairānmaikṣaṇāśaṅkino bhūpālān bhavadīya sainikadhiyā vīkṣyādhvagān vairiṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: The enemies of King <s>Siṅga</s>, suspecting a trap, slowly hide in forest interiors; seeing travelers, they think them your soldiers, O lord of the earth.

children.text: tānālokya malimlucā iti dhiyā pārśvadvayālokinaḥ sannaddhāstvaritaṃ prayānti pathikāḥ śrī siṅgapṛthvīpate // Ckc_7.*43 //
children.translated_text: And the travelers, seeing them and thinking them robbers (<s>malimluca</s>), looking to both sides, gird themselves and proceed in haste. // Ckc_7.*43 //

children.text: atra kāntārasañcāriṇāṃ nāyakavirodhināṃ pathikānāṃ parasparamuddeśyoddeśakatābhāvāt pratīkārapratīteranyonyabhrāntiranyonyabheda eva /
children.translated_text: Here, since the hero's enemies traveling in the wilderness and the travelers mutually mistake each other — without either being the actual intended party — the perception of mutual (mis)recognition constitutes <s>anyonya-bhrānti</s>, a variety of <s>anyonya</s> itself.

children.text: vyatyayo vastunonyastu yo vā vinimayo mithaḥ /
children.translated_text: The transposition of one thing to another, or the mutual exchange —

children.text: parivṛttiriyaṃ proktā mukhyā gauṇīti sā dvidhā // Ckc_7.24 //
children.translated_text: this is called <s>parivṛtti</s> (exchange), declared to be of two kinds: literal (<s>mukhyā</s>) and figurative (<s>gauṇī</s>). // Ckc_7.24 //
An example of literal exchange through transposition (<s>vyatyaya</s>) —

children.text: sujanamayati lakṣṇīrdurjanānujjhati śrīḥ vrajati layamadharmo vardhate dharmamārgaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Lakṣmī</s> (fortune) attends the virtuous, <s>Śrī</s> (prosperity) abandons the wicked, <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness) goes to dissolution, and the path of <s>dharma</s> flourishes —
under the protection of this sovereign, born of the jewel-womb <s>Acyuta</s>'s descent, who is served by the wise, King <s>Siṅgabhūpa</s> the excellent. // Ckc_7.*44 //

children.text:
atra nāyakarājye sujanadurjanayorlakṣmīparivṛttiḥ /
dharmādharmayorlayaparivṛttiśca mukhyata eva pratīṃyata iti vyatyavatī mukhyā nāma parivṛttiriyam /
children.translated_text: Here, in the hero's kingdom, the exchange of fortune between the virtuous and the wicked, and the exchange of dissolution between dharma and adharma, are perceived literally — hence this is <s>parivṛtti</s> of literal exchange (<s>vyatyayavatī mukhyā</s>).
An example of figurative exchange through transposition —
The darkness (blemish) that has been removed from the moon by the fame of King <s>Siṅgabhūpa</s> —

children.text: bhavati hi tadeva lakṣyaṃ vimatakṣitipālavadanakamaleṣu // Ckc_7.*45 //
children.translated_text: that very (darkness) becomes visible in the lotus-faces of the rival kings. // Ckc_7.*45 //

children.text: atra nāyakayaśasāpākṛtasya candrakalaṅkasya virodhinaranāthavadaneṣu lakṣyamāṇatvaṃ tadidamanupapadyamānatayā na mukhyamiti gauṇīyaṃ vyatyayavatī parivṛttiḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the moon's blemish, removed by the hero's fame, being observed in the faces of enemy kings — since this is impossible as a literal fact, this is figurative exchange (<s>gauṇī vyatyayavatī parivṛtti</s>).
An example of literal mutual exchange (<s>vinimaya</s>) —

children.text: śrī siṅgakṣitipālajaitrapaṭahadhvānānu sandhāyino dhāvanto nijarūpagopanakṛte pratyarthipṛthvībhujaḥ /
children.translated_text: The enemy kings, fleeing in pursuit of the sound of King <s>Siṅga</s>'s victory drums, for the purpose of concealing their own identity,

children.text: dattvā vyādhakulāya maṇḍanabharaṃ keyūrahārādikaṃ guñjābījavibhūṣaṇāni vinayātkrīṇanti hīnānyapi // Ckc_7.*46 //
children.translated_text: giving their ornamental load — armlets, necklaces, and the like — to hunter-tribes, humbly purchase even lowly ornaments of <s>Guñjā</s> (Abrus) seeds. // Ckc_7.*46 //

children.text: atra maṇiguñjāvibhūṣaṇayorvinimayayoḥ mukhyatayaiva saṃbhavatīti vinimayavatīyaṃ mukhyā nāma parivṛttiḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the exchange of jewel ornaments for <s>Guñjā</s>-seed ornaments is literally possible — hence this is literal exchange (<s>vinimayavatī mukhyā parivṛtti</s>).
An example of the same, figurative —
O King <s>Siṅgabhūpa</s>, your sword-edge, skilled in the dealings of the crooked (or: in transactions with enemies),
having given trembling to the enemy kings, takes away the prosperity of their seven-limbed kingdom. // Ckc_7.*47 //

children.text: atra nāyakakhaḍge ripubhūpatīṃnāṃ svakampapradānaṃ tebhyaḥ saptāṅgarājyaśriyāmādānaṃ ca mukhyā vṛttyā na saṃbhavatīti gauṇavinimayā nāma parivṛttiḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the hero's sword giving its own trembling to the enemy kings and taking from them the prosperity of the seven-limbed kingdom — this is not literally possible, hence this is figurative mutual exchange (<s>gauṇavinimayā parivṛtti</s>).

children.text: dṛṣṭāntaḥ proktasiddhayai yaḥ siddher'the sā nidarśanā /
children.translated_text: An example used for proving what was stated — when the proof is for the stated purpose — that is <s>nidarśanā</s> (illustration).
It is considered by the wise to be of three kinds, according to whether (the illustration is) prior, subsequent, or simultaneous. // Ckc_7.25 //
Of these, prior illustration (<s>pūrvā nidarśanā</s>) —
Wicked men, when they are royal favorites, commit the utmost cruelty against others.
This sword of King <s>Siṅgabhūpa</s> cuts only the vital points of the enemy. // Ckc_7.*48 //

children.text: atra rājavallabhakrūrajanadṛṣṭāntasya pūrvamuktatvāt pūrvā nāma nidarśanā /
children.translated_text: Here, since the illustration of cruel persons who are royal favorites is stated first, this is called prior illustration (<s>pūrvā nidarśanā</s>).
An example of subsequent (illustration) —
The bow of King <s>Siṅgabhūpa</s> inflicts destruction upon the lives of adversaries.
The attachment of the crooked to the royal ear (court) is for causing pain to others — even when they bow. // Ckc_7.*49 //
Here, since the account of crooked people near the king is stated afterwards, this is subsequent illustration (<s>uttarā nidarśanā</s>).
An example of simultaneous (illustration) —

On earth, ascending from the braid of the <s>Mandākinī</s> (heavenly Ganges) who bows at the courtyard of the sky-woman, it ascends the fragrance of the assembly of those born from the lotus (<s>Brahmā</s>'s assembly).

children.text: śrī siṅgakṣitipālakīrtilatikā tatsaṃśrayāṇāṃ nṛṇāṃ śaṃsatyadbhatamuttarottaratayā jātānubandhodayām // Ckc_7.*50 //
children.translated_text: The creeper of fame of King <s>Siṅga</s> proclaims, wonderfully, to those men who depend on him, a continuously ascending growth. // Ckc_7.*50 //

children.text: atra nāyakaparigraheṇottarottarodayavataḥ kīrtidṛṣṭāntasya nāyakāśritajanottarottaraunnatyalakṣaṇadārṣṭāntikasya ca śaṃsantīti vartamānalakṣaṇaśatra samakālamevoktatvādiyaṃ samā nāma nidarśanā /
children.translated_text: Here, the illustration of fame with its ever-ascending growth through the hero's patronage, and the illustrated (point of) the ever-ascending prosperity of those who depend on the hero — since both are stated at the same time (indicated by the present tense 'proclaims'), this is called simultaneous illustration (<s>samā nidarśanā</s>).

children.text: kathite vā pratīte vā sādṛśye vastunor dvayoḥ /
children.translated_text: When the similarity of two things is either stated or understood,
the declaration of difference is (called) <s>bheda</s> (differentiation); and it is also known as <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast). // Ckc_7.26 //
Here, an example of contrast with one's own kind, where similarity is stated (<s>kathitasādṛśya-svajātīya-vyatireka</s>) —

children.text: śrī siṅgabhūmipatinā na tulāṃ prayānti viśrāṇanakratubhuvo 'pi pare narendrāḥ /
children.translated_text: Other kings, even those who perform the sacrifice of gift-giving, do not equal King <s>Siṅgabhūpa</s> in the balance.

children.text: nandanti tehi viduṣāṃ kavitāvilāsaiḥ so 'yaṃ pratinandayati ca prakāmam // Ckc_7.*51 //
children.translated_text: For they delight scholars with poetic compositions; but he delights them abundantly and also reciprocates (with poetic compositions of his own). // Ckc_7.*51 //

children.text: atra nāyakasya sajātīyaiḥ narendraissaha vitaraṇe sādṛśyamabhidhāya pratiprīṇanahetubhūtakavitāvilāsaviśeṣakathanādayaṃ yathektaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, having stated the similarity between the hero and other kings of his own kind in the matter of generosity, the statement of the specific difference — that his poetic compositions reciprocally delight — makes this contrast as described.
The same (contrast), where similarity is understood (rather than stated) —

children.text: śrī siṅgabhūpa bhavadīyaparigraheṇa dharmāya yadbalavate kavireṣa bhītaḥ /
children.translated_text: O King <s>Siṅgabhūpa</s>, through your patronage, this poet is emboldened for the sake of dharma;

children.text: krītādibandhumuṣitā ca dadāti bhāgau tatte tulāṃ na dadhate prathame narendrāḥ // Ckc_7.*52 //
children.translated_text: and (dharma, personified as) she whose kinsmen were stolen gives back (their) shares — those first among kings do not equal you in the balance. // Ckc_7.*52 //

children.text: atra rakatvena (?) tretādvāparamahīnāthajātisāmye pratīte nāyakasya tadrājyacoritadhamabhāvapratyarpaṇapārabhūta paripālanaviśeṣabhedakathanādayaṃ pratītasādṛśyasajātīyavyatirekaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, with the similarity understood between the hero and the rulers of the <s>Tretā</s> and <s>Dvāpara</s> ages (who are of the same class of kings), the statement of the hero's specific difference — that he restores and protects the dharma stolen by the rulers of those earlier kingdoms — makes this a contrast of one's own kind where the similarity is understood.
An example of contrast with one's own individual, where similarity is stated —

children.text: śrī siṅgabhūpāla bhavān doṣā bhāve bhavāniva /
children.translated_text: O King <s>Siṅgabhūpa</s>, you (at one time) — and faults in (your present) state are like you (then) —
by <s>Śrī</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), indeed, you are [surpassed by] none other than yourself, daily increasing. // Ckc_7.*53 //

children.text:
atra nāyakasya doṣābhāve svenaiva tulyatāmabhidhāya pratyahaṃ vardhamānayā turagādisaṃpadā svasyaiva svato pratidināpekṣayā viśeṣakathanādayaṃ kathitasādṛśye svavyaktivyatirekaḥ /
yadi pratīyamānasādṛśye svavyaktivyatirekasyodāharaṇaṃ saṃbhavati cārutāṃ puṣṇāti vā tadapi nirūpaṇīyam /

children.translated_text: <s>Ekavyatireka</s> (single contrast) in stated resemblance is as follows:
"O <s>Śrīsiṅgadharaṇīpāla</s>, ocean of compassion!
How can <s>Jīmūtavāhana</s>, a non-giver, be your equal?" // Ckc_7.*54 //

Here, since there is no fault in the hero, having stated his equality with himself alone, by the daily increasing prosperity of horses etc. — the stating of the hero's superiority over his own [past] self from a day-to-day perspective — this is <s>svavyakti-vyatireka</s> (self-individual-contrast) in stated resemblance. If an example of self-individual-contrast in perceived resemblance is possible and nourishes beauty, that too should be examined.

Here, of the hero and the <s>Vidyādhara</s> prince (<s>Jīmūtavāhana</s>), whose resemblance is stated through being treasuries of compassion, the distinguishing quality is mentioned only in the latter — thus this is as described.
<s>Ubhayavyatireka</s> (double contrast) in stated resemblance is as follows — in the hero's genealogy:

children.text: saudaryo balabhadramūrtiraniśaṃ devī priyā rukmiṇī pradyumrastanayo 'pi pautranivaho yasyāniruddhādayaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Brotherhood with <s>Balabhadra</s>'s form, his beloved consort <s>Rukmiṇī</s>, his son <s>Pradyumna</s> too, his grandson-host including <s>Aniruddha</s> —

children.text: soyaṃ śrīpatirannavotanṛpatiḥ kiṃ tvānanāmbhoruhe dhatte cāru sudarśanaśriyamasau sarvātma hastāmbuje // Ckc_7.*55 //
children.translated_text: this <s>Śrīpati</s> (husband of <s>Lakṣmī</s>), King <s>Annavota</s>; but on his lotus-face he bears the beauty of <s>Sudarśana</s> (the discus), while that one [<s>Viṣṇu</s>] [bears it] in the lotus of his hand." // Ckc_7.*55 //

children.text: atra balabhadrasaudaryatvādibhirabhihitasādṛśyayoḥ nāyakarusmiṇīnāyakayoḥ sudarśanamukhatvaṃ, sudarśanakaratvaṃ cedubhayagatabhedakadharmakathanādayaṃ kathitasādṛśya ubhayavyatirekaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, of the hero and the lord of <s>Rukmiṇī</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), whose resemblance is stated through brotherhood with <s>Balabhadra</s> etc., the distinguishing qualities stated for both — having <s>Sudarśana</s> on the face vs. having <s>Sudarśana</s> in the hand — this is double contrast in stated resemblance.
<s>Ekavyatireka</s> (single contrast) in perceived resemblance is as follows:
"Making friend into foe, occupied with devouring the twice-born king —
how can <s>Rāhu</s> be a standard of comparison for the sword-edge of <s>Śrīsiṅganṛpāla</s>?" // Ckc_7.*56 //

children.text: atra vivaṇātvena (?) pratītasāmyayoḥ saihikeyakakaukṣeyakayoḥ pūrvatraiva bhedakadharmakathanādayaṃ yathoktaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, of <s>Svarbhānu</s>'s son (<s>Rāhu</s>) and the hero's sword, whose similarity is perceived through their darkening [nature], the distinguishing quality is mentioned only in the first — thus this is as described.
Double contrast in perceived resemblance is as follows:
"<s>Siṅgabhūpati</s> — presiding over all enjoyments, sleepless;
<s>Nīrajāvara</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>) — presiding over the enjoyments of <s>Śeṣa</s> [only], drowsy." // Ckc_7.*57 //

Here, of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and the hero, whose resemblance is perceived through their consecration to protecting the world, the distinguishing qualities stated for both — this is double contrast in perceived resemblance.
Contrast with a similar [standard] (<s>sadṛśavyatireka</s>) in stated resemblance is as follows:
"The royal mountain and the king of gods' mountain — both auspicious, both sheltering;

children.text: ayaṃ śrī siṅgabhūpena rājate na tu vajriṇā // Ckc_7.*58 //
children.translated_text: this one is resplendent with <s>Śrīsiṅgabhūpa</s>, but not the other with <s>Vajrin</s> (<s>Indra</s>)." // Ckc_7.*58 //

children.text: atra kathitasāmyayoḥ śailayoḥ pratīyamānasādṛśyābhyāmeva nāyakatridivanāyakābhyāṃ bhedakathanādayaṃ tathoktaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, of the two mountains whose similarity is stated, through the perceived resemblances with the hero and the lord of heaven respectively, the distinction is stated — thus it is so described.
Contrast with a dissimilar [standard] (<s>visadṛśavyatireka</s>) in stated resemblance is as follows:
"Of the directional elephants and King <s>Siṅga</s>, both born for the welfare of the world, assuredly;
yet in their elephant-nature, those are blind with rut, while in his lineage-eminence, this one is free from pride." // Ckc_7.*59 //

children.text: atra lokahitatvena dikkuñjarāṇāṃ nāyakakuñjarasya ca sāmyamabhidhāya sadṛśābhyomeva mātaṅgatvavaṃśonnatibhyāṃ madāndhatvanirgarvatvābhyāṃ ca bhedakathanādayaṃ kathitasādṛśyo visadṛśavyatirekaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, having stated the similarity of the directional elephants and the hero's elephant through welfare of the world, the distinction is stated through their own shared features — elephant-nature and lineage-eminence — paired with rut-blindness and freedom from pride. This is dissimilar contrast in stated resemblance.
Contrast with a similar [standard] in perceived resemblance is as follows:
"The lord of waters shines with effortless, pure jewels;
this <s>Śrīsiṅgabhūpāla</s> [shines] with qualities mixed with purity." // Ckc_7.*60 //

children.text: atra gambhīratvādinā pratītasāmyayornāyakanadīnāyakayoḥ kathitasādṛśyai reva ratnairguṇaiśca bhedakathanādayaṃ tathoktaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, of the hero and the lord of rivers, whose similarity is perceived through depth and the like, the distinction is stated precisely through the similar [features]: jewels and qualities — thus it is so described.
Dissimilar contrast in perceived resemblance is as follows:

children.text: nidrālau śrutivarjite viṣamukhe vakrāṃ dadhāne satīṃ śeṣe nūnamapāyaśaṅkihṛdayā sthātuṃ samudveginīm /
children.translated_text: "On <s>Śeṣa</s>, who is drowsy, deaf, poison-mouthed, holding a crooked faithful one [on his coils], the earth remains with a heart apprehensive of danger, anxious;

children.text: nistandre viśadaśrutau suvadane vakretarādhvakrame śrī siṅgakṣitipālake vasumatī yāti pratiṣṭhā parām // Ckc_7.*61 //
children.translated_text: on <s>Śrīsiṅgakṣitipālaka</s>, who is sleepless, of clear hearing, fair-faced, on the straight path — the earth attains supreme stability." // Ckc_7.*61 //

Here, of <s>Śeṣa</s> and the distinguished hero, whose similarity is perceived through knowledge and bearing the earth, the dissimilar distinguishing qualities — drowsiness vs. sleeplessness, etc. — being stated, this is dissimilar contrast in perceived resemblance.
Thus some varieties of <s>vyatireka</s> (contrast) have been demonstrated;
by this very path, the discerning should themselves infer others. // Ckc_7.27 //

children.text:
kiñcidārabhyamāṇena kāryaṃ tatsahakāriṇaḥ /
ākasmikasya saṃprāṣtessamāhitamitīhitam // Ckc_7.28 //
children.translated_text: <s>Samāhita</s> (coincidence) is when something begun by a particular agent is accomplished by a cooperating agent — an accidental one that has arrived. // Ckc_7.28 //
Divine (<s>daivika</s>) coincidence is as follows:

children.text: śrī siṅgakṣitipālasainikabhiyā bhūbhṛdguhāgāhināṃ kāntāreṣu cikīṣaṃtā nijapadaprastārasaṃmārjanām /
children.translated_text: "The enemies of <s>Śrīsiṅgakṣitipāla</s>, entering mountain caves out of fear of his soldiers, wishing to sweep away the trail of their own footsteps in the wilderness —

children.text: nirvyūḍhā sahakāritā vidhivaśādasmākamākasmikaiḥ kulyākṣāsalitakandarā parisaraprāraṃbhamaṃbhodharaiḥ // Ckc_7.*62 //
children.translated_text: that cooperation was accomplished, as if by fate, through accidental rain-clouds flooding the ravine-slopes with torrents of water." // Ckc_7.*62 //

children.text: atra palāyamānamārgeṣu nijapadapaṅktimārjanacikīrṣūṇāṃ nāyakavirodhināmākasmikavarṣeṇa tatsuniṣpannamiti daivikaṃ samāhitam /
children.translated_text: Here, the accidental rain accomplishing what the hero's fleeing enemies wished — the sweeping of their footprint-trails on the escape routes — is divine coincidence.
Non-divine (<s>adaivika</s>) coincidence is as follows:
"By the custom of the first awakening of the rainy season, on the pretext of <s>Lakṣmī's</s> smile-flash abandoning sleeplessness from the mind of [<s>Viṣṇu</s>] the enemy of demons,

children.text: daityārerupakārakāraṇatayā jāgarti jāgraddhiyā śrī siṅgasya vibho rdigantavijayaprasthānabherīdhvaniḥ // Ckc_7.*63 //
children.translated_text: as a contributing cause for the assistance of the demon-foe, the battle-drum-sound of the march-of-conquest-to-the-horizons of the mighty Lord <s>Śrīsiṅga</s> keeps him awake with wakeful intellect." // Ckc_7.*63 //

children.text: atra nidrāvyājena lakṣmīgāḍhāliṅganasya śaithilyaṃ cikīrṣatā bhagavatā lavdhasya padmālayātaṅkahetutayā sahakāriṇo nāyakasannāhanissāṇarāṇasya pauruṣeyatayā tadidamadaivikaṃ samāhitam /
children.translated_text: Here, when the Lord (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), under the pretext of sleep, wished to loosen the tight embrace of <s>Lakṣmī</s>, and obtained as a cooperating cause — being a cause of <s>Lakṣmī's</s> alarm — the hero's war-drum sounding for campaign: since this is of human origin, it is non-divine coincidence.
<s>Bhrānti</s> (illusion) is erroneous cognition, arising from latent impressions or from similarity;
it is of two kinds: <s>ālambanavatī</s> (with a substrate) and <s>anālambanavatī</s> (without a substrate). // Ckc_7.29 //
With a substrate (<s>ālambanavatī</s>) is as follows:

children.text: autsukyādanavotasiṅganṛpaterākāramālikhya sā nirvarṇyāyamasau mama priya iti premābhiyogabhramāt /
children.translated_text: Having drawn the form of King <s>Anavotasiṅga</s> out of eagerness, examining it — "This is my very beloved!" — through the delusion of love's importunity,

children.text: āśuddhāya tatopasṛtya tarasā kiñcidvivṛttānanā sānūnaṃ sadarasmitaṃ sacakitaṃ sākāṅkṣamālokate // Ckc_7.*64 //
children.translated_text: quickly rising and approaching swiftly, with face slightly turned, she gazes with jealousy, with gentle smiles, with startled looks, with longing. // Ckc_7.*64 //

children.text: atra nāyakānuraktāyāḥ kasyāścinnāyakacitre ayaṃ sākṣānnāyaka iti pratīteḥ seyaṃ satatanāyakānudhyānavāsanābalena citrastha nāyakākāramālambya jāyata iti saṃskārajā sālambā nāmabhrāntiriyam /
