children.translated_text: Here, a certain woman devoted to the hero, perceiving in the hero's portrait: "This is the hero in person" — this [illusion] arises by the force of the latent impression of constant meditation on the hero, taking the hero's form depicted in the painting as its substrate. Thus this is <s>bhrānti</s> (illusion) with a substrate, born from latent impressions.
Without a substrate (<s>nirālambā</s>) is as follows:

children.text: prācaṇḍyaṃ pratigaṇḍabhairavavibhoralokya yuddhāṅgaṇe dāvanto girikandarāparisaraṃ pratyarthipṛthvībhujaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Seeing the ferocity that rivals dread <s>Bhairava</s> in the battle-arena, the enemy kings flee toward the mountain-cave environs;

children.text: doruddhūtakarālakhaḍgalatikāvyagraṃ tamevāntike prartyādra pratipādapaṃ pratidiśaṃ paśyanti paryākulāḥ // Ckc_7.*65 //
children.translated_text: they see him — the very same one, busy with the terrible sword-creeper brandished by his arm — near them, at every step, in every direction, and become utterly confused." // Ckc_7.*65 //

children.text: atra raṇamukhe tādṛśapracaṇḍimānusandhāyakaṃ nāyakaṃ sākṣātkṛtavatāṃ dviṣatā mavigatena vāsanābalena nāyakasādṛśyālambanaṃ vināpi śailādiṣu yā nayakādipratītiḥ seyaṃ nirālaṃbanā nāma saṃskārato bhrāntiḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the enemies who had directly witnessed such ferocity of the hero on the battlefield — by the force of their unabated latent impression, even without a substrate resembling the hero in mountains etc. — the perception of the hero [everywhere] is <s>nirālambā bhrānti</s> (substrateless illusion) arising from latent impressions.
The second [type] should be known by the learned as also of two kinds:

children.text: atattave tattvarūpā ca tattve cātattvarūpiṇī // Ckc_7.30 //
children.translated_text: <s>atattve tattvarūpā</s> (perceiving truth in the untrue) and <s>tattve atattvarūpiṇī</s> (perceiving untruth in the true). // Ckc_7.30 //
The first is as follows:

children.text: nartuṃ vāñchati dhūrjaṭiḥ phaṇadharāstiṣṭhanti paryantataḥ pratyuttiṣṭhati jāhnavī na sahate mānāgrahaṃ māninī /
children.translated_text: "<s>Dhūrjaṭi</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) wishes to dance, the serpents stand around, the <s>Ganges</s> rises up, the proud lady [<s>Pārvatī</s>] cannot bear the slight of pride,

children.text: serṣyaṃ paśyati pārvatī kamalabhūrāliṅgituṃ ceṣṭate śrī siṅgakṣitināthakīrtimahimanyāścaryadhuryodaye // Ckc_7.*66 //
children.translated_text: <s>Pārvatī</s> looks with jealousy, <s>Brahmā</s> the lotus-born endeavors to embrace — [all this] in the wondrous, supreme manifestation of the fame-glory of <s>Śrīsiṅgakṣitinātha</s>." // Ckc_7.*66 //

children.text: atra sadṛśadhāvalyena yatprāleyaśailādirūpe nāyakayaśasi tattadrūpatayā pratibhānaṃ seyamatattve tattvarūpā bhrāntiḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the perception that the hero's fame, in its form of the snow-mountain etc. due to similar whiteness, is actually that [mountain etc.] — this is <s>bhrānti</s> that perceives truth in the untrue (<s>atattve tattvarūpā</s>).
The second is as follows:

children.text: tṛṣṇākrāntā jalamiti dhiyā saṃplave bhānubhāsāṃ dhāvaṃ dhāvaṃ dhavaladhavalaṃ dhānvinīṣu sthalīṣu /
children.translated_text: "Seized by thirst, thinking it water, running and running through the bright white desert expanses in the flood of sunbeams,

children.text: kṣāmakṣāmā ripunṛpatayaḥ siṅgabhūpāladhāṭyāṃ satyākārānapi na payasāṃ viśvasanti sma kūpān // Ckc_7.*67 //
children.translated_text: emaciated and exhausted, the enemy kings in the campaign of <s>Siṅgabhūpāla</s> do not trust even wells that have the appearance of real water." // Ckc_7.*67 //

children.text: atra bahuśo mṛgatṛṣṇikāpratāritānāṃ nāyakaparipanthināṃ pāramārthikeṣvapi jaleṣu na jalānīti yā pratipattiḥ seyaṃ tattvepyatattvarūpā bhrāntiḥ sādaśyajanitā bhrāntiḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the perception of the hero's adversaries — who have been repeatedly deceived by mirages — that even real waters are 'not water': this is <s>bhrānti</s> that perceives untruth in the true (<s>tattve atattvarūpā</s>), born from similarity.

children.text: bhrānteḥ paraṃparā bhrānteḥṛ śruṅkhalā ityubhe ime /
children.translated_text: The chain (<s>paramparā</s>) of illusions and the linked series (<s>śṛṅkhalā</s>) of illusions — these two

children.text: bhrānteḥ pṛthagiti jñānaṃ bhrāntireveti me matam // Ckc_7.31 //
children.translated_text: are, in my view, varieties of <s>bhrānti</s> (illusion) itself, not separate [from it]. // Ckc_7.31 //
Here, the chain of illusions (<s>bhrāntiparamparā</s>) is as follows:

children.text: śākhāsu prasavāśayā kṣitiruhāṃ karpūrakhaṃḍāśayā peṭīkāmudareṣu mohanavidherante duklāśayā /
children.translated_text: "In the branches of trees, thinking [they are] flowers; in camphor-pieces, thinking [they are] gems; in the bellies of boxes, thinking [it is] the enchantment-powder of the god of love; in the interior of garments —

children.text: śrīsiṅgakṣitināyakendra bhavato gṛhṇanti siddhāṅganāḥ lokālokadarīparīsahabhuvāmākalpakalpaṃ yaśaḥ // Ckc_7.*68 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Śrīsiṅgakṣitināyakendra</s>, the <s>Siddha</s>-women grasp your fame for cosmic cycles upon cosmic cycles, in the caverns of the <s>Lokāloka</s> mountain!" // Ckc_7.*68 //

children.text: atra siddhāṅganānāṃ bahuśo mālākrameṇa nāyakayaśasi jāyamānā prasavādibhrāntireva brāntiparaṃparetyucyate /
children.translated_text: Here, the illusions arising in the <s>Siddha</s>-women's [perception] of the hero's fame — as flowers, etc. — repeatedly in a garland-like sequence, are called the chain of illusions.
The linked series of illusions (<s>bhrāntiśṛṅkhalā</s>) is as follows:

children.text: brahmā haṃsadhiyānurajyati nabhogaṅgādhiyā te khagāḥ kṣīrāṃbhodhidhiyā ca sā taṭavatī jyotsnādhiyā cāmbudhiḥ /
children.translated_text: "<s>Brahmā</s>, thinking it a swan, is attracted; the sky-birds, thinking it the celestial <s>Ganges</s>; and that shore-land, thinking it the Milk Ocean; and the ocean, thinking it moonlight;

children.text: sā kāntiḥ śaradindumaṇḍaladhiyā tvatkīrtimavyāhatāṃ śrī siṅgakṣitinātha sādhujanatāsaṃkalpakalpadruma // Ckc_7.*69 //
children.translated_text: that radiance, thinking it the disk of the autumn moon — O <s>Śrīsiṅgakṣitinātha</s>, [they thus perceive] your unobstructed fame, O wish-fulfilling tree of the good!" // Ckc_7.*69 //

children.text: atra bhrāntīnāmuttarottaraṃ śṛṅkhalānyāyeṃna saṃkalanādiyaṃ bhrāntiḥ śṛṅkhalā nāma bhrāntereva bhedaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the illusions are linked one after another in a chain-like fashion — this variety of <s>bhrānti</s> is called the linked series of illusions.

children.text: ūhā vitarkaḥ sa dvedhā nirṇayānirṇayāvadhiḥ // Ckc_7.32 //
children.translated_text: <s>Ūhā</s> (conjecture) is speculation; it is of two kinds: ending in a conclusion and not ending in a conclusion. // Ckc_7.32 //
Here, the one ending in a conclusion is as follows:

children.text: asau kiṃ kandarpaḥ kimayamamareśānatanayaḥ kimeṣaḥ śrīrāmaḥ kimayamalakānāyakasutaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Is that <s>Kandarpa</s> (the god of love)? Is this the son of the lord of the immortals? Is this <s>Śrīrāma</s>? Is this the son of the chief of <s>Alakas</s> (i.e. <s>Nalakūbara</s>)?

children.text: sakhi jñātaṃ so 'yaṃ yuvatinayanotpādakaphalaṃ nidhānaṃ bhāgyānāṃ jayati khalu siṅgakṣitipatiḥ // Ckc_7.*70 //
children.translated_text: O friend, I know! This is he — the fruit that produced the eyes of young women, the treasury of good fortunes — victorious indeed is <s>Siṅgakṣitipati</s>!" // Ckc_7.*70 //

children.text: atra kandarpādivitarkānantaraṃ so 'yaṃ nāyaka iti nirṇayakathanādayaṃ tathoktaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, after the speculations about <s>Kandarpa</s> and others, the conclusion stating 'this is the hero' — this is as described.
The one not ending in a conclusion is as follows:

children.text: saṃvartapāvakaśikhā kimi kinnu jihvā mṛtyoriyaṃ kimu yugāntakṛtāntadaṃṣṭrā /
children.translated_text: "Is this a flame of the fire of cosmic dissolution? Is this a tongue of Death? Is this the fang of the Destroyer at the end of the age?" —

children.text: ityūhyate samarasīmani vairisainyaiḥ śrī siṅgabhūpakarakampitakhaḍgarekhā // Ckc_7.*71 //
children.translated_text: thus is it speculated on the border of the battlefield by the enemy army — the sword-line trembling in the hand of <s>Śrīsiṅgabhūpa</s>. // Ckc_7.*71 //

children.text: atra kimidaṃ kimidamiti vitarkayatā vimatasainyena seyaṃ nāyakakhaḍgadhāreti nirṇayākathanādayaṃ tathoktaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the enemy army, speculating 'is it this? is it that?' — without arriving at the conclusion 'this is the hero's sword-edge' — thus this is as described.

children.text: vastvantareṇa sthaganaṃ vastuno mīlitaṃ matam // Ckc_7.33 //
children.translated_text: The concealment of a thing by another thing is considered <s>mīlita</s> (concealment). // Ckc_7.33 //
For example:

children.text: nityaṃ śrīanavotasiṅganṛpateraśrāntaviśrāṇana- ślāghāślokakṛtā ca dānarasike nākaukasāṃ nāyake /
children.translated_text: "At King <s>Anavotasiṅga's</s> tireless, ceaseless distribution, [celebrated] in laudatory verses made by the panegyrists of generosity, with the celestial lord as leader in the enjoyment of giving —

children.text: svardhenorvadane nisarganamanāllajjānatirgopyate mandārasya ca bāṣpa vindupaṭalaṃ ścyotanmadhūlīkaṇaiḥ // Ckc_7.*72 //
children.translated_text: the wish-fulfilling cow's natural head-bowing out of shame is concealed by her natural dripping of milk-drops, and the <s>mandāra</s> tree's teardrops are concealed by its naturally oozing honey-drops." // Ckc_7.*72 //

children.text: atra nāyakavitaraṇaślāghayāḥ parābhūtayoḥ kāmadhenukalpavṛkṣayor jāyamānalajjānatibāṣpapūrāḥ svabhāvamukhāvanatipuṣparasābhyāṃ sthagitamiti mīlitamidam /
children.translated_text: Here, the bowing of shame and the flood of tears arising in the wish-fulfilling cow and the wish-tree, humiliated by the praise of the hero's generosity, are concealed by their natural head-lowering and flower-nectar respectively — this is <s>mīlita</s> (concealment).
Its varieties are: concealment by similarity, concealment by quality, and concealment by non-quality. // Ckc_7.34 //
There, [concealment by] similarity (<s>sāmānya</s>) is as follows:

children.text: raicarlīyakulāvataṃsa nṛpate haṃsāḥ praśaṃsānidhe śliṣṭadravyavivekino vijahati prāvīṇyagarvaṃ nijam /
children.translated_text: "O <s>Raicarlīya</s> clan-ornament king, treasury of praise! The swans, discriminators of mixed substances, abandon their own pride of expertise;

children.text: vaktrāntādgalitānmṛṇālakabalān kīlau tava brāhnaṇī prāptādvaitakathānmanāgapi paricchettuṃ cirādakṣamāḥ // Ckc_7.*73 //
children.translated_text: the morsels of lotus-stalks fallen from the inner mouth — O <s>Brāhmaṇī</s> (crane) — unable even slightly to distinguish [them] for a long time from the tales of non-duality [your fame presents]." // Ckc_7.*73 //

children.text: atra kīrtimṛṇālayorekatvarūpaṃ sāmānyamapi sadṛśena sadṛśasthaganamiti mīritameva /
children.translated_text: Here, even though the oneness-form of fame and lotus-stalks constitutes similarity, the concealment of the similar by the similar is indeed <s>mīlita</s> (concealment by similarity).
<s>Pihita</s> (concealment [by quality]) is as follows:

children.text: kasyāśicitkuca maṇḍale navavayomattebhakumbhadvaye dṛṣṭiṃ rāgataraṅgitāṃ vidadhatā śrīsiṅgabhūmībhujā /
children.translated_text: By King <s>Śrī Siṅgabhūmībhuj</s>, casting a glance rippling with passion upon the breast-mounds of a certain woman — (mounds) like the frontal globes of a young elephant intoxicated with fresh youth,

children.text: dākṣiṇyavratabhaṅgabhīrumanasā devena vāmabhruvā- manyāsāmapi sā tathaiva kṛtinā netrendriyeṇārpitā // Ckc_7.*74 //
children.translated_text: by that skillful god, whose mind feared the breaking of his vow of gallantry, that same (glance) was bestowed through the sense-organ of the eye upon the other side-glancing women as well. // Ckc_7.*74 //

children.text:
atra prakaṭitasnehāṃ preyakīṃ paśyato nāyakasya yadanyāsvapi tathāvidhakaṭākṣavyāpāriṇa svakīyabhāvaka prakhyākachākavihitaṃ [bhāvapracchādanaṃ vihitaṃ (?)] tadidaṃ pihitamiti kecidācakṣate /
tadapi sahajānu rāgadṛṣṭivyāpārasya sādhitānurāgadṛṣṭivyāpāreṇa sthaganamiti mīlitameva /
children.translated_text: Here, when the hero gazes upon the beloved (<s>preyasī</s>) who has openly displayed her affection, his directing the same kind of sidelong glance at the other women as well — the concealment of his own disposition effected through a transparent pretext [the concealment of his emotion (?)] — some call this <s>pihita</s> (hidden). But even that, being the concealment of the natural activity of a passion-filled glance by the activity of a cultivated affectionate glance, is actually <s>mīlita</s> (veiling) itself.
An example of the same with a qualifying attribute (<s>tadguṇa</s>) —

children.text: patraprāyalatāpratāna kṛtā nikuñjaiḥ palaśottare (?) svacchāsu sphaṭikasthalīṣu dhavalakṣoṇīrajolepanāḥ /
children.translated_text: In thickets formed mostly of leaf-covered creeper-branches, in clearings beyond the <s>palāśa</s> trees (?), on crystalline ground-surfaces smeared with white earth-dust,

children.text: śoṇagrāvasu gairikendradayujo vidveṣiṇastatkṣaṇāt lakṣyante na hi siṅgabhūpaticamūnāsīradhāṭībhaṭaiḥ // Ckc_7.*75 //
children.translated_text: on red rocks mixed with red ochre and indigo — the enemies are not at all detected in that instant by the soldiers of the vanguard battalions of King <s>Siṅgabhūpati</s>'s army. // Ckc_7.*75 //

children.text: atra nāyakadveṣiṇāṃ nikuñjāpuñjādiguṇasamā śrayaṇena sthagitamiti tadguṇamīlitameva /
children.translated_text: Here, the concealment of the hero's enemies by taking shelter in the qualities of the thickets and other (surroundings) — this being concealment through (matching) attributes — is <s>tadguṇa-mīlita</s> (attribute-matching veiling) itself.

children.text: siṅgakṣmāpatikīrtibhirdhavalite lokatraye svaprabhoḥ kaṇṭhena vyatikālakūṭaghaṭanājīrṇena hṛṣṭā gaṇāḥ /
children.translated_text: When the three worlds are whitened by the fame of King <s>Siṅga</s>, the <s>gaṇas</s> (attendants of Śiva) are delighted that their lord's throat, worn out by the effects of the <s>kālakūṭa</s> poison, (is now concealed);

children.text: varṇe 'pi pratikūlatāṃ vijaharī patyuḥ priyā pārvatī pūrṇendor api mudritā janatayā rūḍhā kalaṅkaprathā // Ckc_7.*76 //
children.translated_text: the beloved <s>Pārvatī</s> sports indifference even to the complexion of her husband; and even of the full moon, the spread of the blemish-reputation is sealed away by the people. // Ckc_7.*76 //

children.text:
atrātadguṇānāmapi kālakaṇṭha.... ....yadvikārā viṣkaraṇaṃ so 'yamatadguṇa iti vyācakṣate /
tadasmin mate 'pi kriyākāraṇānāmasāmarthyādahetvalaṅkāra eva /
children.translated_text: Here, even of those possessing non-matching attributes (<s>atadguṇa</s>), the blue-throated one (<s>Kālakaṇṭha</s>, i.e. <s>Śiva</s>)... ...the manifestation of whose transformation — some explain this as <s>atadguṇa</s> (non-matching attribute veiling). But even in this view, due to the incapacity of the causes of the described actions, this is merely the ornament of <s>ahetu</s> (false cause).
The cognition of a previously experienced object from something similar is considered <s>smaraṇa</s> (recollection). // Ckc_7.35 //
As follows:

children.text: saṃtrāsādupavindhyakānanabilaiḥ paryantaniryanmadhu- srotaskā parilokya gaṇḍadṛṣado vyāmāvakāśaspṛśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Seeing in the sub-<s>Vindhya</s> forest-caverns — from which honey-streams flow out at the edges in terror — the cheek-boulders that reach the span of a <s>vyāma</s> (fathom),

children.text: uddaṇḍapratigaṇjabhairavahṛtāḥ pratyarthibhiḥ pārthivaiḥ smaryante nijagandhabandhuraghaṭāḥ tṛṭyatkaṭagranthayaḥ // Ckc_7.*77 //
children.translated_text: the rival kings recall their own elephants — seized by the fierce <s>Uddaṇḍa-pratigaṇja-Bhairava</s> (King Siṅga) — with their fragrant temples and oozing <s>mada</s> (rut-fluid) knotting at the cheeks. // Ckc_7.*77 //

children.text: atra gaṇḍaśailadarśanena tatsadṛśānāṃ nāyakāpahṛtānāṃ nijagajendrāṇāṃ yā smṛtisso 'yaṃ smṛtyalaṅkāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the recollection of their own lordly elephants — which resemble those cheek-boulders and were seized by the hero — triggered by the sight of the cheek-rocks: this is the ornament of <s>smṛti</s> (recollection).
Activity in accordance with one's intention is called <s>bhāva</s> (disposition). // Ckc_7.36 //
As follows:
By King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>, the learned sovereign, who desires to join the beauty of gracefulness to the limbs of the world through each and every method of art,

children.text: yadyatsaṃvihitaṃ raho vitanute tattatpratīpakramaṃ, prajñāśītavatī vivekacaturā kācitkuraṅgekṣaṇā // Ckc_7.*78 //
children.translated_text: whatever he arranges in private — a certain doe-eyed woman, cool with wisdom and clever with discrimination, undoes all of that in reverse order. // Ckc_7.*78 //

children.text: atra nāyakasya yo 'yaṃ sauṣṭhavopadeśapravṛttiḥ tayorpaṭadvayoranyonyasparśanasukhopameya prāyādityayaṃ bhāvālaṅkāraḥ
children.translated_text: Here, the hero's activity of instructing in gracefulness — the delight of mutual contact between the two, like two pieces of cloth (touching), being primarily comparable (to the pretext) — this is the ornament of <s>bhāva</s> (disposition).
And as follows:
Desiring to sprinkle the chest (of the hero) with the water of <s>Kalyāṇaśṛṅga</s> (the auspicious peak) during the season of fresh spring festivities,

children.text: atyānatena śirakecchati siṅgabhūpe tanmāninī na vijarāti jahāti bāṣpam // Ckc_7.*79 //
children.translated_text: when King <s>Siṅgabhūpa</s> bends excessively with his head — that proud woman does not remove (the water) but releases tears instead. // Ckc_7.*79 //

children.text: atra vakṣasi salilasekaṃ nāyakaḥ śirasi yatsamīhitavān nāyikayā tatśṛṅgasalilaṃ na muktam kintu bāṣpamiti yattadatra nāyakasya hṛdaye kācidanyā hṛdayavallabhaā vasatīti bhāvaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, when the hero desired to sprinkle water on the chest but (bent his head so that it would fall) on the head instead, the heroine did not release the <s>Śṛṅga</s>-water but shed tears — the underlying sentiment (<s>bhāva</s>) being that some other heart's beloved resides in the hero's heart.
<s>Bhāvapratīpa</s> (contrary disposition) has been shown by others to be merely a variety of <s>bhāva</s> itself.
But in my view, since it has the nature of misapprehension, it is actually <s>bhrānti</s> (delusion). // Ckc_7.37 //

children.text:
yathā atraivodāharaṇe yathā nāyakasyāyamabhiprāyaḥ /
mama hṛdaye sthitāṃ tvāmeva tvaṃ kimiti sektumicchasi /
yadi priye māṃ sektumicchasi tarhi śirasi siñceti /
tadāparasyā sthitiśaṅkayā na sektavyo 'yamiti yo 'yaṃ nāyikāyāḥ pratīptotkaṇṭhāṃ bodhayatītyarthāpattiriyam /
evaṃmitarapramāṇasiddhārthānupapattihetukārthāpattiḥ svayamūhanīyā /
children.translated_text: As follows — in this very illustration: the hero's intention is thus: 'You who are established in my heart — why do you wish to sprinkle (me)? If, O beloved, you wish to sprinkle me, then sprinkle on the head.' Thereupon, suspecting the presence of another woman (in his heart), (the heroine's thought) 'this one should not be sprinkled' — this, which reveals the heroine's contrary longing (<s>pratīpa-utkaṇṭhā</s>), is <s>arthāpatti</s> (presumption). In this manner, <s>arthāpatti</s> — which arises from the impossibility of a fact established by another means of knowledge — should be inferred by the reader on one's own.

children.text: iti sarasasāhityacāturīdhurīṇaviśveśvarakavicandrapraṇītāyāṃ śrī siṅgabhūpālakīrtisudhāsāraśītalāyāṃ camatkāracandrikāyāmalaṅkāraviveko nāma saptamovilāsaḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Camatkāracandrikā</s>, composed by <s>Viśveśvara Kavicandra</s>, who is pre-eminent in the skill of elegant literary art, (a work) cool as the essence of the nectar of the fame of King <s>Śrī Siṅgabhūpāla</s> — (ends) the seventh <s>vilāsa</s> (chapter) named <s>Alaṅkāraviveka</s> (Discrimination of Ornaments).
Eighth <s>vilāsa</s> (chapter)
<s>Camatkāracandrikā</s>, composed by <s>Viśveśvara Kavicandra</s> — eighth <s>vilāsa</s> (chapter).
<s>Ubhayālaṅkāranirūpaṇam</s> (Examination of Ornaments Common to Both Word and Meaning)
From words such as 'iva' (like) and others, when <s>upamā</s> (simile) and other (figures) are perceived

children.text: viśiṣṭārthaḥ kavīnāṃ tā ubhayālaṅkṛtayo matāḥ // Ckc_8.1 //
children.translated_text: as conveying a distinguished meaning — those are considered by poets to be <s>ubhayālaṅkṛti</s> (ornaments of both kinds). // Ckc_8.1 //
<s>Upamā</s> (simile), <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor), <s>sāmya</s> (similarity), <s>saṃśayokti</s> (expression of doubt), <s>apahnutti</s> (denial),
<s>samādhyukti</s> (reconciliatory expression), <s>samāsokti</s> (condensed expression), <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy), <s>prastutastuti</s> (praise of the relevant), // Ckc_8.2 //
<s>tulyayogitā</s> (equal conjunction), <s>sahokti</s> (co-statement), <s>samuccaya</s> (accumulation),
<s>ākṣepa</s> (objection), <s>arthāntaranyāsa</s> (corroboration), <s>viśeṣā</s> (distinction), <s>pariṣkṛti</s> (embellishment), // Ckc_8.3 //
<s>dīpana</s> (illumination), <s>krama</s> (sequence), <s>paryāya</s> (alternation), <s>atiśaya</s> (hyperbole), <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia), <s>bhāvanā</s> (realization),
and <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s> (combination) — these twenty-four have been specified by the learned. // Ckc_8.4 //
Where similarity between two things, in accordance with well-known convention, with respect to a (shared) property,

children.text: pratītaṃ kathitaṃ vā syādarthayorupamā hi sā // Ckc_8.5 //
children.translated_text: is either perceived or stated — that is <s>upamā</s> (simile). // Ckc_8.5 //
This (simile) is of three kinds, through the divisions called <s>pada</s> (word-level), <s>vākya</s> (sentence-level), and <s>prapañca</s> (elaborate);

children.text: padopamā dvidhā tatra samāsāt pratyayādapi // Ckc_8.6 //
children.translated_text: of these, <s>padopamā</s> (word-level simile) is twofold: through compound (<s>samāsa</s>) and through suffix (<s>pratyaya</s>). // Ckc_8.6 //
Of these, the first (compound-type) is known to have four varieties: <s>sarvasamāsā</s> (complete compound),
<s>antargatadyotakārthā</s> (with indicator-meaning subsumed within), <s>tulyadharmārthagarbhitā</s> (with common-property-meaning embedded), // Ckc_8.7 //
and <s>antarbhūtobhayārthā</s> (with both meanings subsumed within) — examples of these shall be demonstrated. // Ckc_8.8 //

Of him whose fame spreads to the space of the directions, a treasury of fortune and good destiny, the moon of the <s>Raicarte</s> lineage, equal to <s>Raghupati</s> (Rāma), beloved of the moonlight-beloved (<s>Lakṣmī</s>),

children.text: bāhau śeṣāhidīrghe jalajakaratale bhāti viśvaṃbhareyaṃ krudhyatkālāhidaṃṣṭrāṃ mukhavikaṭamukhīṃ khaḍgarekhāṃ dadhāne // Ckc_8.*1 //
children.translated_text: on his arm — long as <s>Śeṣa</s> the serpent, with a palm ruddy as a lotus — this earth shines, (that arm) bearing the sword-line, terrible-faced like the fangs of the wrathful serpent of Time. // Ckc_8.*1 //

children.text:
atra krudhayadityādipade upamānasyāhidaṃṣṭrāmukhasya tulyadharmasya vikaṭatvasya khaḍgamukhasyopameyasya casvasvaśabdairabhidhānena dyotakārthasya pratibhānāt sarvamupamānopameyatulyadharmadyotakaṃ samāse saṃbhavatīti sarvasamāsā nāmeyaṃ padopamā /
śeṣāhirivadīrghaḥ śeṣāhidīrgha ityatra dyotakārtha upamānāni sāmānyavacanairiti samāsenokta iti seyamantargatadyotakārthā nāma samāsapadopamā /
jalajamiva tāmraṃ karatalaṃ yasyāyaṃ jalajakaratala ityatrānyapadārthaṃsamāsa evadyotakatulya dhayorantarmarbhūtatvādiyamantarbhūtobhayārthā nāma samāsapadopamā /
children.translated_text: Here, in the word 'krudhyat' (wrathful) and the rest, through the designation by their own respective words of the <s>upamāna</s> (serpent-fang-face), the common property (<s>tulyadharma</s>) of terribleness, and the <s>upameya</s> (sword-face) — since the indicator-meaning (<s>dyotakārtha</s>) also shines forth — all four (elements) — <s>upamāna</s>, <s>upameya</s>, common property, and indicator — are present within the compound; hence this word-level simile (<s>padopamā</s>) is called <s>sarvasamāsā</s> (complete compound simile). In 'śeṣāhidīrgha' (long as the serpent <s>Śeṣa</s>), the indicator-meaning and <s>upamāna</s> are expressed by generic terms within the compound — hence this is the compound word-level simile called <s>antargatadyotakārthā</s> (with subsumed indicator-meaning). In 'jalajakaratala' (lotus-palm), where the compound 'whose palm is ruddy like a lotus' subsumes both the indicator and the common property within another word-meaning — this is the compound word-level simile called <s>antarbhūtobhayārthā</s> (with both meanings subsumed within).
The other (type) also exists in four varieties, through the distinctions of suffix-meaning (<s>pratyayārtha</s>);
the suffix too partakes of <s>upamāna</s>, <s>upameya</s>, indicator (<s>dyotaka</s>), and common property (<s>tulya</s>). // Ckc_8.9 //
Of these, the suffix conveying <s>upamāna</s>-meaning — as follows:
By the king, <s>Śrī Siṅgabhūpāla</s>, whose arm is like <s>Rāhu</s> (the great seizer),
the earth is gracefully protected, (by him who is) like a <s>Kalpa</s> wish-fulfilling tree. // Ckc_8.*2 //

children.text:
atra yadyapi rāhuriva rāhuḥ kalpapādapa iva kalpapādapa iti cābhedopacāravyāvṛttyā rāhukalpaśabdayorupamānabhāvinorapyupameye bāhau vṛttiḥ /
tābhyāṃ ca yadyapi svārthe eva bahuckalpappratyayau bhavataḥ tathāpi yathā śūrādibhya utpadyamānāstarabādayaḥ śauryasyaivātiśayamavagamayanti na punaḥśauyaśriyasya tadvadimāvapi guṇabhūtamevopamānārthaṃ bruvāte iti seyamupamānār thapratyayā nāma pratyayopamā /
children.translated_text: Here, although 'Rāhu' (as in 'like Rāhu') and 'Kalpa-tree' (as in 'like a Kalpa-tree') — through the exclusion of the non-difference figurative usage — the words 'Rāhu' and 'Kalpa,' even while functioning as <s>upamāna</s>-denoting terms, are applied to the <s>upameya</s> (the arm). And although the suffixes '-bahu' and '-kalpa' are used in their own (literal) sense, just as suffixes like '-tara' and others arising from words like 'śūra' (hero) convey only an intensification of heroism (not of beauty), similarly these two also express only the <s>upamāna</s>-meaning as a subordinate element — hence this word-level simile is called <s>upamānārthapratyayā</s> (suffix conveying <s>upamāna</s>-meaning).
The suffix conveying <s>upameya</s>-meaning — as follows:
O treasure-house of the ardor and exuberance of battle, comparable to the bow of <s>Kalyāṇācala</s> (Mount Meru), O ornamental jewel of King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>, of irresistible and terrible prowess,

children.text: pārāvārabirāviṇīṣu vijayaprasthānabherīṣu te kākakrośi kuraṅgadhāvi ca kulaṃ vidveṣiṇāṃ jāyate // Ckc_8.*3 //
children.translated_text: at (the sound of) your victory-march drums, which wail like pigeons, the family of your enemies becomes one that caws like crows and flees like deer. // Ckc_8.*3 //

children.text:
atra pārāvārā iva rudanti pārāvāravirāviṇya ityatra kartaryupamāna iti sāmānādhikaraṇyena kartavye ca pratyaye upameyārthapratyayā nāma padopamā /
anayaiva bhaṅgayā kākakrośikuraṅgadhāvītyatrāpi draṣṭavyam /
children.translated_text: Here, in 'pārāvāravirāviṇī' (wailing like pigeons), since the <s>upamāna</s> is in the agent and the suffix is to be construed in co-reference (with the agent), the suffix conveys the <s>upameya</s>-meaning — hence this word-level simile is called <s>upameyārthapratyayā</s> (suffix conveying <s>upameya</s>-meaning). By the same analysis, 'kākakrośī' (cawing like crows) and 'kuraṅgadhāvī' (fleeing like deer) should also be understood.
The suffix conveying indicator-meaning (<s>dyotakārtha</s>) — as follows:
In King <s>Śrī Siṅgabhūpati</s>, the ornament (of his line), who has resorted to the <s>Pārijāta</s> tree like Mount <s>Kalyāṇa</s> (Meru), the lamp of (his) encampment,
the earth, growing daily through meritorious deeds, attains stability like the line of <s>Recarla</s> kings. // Ckc_8.*4 //

children.text:
atra kalyāṇaśailo meruḥ tadvadityatra tatra tasyevitībārthe vatiḥ /
recarlasantativadityatra tu tena tulyaṃ kriyā cedvatiṃriti dyotakārtha eva na punastulyakriyārtha iti dyotakārthapratyayā nāma padopamā /
children.translated_text: Here, <s>Kalyāṇaśaila</s> (the auspicious mountain) is <s>Meru</s>; in 'tadvat' (like that), the suffix '-vat' has the meaning 'as if his own' (i.e. indicating comparison). In 'Recarlasantativat' (like the Recarla lineage), however, the suffix '-vat' (has the meaning) 'if the action is equal to that' — thus it conveys only the indicator-meaning, not the meaning of equal action — hence this word-level simile is called <s>dyotakārthapratyayā</s> (suffix conveying indicator-meaning).
The suffix conveying common-property-meaning (<s>tulyadharmārtha</s>) — as follows:

children.text: uddaṇḍapratigaṇḍhabhairavavibho rajyatkaṭākṣe ruṣā gehīyanti virodhināṃ giriguhā stalpāyate śādvalam /
children.translated_text: O <s>Uddaṇḍa-pratigaṇḍha-Bhairava</s> lord, when your sidelong glance falls in anger, the enemies take to mountain caves as if they were houses (<s>gehīyanti</s>), the grasslands serve as their beds (<s>stalpāyate</s>),

children.text: saudhīyanti taṭe ca te kapicamūcāraṃ caranto vane paśyanti prabhudarśamugraśabarāneṇīsutīyanti ca // Ckc_8.*5 //
children.translated_text: the riverbanks serve as their palaces (<s>saudhīyanti</s>), and wandering in the forest like monkey-troops, they see the fierce <s>Śabara</s> tribesmen as sights of (their former) lord, and they behave like doe-offspring (<s>eṇīsutīyanti</s>). // Ckc_8.*5 //

children.text: atra gehānīvācaranti gehīyantītyatra kyac pratyaya upamānādācāra iti kriyāviśeṣalakṣaṇe tulyadharmārtha eva samutpanna iti seyaṃ tulyadharmārthapratyayā nāma padopamā /
children.translated_text: Here, in '<s>gehīyanti</s>' (they behave as if in houses), the <s>kyac</s> suffix, derived from the <s>upamāna</s> 'house' in the sense of 'acting like,' produces precisely the common-property-meaning in the characteristic of a specific action — hence this word-level simile is called <s>tulyadharmārthapratyayā</s> (suffix conveying common-property-meaning).

children.text: saivādhikaraṇakyacā yathā atra saidha iva ācarati saudhīyantītyatrādhārakyacpratyayo 'pi tulyadharmārtha eveti seyaṃ tādṛśī /
children.translated_text: The same with the locative <s>kyac</s> — as follows: here, in '<s>saudhīyanti</s>' (the riverbanks act like palaces), the locative <s>kyac</s> suffix also conveys precisely the common-property-meaning — hence this is of the same type.

children.text: saiva kriyayā yathā uddaṇḍapratigaṇjabhairava bhavadbāṇā raṇe vidbiṣāṃ bhetālanti halāhalanti dahanajvālanti kālanti ca /
children.translated_text: The same through verbal action — as follows: O <s>Uddaṇḍa-pratigaṇja-Bhairava</s>, your arrows in battle against the enemies act like <s>Vetālas</s> (vampiric beings), act like <s>Hālāhala</s> (deadly poison), act like flames of fire, act like <s>Kāla</s> (Death);

children.text: śrīsiṅgakṣitipāla pālitaguṇa tvatkīrtivisphūrtayo nīhāranti haranti nirjaravarāhāranti hāranti ca // Ckc_8.*6 //
children.translated_text: O King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>, protector of virtues, your manifestations of fame act like frost (<s>nīhāranti</s>), act like <s>Hari</s> (<s>haranti</s>), act like the food of the celestials (<s>nirjaravarāhāranti</s>), and act like necklaces (<s>hāranti</s>). // Ckc_8.*6 //

children.text: atra bhetālantītyādiṣu kriyāsu tadivācaratītyācāralakṣaṇatulyadharmārthe kvibuptanna iti seyamapi tulyadharmārthapratyayā nāma padopamā /
children.translated_text: Here, in the verbs '<s>bhetālanti</s>' (act like Vetālas) and the rest, the <s>kvip</s> suffix, with the common-property-meaning of 'acting like that' in the characteristic of behavior — hence this too is the word-level simile called <s>tulyadharmārthapratyayā</s> (suffix conveying common-property-meaning).
From the similarity of word-meanings to each other, and likewise of sentence-meanings,

children.text: vākyopamā dvidhā jñeyā tatrādyā dvividhā matā // Ckc_8.10 //
children.translated_text: <s>vākyopamā</s> (sentence-level simile) is to be known as twofold; of these, the first is considered to be of two kinds: // Ckc_8.10 //
<s>pūrṇā</s> (complete) and <s>luptā</s> (elliptical); the complete one here is well-furnished with four components. // Ckc_8.11 //
As follows:

children.text: yathā rākācandre sakalajagadānandajanane saroje gaure bā surabhitadaśāśāpariṣadi /
children.translated_text: Just as in the full-moon, which generates the delight of the entire world, in the white lotus, or in the fragrant assembly of the ten directions,

children.text: mahāratnollāsinyurasi danujāreriva ruciṃ parāṃ dhatte siṅgakṣitipa bhavatī śrīratitarām // Ckc_8.*7 //
children.translated_text: or in the chest resplendent with great jewels — like (the splendor) of the slayer of demons (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), so too does your <s>Śrī</s> (prosperity/beauty), O King <s>Siṅga</s>, bear supreme radiance exceedingly. // Ckc_8.*7 //

Here, through the conjunction of all four components — <s>upamāna</s> (standard of comparison), <s>upameya</s> (thing compared), <s>dyotaka</s> (indicator), and <s>tulyadharma</s> (common property) — this is a <s>pūrṇā vākyopamā</s> (complete sentence-level simile) possessing word-meaning similarity.
The elliptical (<s>luptā</s>) type is threefold, arising from the omission of the common property, the indicator, or both. // Ckc_8.12 //
Here, the type with omission of the common property (<s>tulyadharmalopa</s>) — as follows:
O King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>, protector of the earth, your succession of fame
vies proudly with the floods of moonlight, emboldened by the support of the mighty. // Ckc_8.*8 //

children.text: atra tulyadharmasya dhavalimāderanabhidhāne 'pi prasiddhibalenopamānopameyabhāvasya pratīteriyaṃ tulyadharmavatī vākyopamā /
children.translated_text: Here, even though the common property of whiteness is not explicitly stated, since the relationship of <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s> is perceived through the force of well-known convention — this is a <s>vākyopamā</s> (sentence-level simile) with (omitted) common property.
The same with omission of the indicator (<s>dyotakalopa</s>) — as follows:
O King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>, protector of the earth, the jewel-mountain (<s>Ratnasānu</s>) and you as well —
both radiant with luminous bangles, both resplendent with auspicious forms. // Ckc_8.*9 //

children.text:
atra ivādidyotakamantareṇāpi ratnasānunāyakaratnayorupamānopameyayoritaretarayoginaikaśeṣeṇa tadviśeṣaṇayossamudāyenana ca dvayoḥ sādṛśyaṃ pratīyata itīyaṃ dyotakalopavatī nāma padārthasāmyavatī vākyopamā /
nātra śleṣaśaṅkā /
siddhasādṛśyayoḥ tantreṇābhidhānaṃ śleṣaḥ /
sādṛsyaṃ punarupamānopameyabhāvavivakṣā /
tena śleṣasya dyotakalopopamāyāśca viviktaviṣayatā vyakttaiva /
children.translated_text: Here, even without an explicit marker like 'iva,' the similarity of the <s>upamāna</s> and <s>upameya</s> — the 'jewel-mountain' and 'hero-jewel' — is perceived through mutual conjunction (<s>itaretarayoga</s>) in a single compound (<s>ekaśeṣa</s>), by means of their qualifiers taken together rather than individually. Thus this is the <s>dyotakalopavaī</s> (marker-elided) variety of <s>padārthasāmyavatī vākyopamā</s> (sentential simile based on word-meaning similarity). There is no suspicion of <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia) here: <s>śleṣa</s> is the joint expression (<s>tantra</s>) of two meanings already established as similar; but similarity itself is the intention to establish the <s>upamāna-upameya</s> relationship. Thus <s>śleṣa</s> and the marker-elided <s>upamā</s> have clearly distinct domains.
<s>Ubhayalopavatī</s> (both-elided) — as follows:

children.text: na karpūrā na nīhārā na ca śāradacandrikāḥ /
children.translated_text: "These are not camphor, not frost, not autumn moonbeams —
rather, the glories of King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>'s fame sparkle forth." // Ckc_8.*10 //

children.text:
atra tulyadharmadyotakābhyāṃ vināpi nāyakakīrtiṣu karpūrādibhrāntipratyākhyānenaiva tadupamānopameyabhāvapratīteriyamubhayalopavatī nāma padārthasāmyavatī vākyopamā /
kecidenāṃ trilopavatīmapi manyanete /
upamānopameyayoranyatarakathane kasya sādharmyamityasaṃmatamityasmākam /
children.translated_text: Here, even without both the shared quality (<s>tulyadharma</s>) and the explicit marker (<s>dyotaka</s>), through the mere denial of the camphor-identification etc. with respect to the hero's fame, the <s>upamāna-upameya</s> relationship is perceived — thus this is the <s>ubhayalopavatī</s> (both-elided) variety of <s>padārthasāmyavatī vākyopamā</s>. Some consider this a <s>trilopavatī</s> (triple-elided) type as well. But our view is that when the statement of either the <s>upamāna</s> or <s>upameya</s> is absent, the question 'similarity with what?' renders this unacceptable.
The sentential-meaning-based simile (<s>vākyārthagāminī upamā</s>) is of four kinds: single-marker (<s>ekadyotakā</s>),
multiple-marker (<s>anekadyotakā</s>), marker-absent (<s>dyotakaśūnyā</s>), and possessing dissimilarity (<s>vaidharmyavatī</s>). // Ckc_8.13 //
<s>Ekadyotakā</s> (single-marker) — as follows:
King <s>Siṅga</s> shines on the throne, with a trembling pearl necklace on his chest,
charming with long pendant clusters — like a wish-fulfilling tree on the bank of <s>Sumeru</s>. // Ckc_8.*11 //

children.text: atra merutaṭa siṃhāsanayoḥ kalpavṛkṣanāyakayostabakahārayośca parasparamupamānopameya bhāvavivakṣāyāṃ viśeṣaṇaviśeṣyabhāvakalpanayā dvayoreva vākyārthayoḥ kalpitatvādekenaiva dyotakaśabdena tayoḥ parasparamupamānopameyabhāvo 'bhihita iti seyamekadyotakā nāma vākyārthasāmyavatī vākyopamā /
children.translated_text: Here, when the <s>upamāna-upameya</s> relationship is intended between the bank of <s>Meru</s> and the throne, between the wish-fulfilling tree and the hero, and between the flower-clusters and the necklace — through the device of qualifier-qualified construction, since only two sentential meanings are fashioned, a single marker-word ('iva') conveys the mutual <s>upamāna-upameya</s> relationship of both. Thus this is the <s>ekadyotakā</s> (single-marker) variety of <s>vākyārthasāmyavatī vākyopamā</s> (sentential simile based on sentence-meaning similarity).
<s>Anekadyotakā</s> (multiple-marker) — as follows:
King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>, of great fortune, like the sun,
destroys the host of enemies as if (destroying) darkness, in battle as if in the sky. // Ckc_8.*12 //

children.text: atra vākyadvayaikatāpattikāmanayā kartuḥ karmaṇo 'dhikaraṇāccopamānāt pṛthak pṛthag dyotakaśabdaḥ kṛta iti seyamanekadyotakā nāma vākyārthasāmyavatī vākyopamā /
children.translated_text: Here, by the method of constructing two sentences as one, a separate marker-word is employed for the agent, the object, and the location with respect to the <s>upamāna</s> — thus this is the <s>anekadyotakā</s> (multiple-marker) variety of <s>vākyārthasāmyavatī vākyopamā</s>.
<s>Dyotakahīnā</s> (marker-absent) — as follows:

children.text: devānāṃ divi rakṣaṇāya maghavā jāgarti daṃbholinā sādhūnāṃ bhūvi siṅgabhūpatirayaṃ khaḍgena śātāsriṇā /
children.translated_text: "In heaven, <s>Maghavā</s> (<s>Indra</s>) stays awake to protect the gods, with his thunderbolt; on earth, this King <s>Siṅgabhūpati</s>, with his sharp-edged sword, (protects) the virtuous.

children.text: ratnādau prathamo mudā viharate rambhādibhirvaibhavā- drājādrāvitaro 'pi ropitayaśāśśuddhāntakāntājanaiḥ // Ckc_8.*13 //
children.translated_text: The former sports joyfully with <s>Rambhā</s> and others through divine splendor; the latter too, having established his fame, (sports) with the women of the inner apartments." // Ckc_8.*13 //

children.text: atra suranāyakayoḥ svarlokabhūlokayoḥ devabhūdevānāṃ dambholikaravālayośca tulyaikaśriyā samāveśādivādidyotakamantareṇāpi vākyārthānāmupamānopameyabhāvo gamyata ityayaṃ dyotakaśūnyā nāma vākyārthasāmyavatī vākyopamā /
children.translated_text: Here, through the equal splendor of the god-king and the earthly king, of the celestial and terrestrial worlds, of the gods and earthly nobles, and of the thunderbolt and sword — the <s>upamāna-upameya</s> relationship of the sentential meanings is understood even without an explicit marker like 'iva.' Thus this is the <s>dyotakaśūnyā</s> (marker-absent) variety of <s>vākyārthasāmyavatī vākyopamā</s>.
<s>Vaidharmyavatī</s> (possessing dissimilarity) — as follows:

children.text: avivekī na surabhivaccintāmaṇiriva na yāti kāṭhinyam /
children.translated_text: "He is not indiscriminate like the <s>Surabhī</s> (wish-granting cow); he does not reach hardness like the <s>Cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-jewel);
King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>, the crest-jewel — auspicious, auspicious! — is the good fortune of the earthly world." // Ckc_8.*14 //

children.text: atropamānopameyadyotakeṣu stsu yoyamaviveko nāma dharmaḥ so 'yamupamāna eva kavinā niyamyata itīyaṃ vaidharmyavatī nāma vākyopamā /
children.translated_text: Here, among the <s>upamāna</s>, <s>upameya</s>, and marker, the quality called 'indiscriminate' is restricted by the poet to the <s>upamāna</s> alone — thus this is the <s>vaidharmyavatī</s> (dissimilarity-possessing) variety of <s>vākyopamā</s>.
Where, through a turn of expression, similarity between sentential meanings is apprehended
— and (this is presented) at length between the two sentential meanings — that is <s>prapañcopamā</s> (elaborate simile). As follows: // Ckc_8.14 //

children.text: seyaṃ dvedhā hi rūpeṇa prakṛtāprakṛteti ca /
children.translated_text: This is of two forms: natural (<s>prakṛta</s>) and modified (<s>aprakṛta</s>).
Of these, the natural form is of four kinds: complete simile (<s>sakalopamā</s>), // Ckc_8.15 //

children.text: ekadeśopamā cānye mālikā mekhaleti ca // Ckc_8.16 //
children.translated_text: partial simile (<s>ekadeśopamā</s>), garland (<s>mālikā</s>), and girdle (<s>mekhalā</s>). // Ckc_8.16 //
Of these, <s>sakalopamā</s> (complete simile) — as follows:
"With mountains led by <s>Maināka</s> — that is, with elephants in rut; with waves — that is, with horses; with the best warriors like crocodile-elephants;

children.text: raicarlīyakulendunā svapatinā daityāriṇeva sphuṭaṃ senā sindhuriva prayāti nitarāṃ kenāpi durlaṅghatām // Ckc_8.*15 //
children.translated_text: with its own lord, the moon of the noble lineage — clearly, like the ocean with the enemy of the <s>Daityas</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), the army marches forth, utterly impassable by anyone." // Ckc_8.*15 //

children.text: atra sindhoḥ senāyāśca durlaṅghatayābhidhīyamānasādṛśyayorupamānopameyabhāvavivakṣāyāṃ yathā mainākādiśailānāṃ mātaṅgādīnāṃ samudrasenādharmāṇāṃ pratītasādṛśyānāṃ pṛthak pṛthag dyotakaśabdayogādativistareṇāvayavinoravayavānāṃ ca yathocitaṃ sākalyena vākyārthayoraupamye bhaṅgiḥ seyaṃ sākalyavatī nāma prakṛtirūpā prapañcoktiḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, when the similarity in impassability between the ocean and the army is being stated as the <s>upamāna-upameya</s> relationship, just as the mountains like <s>Maināka</s>, the great elephants, and other properties of ocean and army — whose similarity is already perceived — are each given separate marker-words, so through very extensive description the simile is applied wholly and appropriately to both the whole (<s>avayavin</s>) and its parts (<s>avayava</s>). This is the <s>sākalyavatī</s> (possessing completeness) variety, a <s>prapañcokti</s> in natural form.
<s>Ekadeśavatī</s> (partial) — as follows:
"King <s>Siṅga</s> shines — with fingers like fresh leaf-buds,
with nail-radiance like flowers, with his pair of arms like a pair of branches." // Ckc_8.*16 //

children.text: atra kalpavṛkṣanāyakayorupamānopameyabhāve vaktavye kalpavṛkṣalakṣaṇamupamānaṃ parityajya tadekadeśena sahopameyaikadeśo bāhuyugalāśaṃsāvayavaiḥ (kisalaya) kisalayakusumaissaha bhujayugāṅgānyaṅgulyaḥ nakharucayaśca pṛthak pṛthag dyotakaśabdaprayogādvistareṇopamitānītīyamekadeśavatī nāma prakṛtarūpā prapañcopamā /
children.translated_text: Here, where the <s>upamāna-upameya</s> relationship should be stated between the wish-fulfilling tree and the hero, the <s>upamāna</s> — namely the wish-fulfilling tree as a whole — is set aside, and instead a part of the <s>upameya</s> — the pair of arms and bodily parts like fingers and nail-radiance — is compared extensively with parts (of the tree) — leaves, flowers — using separate marker-words for each. This is the <s>ekadeśavatī</s> (partial) variety, a <s>prapañcopamā</s> in natural form.
<s>Mālikā</s> (garland) — as follows:

children.text: karpūrairiva kaumudairiva kulaiḥ kāśairiva svarṇadī-kallolairiva kaitakairiva dalaiḥ kādambayūthairiva /
children.translated_text: "Like camphor, like moonbeams, like sprays of <s>kāśa</s> grass, like waves of the golden river,

children.text: śrīgandhairiva śāradairiva ganaiḥ śītāṃśubiṃbairiva vyāptaṃ siṅganarendrakīrtivibhavaiḥ trailokyamālokyate // Ckc_8.*17 //
children.translated_text: like <s>kaitaka</s> petals, like flocks of <s>kādamba</s> birds, like <s>śrīgandha</s> (sandalwood), like autumn clouds, like discs of the cool-rayed moon — the three worlds appear pervaded by the splendors of King <s>Siṅga</s>'s fame." // Ckc_8.*17 //

children.text: atra nāyakakīrtirekaikaprakarṣapratītaye mālikāprakāreṇa karpūrādibhirupamīyata itīyaṃ mālikā nāma prakṛtarūpā prapañcopamā /
children.translated_text: Here, the hero's fame is compared through the garland method (<s>mālikā-prakāra</s>) with camphor and the rest, each for the perception of a distinct excellence. This is the <s>mālikā</s> (garland) variety, a <s>prapañcopamā</s> in natural form.
<s>Mekhalā</s> (girdle) — as follows:

children.text: prajñeva kīrtiramalā tava siṅgabhūpa prajñāpi khaḍga iva tīvratarā vibhāti /
children.translated_text: "Your fame shines spotless like wisdom, O King <s>Siṅga</s>; and your wisdom shines sharper like a sword;

children.text: khaḍgaḥ pratāpa iva śātravacittadāhī prāntān diśāṃ bhajati kīrtiriva pratāpaḥ // Ckc_8.*18 //
children.translated_text: your sword burns the minds of enemies like your prowess; and your prowess reaches the ends of the directions like your fame." // Ckc_8.*18 //

children.text: atrābhidhīyamānasādṛsyānāṃ prajñādīnāṃ raśanānyāyena saṃkalayya saprapañcatayā kathanātseyaṃ mekhalā nāma prakṛtarūpā prapañcopamā /
children.translated_text: Here, the objects whose similarity is being stated — wisdom and the rest — are linked together in the manner of a girdle (<s>rasanā-nyāya</s>), and described with elaboration. This is the <s>mekhalā</s> (girdle) variety, a <s>prapañcopamā</s> in natural form.

children.text: uktā vikṛta rūpeti yānyā sāpi caturvidhā /
children.translated_text: The modified form (<s>vikṛtarūpa</s>) has been mentioned; it too is of four kinds,
designated as: reversal (<s>viparyāsa</s>), mutual (<s>ubhaya</s>), fabricated (<s>utpādya</s>), and self-referential (<s>ananvaya</s>). // Ckc_8.17 //
Of these, <s>viparyāsopamā</s> (reversed simile) — as follows:

children.text: koṇe kutracidāsatāṃ kariṇiki kroḍādayaḥ kecana prācīnāstadupāśrayānvayamamī doṣānna bhāṣāmahe /
children.translated_text: "Let <s>Kariṇikī</s> (Kuvera's elephant) and the like sit in some corner — those are ancient; we do not speak of their faults, as they depend on their lineage.

children.text: keyūraṃ smaragasmarasya śayanaṃ śaurergirāṃ śāsitā śrīsiṅgakṣitināyakena samatāṃ śeṣāhirevārhati // Ckc_8.*19 //
children.translated_text: The armlet of <s>Smara</s> (<s>Kāmadeva</s>), the couch of <s>Śauri</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), the ruler of speech — only <s>Śeṣa</s> (the cosmic serpent) deserves equality with King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>." // Ckc_8.*19 //

children.text: atra pratīyamāne dharaṇīdhaureyatve śeṣādīnāmupamānatvaṃ nāyakasyopameyatvamiti marvādāyāṃ varṇanīyasyātiśayaṃ vivakṣatā kenāpi vaktā viparyāsādupamānopameyabhāvaḥ kalpita iti seyaṃ viparyāsopamā nāma vikṛtarūpā prapañcopamā /
children.translated_text: Here, when the earth-bearing capacity of <s>Śeṣa</s> and others is perceived, the conventional arrangement is that they should be the <s>upamāna</s> and the hero the <s>upameya</s>; but some speaker, wishing to express the hero's superiority, has reversed the <s>upamāna-upameya</s> relationship. This is the <s>viparyāsopamā</s> (reversed simile), a <s>prapañcopamā</s> in modified form.
<s>Ubhayopamā</s> (mutual simile) — as follows:
"O King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>, while you extend the protection of the good and the chastisement of the wicked,
your army attains impassability like the ocean; and the ocean (attains impassability) like your army." // Ckc_8.*20 //

Here, when the mutual <s>upamāna-upameya</s> relationship between the army-commander hero's army and the ocean is intended, the reversal of the well-known (roles) on one side (makes this) the <s>ubhayopamā</s> (mutual simile), a <s>prapañcopamā</s> in modified form.
<s>Utpādyopamā</s> (fabricated simile) — as follows:

children.text: kālāpāṃ yadakalpapādapamahāśākhā samālaṃbate śrīsiṅgakṣitipālabāhuranayā tulyaḥ kṛpāṇojjvalaḥ /
children.translated_text: "The arm of King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>, radiant with sword, grasps the great branches of the epoch-wish-fulfilling tree;

children.text: hemādrerupari sthite yadi vidhau pāścātyagaurāndhatā tacchatraṃ kṛtaśātakumbhakalaśaṃ jātopamānaṃ bhavet // Ckc_8.*21 //
children.translated_text: if the moon, stationed atop the golden mountain, were to have the darkness of the western horizon — then the golden-dome umbrella would have a fitting standard of comparison." // Ckc_8.*21 //

children.text:
atra kalpapādapaśākhāyāḥ kālāhisaṃkalpamutpādyānayā sakṛpāṇo nāyakapāṇirupamīyata iti seyamutpādyopamā nāma vikṛtarūpā prapañcopamā /
evamuttarārdhe 'pi yojanīyam /
children.translated_text: Here, by fabricating the <s>kālāhi</s> (time-serpent) concept for the branch of the wish-fulfilling tree, the hero's hand with sword is compared. This is the <s>utpādyopamā</s> (fabricated simile), a <s>prapañcopamā</s> in modified form. The second half should be construed similarly.
<s>Ananvayopamā</s> (self-referential simile) — as follows:
"King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s> shines like King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>,
in warding off the rut-elephants of indomitable adversaries." // Ckc_8.*22 //

children.text: atropamānopameyabhāva ekasyaivānanvita itīyamananvayā nāma vikṛtā prapañcopamā /
children.translated_text: Here, since the <s>upamāna-upameya</s> relationship is self-referential (<s>ananvita</s>) — applying to one and the same entity — this is the <s>ananvayā</s> (self-referential) variety, a modified <s>prapañcopamā</s>.
Where through figurative usage (<s>upacāra</s>) the <s>upamāna</s> (standard of comparison) is presented as identical with the <s>upameya</s> (thing compared),
such that the <s>upamāna</s> shines forth in the form of the <s>upameya</s> — that is defined as <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor). // Ckc_8.18 //
Based on predominance, this is of three kinds, arising from word, meaning, or both.

children.text: śabdapradhānaṃ prakṛtaṃ vikṛtaṃ ceti tad dvidhā // Ckc_8.19 //
children.translated_text: The word-predominant type is of two kinds: natural (<s>prakṛta</s>) and modified (<s>vikṛta</s>). // Ckc_8.19 //

children.text:
ādyantavikṛtaiśśabdairgrathitaṃ taccaturvidham /
samastaṃ vyastamubhayaṃ saviśeṣaṇamityapi // Ckc_8.20 //
children.translated_text: The (natural type), constructed with words that are modified at the beginning or end, is of four varieties: compound (<s>samasta</s>), separated (<s>vyasta</s>), both (<s>ubhaya</s>), and with-qualifier (<s>saviśeṣaṇa</s>). // Ckc_8.20 //
Of these, the compound <s>rūpaka</s> (<s>samāsavad rūpaka</s>) — as follows:
"The streams from the rain-cloud of King <s>Siṅga</s>'s sword
extinguish the forest-fire of the prowess of (enemy) heroes." // Ckc_8.*23 //

children.text: atra sādṛśyādi vivakṣāyāmabhedopacāreṇopameyasya karavālasya payomugiva payomugiti payomukpayodanirūpaṇīyatve sāmānyevādya prayogādupamārthastirobhūtaḥ samāsaśca kṛta iti tadidaṃ samastaṃ nāma prakṛtiśabdapradhānarūpakam /
children.translated_text: Here, when similarity etc. is intended, through the figurative usage of non-difference, the <s>upameya</s> 'sword' is described as 'rain-cloud' (<s>payomuc</s>) — and since where 'rain-cloud-like rain-cloud' should be analyzed, the first usage as a general term causes the <s>upamāna</s>-meaning to become obscured, and a compound is formed — this is the <s>samasta</s> (compound) variety of the natural word-predominant <s>rūpaka</s>.
<s>Vyasta</s> (separated) — as follows:

children.text: śrīsiṅgakṣitināyakasya yaśasāṃ candreṇa sāndrā ruciḥ yatprāptā tapanaṃ pratāmapabhito loke tadatyadbhutam /
children.translated_text: "The moon of the fame of King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s> has an intense radiance; that it has reached the sun — the prowess of fear — in the world, that is truly wondrous.

children.text: evaṃ nāticamatkṛtaṃ tadanayoratyantamāśliṣyator āpatyātithayo bhavanti yadamī pratyarthipṛthvībhūjaḥ // Ckc_8.*24 //
children.translated_text: But this is not so astonishing: for when these two are in close embrace, the offspring that are born are these enemy kings." // Ckc_8.*24 //

children.text: atra yaśaso candreṇa pratāpaṃ tapanamiti dvayorupamānayorupameyaśabdasāmānādhikaraṇyādupamānārthastirohitaḥ samāsaśca kṛta iti samastaṃ nāma prakṛtaśabdapradhānaṃrūpakam /
children.translated_text: Here, with 'the moon of fame' and 'the sun of prowess' — since the two <s>upamāna</s>-words are placed in co-reference with the <s>upameya</s>, the <s>upamāna</s>-meaning is obscured and a compound is formed — this is the <s>samasta</s> (compound) variety of the natural word-predominant <s>rūpaka</s>.
The <s>ubhaya</s> (both compound and non-compound) form — as follows:
"O King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>, your sword is the fang of the arm-staff-serpent;
for the enemy kings, (your) fame is the moonbeam (<s>candrikā</s>) bereft of its moon-disc." // Ckc_8.*25 //

children.text: atra bhujābhujaṅgamasya samastatvaṃ daṃṣṭretyasamastamiti tadidamubhayaṃ nāma prakṛtiśabdapradhānaṃ rūpakam /
children.translated_text: Here, 'arm-serpent' (<s>bhuja-bhujaṅgama</s>) is in compound form, while 'fang' (<s>daṃṣṭrā</s>) is in non-compound form — thus this is the <s>ubhaya</s> (both) variety of the natural word-predominant <s>rūpaka</s>.
<s>Saviśeṣaṇa</s> (with-qualifier) — as follows:
"The inner apartments of King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s> — the <s>Mandara</s> mountain whose interior pathways are blocked —
the army of the enemies becomes the ocean churned by that (<s>Mandara</s>), yielding <s>amṛta</s> (nectar)." // Ckc_8.*26 //

children.text: atra nāyakamandarakṣubhitaviśeṣaṇamiva viśiṣṭaireva vāhinīnāthavairivāhinyo rūpaṇamiti saviśeṣaṇaṃ nāmedaṃ prakṛtiśabdapradhānarūpakam /
children.translated_text: Here, just as the hero is metaphorically described as <s>Mandara</s> with its (appropriate) qualifiers, so the army-lord's enemy forces are metaphorically described as qualified by the corresponding attributes — thus this is the <s>saviśeṣaṇa</s> (with-qualifier) variety of the natural word-predominant <s>rūpaka</s>.
Of these, the chain (<s>paramparā</s>) type — as follows:
"A banner-pennant of virtues, a whitewash-plaster for the palace of the three worlds,
your fame, O King <s>Siṅga</s>, is the preceding moon for the ocean of good people." // Ckc_8.*27 //

children.text:
atra guṇānāṃ ketutayā rūpaṇaṃ prathamam /
tatsaṃbandhitayā dukūlapaṭṭikā dvitīyam /
tasyā yaśasā tṛtīyam /
iti seyaṃ paraṃparā nāma vikṛtaśabdapradhānarūpakam /
tadidaṃ vaidharmyeṇāpi saṃbhavati /
children.translated_text: Here, the first metaphorical description is of the virtues as a banner; the second is the cloth-pennant related to that (banner); the third is the fame related to that (pennant). Thus this is the <s>paramparā</s> (chain) variety, a modified word-predominant <s>rūpaka</s>. This can also occur with dissimilarity (<s>vaidhmya</s>).
As follows:
"The thunderbolt-edge splitting mountains, the fresh cloud-stream burning the impurity of the <s>Kali</s> age,

children.text: vilasati kaṭākṣarekhā tava siṅgakṣitipa kalpavṛkṣasurekhā // Ckc_8.*28 //
children.translated_text: the sidelong glance of yours, O King <s>Siṅga</s>, shines as the <s>Surekha</s> (beautiful line) of the wish-fulfilling tree." // Ckc_8.*28 //

children.text:
etadeva rupakasya rupakahetutayā rūpakahedurupakamiti kecidācakṣate /
tadapi nāma vaikṛtameva /
children.translated_text: Some call this very type <s>rūpaka-hetu-rūpaka</s> (metaphor-as-cause-of-metaphor), since the metaphor itself becomes the reason for another metaphor. But that too is simply the modified type.
<s>Mekhalā</s> (girdle) — as follows:

children.text: rāja kumāra dviradairdviradaṃ śilābhiśśilā śikhā saudhaiḥ /
children.translated_text: "Kings by elephants, elephants by rocks, rocks by peaks, peaks by mansions /
adorned with elegant palaces and aerial mansions, this is the royal capital on the king's mountain. // Ckc_8.*29 //

children.text:
atra rājakumāradviradādīnāṃ rūpakāṇāṃ raśanā nyāyāduttarottarasaṃkalanyā rūpitatvādiyaṃ mekhalā nāma vikṛtaśabdapradhānaṃ rūpakam /
tadidaṃ śṛṅkhaleti kecidācakṣate /
tannāmabhemātram /
children.translated_text:
Here, since the <s>rūpakas</s> (metaphors) of the prince, elephant, and so on are linked in successively increasing combination following the chain principle, this is the <s>mekhalā</s> (girdle) variety — a <s>rūpaka</s> predominated by modified expression.
Some call this <s>śṛṅkhalā</s> (chain). That is merely a difference of name.
<s>Mālikā</s> (garland) — as follows:

children.text: cūḍāratnaṃ nṛpaṣariṣadāmarthināṃ pārijāto rakṣālāsaḥ sucaritavatāṃ bhāgyarāśernidhānam /
children.translated_text: The crest-jewel of royal assemblies, the <s>Pārijāta</s> (wish-fulfilling tree) of supplicants, the playfulness of good fortune for the well-conducted, the treasure-house of the accumulated mass of merit,

children.text: līlāraṅgo varatanudṛśmar (?) galā durnayānāṃ siṅgakṣoṇītalapatirayaṃ rājate rājaśaile // Ckc_8.*30 //
children.translated_text: the pleasure-garden of those with beautiful forms, the (?)-necked one for the wicked, this lord of the earth King <s>Siṅga</s> shines resplendent upon the royal mountain. // Ckc_8.*30 //

children.text: atra ekasminnava nāyake mālikāprakāreṇa rūpakāṇāṃ nirūpaṇādidaṃ mālikā nāma vikṛtaśabda pradhānaṃ rupakam /
children.translated_text: Here, since metaphors are described in garland-fashion (<s>mālikā-prakāra</s>) applied to a single hero, this is the <s>mālikā</s> (garland) variety — a <s>rūpaka</s> predominated by modified expression.
<s>Rūpaka-rūpaka</s> (metaphor upon metaphor) — as follows:
King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>, whose arm is the serpent of the sword,
devours entirely the moon-orb of jewels belonging to the enemy kings. // Ckc_8.*31 //

children.text:
atra vallītvenāropitasya kṛpāṇasya bhujagatayā rūpaṇādidaṃ rūpakarūpakaṃ nāma vikṛtaśabdapradhānarūpakam /
tadetaccatuṣṭayamapi paraṃparādivaikṛtena nibaddhamiti vikṛtamityucyate /
children.translated_text:
Here, since the sword, which has been figuratively attributed as a creeper, is further metaphorically described as a serpent through the arm — this is the <s>rūpaka-rūpaka</s> (metaphor upon metaphor) variety, a <s>rūpaka</s> predominated by modified expression.
This set of four is also called <s>vikṛta</s> (modified) because it is composed through successive (layers of) modification.
The meaning-predominated (<s>artha-pradhāna</s>) type, according to the predominance of the principal element (<s>aṅgin</s>) and the subordinate element (<s>aṅga</s>), is of two kinds.
The principal-element-predominated (<s>aṅgi-pradhāna</s>) type is demonstrated through <s>rūpaka</s> and other figures to be of four kinds. // Ckc_8.21 //
These are distinguished as <s>sakala</s> (complete), <s>vikala</s> (incomplete), <s>yukta</s> (congruent), and <s>ayukta</s> (incongruent). // Ckc_8.22 //
Of these, <s>sakala</s> (complete) — as follows:
Dripping with the essence of nectar from eloquent speech, specially beautiful with the broad petals of eyes,

children.text: śrīsiṅgabhūpa bhavadīyamukhāravinda- madhyāsyate kamalayā paramādareṇa // Ckc_8.*32 //
children.translated_text: O King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>, <s>Kamalā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) sits upon your lotus-face with supreme delight. // Ckc_8.*32 //

children.text: atra nāyakamukhāravindāvayavinopamānopameyau kathitasādṛśyaiḥ sarasoktimarandalocanapalāśaiḥ svāvayavaissaha yathāvivakṣitaṃ sākalyena rūpitāviti tadyogyavastvādhāratvakathanādasyaiva prādhānyamiti ca tadidaṃ sakalaṃ nāmāṅgipradhānamarthapradhānaṃ rupakam /
children.translated_text: Here, the hero's lotus-face (<s>mukhāravinda</s>) as the principal (<s>avayavin</s>), and its parts — eloquent speech-nectar, eye-petals — as the subordinate parts (<s>avayava</s>), are both metaphorically described together with their respective counterparts (flower-nectar, flower-petals) in full completeness as intended. Since the statement of it being the proper receptacle for that worthy entity (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) establishes its predominance — this is the <s>sakala</s> (complete) variety, a meaning-predominated <s>rūpaka</s> with principal-element predominance.
<s>Vikala</s> (incomplete) — as follows:
The face of King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>, beautiful with the moonlight of its smile,
is enjoyed; one perceives (in it) blooming eye-lotuses. // Ckc_8.*33 //

children.text: atra smitajyotsnayoravayavayoḥ nirūpaṇaṃ nirūpyāvayavena pūrṇendulakṣaṇasyopamānasyānabhidhānāt tadidaṃ vikalaṃ nāmāṅgipradhānaṃ rūpakam /
children.translated_text: Here, the subordinate parts — smile and moonlight — are metaphorically described, but the principal counterpart (the full moon) of the face (<s>upamāna</s>) is not mentioned. Hence this is the <s>vikala</s> (incomplete) variety, a principal-element-predominated <s>rūpaka</s>.
Served by royal swans, with the beauty of lotus-fibers of royal fame,
you, O King <s>Siṅgabhūpa</s>, become a lotus-pond. // Ckc_8.*34 //

children.text:
atrāropyamāṇayoḥ parasparasaṃgateryogyatvādidaṃ yukttaṃ nāmāṅgipraghānaṃ rūpakam /
atra yadyapi padmākara iti gauṇavṛttirvyapāśrayata iti śadba eva viśeṣaṇairalaṅkiyate tathāpi padmāyā ākara iti śleṣasāmarthyena mukhyasyeva bhavati śadbhārthasya prādhānyamavagamyata ityarthapradhānamevaitat /
children.translated_text:
Here, since the mutually superimposed elements have appropriate mutual congruence, this is the <s>yukta</s> (congruent) variety, a principal-element-predominated <s>rūpaka</s>.
Here, although the figurative usage <s>padmākara</s> (lotus-pond) relies on secondary meaning, and the word itself is embellished by its modifiers, nonetheless through the power of double meaning (<s>śleṣa</s>), the primary sense prevails — meaning and word both having predominance — hence this is indeed meaning-predominated.
<s>Ayukta</s> (incongruent) — as follows:

children.text: kīrtyamṛtaṃ śuci dadhatī dhārāgaralena vidadhatī bhītim /
children.translated_text: Bearing the pure nectar of fame, and instilling fear with the poison-stream of its edge,
O King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>, your sword-river <s>Kālindī</s> (Yamunā) gleams. // Ckc_8.*35 //

children.text: atrāropyamāṇayoḥ sudhāgaralayoḥ svabhāva viruddhatvena parasparasaṃgatyayogatvādayukttaṃ nāmāṅgipradhānaṃ rupakam /
children.translated_text: Here, since nectar and poison — the superimposed elements — are by nature mutually contradictory and therefore incongruent with each other, this is the <s>ayukta</s> (incongruent) variety, a principal-element-predominated <s>rūpaka</s>.
The wise know the subordinate-element-predominated (<s>aṅga-pradhāna</s>) type to be of four kinds,
distinguished by the conditions of being natural (<s>sahaja</s>), acquired (<s>āhārya</s>), their combination (<s>tadyoga</s>), and their disparity (<s>tadvaiṣamya</s>). // Ckc_8.23 //
Of these, natural subordinate-element-predominated (<s>sahajāṅga-pradhāna</s>) — as follows:
Adorned with clusters of breast-buds, bedecked with smile-blossoms, with tender delicate arm-creepers reddened at their leaf-tips of lips,

children.text: sāmantakṣitipairupāyanatayā sevāturairarpitāḥ śrīsiṅgakṣitipālamādaramayaṃ kurvanti kanyālatāḥ // Ckc_8.*36 //
children.translated_text: offered by feudatory kings as tribute with devotion — these maiden-vines delight King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s> with affection. // Ckc_8.*36 //

children.text: atra kanyāpakṣe payodhara mandasmitabhujādaralakṣaṇānāṃ latāpakṣe mañjarīprasūnadvirephapatrlavarūpāṇāṃ cāvayavānāṃ nāyakotsukīkaraṇe prādhānyamiti sahajāṅgapradhānarūpakamidam /
children.translated_text: Here, in the maiden-aspect, the parts — breasts, gentle smile, arms, and lips — and in the creeper-aspect, the parts — flower-clusters, blossoms, bees, and leaves — have predominance in arousing the hero's desire. Hence this is a natural subordinate-element-predominated <s>rūpaka</s>.
Acquired-predominated (<s>āhārya-pradhāna</s>) — as follows:
With scorching heat of the prowess that spreads to the ends of the directions, favorable in its rising for the delight of the lotuses of kinsmen,
causing the downfall of the pride of the departure of fierce terrifying enemies, (this fame) girds itself for the destruction of the <s>ketaka</s>-leaf of enemy kings' glory. // Ckc_8.*37 //

children.text: atra nāyakavijayayātrāpakṣe pratāpabandhuvairikīrtilakṣaṇānāṃ śaratpakṣe ātapapuṇḍarīkaketakaprasūnānāṃ cāvayavatayā kalpitatvādāhāryāṇāṃ saṃnahane prādhānyamityāhāryāṅgapradhānaṃ rūpakamitīdamubhaya prādhānyam /
children.translated_text: Here, in the context of the hero's victory-march, prowess, kinsmen, enemies, and glory — and in the autumn context, heat, lotuses, <s>ketaka</s> flowers — since these are artificially attributed as subordinate parts, and their predominance lies in the girding (for battle), this is an acquired subordinate-element-predominated <s>rūpaka</s>. This is also a case of dual predominance.
Their combination (<s>tadyoga</s>) — as follows:
O fierce and terrifying lord, from the fire of your sword's prowess rises the dense cloud of sword-smoke, fierce with sparks of wrath,
with flames blazing from the arrow-tips spread across the hollows of the directions — (this fire) is perceived (consuming) the dense forest of the enemy kings' armies. // Ckc_8.*38 //

children.text: atra nāyakapratāpapakṣe kṛpāṇakrodhaviśikhamukhalakṣaṇānāmāhāryāṇāmanalapakṣe dhūmasphuliṅgaśikhānāṃ sahajānāṃ cāvayavānāṃ rupakāṇāṃ vairirājanyakṣobhakaraṇe prādhānyamiti sahajāhāryāṅgapradhānaṃ rūpakamidam /
children.translated_text: Here, in the hero's prowess context, the acquired parts — sword, wrath, and arrow-tips — and in the fire context, the natural parts — smoke, sparks, and flames — since both types of subordinate metaphors have predominance in causing terror to the enemy kings, this is a natural-and-acquired combined subordinate-element-predominated <s>rūpaka</s>.
Disparity (<s>vaiṣamya</s>) — as follows:
Upon the arm-serpent of King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>, with copper-colored finger-leaves, firmly rooted on the broad and beautiful shoulder, resplendent with auspicious lines of bangles,
far-reaching, chastising wicked fortress-ministers with anointed arrogance — the earth rests comfortably upon that shoulder, steadfast in its position. // Ckc_8.*39 //

children.text: atra bhujāvayavino bhujagatayā rūpaṇe kṛte tadavayavānāmaṅgulīnāṃ patrlavatārūpayā rūpaṇayā padāntarāṇāṃ skandhaśubharekhāṇāṃ rūpaṇaṃ ceti sarvato vaiṣamyāt tāmrāṅgutryādīnāṃ bhāgyadvārā dharaṇībharaṇasthairye prādhānyācca tadidaṃ viṣamāṅgapradhānaṃ rūpakam /
children.translated_text: Here, when the arm (<s>avayavin</s>) is metaphorically described as a serpent, its subordinate parts — the fingers as leaves, the shoulder and auspicious lines as other elements — are described in completely disparate (non-matching) metaphorical attributions. Since the copper-colored fingers and the rest have predominance through fortune in supporting the earth steadfastly, this is the disparate subordinate-element-predominated (<s>viṣamāṅga-pradhāna</s>) <s>rūpaka</s>.

children.text: dvidhā śabhdārthamukhyassyāt kevalaṃ vyatireki ca // Ckc_8.24 //
children.translated_text: The type predominated by both word and meaning is of two kinds: simple (<s>kevala</s>) and contrastive (<s>vyatirekin</s>). // Ckc_8.24 //
<s>Kevala</s> (simple) — as follows:
Causing the delight of blue lotuses, eager for the anointing of the dark-complexioned one,
may King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>, the moon who is also the maker of nectar, shine forth. // Ckc_8.*40 //

children.text: atra nāyakāvayavinaḥ kuvalayasya candratayā rūpaṇena śabdaprādhānyamuktaśliṣṭaviśeṣaṇa viśeṣādarthasya prādhānyamiti kevalā nāmedamubhayapradhānaṃ rūpakam /
children.translated_text: Here, through the metaphorical description of the hero's subsidiary (<s>kuvalaya</s>, blue lotus) as the moon, word-predominance is established; and through the skillfully joined specific attributes, meaning-predominance is also established — hence this is the <s>kevala</s> (simple) variety, a <s>rūpaka</s> with dual predominance of both word and meaning.
<s>Vyatirekika</s> (contrastive) — as follows:

children.text: abhaṅgo vārāśiḥ vigalitakalaṅko himarucir vivekī hemādriḥ kalitanijamūrtī ratipatiḥ /
children.translated_text: An unbroken ocean, a spotless moon, a discerning golden mountain, <s>Ratipati</s> (Kāmadeva) embodied in his own form,

children.text: anindyo devendraḥ kuṭilagatihīno bhujagarāḍ janānāṃ bhāgyena kṣitimavati siṅgakṣitipatiḥ // Ckc_8.*41 //
children.translated_text: a blameless <s>Devendra</s>, the serpent-king free of crooked movement — by the fortune of the people, King <s>Siṅga</s> protects the earth. // Ckc_8.*41 //

children.text: atra vārāśiprabhṛtīnāmabhaṅgādiviśeṣaṇāṅkuritavyatirekāṇāṃ nāyakasāmānādhikaraṇyena kathanādarthata śśabdataḥ prādhānyamavadhāryata iti vyatirekavannāmobhayapradhānaṃ rūpakam /
children.translated_text: Here, since the ocean and others — qualified by contrast-indicating attributes like 'unbroken' — are stated in co-reference with the hero, both meaning-predominance and word-predominance are discerned. Hence this is the <s>vyatirekavat</s> (contrastive) variety, a <s>rūpaka</s> with dual predominance.
Thus the form of <s>rūpaka</s> has been described in eighteen varieties.
The mixed (<s>saṅkīrṇa</s>) type, due to its composite nature, does not exceed (these varieties) through combination. // Ckc_8.25 //
<s>Vidyādhara</s>'s (categorization into) separated (<s>vyasta</s>) and other types within <s>rūpaka</s> does not produce aesthetic wonder (<s>camatkāra</s>).
The root cause (of this deficiency) is his difficulty in constructing examples (<s>lakṣya</s>). // Ckc_8.26 //
Where the similarity of two things is apprehended through the elegance of expression of both,
yet differs from both <s>upamā</s> (simile) and <s>rūpaka</s> (metaphor) — that is <s>sāmya</s> (similarity), the pride of equality. // Ckc_8.27 //

children.text:
seyaṃ prapañcadṛpṭāntaprativastūktibhistridhā /
avivādiḥ prapañcoktiḥ sāmyotkarṣāprakarṣa bhāk // Ckc_8.28 //
children.translated_text:
This (<s>sāmya</s>) is of three kinds: <s>prapañcokti</s> (elaborate statement), <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (illustration), and <s>prativastūkti</s> (counter-statement).
The undisputed <s>prapañcokti</s> possesses equality, superiority, and inferiority. // Ckc_8.28 //
Here, the equality-possessing <s>prapañcokti</s> — as follows:
... with fruits of observance and words ripened for the learned,

children.text: svaraṃ vīṇākvāṇairlalitamupadhā vārasudṛśāṃ jigīṣā yātrāyāṃ bharitadiśi siṅgakṣitipatiḥ // Ckc_8.*42 //
children.translated_text: with the melody of <s>vīṇā</s> sounds sweetly for beautiful courtesans — King <s>Siṅga</s>, desirous of conquest on the march, fills the directions. // Ckc_8.*42 //

children.text:
atra kulagiri drākṣāphalavipañcīkvāṇānāmupamānānāṃ mattebhasāhityagāyikāsvarāṇāmupameyānāṃ tulādhṛtavatsāmyamitītyādidyotakamantareṇāpi caturoktibhaṅgyā pratīyata iti seyaṃ sāmyavatī prakṛtaprapañcoktirnāma sāmyālaṅkārabhaṅgaḥ /
seyaṃ vikṛtāpi saṃbhavati /
children.translated_text:
Here, the <s>upamānas</s> (standards of comparison) — mountain-grapes, fruits, and <s>vīṇā</s>-tones — and the <s>upameyas</s> (things compared) — the company of intoxicated elephants, singer's melodies — are held in balance as equals. Even without an explicit marker of comparison, the equality is perceived through the fourfold elegance of expression. Hence this is the equality-possessing natural <s>prapañcokti</s>, a variety of <s>sāmya</s> (similarity) alaṅkāra.
This can also occur in modified form.
As follows:

children.text: mimīte mattebhaiḥ kulagirikulaṃ tuṅgaśikharaṃ phalāni drākṣāṇāṃ vacanaparipākaiḥ kṛtadhiyām /
children.translated_text: He measures the lofty peaks of the noble mountain ranges with intoxicated elephants, the fruits of grapes with the ripened words of the learned,

children.text: vipañcīnikvāṇaṃ śrutibhirupadhā vārasudṛsāṃ jigoṣā yātrāyāṃ bharitadiśi siṅgakṣitipatiḥ // Ckc_8.*43 //
children.translated_text: the <s>vīṇā</s>-melody with the songs of beautiful courtesans — King <s>Siṅga</s>, desirous of conquest on the march, fills the directions. // Ckc_8.*43 //

children.text: atra kulaśailādīnāmupameyatvaṃ mattebhānāmupamānatvaṃ ca prasiddhavaiparīṃtyena kalpitamiti seyaṃ vikṛtaprapañcoktirnāma sāmyabhedaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, since the <s>upameya</s>-status of the mountain ranges and the <s>upamāna</s>-status of the intoxicated elephants are assigned in reverse of their well-known roles, this is the modified <s>prapañcokti</s>, a variety of <s>sāmya</s>.
The natural (variety), with superiority — as follows:

children.text: mā garvīyata medini sumanaso recarlavaṃśāgraṇīḥ śrīsiṅgakṣitipālako vitaraṇairmuṣṇāti tṛṣṇāmiti /
children.translated_text: O earth, do not be proud! O you who are the foremost of the (?)-lineage, King <s>Siṅga</s> steals away thirst through his gifts — thus (you might say).

But there exist such industrious ones as the <s>Surabhī</s> (wish-granting cow), the <s>Kalpadruma</s> (wish-fulfilling tree), the <s>Cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-jewel) lines, and the <s>Siddharasa</s> (elixir) — victorious with their clouds of compassion and their supporting frameworks. // Ckc_8.*44 //

children.text:
atra bhobho viśvaṃbharāmarāḥ kimanenaiva vitaraṇaśālinā nāyakena garvāyadhve /
diviṣadāṃ punaranekasantatikalpavṛkṣādayo dātāra ityupamānotkarṣādiyamutkarṣavatī prapañcoktirnāma sāmyabhaktiḥ /
children.translated_text: Here — O earth, O gods! What is the use of being proud of this gift-bestowing hero alone? For the celestials have many lineages of wish-fulfilling trees and other donors. Since the <s>upamāna</s> (standard of comparison) is shown as superior, this is the superiority-possessing <s>prapañcokti</s>, a variety of <s>sāmya</s>.
The same, with inferiority — as follows:

children.text: kurvanmārjitamambare jalanidhau saṃkṣālayan gharṣayan dehaṃ meruśilāsu candraki javaṃ nakttaṃ divaṃ bhrāmyase /
children.translated_text: O moon, polishing (yourself) in the sky, washing in the ocean, rubbing your body on the stones of <s>Meru</s>, you wander swiftly night and day.

children.text: kiṃ kṛtvā hṛdi siṅgabhūpatiyaśo rājāsi kiṃ bhrūmahe satyaṃ śakyamapohituṃ nahi nahi svābhāvikī śyāmikā // Ckc_8.*45 //
children.translated_text: What have you accomplished? Having taken the fame of King <s>Siṅgabhūpa</s> to heart — are you a king? What can we say? Truly, the natural darkness (of your spots) cannot be removed — no, no indeed! // Ckc_8.*45 //

children.text:
atropameyānnāyakayaśovilāsādupamānasya candrasyāpakarṣa ityapakarṣavatī nāma prapañcoktiḥ /
anayaiva bhaṅgyā vikṛtirapi lakṣaṇīyā /
children.translated_text:
Here, compared to the <s>upameya</s> — the hero's fame-splendor — the <s>upamāna</s> moon is shown as inferior. Hence this is the inferiority-possessing <s>prapañcokti</s>.
By this same method, the modified variety can also be understood.
When a good marker of similarity exists along with a real counterpart, it is called <s>dṛṣṭāntokti</s> (illustrative statement).
This, through mixed and unmixed actions and the like, becomes manifold. // Ckc_8.29 //
Here, with mixed action — as follows:
Returning as she returns, advancing as she advances,
like a shadow, <s>Lakṣmī</s> (prosperity) constantly follows the glance of King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>. // Ckc_8.*46 //

children.text:
atra kevalanivartanādikriyāyogajanitaṃ sāmyaṃ vā dṛṣṭāntapūrvamiti seyaṃ kevalakriyāyogavatī dṛṣṭāntoktiḥ /
miśrakriyāyogavatī saiva yathā atraiva dvitīyapādasthāne kṛtaprasādāṃ racitaprasādetipāṭhe nivartanakriyā prasādaguṇanimittasāmyā miśrakriyāyogavatīyaṃ dṛṣṭāntoktiḥ /
evaṃ miśrāmiśrajātiguṇadravyayoganimittā dṛṣṭāntoktayo draṣṭavyāḥ /
nanu dṛṣṭāntoktteḥ dṛṣṭāntālaṅkārasya vā ko viśeṣaḥ /
śrūyatām /
laukikaparīkṣakāṇāṃ yasminnarthe bṛddhisāmyaṃ sa dṛṣṭānta ityarthaṃ prati na kaścidbhedaḥ /
uktibhaṅgimuddiśya punaraneko vidyate /
yathā hi sādhyasiddhiprayojano dṛṣṭāntaḥ /
sādharmyaṃsiddhiprayojanādṛṣṭāntoktiḥ /
dṛṣṭānte dyotakagandho 'pi nānusandhīyate /
iha tu dyotakaprayogasyādhikāra ityādyata eveyamubhayālaṅkriyā /
children.translated_text:
Here, the similarity born of the conjunction of mere actions of returning and the like, presented with an illustration — this is the <s>dṛṣṭāntokti</s> (illustrative statement) possessing only pure action-conjunction.
The same with mixed action-conjunction: in this very verse, with the alternative reading '<s>kṛtaprasādāṃ racitaprasāda</s>' in place of the second quarter — since the action of returning is combined with the quality of grace/beauty — this becomes a <s>dṛṣṭāntokti</s> possessing mixed action-conjunction.
Likewise, <s>dṛṣṭāntoktis</s> possessing mixed and unmixed conjunctions of class, quality, and substance should be observed.
Now, what is the difference between <s>dṛṣṭāntokti</s> and <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (illustration) as an alaṅkāra?
Listen: For worldly examiners, when there is equality of cognition regarding a certain meaning, that is <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> (illustration) — in this respect there is no difference regarding the meaning. But with regard to the mode of expression, there are many differences. Just as <s>dṛṣṭānta</s> has the purpose of establishing what is to be proved, <s>dṛṣṭāntokti</s> has the purpose of establishing concordance (<s>sādharmya</s>). In <s>dṛṣṭānta</s>, not even a trace of an explicit marker is employed; but here, the use of an explicit marker is the norm — thus from the very beginning this is a figure ornamenting both (sides).
Having presented a certain subject, through the arrangement of something possessing the same characteristics —
similarity is understood — this is called <s>Prativastūkti</s> (counter-statement). // Ckc_8.30 //
<s>Prativastūkti</s> is considered to be of two kinds, having the semblance of <s>Dṛṣṭāntokti</s> (illustration-statement) and <s>Prapañcokti</s> (elaboration-statement). // Ckc_8.31 //
<s>Prativastūkti</s> with the semblance of <s>Dṛṣṭāntokti</s>, for example:

children.text: mattebhāsurabhāsurājinapaṭe sphūrjatkaṭe dhūrjaṭe- rāśaṅkyeta yataḥ kutaścana mṛge nyakkāraḍhakkāravaḥ /
children.translated_text: Since from <s>Dhūrjaṭi</s> (Śiva), who wears a resplendent elephant-hide garment and whose matted locks bristle, one might apprehend a roar of contempt toward some deer or other,

children.text: yadyanyairanavadyapadyayaśasaḥ śrīsiṅgabhūśārṅiṇo bhūpālairabhilakṣyate raṇamukhe bhrūbhaṅgabhīmaṃ mukham // Ckc_8.*47 //
children.translated_text: so too, when the face of <s>Śrī Siṅgabhūpāla</s>, whose fame is of faultless verses, fierce with the furrowing of brows, is observed on the battlefield by other kings — // Ckc_8.*47 //

children.text:
atra dṛṣṭāntarūpaṃ vastu prathamamupanyastam /
