dārṣṭāntikaṃ prativastu paścāditi dṛṭāntoktichāyāvatīyaṃ prativastūktirnāma sāmyabhaktiḥ /
children.translated_text: Here the illustrative object (<s>dṛṣṭānta</s>) is presented first, and the counter-object (<s>prativastu</s>) corresponding to the illustration follows afterward — thus this <s>Prativastūkti</s> bearing the semblance of <s>Dṛṣṭāntokti</s> is a variety of <s>sāmyabhakti</s> (similarity-type).
<s>Prativastūkti</s> with the semblance of <s>Prapañcokti</s>, for example:

children.text: śrīsiṅgakṣitipāśrayā yadi kathā merorna me rocate tadvaktrasya vilokanaṃ yadi vṛthā candrasya saṃdarśanam /
children.translated_text: If the talk is about the refuge of <s>Śrī Siṅgakṣitipāla</s>, then the sight of <s>Meru</s> does not please me; if the beholding of that face is futile, then the viewing of the moon is pointless;

children.text: tadgoṣṭhī yadi pṛṣṭhato na viśate sā mādhavī mādhurī tatsevā yadi siddhameva sudhiyāmavyājabhavyārjanam // Ckc_8.*48 //
children.translated_text: if that company does not enter from behind, then the sweetness of the <s>Mādhavī</s> creeper is in vain; if that service is accomplished, then for the wise, unpretentious and noble acquisition is assured. // Ckc_8.*48 //

children.text: atropamānāpakarṣastriṣvartheṣu caturthe tu samatvamiti prapañcoktichāyāvatī prativastūktiḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, in the first three meanings there is diminishment of the <s>upamāna</s> (standard of comparison), while in the fourth there is equality — thus this is <s>Prativastūkti</s> bearing the semblance of <s>Prapañcokti</s>.
Thus the <s>alaṅkāra</s> (figure of speech) of similarity has been described in general terms.
But the distinctions should be observed by the discerning in the elaboration of examples. // Ckc_8.32 //
Where the mind vacillates due to excessive similarity between two things,
that is regarded as <s>Saṃśayokti</s> (expression of doubt), which may be <s>ekaviṣayā</s> (single-object) or <s>anekaviṣayā</s> (multi-object). // Ckc_8.33 //

children.text:
syādekaviṣayānekaṃ yatraikatra viśahkyate /
yatratvaikamanekatra sānekaviṣayā smṛtā // Ckc_8.34 //
children.translated_text: Where many things are doubted in a single object, that is <s>ekaviṣayā</s>; where one thing is doubted in many objects, that is known as <s>anekaviṣayā</s>. // Ckc_8.34 //
An example of <s>ekaviṣayā</s>:

children.text: śākāhāraparigraho giridarīṣvekāntacintā ratiḥ śayyā sthaṇḍila eva bhūtidhavalā mūrtirjaṭālaṃ śiraḥ /
children.translated_text: A diet of vegetables, delight in solitary contemplation in mountain caves, a bed on bare ground, a body white with sacred ash, a head covered with matted locks,

children.text: aṅgānyasthimayāni hanta sutarāṃ kiṃ vā tapasvī bhavā- nuddaṇḍapratigaṇḍabhairavavibhoḥ kiṃ vā virodhī nṛpaḥ // Ckc_8.*49 //
children.translated_text: limbs that appear skeletal — alas! Is this an ascetic, or is this a king hostile to the Lord whose fierce cheek is terrible with upraised staff? // Ckc_8.*49 //

children.text: atraikasminneva puruṣalakṣaṇe vastuni tapasmitvanāyaka virodhitvalakṣaṇayorvastutorabhidhīyamānasāmānyapratīterviśeṣādarśanādubhayagataviśeṣasmaraṇācca vimarśa iti jñeyamekayiṣayā nāma saṃśayoktiḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, regarding a single object — a person's appearance — since the common perception of the two properties, namely asceticism and enmity toward the hero, is being expressed, and since the distinguishing features are not visible, yet the distinctive characteristics pertaining to both are recalled, this deliberation (<s>vimarśa</s>) should be understood as <s>Saṃśayokti</s> called <s>ekaviṣayā</s>.
An example of <s>anekaviṣayā</s>:

children.text: dvau netrānandakandau jagati kuvalayaprīṇane jāgarūkau sanmārgaikapradārapravaṇanijamatī pūryamāṇau kalābhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Two sources of delight for the eyes exist in the world, ever wakeful in gladdening the lotuses, inclined to illuminating the sole path of virtue, being filled with digits (<s>kalā</s>).

children.text: tatkovā siṅgapṛthvītilakaḥ konu rākāmṛgāṅkaḥ kā jyotsnā kā ca kīrtiściramati vimṛśan naiva nājāmi tattvam // Ckc_8.*50 //
children.translated_text: Who then is <s>Siṅgapṛthvītilaka</s>? Who is the full-moon? Which is moonlight and which is fame? Deliberating long, I cannot at all determine the truth. // Ckc_8.*50 //

children.text:
atrābhidhīyamānasādṛśyayornāyakatārakānāyakayoḥ pratyekamubhayamā śaṅkyata iti seyam /
iyaṃ pratīta sāmyāpi saṃbhavati yathā atraiva kā ñcotsnā kā ca kīrtiriti jyotsnāpratīta dhāvalyādisāmyayoḥ pratyekamubhayamāśaṅkyata iti seyaṃ pratīta varṇanasāmyānekaviṣayā /
evamekaviṣayāpi lakṣaṇīyā /
nanu vitarkasaṃśayālaṅkārayoḥ ko viśeṣaḥ /
śrūyatām /
koṭidvayāvalambivimarśaḥ saṃśayaḥ /
nyakkṛtaikakoṭistu vitarkaḥ /
kiñcinnirṇayāmanno vitarkaḥ /
vitarkāsannaḥ saṃśayaḥ /
tathā hi saṃdihāno vitarkakoṭimāruhya tarkakakṣyāṃ parityajya tattvamevābhiniviśate /
children.translated_text: Here, regarding the two objects possessing expressed similarity — the hero and the moon — each is doubted to be the other; thus this is that type. This can also occur with perceived similarity, as in the same verse: 'which is moonlight and which is fame?' — since each of the two, moonlight and fame, possessing similarity in whiteness and such qualities, is doubted to be the other, this is <s>anekaviṣayā</s> based on similarity of perceived description. The <s>ekaviṣayā</s> type should be understood similarly. Now, what is the distinction between the <s>alaṅkāras</s> of <s>Vitarka</s> (conjecture) and <s>Saṃśaya</s> (doubt)? Listen: <s>Saṃśaya</s> is deliberation resting on two alternatives. <s>Vitarka</s>, however, has one alternative set aside. Moreover, <s>Vitarka</s> approaches a determination; <s>Saṃśaya</s> is close to <s>Vitarka</s>. Thus, a doubting person, ascending the alternative of conjecture, abandoning the level of reasoning, settles upon the truth itself.
Where something is concealed and something else — whether similar or dissimilar —

children.text: anyasya vastuno nyāso yatra sāpaṅnutirmatā // Ckc_8.35 //
children.translated_text: is placed in its stead, that is regarded as <s>Apahnuti</s> (concealment/denial). // Ckc_8.35 //
An example of <s>Apahnuti</s> with the placement of a similar object:

children.text: neyaṃ śāradakaumudī sakhi yaśaḥ śrīsiṅgapṛthvīpateḥ naitaccañcalacañcarīkapaṭalaṃ taddveṣiṇāṃ duryaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: This is not the autumnal moonlight, O friend — it is the fame of <s>Śrī Siṅgapṛthvīpati</s>; this is not a swarm of flitting bees — it is the infamy of his enemies;

children.text: nedaṃ kokilakūjitaṃ mṛgadṛśāṃ tatkīrtisaṃgītami- tyālāpānanusaṃdadhāti sudṛśo dūrapriyāyāḥ sakhi // Ckc_8.*51 //
children.translated_text: this is not the cooing of the cuckoo — it is the song of his glory for the doe-eyed women: thus a lady whose beloved is far away strings together such utterances, O friend. // Ckc_8.*51 //

children.text: atra satyarūpāpi candrikācañcarīkakokilakūjitāni vacanādapahnutya pratīyamanasādṛśyāni nāyakakīrtitatparipandhiduṣkīrtigāyikāsvaralakṣaṇānyanyāni vastūnyupanyastānīti seyaṃ sādṛśyavatyapahnutiḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, though the moonlight, bees, and cuckoo's cooing are real, they are verbally denied, and other objects — possessing perceived similarity, characterized as the hero's fame, the infamy of his adversaries, and the song of female singers — are placed instead. Thus this is <s>Apahnuti</s> possessing similarity (<s>sādṛśyavatī</s>).
An example of the dissimilar type (<s>asādṛśyavatī</s>):

children.text: netraṃ hanta vataṃsaguccharajasā bāṣpāyate dūṣitaṃ gātraṃ spṛṭamanena mandamarutā romāñcamālaṃbate /
children.translated_text: Alas, the eye weeps, contaminated by the dust of the ear-ornament's cluster; the body, touched by this gentle breeze, experiences horripilation;

children.text: nānyatkāraṇamityudīritavatī kāciddhṛdīcchāgate śrīsiṅgakṣitipālake nijasakhī mandasmitairlajjate // Ckc_8.*52 //
children.translated_text: there is no other cause — so declares a certain woman, while in her heart she desires <s>Śrī Siṅgakṣitipālaka</s>, and her own friend smiles gently in embarrassment. // Ckc_8.*52 //

children.text: atra lajjāśīlayā (kayā) cajidānaṃdabāṣparomāñcakāraṇaṃ nāyakaviṣayamanurāgamapahnutya visadṛśavirāgapavanalakṣaṇakāraṇopanyāsaḥ kalpita iti seyamasādṛśyavatī nāmāpahnutiḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, a bashful woman conceals the cause of tears of joy and horripilation — namely, her love directed toward the hero — and fabricates a dissimilar cause, characterized by dust and wind. Thus this is the <s>Apahnuti</s> called <s>asādṛśyavatī</s> (possessing dissimilarity).
<s>Samādhyukti</s> (superimposition-expression) is considered to be the superimposition of the properties of one thing upon another. // Ckc_8.36 //

children.text: anyasyānyadharmasya tadubhayasya ceti vyutpattyā dharmiṇoradhyāse dharmasyādhyāse dharmadharmiṇoradhyāse ca trividhaḥ samādhiḥ /
children.translated_text: By derivation — of another <s>dharmin</s> (property-bearer), of another <s>dharma</s> (property), and of both — <s>samādhi</s> (superimposition) is threefold: superimposition of property-bearers (<s>dharmisamādhi</s>), superimposition of properties (<s>dharmasamādhi</s>), and superimposition of both property and property-bearer (<s>ubhayasamādhi</s>).
An example of superimposition of property-bearers alone:

children.text: pakṣāṇāṃ kurute sa tatkṣaṇamayaṃ yutpakṣarakṣāmaṇiḥ durgāpāśrayaṇaṃ tvabhīrumanasornaivāsya saṃbhāvyate /
children.translated_text: He instantly provides protection of wings — that jewel of wing-protection; but taking refuge in a fortress is never expected of his fearless mind.

children.text: itthaṃ cintayatāmiva kṣitijaye śrīsiṅgapṛthvīpate tvayyāsannacare kulakṣitibhṛtāṃ labghodayā stabdhatā // Ckc_8.*53 //
children.translated_text: Thus, as if deliberating, O <s>Śrī Siṅgapṛthvīpati</s>, when you advance nearby in conquest of the earth, the mountain-kings attain a state of established immobility. // Ckc_8.*53 //

children.text: atra pakṣaparirakṣaṇādi dharmāropamapahāya nāyake taddharmavataḥ parvataśāsanasyaivādhyāsādayaṃ dharmisamādhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, setting aside the superimposition of properties such as protection of wings and the like, the property-bearer — the mountain-ruler itself, possessing those properties — is superimposed upon the hero. Thus this is <s>dharmisamādhi</s> (superimposition of property-bearers).
An example of <s>dharmasamādhi</s> (superimposition of properties):

children.text: śrīsiṅgabhūpāla tava pratāpe jitvā pradīpte tapanapratāpam /
children.translated_text: O <s>Śrī Siṅgabhūpāla</s>, when your valor blazes forth, having conquered the heat of the sun,
this fame of yours, with its inner parts budding, freely embraces the horizons. // Ckc_8.*54 //

children.text: atra nāyakapratāpanāyakakīrtī diktaṭeṣvacetanāsu yathākramaṃ bhaṭapratibhaṭatatsalakṣaṇadharme samārepamapahāya jayaparājayaharṣāliṅganataraṅgollāsarūpataddharmā eva samāropitā iti seyaṃ dharmasamādhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the hero's valor and the hero's fame, upon the inanimate horizons, setting aside the superimposition of the property-bearers characterized as warriors, adversaries, and their companions respectively, only the properties themselves — victory, defeat, joy, embracing, and the surging forth — are superimposed. Thus this is <s>dharmasamādhi</s>.
An example of superimposition of both the properties and the property-bearers:

children.text: prāk saṃbhūta bhiyābhibhūtaraśanāpṛṣṭhe kṛtāhaṃ kitāṃ daṃṣṭrāgreṇa vikampitā paraśatairākramya nītāṃghriṇā /
children.translated_text: Previously, having been placed on the back of <s>Śeṣa</s>, who was overcome with fear, I was made to tremble at the tip of the tusk; having been invaded by hundreds of enemies, I was carried away on foot;

children.text: raktteḥ kardamitojjhitā pitṛgirā netikṛṣṇeti kiṃ (?) raicarlīyakulodbhavena bhavatā seyaṃ sthirā manyate // Ckc_8.*55 //
children.translated_text: stained with blood, I was abandoned; summoned by the father's voice, 'Come, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>' — what? By you, born in the lineage of the Raicarlī clan, am I to be considered stable? // Ckc_8.*55 //

children.text: atra nāyake nārāyaṇasya dharmiṇāṃ taddhardhāṇāṃ matsyādibalabhadrāntāvatārakalpitānāṃ jaldhisaṃkṣobhaṇā diraśanāsamāropaṇādayamubhayasamādhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the superimposition upon the hero of the property-bearers — the imagined <s>avatāras</s> of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> from <s>Matsya</s> to <s>Balarāma</s> — along with their properties such as churning the ocean and the like, constitutes <s>ubhayasamādhi</s> (superimposition of both).
Where the <s>upameya</s> (thing compared) is understood from what is stated about the <s>upamāna</s> (standard of comparison),
due to extreme familiarity — the wise call that <s>Samāsokti</s> (concise expression). // Ckc_8.37 //

children.text: ślāghāṃ garhāmupālaṃbhaṃ prāpteyaṃ trividhā bhavet // Ckc_8.38 //
children.translated_text: <s>Samāsokti</s> becomes threefold, involving <s>ślāghā</s> (praise), <s>garhā</s> (censure), and <s>upālaṃbha</s> (reproach). // Ckc_8.38 //
An example of the praise-type (<s>ślāghāvatī</s>):
By <s>Dhanvin-Sindhu</s> (the archer-river), who is a kinsman in binding the wounds of travelers afflicted by thirst and misery,
the fulfillment of birth is now attained. // Ckc_8.*56 //

children.text: atra pathikajanaprāṇarakṣaṇa marudeśasamādhinopamānena pratīyamānayā ca pathikajanarakṣaṇalakṣaṇasādhāraṇadharmasya kalidoṣakaluṣībhūtarājalokabhūlokaikaparāyaṇasya siṅgabhūpālasyoktisiddhau tacchāyaiva ślāghā pratīyata iti seyaṃ ślāghāvatī samāsoktiḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, through the <s>samādhi</s> (superimposition) upon the desert — by means of the <s>upamāna</s> — and through the similarity perceived in the common property of protecting traveler-folk, the praise of <s>Siṅgabhūpāla</s>, who is the sole refuge of the royal world and the earthly world polluted by the blemishes of <s>Kali</s>, is perceived as implicit through the statement itself (<s>uktisiddha</s>). Thus this is <s>Samāsokti</s> of the praise-type.
The same as the censure-type (<s>garhāvatī</s>), for example:

children.text: ekā daityagurorubhe murabhidastisraḥ paśūnāṃ prabhor aṣṭau dvādaśa padmagarbhaguhayorlaṅkāpaterviśatiḥ /
children.translated_text: One eye belongs to the preceptor of the <s>Daityas</s>; two to the slayer of <s>Mura</s>; three to the Lord of beasts (<s>Paśupati</s>); eight to <s>Padmagarbha</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>); twelve to <s>Guha</s> (<s>Skanda</s>); twenty to the lord of <s>Laṅkā</s> (<s>Rāvaṇa</s>);

children.text: asmākaṃ tu dṛśaḥ sahasramiti mā garvīya vāstoṣpate mākrodhītarāgatismaraṇatokta lajjā nu ...... tebhavet (?) // Ckc_8.*57 //
children.translated_text: but we have a thousand eyes — do not be proud, O <s>Vāstoṣpati</s>! Do not be angry — remembering another course, would there not be shame...? // Ckc_8.*57 //

children.text: atrāhalyābhisaraṇadoṣanimittasiddhalocana sahasreṇa tadādhikyādeva bhārgavādiviśiṣṭajanatiraskāriṇā duścyavanenaivopamānena pratīyamānasāmānyasyānyāyopārjitasamṛddheḥ nyāyamārgapravaṇa siṅgabhūpālādiprabhuvargavibhāṣeṇa kasya cid bhūpālādhamasyopameyasyoktisiddhāvupamāna dvāreṇaivopameyanindā vivakṣiteti garhāvatīyaṃ samāsoktiḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, by the <s>upamāna</s> itself — <s>Duścyavana</s> (Indra), who possesses a thousand eyes as a result of the sin of approaching <s>Ahalyā</s>, and who by that very excess belittles distinguished persons such as <s>Bhārgava</s> and others — the censure of the <s>upameya</s>, some base king who has acquired wealth by unjust means, while the righteous <s>Siṅgabhūpāla</s> and other lords following the path of justice serve as contrast, is conveyed through the <s>upamāna</s> itself. Thus this is <s>Samāsokti</s> of the censure-type.
An example of the reproach-type (<s>upālaṃbhavatī</s>):

children.text: api mṛdulairapi pravālairapi kusumairapi tiktatāṃ viditvā /
children.translated_text: Even with tender shoots, even with flowers, even knowing its bitterness,

children.text: upavasasi sakhe palāśayā kiṃ pariṇatavānapi tikta eva nimbaḥ // Ckc_8.*58 //
children.translated_text: why do you dwell near the <s>Palāśa</s> tree, O friend? Even when mature, the <s>Nimba</s> (neem) tree is indeed bitter. // Ckc_8.*58 //

children.text: atra tiktatā mūrdhābhiṣikttena nijenaivopamānena pratīyamānasādṛsyasyaiva niṣkamparase guṇahīnasya kasyacidavarṇanīyasyoktisiddhau pariṇatavānapi tikta evetyupālaṃbhoktirupamānajādupameyamavalaṃbata itīyamupālaṃbhavatī samāsoktiḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the bitterness — through the <s>upamāna</s> crowned as supreme — and the perceived similarity, serve to express reproach toward some indescribable person devoid of virtues and steadfast in his unpleasant disposition, established through the statement itself: 'even when mature, it is indeed bitter.' The reproach-expression, based on the <s>upamāna</s>, reaches the <s>upameya</s>. Thus this is <s>Samāsokti</s> of the reproach-type.
An example of the expressed-similarity praise-type (<s>abhidhīyamānasādṛśyā ślāghāvatī</s>):

children.text: dhṛterādhārasya sphuṭaraṭita śuddhaiḥ kṛtamudā sarasvatyā nityaṃ prakaṭitasuvahṇaprasarayā /
children.translated_text: Of him who is the foundation of steadfastness, with joy produced by clearly resounding pure sounds, by <s>Sarasvatī</s> ever manifesting a stream of excellent fire,

children.text: sudharmātambānāmiha sumanasāmekavasate- ssuvarṇādreḥ kṣoṇībharaṇamucitaṃ netaragireḥ // Ckc_8.*59 //
children.translated_text: the bearing of the earth is fitting for <s>Suvarṇādri</s> (the golden mountain, <s>Meru</s>) alone, the sole abode of <s>Sudharmā</s>, of the celestial assembly, and of the flowers — not for any other mountain. // Ckc_8.*59 //

children.text: atra suvarṇagiriṇaivopamānena dhṛtyādhāratvādibhirabhidhīyamānasādṛśyasya siṅgabhūpālasyopameyasyoktisiddhāvupamānamukhādivopameyasya ślāghā pratīyata iti seyaṃ yathoktā /
children.translated_text: Here, through the <s>upamāna</s> of <s>Suvarṇagiri</s> (Mount Meru) itself, with the expressed similarity consisting of being the foundation of steadfastness and such qualities, the praise of the <s>upameya</s> — <s>Siṅgabhūpāla</s> — is perceived as if through the mouth of the <s>upamāna</s>, when it is established through the statement. Thus this is as described.
The same as the censure-type (<s>garhāvatī</s>), for example:
Abstinence from sense objects is indicated by living on air; complete immersion on the sandbank reveals the removal of evil deeds;

children.text: itthaṃ viddhamupāsya tairthikajana grāsādudagrātmane māyāmāṃsalaśiṃśumāra bhavate dūreṇa baddhāñjaliḥ // Ckc_8.*60 //
children.translated_text: thus, worshipping a venerable one, by swallowing the community of pilgrims, to the crocodile (<s>śiṃśumāra</s>) of great soul, full of deceit and flesh — salutations from afar! // Ckc_8.*60 //

children.text: atra śiṃśumāreṇopamānenābhidhīyamānasādṛsyasya kasyaciddvāravartino dāṃbhikasyopameyasyoktisiddhādupamānamukhādupameyasya garhā pratīyata iti seyamabhidhīyamānasādṛśyagarhāvatī samāsoktiḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, through the <s>upamāna</s> of the crocodile, the censure of the <s>upameya</s> — some hypocritical gatekeeper possessing expressed similarity — is perceived through the <s>upamāna</s>, when established through the statement. Thus this is <s>Samāsokti</s> of the censure-type with expressed similarity.
The same as the reproach-type (<s>upālaṃbhavatī</s>), for example:
Of the ocean — the cause of fulfilling the desires of the wise, adorned with propriety, sustaining many lives, possessed of beauty,

children.text: jātaśriyo himakarasphuraṇeddhakānter jāḍyaṃ na cediha tulāmupayāti ko 'nyaḥ // Ckc_8.*61 //
children.translated_text: with splendor enhanced by the radiance of the moon — if the sluggishness does not measure up, who else does? // Ckc_8.*61 //

children.text:
atrāṃbudherevopamānasyopālaṃbhāt tadupameyasyābhidhīyamānasādṛśyasya kasyacidguṇavato 'pi vilambakāriṇe upālaṃbhaḥ pratīyata iti seyamabhidhīyamānasādṛśyopālaṃbhavatī samāsoktiḥ /
anena ślāghādisaṃkaravatyapi vyākhyātā /
children.translated_text: Here, from the reproach of the <s>upamāna</s> itself — the ocean — the reproach of its <s>upameya</s>, some virtuous but dilatory person possessing expressed similarity, is perceived. Thus this is <s>Samāsokti</s> of the reproach-type with expressed similarity. By this, the mixed type involving praise and other elements is also explained.
Here, an example of the type mixed with praise and censure (<s>ślāghāgarhaṇasaṃkaravatī</s>):

children.text: vārādhārāḥ kati na suvate duryaśorāśihetor antarjantuvyatikaravasālaṃbitān kṣudraśaṃkhān /
children.translated_text: How many are the rain-showers that bring forth petty conchs clinging to the contact of inner creatures, for the sake of heaps of infamy!

children.text: so 'yaṃ bhūmnāmāvādharudadhiryatra bhāgyāvadhīnāṃ saubhāgyānāṃ janiruditavān dakṣiṇāvartaśaṅkhaḥ // Ckc_8.*62 //
children.translated_text: This very ocean, where among the fortunate ones dependent on destiny the auspicious right-turning conch (<s>dakṣiṇāvartaśaṅkha</s>) has arisen, bears the earth in abundance. // Ckc_8.*62 //

children.text:
atra prathamārdhe kṣudraśaṅkhasamutpattisthānajalāśayānāmupamānākathanādeva tadupameyānāṃ pratīyamānasādṛsyānāṃ kṣudrakṣudrakṣatriyotpattisthānānāmanyanarapālavaṃśānāmuktteḥ siddhāvupamānadvāreṇaivopameya garhā pratīyate /
uttarārdhe ca dakṣimaṇāvartaśaṅkhajanakakṣīrasāgareṇaivopamānena kathitasādṛśyasya nāyakāva taramapariṇatabhāgadheyasya recarlavaṃśasyoktisiddhā vupamānamukhenaivopameyasya ślāghā pratīyate /
tadiyaṃ garhāślāghāsaṃkaravatī samāsoktiḥ /
evamanye bhedā lakṣaṇīyāḥ /
eṣāṃ vikṛtā api saṃbhavatanti /
children.translated_text: Here, in the first half, since the <s>upamāna</s> — the water-bodies that are the birthplace of inferior conch-shells — is not mentioned, the <s>upameya</s> — the lineages of other kings, the birthplaces of inferior petty warriors — is perceived through established similarity. Thus, through the <s>upamāna</s> alone, censure of the <s>upameya</s> is perceived. In the second half, through the <s>upamāna</s> alone — the milk-ocean that is the birthplace of the auspicious dextral conch — censure through the stated similarity with the hero's <s>Recarla</s> lineage, whose fortune is unsurpassed, is perceived as praise of the <s>upameya</s> through the <s>upamāna</s>. Thus this is a <s>samāsokti</s> (compressed expression) possessing a mixture of censure and praise. Similarly, other varieties should be identified. Modified types of these also occur.
As follows:
"Performing the protection of the garden, having seized a hundred crores (of wealth),

children.text: kareṇa pālayan lokān bhāsate siṅgabhūpatiḥ // Ckc_8.*63 //
children.translated_text: with his hand protecting the people, King <s>Siṅgabhūpati</s> shines." // Ckc_8.*63 //

children.text:
atra varṇanīyasya nāyakasya samucitāyā mupameyatāyāṃ viparyāsopamānyāyenopamānīkṛtasya ślāghāyā viśeṣeṇa balābhidhīyamāna sāmānyaśatamanyoḥ pratītaślāghe pratīte iti seyaṃ vikṛtā kathitasāmānyā samāsoktiḥ /
evamadanīyāni(?) bhedāntarāṇyapi svayamavagantavyāni /
nanu upamāsamāsokttyoḥ ko viśeṣaḥ /
śrūyatām /
upameye upamānāropaṇaṃ samādhiḥ upamāne upameyadharmādhyāsaḥ samāsoktiḥ iti vyakta evānayorbhedaḥ /
children.translated_text:
Here, though the hero being described should properly be the <s>upameya</s>, he has been made the <s>upamāna</s> by the method of reversed simile (<s>viparyāsopamā</s>), and the praise conveyed through the particular force of the shared general qualities expressed in 'hundred' and others is perceived as praise — thus this is the modified (<s>vikṛtā</s>) variety of <s>samāsokti</s> with stated commonality. Similarly, other sub-varieties should also be discerned independently.
Now, what is the difference between <s>upamā</s> (simile) and <s>samāsokti</s> (compressed expression)? Listen: In <s>upamā</s>, there is superimposition of the <s>upamāna</s> upon the <s>upameya</s> — that is the identification (<s>samādhi</s>); in <s>samāsokti</s>, there is superimposition of the <s>upameya</s>'s qualities upon the <s>upamāna</s> — thus the difference between the two is manifest.
Where substances, qualities, and actions, having attained the state of being something else,
are conceived otherwise by the wise — they call that <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy). // Ckc_8.39 //

children.text:
śarūpaphalahetutvād bhāvādbhāvānuyāyinām /
dravyādīnāṃ vikalpena bhavediyamanekadhā // Ckc_8.40 //
children.translated_text:
Through the variation of substances and the like — which accompany (other) states — on the basis of their being similar in form, result, or cause,
this (<s>utprekṣā</s>) becomes manifold. // Ckc_8.40 //
Of these, <s>dravya-svarūpotprekṣā</s> (fancy of substance-as-nature) — as follows:

children.text: nārhasthitiśca suraveśmani sarvadeti citte vicintya payasāmadhipaṃ vihāya /
children.translated_text: "'Residence in the celestial abode is not always suitable' — having reflected thus in his mind, abandoning the lord of the waters,

children.text: recarlavaṃśamavatīrṇa ivācyuto 'yaṃ śrīsiṅgabhūpatiridaṃ paripāti viśvam // Ckc_8.*64 //
children.translated_text: as if descended into the <s>Recarla</s> lineage, this <s>Acyuta</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>, protects this entire world." // Ckc_8.*64 //

children.text: atra nāyakasya recarlavaṃśānatīrṇalakṣmīnāyakarūpeṇa saṃbhāvanamiti seyaṃ dravyasvarūpetprekṣā /
children.translated_text: Here, the hero is fancifully conceived as <s>Lakṣmī</s>'s lord descended into the <s>Recarla</s> lineage — thus this is <s>dravya-svarūpotprekṣā</s> (fancy of substance-as-nature).
<s>Dravya-phalotprekṣā</s> (fancy of substance-as-result) — as follows:
"I think: for the purpose of protecting the second serpent-lineage, for the purpose of kissing the mountain-breasts of the direction-maidens,

children.text: bṛndārakopanasīmni himācalārthaṃ śrīsiṅgabhūpatiyaśo viśati trilokam // Ckc_8.*65 //
children.translated_text: for the purpose of the <s>Himālaya</s> at the boundary of the celestial garden — the fame of King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s> enters the three worlds." // Ckc_8.*65 //

children.text: atra kīrteḥ trilokapraveśasya prayojanatayā dvitīyabhujageśvarādidravyāṇāṃ kathanādiyaṃ tathoktā /
children.translated_text: Here, since substances such as the second serpent-lord and others are stated as the purpose (result) of fame's entry into the three worlds, this is so called.
<s>Hetubhūta-dravyotprekṣā</s> (fancy of substance-as-cause) — as follows:
"With the direction-elephants reassured, the mountain-ranges unshaken, the great serpent-king on top gleaming, the primordial tortoise radiant —

children.text: śrīsiṅgabhūmipatinā racitapratiṣṭhā prīṇāṃti bhūmirapareṇa sumerūṇeva // Ckc_8.*66 //
children.translated_text: the earth, with its foundation established by King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>, delights as if by another <s>Sumeru</s>." // Ckc_8.*66 //
Here, since the hero — the substance that is the cause of the earth's stability — is fancifully conceived as another <s>Sumeru</s>, this is <s>dravya-hetūtprekṣā</s> (fancy of substance-as-cause).
<s>Guṇa-svarūpotprekṣā</s> (fancy of quality-as-nature) — as follows:
"The passions of the young women with full bodies and trembling eyes, directed towards you, O King <s>Siṅga</s>,

children.text: kallolitā iva kaṭākṣavilāsabhaṅgyo mandasmitaiḥ kusumitā ivasāpadeśaiḥ // Ckc_8.*67 //
children.translated_text: their sidelong glances and coquettish gestures are as if rippling (like waves); their gentle smiles are as if blossoming (like flowers) along with pretexts." // Ckc_8.*67 //

children.text: atra nāyakaviṣayāṇāṃ taruṇījanānurāgāṇāṃ kallolitādirūpeṇa saṃbhāvanaṃ kṛtamiti seyaṃ tathoktā /
children.translated_text: Here, the amorous feelings of young women directed toward the hero are fancifully conceived in the form of rippling waves and the like — thus this is so called.
And as follows:
"O King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>, your literary skill
causes poets to sprout forth inwardly, as if it were bliss (<s>ānanda</s>) embodied." // Ckc_8.*68 //

children.text: atra sāhityacāturyasya mūrtimadānandatayā saṃbhāvanaṃ kṛtamiti seyaṃ tathoktā /
children.translated_text: Here, the literary skill is fancifully conceived as embodied bliss — thus this is so called.
<s>Guṇa-hetūtprekṣā</s> (fancy of quality-as-cause) — as follows:
"At the moon who has taken refuge in the crowns of kings, as if out of rivalry, your fame-dancer,
colored with the hue of king's-crown jewels, shines in the world, O King <s>Siṅga</s>." // Ckc_8.*69 //

children.text: atra spardhāyā guṇatvaṃ hetutvaṃ ceti seyaṃ tathoktā /
children.translated_text: Here, since rivalry is both a quality and a cause, this is so called.
<s>Guṇa-phalotprekṣā</s> (fancy of quality-as-result) — as follows:
"Having made all remaining serpents into complete serpents, all oceans into milk-oceans, all elephants into divine elephants,

children.text: śrīsiṅgabhūpatiyaśo viśadaṃ trilokaṃ sraṣṭuḥ sabhāmanunayārthamiva prayāti // Ckc_8.*70 //
children.translated_text: the brilliant fame of King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s> proceeds to the assembly of the Creator, as if for the purpose of conciliation." // Ckc_8.*70 //

children.text: atrānunayasya guṇatvam phalatvaṃ ceti seyaṃ tathoktā /
children.translated_text: Here, since conciliation is both a quality and a result, this is so called.
<s>Kriyā-svarūpotprekṣā</s> (fancy of action-as-nature) — as follows:

children.text: śrīsiṅgabhūtalapateḥ śritapārijāta- saṃjñāṅkitasya yaśasā mahatā parītaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Enveloped by the great fame of King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>, which is marked by the name 'Sheltering <s>Pārijāta</s>,'
the wish-fulfilling tree, discerning its own fruitlessness, plunges yet again, as it were, into the milk-ocean." // Ckc_8.*71 //

children.text: atra kalpavṛkṣasya nāyakakīrtyā yadāvaraṇaṃ tatpayodhimajjavarūpeṇa saṃbhāvitamiti seyaṃ tathoktā /
children.translated_text: Here, the envelopment of the wish-fulfilling tree by the hero's fame is fancifully conceived in the form of plunging into the ocean — thus this is so called.
<s>Kriyā-phalotprekṣā</s> (fancy of action-as-result) — as follows:

"The flame-clusters of the <s>Vāḍabā</s> (submarine) fire, which swallows the waters of the ocean of heroes' milk with a roaring 'dhagadhaga' sound, with the violent trembling produced by the onslaught and the compassion (born of its heat) —

children.text: antassaṃtāpabādhāṃ śamayitumiva tāṃ siṅgabhūpālakīrti- jyotsnā kṛtsrātiśītā praviśati kuharaṃ mandarīṇāṃ darīṇām // Ckc_8.*72 //
children.translated_text: as if to cool the inner burning torment, the fame-moonlight of King <s>Siṅga</s>, utterly frigid, enters the hollows and caves of the mountain-ranges." // Ckc_8.*72 //
Here, 'as if to cool' — this is the action-as-result (type).
<s>Kriyā-hetūtprekṣā</s> (fancy of action-as-cause) — as follows:
"As if angered by the offense of competing with the supreme generosity of King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>, the wielder of the <s>Śārṅga</s> bow,

children.text: āmūlavellitalatāvalayāpadeśā- tkalpadrumā nigalitāḥ prabhuṇā prajānām // Ckc_8.*73 //
children.translated_text: the wish-fulfilling trees were uprooted by the lord of the people, under the pretext of a mass of creepers torn up from the roots." // Ckc_8.*73 //
Here, since the committing of an offense is both an action and a cause, this is so called.
This is merely illustrative (<s>upalakṣaṇa</s>); the same method should be applied to cognate types as well. // Ckc_8.41 //
Thus, several varieties of <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy) have been examined.
Further varieties, expressed in the subsequent four (verses), should be identified by the discerning. // Ckc_8.42 //
<s>Aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> (praise of the irrelevant) is the praise of what is not the actual subject. // Ckc_8.43 //
As follows:

children.text: dhanyāste girayo jayanti yadamī śrīsiṅgapṛthvīpater- yātavyā nahibhūbhṛto 'pyalamayaṃ rājāpi candrassakhī /
children.translated_text: "Blessed are those mountains that triumph — for they are on the path to be traversed by King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>! Even this king cannot (equal them), and the moon is but a friend.

children.text: tatra śrībharitānyapi kṣitiruhāṃ bṛndāni bhāgyādhikā- nyuddaṇḍīkṛtapuṇḍarīkamahimāpyekaṃ kṛtārtha saraḥ // Ckc_8.*74 //
children.translated_text: There, even the groves of trees laden with beauty are more fortunate; and a single lake, with its glory of lotuses raised aloft, is fully fulfilled." // Ckc_8.*74 //

children.text: atrāpi jigīṣornāyakasya yātavyapakṣasthitermūrdhābhiṣikttairātmanindāyāṃ prastutāyāmaprastutānāṃ giricandrasarasāṃ praśaṃsanaṃ vihitamiti seyamaprastutapraśaṃsā /
children.translated_text: Here, when the hero is on the point of setting out for conquest and the self-deprecation of the anointed kings standing in the opposing camp is the actual subject — the praise of the irrelevant mountains, moon, and lake is offered instead. Thus this is <s>aprastutapraśaṃsā</s> (praise of the irrelevant).
Where the narration of one (person or thing), for the purpose of praise or censure,

children.text: yatsamīkṛtya kathanaṃ sā matā tulyayogitā // Ckc_8.44 //
children.translated_text: is made by equating with others possessing superior qualities of the opposite party — that is considered <s>tulyayogitā</s> (equal conjunction). // Ckc_8.44 //
<s>Tulyayogitā</s> — as follows:

children.text: rādheyaṃ rajanīkaraṃ ratipatiṃ ratnākaraṃ rāghavam ratnaṃ vaidharaṇīdharaṃ rasanidhiṃ rantiṃ rasālaṃ ravim /
children.translated_text: "<s>Rādheya</s> (<s>Karṇa</s>), the moon, <s>Ratipati</s> (<s>Kāmadeva</s>), the ocean of jewels, <s>Rāghava</s> (<s>Rāma</s>),

children.text: raicarlīyakulodvahaṃ ca sṛjatā lokopakārakriyā- hetorlokapitāmahena karuṇāsarvasvamāviṣkṛtam // Ckc_8.*75 //
children.translated_text: a gem, <s>Vaidharaṇīdhara</s> (<s>Śeṣa</s>), the treasure-house of <s>rasa</s>, <s>Rati</s>, the mango tree, and the sun — by the Grandfather of the world (<s>Brahmā</s>), creating these along with the scion of the <s>Recarla</s> lineage, for the purpose of benefiting the world, the entire essence of compassion has been manifested." // Ckc_8.*75 //

children.text: atra lokopakāraparāyaṇatvalabdhastutīnāṃ karṇādīnāṃ tulyayogena nāyakastutervihitatvādiyaṃ stutyarthā tulyayogitā /
children.translated_text: Here, since the praise of the hero is accomplished by equal conjunction (<s>tulyayoga</s>) with <s>Karṇa</s> and others — who have received praise for their dedication to the welfare of the world — this is <s>tulyayogitā</s> for the purpose of praise.
For the purpose of censure — as follows:
"From the smelting of base metals, from handling serpents,

children.text: śrīsiṅgabhūparaṇaṇānyanapāśrayācca vāñchanti jīvitamaho viṣamā manuṣyāḥ // Ckc_8.*76 //
children.translated_text: from causing the torment of others, from authority over women, from dependence on other kings without the refuge of King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s> — people desire to live! Alas, how perverse are human beings!" // Ckc_8.*76 //

children.text: atra kevalavadhūpātānapariṇāmatvena labhdagarhāṇāṃ dhātuvādādīnāṃ tulyakakṣyānikṣepānnāyaketararājāśrayaṇasya sāmyaṃ nindārthaṃ pratīyata iti seyaṃ tathoktā /
children.translated_text: Here, since the mere non-transformative debasement of women is the basis of the censure gained by alchemy and the like, and the seeking of refuge with kings other than the hero is cast into the same category — the similarity perceived is for the purpose of censure. Thus this is so called.

children.text: doṣasya yo guṇībhāvo doṣībhāvo guṇasya yaḥ /
children.translated_text: Where a fault becomes a virtue, or a virtue becomes a fault —
that is <s>leśa</s> (hint); therefore there is no other (figure called) <s>vyājastuti</s> (ironic praise) — it is the same. // Ckc_8.45 //
Here, where a fault becomes a virtue — as follows:
"From the multitudes of crowns of rival kings crushed by fraudulent tribute, with weapons and deceitful substances placed by their own trusted friends,

children.text: tvāmārādhayatāṃ yaśodhananidhe śrīsiṅgapṛthvīpate sākṣāt sevitumicchato 'vanipatīn manyasva mānyottamān // Ckc_8.*77 //
children.translated_text: those who worship you, O treasure-house of fame, O King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s> — the kings who desire to serve you directly, consider them worthy of the highest honor." // Ckc_8.*77 //

children.text: atra yeyamupagautamītaṭaṃ paryaṭatāmāṭavikamahīpatīnāṃ kuṭilopāyapāṭavastutiḥ seyamanuprāṇitarājamārgapraṇayino nāyakasya manasi doṣatayā pratibhāsyata ityabhiprāyeṇa caturamatibhiramātyaiḥ pramukhanaiṣṭhuryaparijihīrṣayā kūṭopāyaprayogarūpo doṣo 'pi nāyakacaraṇasenāsādhanadhanārjanalakṣaṇaguṇatayā nirūpita iti so 'yaṃ doṣasya guṇībhāvo nāma leśataḥ śanairananyaviditamucyata iti leśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the praise of the crafty stratagems of the forest-dwelling tribal kings who wander along the banks of the Godāvarī — this, with the intention that it would appear as a fault in the mind of the hero who is devoted to the straight royal path — is expressed by clever ministers who wish to avoid overt harshness. The fault of resorting to crafty stratagems is presented as a virtue — namely, the acquisition of wealth for attaining the hero's feet. This transformation of a fault into a virtue is called <s>leśa</s>, because it is expressed gradually, imperceptibly, unknown to others.
Where a virtue becomes a fault — as follows:

children.text: etāvtyapi vipriye priyasakhi prāṇeṣu kā prārthanā kiṃ vā tena śaṭhena nirdayahṛdā recarlavaṃśendunā /
children.translated_text: "O dear friend, despite so much unkindness, what entreaty should be made for life? What use is that deceitful, hard-hearted moon of the <s>Recarla</s> lineage,

children.text: yasyāgaḥ parimārjanāya kṛtināmagresarasya sphuṭaṃ sāmnāṃ sāradhumādhure sahabhuvāṃ śikṣeva nityavratam // Ckc_8.*78 //
children.translated_text: before whom, for the wiping away of offenses, clearly, the sweet autumn-fragrant entreaties of the accomplished ones, like co-born companions, are a perpetual vow of instruction?" // Ckc_8.*78 //

children.text: atra kācidanatidhīrā nāyakā mānāgraha parigrahānuguṇamarthaṃ sakhīnāyakāgrataḥ pratijñāya padanirvāhamāśaṅkamānā sakhījanaparihāsaparijihīrṣayā cāṭuvādādilakṣaṇamastosaṃ mānapratyūhakāraṇaṃ nāyakaguṇagrāmaṃ doṣībhāvena samupanyasyatīti so 'yaṃ guṇasya doṣībhāvo nāma leśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, a heroine who is not overly resolute (<s>anatidhīrā</s>), having declared a position suited to her determination to maintain her offended pride before her friend and the hero, and apprehending difficulty in carrying through her resolve, and wishing to avoid the mockery of her companions — presents the hero's host of virtues, such as eloquent flattery and the like (which are actually the means of dissolving her pride-offence), as faults. This transformation of a virtue into a fault is the <s>leśa</s> (hint).
And as follows:

children.text: chāyāpahāre racite 'ravindaiḥ śrīsiṅgabhūpāla na modase tvam /
children.translated_text: "Since the shade-robbery has been accomplished by the sun-lotuses, O King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>, you do not rejoice.

children.text: chāyāpahāreṇa sahādirāja- ślokāpahāraṃ kuruṣe kimetat // Ckc_8.*79 //
children.translated_text: Along with the shade-robbery, O first among kings, are you committing fame-robbery too? What is this?" // Ckc_8.*79 //

children.text: atra rājakīrtyapahāralakṣaṇasya nāyakaguṇasya śabdaśaktyā camatkārāya doṣatayā kathanād vyājastutirapi sa eva /
children.translated_text: Here, since the hero's virtue of fame-stealing is narrated as if it were a fault, through the power of verbal expression, for the sake of aesthetic delight — this is <s>vyājastuti</s> (ironic praise), which is itself that very <s>leśa</s>.
The conjunction of agents and the like together with other actions etc.
is <s>sahokti</s> (co-statement); it is of two kinds: with dissimilarity and with similarity. // Ckc_8.46 //
<s>Asādṛśyavatī</s> (with dissimilarity) — as follows:
"Together with the expansions of your fame, O King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>,
the rows of feudatory kings flee to the ends of the directions." // Ckc_8.*80 //

children.text: atra śatrulakṣakatvapadārtho visadṛśaiḥ nāyaka kīrtivistāraiḥ kathitā pratītasādṛśyaiḥ saha deśāntaradhāvanakriyāyāṃ samāviṣṭa iti seyaṃ tathoktā /
children.translated_text: Here, the entity characterized as an enemy-marker — the rows of feudatory kings — is conjoined with the hero's fame-expansions, which are dissimilar (to them), in the action of fleeing to distant lands, though they share perceived similarity. Thus this is so called.
<s>Sādṛśyavatī</s> (with similarity) — as follows:

children.text: kṣoṇībhṛtkaṭakoparodhanapaṭuḥ vyāpārabhavyodayā- māśāpūraṇa kāraṇaśriyamiva prāpnoti kīrtiśriyam /
children.translated_text: "Skillful in besieging enemy royal fortresses, with an auspicious rise of enterprise, attaining the splendor of fame as if the splendor of fulfilling the directions,

children.text: śrīsiṅgakṣitipālamaṇḍanamaṇe recarlavaṃśāgraṇī- rānandānanusandadhāti viduṣāṃ dravyaiḥ svakāvyairiva // Ckc_8.*81 //
children.translated_text: the foremost of the <s>Recarla</s> lineage, the ornamental jewel of King <s>Śrī Siṅga</s>, produces delight in the learned with wealth, as if with his own poetic compositions." // Ckc_8.*81 //

children.text:
atra śabdaśaktyābhidhīyamānasamānadharmayoḥ lakṣmīkīrtyoḥ sādṛśyapratīyamānaspṛhaṇīyatvādinā dharmayoḥ dravyakāvyāyośva sādṛsyamivena dyotyate /
sahārthaśva vākyārthasāmarthyana labhyate /
na cātropamānaśahkā kāryā /
upamāyāmupameyasyaiva kriyāsamāveśaḥ /
upamānasyopameyamukhena sākṣāt /
iha tu dvayossamaprādhānyena karmakaraṇabhāvādivivakṣāyāṃ prāptyānandā nusaṃdhānādikriyāsamāveśa iti śleṣodbhāvitopamānachāyā itīyaṃ sādṛśyavatī samāsoktiḥ /
evaṃ viviktādi bhedena kartrādīnāṃ prāyopamānānāṃ bhedāssvayamupagantavyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the similarity between <s>Lakṣmī</s> (prosperity) and fame — whose shared qualities are being expressed through verbal power — is indicated by 'iva'; and the similarity of wealth and poetic compositions is also (indicated). The co-meaning is obtained through the capacity of the sentential meaning. There should be no suspicion of <s>upamā</s> (simile) here: in <s>upamā</s>, it is the <s>upameya</s> alone that is conjoined with the action; the <s>upamāna</s> is (related) directly through the <s>upameya</s>. But here, both are conjoined with equal predominance in the actions of attaining, producing delight, etc., with the intention of agent-instrument distinction — and since the <s>upamāna</s>-semblance is evoked through <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia), this is the <s>sādṛśyavatī</s> (similarity-possessing) <s>sahokti</s>. Similarly, the varieties arising from the distinction of agent and the like — which are mostly <s>upamāna</s> — should be discerned independently.
The placement of multiple substances, qualities, and actions together with other substances etc.
is <s>samuccaya</s> (accumulation); and other meanings are merely divisions of the same. // Ckc_8.47 //

children.text:
sa tāvaccaturdhā /
dvipadāśrayo bahupadāśraya ubhayavargāśrayo 'nubhayāśrayaśceti /
tatra dvipadāśrayo dvidhā pratipadadyotaka uttarapadadyotakaśceti /
children.translated_text: That (<s>Samuccaya</s>) is of four kinds: <s>dvipadāśraya</s> (resting on two elements), <s>bahupadāśraya</s> (resting on many elements), <s>ubhayavargāśraya</s> (resting on both groups), and <s>anubhayāśraya</s> (resting on neither). Among these, <s>dvipadāśraya</s> is twofold: <s>pratipadadyotaka</s> (indicator in each word) and <s>uttarapadadyotaka</s> (indicator in the latter word).
Of these, the first is as follows:
Possessing extraordinary qualities of purity, radiating a splendor surpassing that of kings,

children.text: śrīsiṅgabhūpāla bhuvi tbadīyā mūrtiśva kīrtiśva mudaṃ tanoti // Ckc_8.*82 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Śrīsiṅgabhūpāla</s>, your form and fame spread delight upon the earth. // Ckc_8.*82 //

children.text:
atra mūrtiḥ kīrtiriti dve vastunī pratipadaṃ dyotakena cakāreṇa ekasyāṃ tanotīti kriyāyāṃ samuccitya niveśite /
tena tanuta iti dvivacanaṃ cārthe dvandvasamāsaśva bhavatīti so 'yaṃ kriyāyāṃ dravyasamuccayo nāma pratipadadyotako dvipadāśrayassamuccayabhedaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the two entities — 'form' and 'fame' — are conjoined by the indicative particle 'ca' in each word into a single action, 'spreads' (<s>tanoti</s>). Therefore the dual number 'they spread' does not occur, nor does a <s>dvandva</s> compound arise — thus this is the variety of <s>Samuccaya</s> called <s>pratipadadyotaka dvipadāśraya</s> (two-element accumulation with indicator in each word), being an accumulation of substances in a single action.
The same with the indicator in the latter word is as follows:
The retinue blinded by the display of activities intoxicated with pride, the brilliance of the resounding kettledrum's thundering clang directed against the enemy, mixed together,

children.text: jikīṣā saṃraṃbhastava sapadi siṅgakṣitipate vipakṣāṇāṃ lakṣṇī calayati samutkaṇṭhayati ca // Ckc_8.*83 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Siṅgakṣitipate</s>, your desire to conquer and your fury at once agitate and fill with longing the fortune of your adversaries. // Ckc_8.*83 //

children.text:
atra calanotkaṇṭhālakṣaṇe dve vastunī uttarapadavartinā dyotakenaikasminneva vipakṣalakṣmīlakṣaṇe dharmabhūte dvavye samuccayenaikakālameva niveśita iti so 'yamuttarapadagatadyotako nāma dvipadāśrayasamuccayabhedaḥ /
bahupadāśrayo 'pi pūrvapad dvidhā /
children.translated_text: Here, the two entities characterized as agitation and longing are conjoined by the indicator situated in the latter word into a single entity characterized as the fortune of the adversaries, which serves as the object, simultaneously — thus this is the variety of <s>dvipadāśraya Samuccaya</s> called <s>uttarapadadyotaka</s> (with the indicator in the latter word). The <s>bahupadāśraya</s> (many-element) type is also twofold, like the previous one.
Of these, the first is as follows:

children.text: nyāyakramaśca bhujadaṇḍaparākramaśca kālajñatā ca karuṇā ca kṛtajñatā ca /
children.translated_text: Propriety of conduct, prowess of the arm's staff, knowledge of the right time, compassion, gratitude,

children.text: kāvyajñatā ca kavitā ca vadānyatā ca tvāṃ siṅgabhūpa......prapariṣkaroti // Ckc_8.*84 //
children.translated_text: knowledge of poetry, poetic skill, and munificence — these adorn you, O <s>Siṅgabhūpa</s>. // Ckc_8.*84 //

children.text:
atra nyayaparākramādayaḥ pratipadāśrayadyotakenaikasyāṃ pariṣkaraṇakriyāyāṃ samuccayena niveśyante /
tena pariṣkurvantīti bahuvacanaṃ dvandvasamāsaśca na bhavitīti so 'yaṃ pratipadagatadyotakonāma bahupadāśrayasamuccayabhedaḥ /
so 'yaṃ ca kāraṇabāhulyena purāṇachāyāṃ smṛtipathamavatāraya nnātīva camatkārakārītyasmākaṃ matam /
tathāpi purātanagatānugatikāśraddhayā samudāhṛtaṃ tadidaṃ sarasasāhityasiddhāntamarmajñaistititikṣatavyam /
children.translated_text: Here, propriety, prowess, and the rest are conjoined by the indicator attached to each word into a single action of adorning. Therefore the plural 'they adorn' and a <s>dvandva</s> compound do not arise — thus this is the variety of <s>bahupadāśraya Samuccaya</s> called <s>pratipadagatadyotaka</s> (with the indicator in each word). And this type, owing to the abundance of causes, evokes the flavor of the <s>Purāṇas</s> and brings them onto the path of memory, so in our opinion it does not produce much <s>camatkāra</s> (aesthetic wonder). Nevertheless, it has been illustrated here out of reverent adherence to the ancients' tradition, and this should be tolerated by those who know the essence of the principles of elegant literature.
The second is as follows:
Resting upon the coils of <s>Ananta</s>, sovereignty, fondness for the discus, and the nature of dense substance —
in <s>Śrīsiṅgabhūpa</s>, who is a refuge like the <s>Pārijāta</s> tree, these manifest his being a visible <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>. // Ckc_8.*85 //

children.text:
atrānantabhogāśrayādīni vastūnyuttarapadavartinā cakāreṇa vyanaktītyekasyāṃ kriyāyāṃ samuccīyante na vyañjayantīti bahuvacanaṃ samāsaśca na bhavatīti so 'yamuttarapadagatadyotako nāma bahupadāśrayasamuccayabhedaḥ /
ubhayavargāśrayaḥ punaruttarapadavartidyotaka eva /
children.translated_text: Here, the entities — resting upon <s>Ananta</s>'s coils and the rest — are accumulated by the particle 'ca' situated in the latter word into a single action 'manifests' (<s>vyanakti</s>); the plural 'they manifest' and a compound do not arise — thus this is the variety of <s>bahupadāśraya Samuccaya</s> called <s>uttarapadadyotaka</s> (with the indicator in the latter word). The <s>ubhayavargāśraya</s> (resting on both groups) type has only the indicator in the latter word.
For example:
O <s>Śrīsiṅgabhūpāla</s>, through the excess of merit of the master poets, this has become manifest —

children.text: kāvyaṃ praśastaṃ tava kagīrtanaṃ ca satāṃ śriyāṃ sajjanarañjanaṃ ca // Ckc_8.*86 //
children.translated_text: excellent poetry and the celebration of your fame, and the prosperity of the virtuous and the delight of good people. // Ckc_8.*86 //

children.text:
atra kāvyaṃ kīrtanaṃ ceti dve kriye /
śrīsadbhāvaḥ sajjanānurañjanañceti dvau guṇau /
evaṃ bahūnyapi vastūni dvandvaśa uttarapadavartinā dyotakenāvirāsīdityekasyāṃ kriyāyāṃ niveśyante /
tena santīti bahuvacanaṃ dvandvasamāsaśca na syāditi so 'yamubhyavargāśrayassamuccayaḥ /
anubhayāśrayaḥ punaravidyamānadyotakatvādanvācayasyevāsya viṣayo dīpakenāhṛta itī nodāhriyate /
itaretarayogo 'pi dvipadāśrayādibhedena caturvidhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, 'poetry' and 'celebration' are two actions; 'the state of prosperity' and 'the delighting of good people' are two qualities. Thus, even though there are many entities, they are conjoined in pairs by the indicator situated in the latter word into a single action 'has become manifest.' Therefore the plural 'they are' and a <s>dvandva</s> compound do not arise — thus this is <s>ubhayavargāśraya Samuccaya</s> (accumulation resting on both groups). The <s>anubhayāśraya</s> (resting on neither) type, since it lacks an indicator, has its scope subsumed by <s>Anvācaya</s> (inclusion) and <s>Dīpaka</s> (illumination), and therefore is not illustrated here. <s>Itaretarayoga</s> (mutual connection) is also of four kinds, with the distinctions of <s>dvipadāśraya</s> and so forth.
Among these, <s>dvipadāśraya Itaretarayoga</s> with the indicator in the latter word is as follows:
O jewel among kings <s>Śrīsiṅgabhūpati</s>, behold the great splendor of prosperity at the rising of both you and the sun —
of both who delight in bestowing auspiciousness upon those who seek refuge, through the service of having ascended to the station of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, abundantly. // Ckc_8.*87 //

children.text:
atra nāyakaprabhānāyakau dve dravye paśyetyekasmin guṇapade yaditaretarayogena niveśite taddvayorityatra tadviśeṣaṇayośca dvivacanavikṣāyāṃ samāsaśca bhavatīti so 'yaṃ tathokta itaretarayogassasuccayabheda eva /
evamitaretarayoge 'pi dyotakayogā udāhartavyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the two substances — the hero's radiance and the hero (the king and the sun) — are placed by mutual connection into a single qualitative word 'behold,' and in the expression 'of both,' the dual number referring to their qualifications and a compound do arise — thus this is the so-called <s>Itaretarayoga</s>, which is indeed a variety of <s>Samuccaya</s>. Similarly, in <s>Itaretarayoga</s> too, examples with indicators should be illustrated.
The same with <s>anubhayāśraya</s> (resting on neither) is as follows:
A motionless, innocent glance with modesty lowered, a gesture, a smile's beauty blossoming on the surface of the cheek —

children.text: śrīsiṅgabhūmiramaṇe taruṇījanānāṃ bhāvasthitiṃ piśunayanti sakhījanāya // Ckc_8.*88 //
children.translated_text: O lord of the land <s>Śrīsiṅga</s>, these betray to the company of friends the state of emotion of the young women. // Ckc_8.*88 //

children.text:
atrāvalokitaceṣṭāsmitamiti vastvanitaretarayogena taruṇījanānurāga nivedanakriyāyāṃ niveśyata iti so 'yamanubhayāśrayetaretarayogassamuccaya eva /
samāhāro 'pi pūrvavaccaturvidhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the entities — glance, gesture, and smile — are placed by mutual connection into the action of communicating the young women's love; thus this is <s>anubhayāśraya Itaretarayoga</s>, which is indeed a variety of <s>Samuccaya</s>. <s>Samāhāra</s> (aggregation) is also of four kinds, as before.
Among these, the <s>anubhayāśraya</s> type is as follows:

children.text: saundaryaṃ madane sukhaṃ surapatau bhāgyaṃ nidhīnāṃ prabhau kāruṇyaṃ raghunāyake caturimā cāṇūramalladviṣi /
children.translated_text: Beauty in <s>Madana</s>, happiness in <s>Surapati</s>, fortune in the lord of treasures, compassion in the lord of the <s>Raghus</s>, cleverness in the enemy of <s>Cāṇūra</s> and <s>Malla</s>,

children.text: dharmo dharmatanūbhave vitaraṇaṃ vidyādharādhīśvare tatsarvaṃ śritavatsale vilasati śrīsiṅgabhūmīśvare // Ckc_8.*89 //
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> in the son of <s>Dharma</s>, generosity in the lord of the <s>Vidyādharas</s> — all that shines in <s>Śrīsiṅgabhūmīśvara</s>, who is devoted to those who seek his refuge. // Ckc_8.*89 //

children.text:
atra sarvaṃ tadityanena saundaryādīnāṃ samudāya evānusandhīyate /
tasya ca tirobhūtāvayavabhedatve samāhāraḥ /
sa ceha tadityekavacanāntena napuṃsakena ca kathyate /
na ceha kvacidapi cakārādirvidyate /
dyotaka iti so 'yamunabhayāśrayaḥ samahāraḥ samuccaya eva /
itare dyotakavantaḥ samāhārāḥ svayamūhyāḥ /
anvācayastu kriyāviṣaya eva /
tatra dyotakastūttarapadāśraya eva /
children.translated_text: Here, by the words 'all that' (<s>tatsarvam</s>), the aggregate of beauty and the rest is apprehended as a whole. And since the distinction of its parts has become concealed, it is <s>Samāhāra</s> (aggregation). This is expressed here by the neuter singular ending in 'that' (<s>tat</s>). And nowhere here does the particle 'ca' or the like appear as an indicator — thus this is <s>anubhayāśraya Samāhāra</s>, which is indeed a variety of <s>Samuccaya</s>. The other types of <s>Samāhāra</s> possessing indicators should be inferred by oneself. <s>Anvācaya</s> (inclusion), however, pertains only to actions. In that case, the indicator is only in the latter word.
For example:
O lord fearsome as <s>Bhairava</s> against the arrogant adversary, O wish-fulfilling tree of resolve, O crest-jewel among kings <s>Śrīsiṅgakṣitipāla</s>, O deliverer of the flood of fame's victories,

children.text: sādhūnāṃ parirakṣaṇāya dharaṇīṃ jitvā bhajethāḥ śriyaṃ paṅktiñca pratiyāyināṃ punarapi sve sve pade sthāpitā // Ckc_8.*90 //
children.translated_text: having conquered the earth for the protection of the virtuous, may you enjoy prosperity, and may the ranks of those who had fled be established again each in their own place. // Ckc_8.*90 //

children.text: atra bhajethā iti nāyakakartṛkāṃ śrīkarmakatvena kriyāmupanyasya tatkartṛkameva pratipālanakarmasaṃsthāpanakriyāṃ tva nvācayena niveśitamiti so 'yamanvācayo 'pi samuccayabheda eva /
children.translated_text: Here, having presented the action 'may you enjoy' (<s>bhajethāḥ</s>) with the hero as agent and prosperity as object, the action of protection and the action of establishing in their places, also having the same agent, are placed alongside by <s>Anvācaya</s> (inclusion) — thus this <s>Anvācaya</s> too is indeed a variety of <s>Samuccaya</s>.
An objection to an injunction by prohibition, or to a prohibition [by an injunction], is <s>Ākṣepa</s> (reproach). // Ckc_8.48 //
<s>Ākṣepa</s> by injunction is as follows:

children.text: kāntārakṣitivāsakhinnamanasā kānta tvayā sevituṃ śrīsiṅgakṣitināthamandhranagarī gamyeti ced gamyatām /
children.translated_text: O beloved, you whose mind is wearied by dwelling in the wilderness — to serve <s>Śrīsiṅgakṣitinātha</s>, if it is said 'go to the city of <s>Andhra</s>,' then let it be gone to!

children.text: panthānaḥ prabhavantu te śivatamāḥ sītā (bhūyāt?) prasanno nṛpo (?) yaṃ deśaṃ pradadhāti te sukṛtadhīstatraiva janmāstu me // Ckc_8.*91 //
children.translated_text: May the roads be most auspicious for you, may <s>Sītā</s> be gracious, may the king be pleased — and in whatever land your meritorious wisdom places you, may my birth too be there! // Ckc_8.*91 //

children.text: atra gamyatāmiti kathitasya vidhivākyasyaivānukūlayaiva janmāntarāśiṣā maraṇasūcanāniṣedhaḥ kriyata iti so 'yaṃ vidhyākṣepaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the injunctive statement 'let it be gone to' (<s>gamyatām</s>) is itself negated by the suggestion of death through the favorable blessing for the next birth — thus this is <s>Vidhyākṣepa</s> (reproach through injunction).
<s>Ākṣepa</s> through prohibition is as follows:

children.text: na hi vayaṃ kavayaḥ kavayastu ye nagariguṇānasato 'pi vivṛṇvate /
children.translated_text: Indeed, we are not poets — poets are those who elaborate even non-existent virtues of courtesans.

children.text: nigadituṃ na hi siṅgavasundharābhuji santo 'pi guṇānvayamīśmahe // Ckc_8.*92 //
children.translated_text: To describe the virtues of <s>Siṅgavasundharā</s>'s lord, even though they exist, we are truly unable. // Ckc_8.*92 //

children.text: atra neśmahe iti niṣedhena kavitvalakṣaṇasyāropitaguṇavarṇanasya niṣedhaḥ dharmata iti so 'yaṃ vidhyākṣepaḥ (niṣedhākṣepaḥ?) /
children.translated_text: Here, by the prohibition 'we are unable' (<s>neśmahe</s>), there is a negation that by implication negates the attribution of fabricated qualities, which is the defining characteristic of poetic skill — thus this is <s>Niṣedhākṣepa</s> (reproach through prohibition).
When, having introduced some subject matter, there is the placement of another matter capable of establishing it,
that should be known as <s>Arthāntaranyāsa</s> (corroborative illustration), which is the statement of another thing to be uttered. // Ckc_8.49 //
For example:

children.text: siṅgakṣoṇīramaṇasaraṇiṃ mānamunmānadhītvaṃ yadyad dravyaṃ karayasi paraṃ pratyahopārjanena /
children.translated_text: O path of <s>Siṅgakṣoṇīramaṇa</s>, whatever wealth you acquire day by day through pride-destroying exertion directed against adversaries,

children.text: tattatpātre nihitamasakṛdvismarasyeva citte kāryasyānte ka iva hi bhavet kāṅkṣaṇā yaḥ prabhūṇām // Ckc_8.*93 //
children.translated_text: that, once placed in a worthy recipient, you seem to forget entirely in your mind — for who among the mighty would have longing after the deed is done? // Ckc_8.*93 //

children.text:
atra nāyakasya pātradattadharmadravyānanuśocanalakṣaṇaṃ vastu prastutya tatsādhanasamarthaṃprabhusvabhāvalakṣaṇaṃ vastvantaramupanyastamiti sāhasaṃ ṣaṅguṇaṃ hi /
atra kīrteḥ saptārṇavalaṅghanamupanyasya tatsādhanasamarthasya ṣaḍguṇastrisāhasavastvantarasyopanyāsādayaṃ tathoktaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, having introduced the subject matter characterized as the hero's non-regretting of wealth given to worthy recipients, another subject matter — characterized as the nature of great lords — capable of establishing it, is presented. Thus this is so called. Here, having presented the fame's crossing of the seven oceans, through the presentation of another subject matter of the six-fold and three-thousand-fold capable of establishing it, this is so designated.
Where there is the perception of a deficiency of substance and the like in the object being praised,
that which serves to bring about the apprehension of a special quality is considered <s>Viśeṣokti</s> (specification). // Ckc_8.50 //
For example:

children.text: na yānaṃ prasunaṃ na ca surabhaigandhi praharaṇaṃ na maurvī vācāṭī na ca dhanurayatnātimadhuram /
children.translated_text: No vehicle, no flowers, no fragrant perfume, no weapons, no twanging bowstring, no bow sweet without effort —

children.text: tathāpi śrīsiṅgakṣitipatirayaṃ cañcaladṛśāṃ vidhatte saṃmohaṃ manasi nitarāṃ manmatha iva // Ckc_8.*94 //
children.translated_text: yet this king <s>Śrīsiṅgakṣitipati</s> produces utter infatuation in the minds of the doe-eyed women, just like <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of love). // Ckc_8.*94 //

children.text: atra puṣparathādidravyāsaṃbhave 'pi nāyakena yadidaṃ mattakāśī cittasaṃmohanakaraṇaṃ tena rūpādiśaviśeṣakāraṇaṃ pratīyata iti seyaṃ pratīyamānaheturviśeṣoktiḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, even though the material accessories such as the flower-chariot and the rest are absent, the hero's causing of infatuation in the minds of the proud-glanced women implies a special cause such as beauty and the like — thus this is <s>Viśeṣokti</s> with an implied cause (<s>pratīyamānahetu</s>).
Similarly, <s>Viśeṣokti</s> with an expressed cause (<s>abhidhīyamānahetu</s>) should also be observed.
The embellishment of actions and the like by means of qualifiers is <s>Parikara</s> (embellishment). // Ckc_8.51 //
With the primordial tortoise reassured, with the great mountain made to shine, with <s>Ananta</s> filled with eagerness —
the arm-staff of <s>Śrīsiṅgakṣitināyaka</s> bears the circle of the earth. // Ckc_8.*95 //

children.text: atrāśvastetyādiviśeṣaṇairmahī vahanakriyāyā ananyasādhāraṇalakṣaṇa upaskāra iti so 'yaṃ kriyāparikaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, by the qualifiers beginning with 'reassured' and the rest, the action of bearing the earth is embellished with a characteristic that belongs to no other — thus this is <s>Kriyāparikara</s> (embellishment of action).
Similarly, <s>Kārakaparikara</s> (embellishment of the agent) and other types should be inferred by oneself.
In my opinion, <s>Ekāvalī</s> (string) is not different from <s>Parikara</s>. // Ckc_8.52 //
For example:
In protecting the earth, in power, in advancing, in the ocean of merit — by King <s>Siṅgamahīpati</s>,

children.text: dharaṇī kuśalaṃ gamitā hariṇā hariṇā hariṇā hariṇā hariṇā // Ckc_8.*96 //
children.translated_text: the earth has been brought to welfare by <s>Hari</s>, by <s>Hari</s>, by <s>Hari</s>, by <s>Hari</s>, by <s>Hari</s>. // Ckc_8.*96 //

children.text:
atra hariṇā hariṇā ityādi śabdaikāvalyā vibhinnārthayā nāyakalakṣaṇaṃ kartṛkārakamupaskriyata iti so 'yaṃ śabdaikāvalī kārakaparikarabheda eva /
evamarthaikāvalyubhayaikāvalyau ṭraṣṭavyau /
children.translated_text: Here, the repetition 'by <s>Hari</s>, by <s>Hari</s>' and so forth, through a string of identical words (<s>śabdaikāvalī</s>) bearing different meanings, embellishes the agent-factor (<s>kartṛkāraka</s>) characterized as the hero — thus this <s>Śabdaikāvalī</s> (verbal string) is indeed a variety of <s>Kārakaparikara</s> (embellishment of the agent). Similarly, <s>Arthaikāvalī</s> (string of meanings) and <s>Ubhayaikāvalī</s> (string of both) should be observed.
When a word denoting action, genus, quality, or substance, occurring in one place,
serves to illuminate other sentences, that is called <s>Dīpaka</s> (illumination). // Ckc_8.53 //
Its varieties are <s>Arthāvṛtti</s> (recurrence of meaning), <s>Padāvṛtti</s> (recurrence of word), combination, and others. // Ckc_8.54 //
Among these, <s>Kriyādīpaka</s> (illumination through action) is as follows:

children.text: ārūḍhāni yaśāṃsi tetribhuvanaṃ śrīsiṅgapṛthvīpate gotragrāvamahāguhāḥ kṣitibhujāṃ bṛndāni mandaujasām /
children.translated_text: Your glories have ascended the three worlds, O <s>Śrīsiṅgapṛthvīpate</s>; the hosts of feeble kings have entered the great caves of their clan-mountains;

children.text: tallakṣmīlalitāni lālitagirāṃ vidvajjanānāṃ gṛhān tadvākyāni ca tāvastutikathāślokyāni karṇau satām // Ckc_8.*97 //
children.translated_text: the homes of learned men of eloquent speech are graced by that prosperity; and your words of praise and renown have reached the ears of the virtuous. // Ckc_8.*97 //

children.text:
atra kriyāvācinā gūḍhānītīvapadena prathamapādādivartinā sarvavākyāni dīpyanta iti tadidamādidīpakam /
evaṃ madhyāntyakriyādīpakaṃ jātidīpakādayo 'pi bhedāḥ draṣṭavyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, all the sentences are illuminated by the action-denoting word 'have ascended' (implied as 'have entered/reached'), which occurs in the first quarter and pervades all the sentences — thus this is <s>Ādidīpaka</s> (initial illumination). Similarly, the varieties of <s>Madhyadīpaka</s> (middle illumination), <s>Antyadīpaka</s> (final illumination), <s>Jātidīpaka</s> (genus illumination), and others should be observed.
Among the varieties of <s>Dīpaka</s>, <s>Arthāvṛtti</s> (recurrence of meaning) is as follows:
They sport with the moonlight-lilies of the Lord of Serpents' vicinity, they play with the pearls and stars of the elephants of the quarters,

children.text: dīvyanti divyavanitāsmitacandrikābhiḥ śrīsiṅgabhūpa tava kīrtivilāsacandrāḥ // Ckc_8.*98 //
children.translated_text: they revel with the moonbeams of the smiles of divine women — O <s>Śrīsiṅgabhūpa</s>, these are the playful moons of your fame. // Ckc_8.*98 //

children.text: atra krīḍārtha eva pādādikriyāsvāvartamānaḥ sarvavākyāni dīpayatīti seyamarthāvṛttirapi dīpakameva /
children.translated_text: Here, the meaning of 'sporting,' recurring in the actions at the beginning of each quarter, illuminates all the sentences — thus this <s>Arthāvṛtti</s> (recurrence of meaning) is also indeed <s>Dīpaka</s>.
<s>Padāvṛtti</s> (recurrence of word) is as follows:
This king of the <s>Recarlava</s> dynasty makes <s>kumuda</s> (white water-lily / the moon / delight) exceedingly —
the king too, born of the ocean, causes the white lotus (<s>kumuda</s>) to bloom. // Ckc_8.*99 //

children.text:
tatra prajāsantoṣaḥ kairavaścetyarthayorāvartamānaṃ kumudamiti padaṃ dve vā dīpayati padāvṛttirapi dīpakameva /
ābhyāmeva tadubhayāvṛttirapi vyākhyātā /
yathātraiva rājetyarthaḥ śabdaścāvartamānavākyadvayamuttejayata iti seyamubhayāvṛttirapi dīpakameva /
children.translated_text: Here, the word '<s>kumuda</s>' — revolving between the two meanings 'delight of the subjects' (<s>prajāsantoṣa</s>) and 'white lotus' (<s>kairava</s>) — illuminates two (meanings); the repetition of a word (<s>padāvṛtti</s>) is also itself a <s>dīpaka</s> (illuminator). By these same (principles), the repetition of both (<s>ubhayāvṛtti</s>) is also explained: as in this very example, the meaning and the word '<s>rāja</s>' (king/moon), revolving in two sentences, illuminate both — this repetition of both is also itself a <s>dīpaka</s>.
The <s>saṃpuṭa</s> (encased) type, consisting of the repetition of three or four words, is as follows:

children.text: kīrtiḥ krīḍati siṅgabhūpa talapaterniryatnaratnāṅkuraṃ pātālo phaṇilokapuṅgavaphaṇāprāsādamāseduṣī /
children.translated_text: "The fame of King <s>Siṅgabhūpa</s> sports: having reached the netherworld (<s>pātāla</s>) — effortless jewel-sprouts upon the palace-hoods of the chief serpents of the serpent-world;
the birthplace of <s>Lakṣmī</s>, the ocean — in the waves threaded with swinging cradles; in heaven — with the cheek-circles of celestial women's playful smiles." // Ckc_8.*100 //

children.text:
atra kriyākartṛkasaṃbandhapadāni prativākyāmāvṛttāni saṃpuṭatayā dīpayantīti saṃpuṭāvṛttirapi dīpakameva /
evaṃ bhedāntarāṇi yathāsaṃbhavamanugantavyāni /
children.translated_text: Here, the words denoting the relation of action and agent, being repeated in each sentence in the manner of an encasement (<s>saṃpuṭa</s>), illuminate — hence the <s>saṃpuṭa</s>-repetition is also itself a <s>dīpaka</s>. Thus, other varieties should be understood as applicable.

children.text: paripāṭhyā tu bhaṇanaṃ śabdasyārthasya vā kramaḥ // Ckc_8.55 //
children.translated_text: <s>Paripāṭī</s> (serial order) is the sequential arrangement of words or meanings. // Ckc_8.55 //
Here, the serial order of words is threefold: of compound words, of non-compound words, and of both.
An example of compound-word serial order (<s>samastaśabdakrama</s>):
"By the mode of valor, beauty, purity, and grace, of King <s>Siṅgabhūpa</s>,
the sun, the moon, and fire bear comparison." // Ckc_8.*101 //

children.text: atra samāsaparipatitānāṃ guṇānāñca krameṇa pratyekaṃ yojanamiti samastaśabdakramo 'yam /
children.translated_text: Here, the sequential pairing of the qualities that have fallen into a compound, each with its respective (standard of comparison), is this compound-word serial order.
An example of non-compound-word serial order (<s>asamastaśabdakrama</s>):
"This King <s>Siṅga</s>, lord of the earth, performs obeisance, honor, and disrespect
toward elders, toward the learned, and toward enemies (respectively)." // Ckc_8.*102 //

children.text: atra pūrvādīnāṃ namaskārādīnāṃ samāsarahitādīnāṃ yathākramamananvayo vivakṣita iti so 'yamasamastaśabdakramaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the intended non-sequential construal of 'elders' etc. (which are non-compound words) with 'obeisance' etc. (respectively) constitutes this non-compound-word serial order.

children.text: samastāsamastaśabdakramarupa ubhayakramo yathā hariśvandro rakṣākaraṇarucisatyeṣviti pūrvodāhṛtam //
children.translated_text: An example of the combined type (<s>ubhayakrama</s>), involving both compound and non-compound word order, is as previously illustrated: '<s>Hariścandra</s> in protection, performance, devotion to truth' etc.

children.text:
atra prathamatṛtīyayoḥ pādayoḥ samastānāṃ rakṣākaraṇādīnāñca guṇānāmasamaktānāṃ tadguṇakatāṃ hariśvandro gāṅgaiyamiti cobhayatra padaśleṣasāmarthyakathitānāṃ hariśvandrahariśvandrānāṃ gāṅgeyagāṅgeyānāṃ ca kramasamanvayo na vivakṣita hati so 'yamubhayakramaḥ /
vākyakramastu svayamunneyaḥ /
arthakramo dvividhaḥ /
deśataḥ kālataśva /
children.translated_text: Here, in the first and third feet, the serial construal of the compound words 'protection, performance' etc. with the qualities (of the respective heroes), and of the non-compound words '<s>Hariścandra</s>,' '<s>Gāṅgeya</s>' etc. — whose serial construal with both (sets of) words is indicated by the power of verbal <s>śleṣa</s> (double meaning) — is not intended (to be taken individually). This is the combined serial order. The sentence-level serial order (<s>vākyakrama</s>) is to be inferred by oneself. The serial order of meanings (<s>arthakrama</s>) is twofold: by place (<s>deśa</s>) and by time (<s>kāla</s>).
Of these, the first (spatial serial order) is as follows:
"O King <s>Siṅga</s>, your army's campaign turns enemy women in the forest into those whose garments are stolen by <s>Śabara</s> tribesmen — your fame's radiance (serves as their covering):"

children.text: paśvārdhe paridhānatāṃ hi dadhate saṃvyānatāṃ vakṣasi prāyo mūdhnyavaguṭhanatvamadhare...dasāṃ vā stumaḥ // Ckc_8.*103 //
children.translated_text: "on the lower half (it serves) as a garment; on the chest as a wrap; mostly on the head as a veil; on the lip... or shall we praise (further)?" // Ckc_8.*103 //

children.text:
atra vardhamanāyāḥ nāyakakorteḥ pratināyakaśuddhāntakāntāśarīrapradeśeṣu kramasaṃkrāntyā yo 'yaṃ paridhānādaupamyalābhaḥ /
evaṃ deśato'rthakramaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the growing fame of the hero, as it progressively transfers across the body-parts of the enemy's inner-chamber ladies in the form of garment-like comparison — this is the serial order of meaning by place (<s>deśato'rthakrama</s>).
An example by time (<s>kālataḥ</s>):

children.text: apāṃ śoṣoddhārā vipatanabhiyā haṃsagilanā- ttuṣāraissītārtī virahijanaśayyādikatayā /
children.translated_text: "The drying up of waters, the plucking out (of lotuses), the fear of falling, the swallowing by geese, the cold distress from frost, the serving as beds for those separated from loved ones —

children.text: vidhitvā sāpāyaṃ jalaruhakulaṃ tadvijahatī sthitiṃ dhatte siḍgakṣitipatirapāye tvayi ramā // Ckc_8.*104 //
children.translated_text: having thus wrought this destruction upon the lotus family, she who abandons that (family) establishes her abode (elsewhere); yet King <s>Siṅga</s>, O ruler — even when <s>Ramā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) departs, (she returns to) you." // Ckc_8.*104 //

children.text: atra jalaśoṣādīnāṃ jalajāpāyahetūnāṃ grīṣmādivasantāvadhi kālakrameṇa bhaṇanāt kālator'thakramo 'yam /
children.translated_text: Here, the enumeration of the causes of the destruction of lotuses — drying of water, etc. — follows the seasonal order from summer through to spring. This is the serial order of meaning by time (<s>kālato'rthakrama</s>).

children.text: miṣato vākrapravṛttiryā sa paryāya itīryate // Ckc_8.56 //
children.translated_text: Indirect action under a pretext (<s>miṣa</s>) is called <s>paryāya</s> (roundabout expression). // Ckc_8.56 //
As:

children.text: hanta krośati śārikānavarataṃ mṛdhnāti līlāmṛgaḥ śrāntāḥ kelicaṇautikāra vikaṭairbāhye sthitā vallakī /
children.translated_text: "Alas, the <s>śārikā</s> (myna bird) cries incessantly, the pet deer keeps rubbing, the playful <s>caṇḍotikā</s> birds are exhausted — the <s>vallakī</s> (lute) stands outside with its harsh (sounds)"

children.text: ityālāpini nirgate priyasakhīvarge navoḍhā priyā bhūpālena sakhījanānusaraṇaṃ sparśena vistāritā // Ckc_8.*105 //
children.translated_text: — thus speaking, the clever group of friends departed; and the newly-wed beloved was expanded (in joy) by the king's touch, following behind the group of friends. // Ckc_8.*105 //

children.text:
atra rahobhaṅgabhīruṇā vidagdhasakhīvargeṇākrośanākarṇanādimiṣātsukhena nirgamopāyo 'bhihita iti so 'yaṃ paryāyaḥ /
evaṃ kāryamiṣataḥ kāraṇokte ravivakṣādayo 'sya bhedāḥ svayamunneyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the clever group of friends, fearing the disruption of privacy, under the pretext of hearing the cries (of birds) etc., pleasantly devised a means of departure. This is <s>paryāya</s> (roundabout expression). Similarly, when a cause is stated under the pretext of an effect, and other varieties such as desire to speak etc. — these sub-types should be inferred by oneself.
That which is the expression of a particular (quality or action) that does not produce excessive astonishment —
that is <s>atiśayokti</s> (hyperbole), the very life-force of all figures of speech. // Ckc_8.57 //

children.text:
guṇakriyāgocareyaṃ na jātidravyagāminī /
na hi dravyasya jātervā sākṣādatiśayaḥ vkacit // Ckc_8.58 //
children.translated_text: This (hyperbole) pertains to qualities (<s>guṇa</s>) and actions (<s>kriyā</s>), not to universals (<s>jāti</s>) or substances (<s>dravya</s>); for there is never directly any hyperbole of a substance or universal. // Ckc_8.58 //
Of the sub-types involving hyperbole of qualities — an example of hyperbole of courage (<s>dhairyātiśaya</s>):

children.text: rūkṣāhaṃkṛtayo na santi lalita bhedaṃ gatena bhruvau dṛkkoṇo 'pi na rāgameti hasitaṃ mandaṃ ca nāntarhitam /
children.translated_text: "There are no harsh traces of pride, O graceful one — no arch has entered the brow; the corner of the eye does not show passion; the gentle smile is not concealed;

children.text: dṛṣṭvāpi pratigarjatāṃ kṣitibhujāṃ saṃraṃbhagarbhaśriyā mūrtirdāruṇaceṣṭayāpyavikṛtā śrīsiṅgapṛṣvīpateḥ // Ckc_8.*106 //
children.translated_text: even upon seeing the enemy kings roaring back with the splendor pregnant with fury — the form of King <s>Siṅgapṛthvīpati</s> remains unaltered even by their terrible conduct." // Ckc_8.*106 //

children.text: atra mahāraṇasaṃhaṃbhe nāyakasya bhrūbhedādivikārābhāvakathanāddhairyaviśeṣo vivakṣita iti seyaṃ guṇātiśayoktiḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the statement of the hero's absence of changes such as knitting of brows etc. amid the great tumult of battle is intended to express the particular quality of courage (<s>dhairya</s>) — hence this is <s>guṇātiśayokti</s> (hyperbole of quality).
An example of hyperbole of action (<s>kriyātiśaya</s>):

children.text: śrīsiṅgabhūpa bhavatīyaparigraheṇa dharmāya yad balavate kavireṣa bhītaḥ /
children.translated_text: "O King <s>Siṅgabhūpa</s>, through your patronage, this poet is emboldened for the sake of <s>dharma</s>;

children.text: tretādibandhumuṣitau tu dadhāti bhāgau tatte tulāṃ na dadhate prathame narendrāḥ // Ckc_8.*107 //
children.translated_text: and (dharma, personified as) she whose kinsmen were stolen (in the <s>Tretā</s> and other ages) gives back their shares — the foremost among kings do not equal you in the balance." // Ckc_8.*107 //

children.text: atra nāyakagatadharmaparipālanakriyāviśeṣo vivakṣita iti seyaṃ kriyātiśayokriḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the particular action of protecting <s>dharma</s> pertaining to the hero is intended to be expressed — hence this is <s>kriyātiśayokti</s> (hyperbole of action).
<s>Śleṣa</s> (paronomasia) is regarded as the expression of multiple meanings by a single word. // Ckc_8.59 //
As:

"Renowned for their magnanimity, having performed the protection of lineages, established on the surface of the earth (or: having ascended the king's domain), of contrary conduct (or: opposing currents),

children.text: śrīsiṅgabhūpatiyasāṃsi nirūḍhasattvā- nullaṅghayanti viṣamānapi vāhinīśān // Ckc_8.*108 //
children.translated_text: the armies of King <s>Siṅgabhūpa</s>, endowed with firm courage (or: firmly grounded beings), do not transgress even the formidable commanders of forces (or: lords of rivers, i.e. oceans)." // Ckc_8.*108 //

children.text: atra vāhinīśapadena samudrasāmantarājalakṣaṇamarthadvayaṃ tadviśeṣaṇe tu tadanukūlārthadvayaṃ ca śliṣṭamiti so 'yaṃ śleṣālaṅkāraḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, the word '<s>vāhinīśa</s>' (commander of forces/lord of rivers) conveys the twofold meaning of oceans and feudatory kings; and its qualifiers also convey the corresponding twofold meanings. This is the figure of <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia).

children.text: udbhedā yatra bhāvasya bāvanā seyamīritā // Ckc_8.60 //
children.translated_text: Where there is the evocation (<s>bhāvanā</s>) of an emerging emotion — that is declared (as this figure). // Ckc_8.60 //
As:
"In the casket of <s>jāti</s> (jasmine) flowers, to be offered to King <s>Siṅgabhūpatilaka</s> by the hand of her own friend —

children.text: ardhīkṛtālakakucāphaṇi kahkaṇena mudrā kṛtā smarajitā likhitena tanvyā // Ckc_8.*109 //
children.translated_text: a seal (<s>mudrā</s>) was made by the slender woman with a drawn image of the Conqueror of <s>Smara</s> (Kāmadeva), with a bracelet on the bee(-adorned) braid and breast." // Ckc_8.*109 //

children.text: atra vidagdhayā kayāpi kāminyā priyayogyānāṃ puṣpāṇāṃ puṣpaśarapuṣpaṃdhayagandhavahābhimarśaḥ śaṅkyate so 'yaṃ bhāvaḥpuṣpaṃdhayādipratibhaṭatayā rakṣāhetubhiralakaphaṇismarajitpadairuddhidyate sūcyata iti seyaṃ bhāvanā /
children.translated_text: Here, some clever woman, suspecting that the fragrance-bearing wind — in the guise of <s>Puṣpadhvaja</s>'s (Kāmadeva's) flower-arrows — might touch the flowers suitable for her beloved, uses the words '<s>alaka</s>' (braid), '<s>phaṇi</s>' (serpent), and '<s>Smarajit</s>' (Conqueror of Love = Śiva) as protective devices against <s>Puṣpadhvaja</s> and his allies — thus evoking and suggesting the emotion. This is <s>bhāvanā</s> (evocation).
The mutual combination of the expanse of figures of speech —
pertaining to word, meaning, or both — is declared by the learned to be <s>saṃsṛṣṭi</s> (combination). // Ckc_8.61 //

children.text:
atra kevalaśabdālaṅkārasaṅkaraḥ śabdālaṅkāraḥ /
kevalārthālaṅkārasaṅkaror'thālaṅkāraḥ /
ubhayālaṅkārasaṅkara ubhayālaṅkāraḥ /
śabdārthālaṅkārayoḥ śabdobhayālaṅkārayorarthobhayālaṅkārayośva saṅkara ubhayālaṅkāra eva svārthālaṅkāravaśāt saṅkarasyobhayāśritatvasiddheḥ saṃbhāvyamānatvāt /
children.translated_text: Here, the combination of word-figures alone is a word-figure (<s>śabdālaṅkāra</s>); the combination of meaning-figures alone is a meaning-figure (<s>arthālaṅkāra</s>); the combination of both-figures is a both-figure (<s>ubhayālaṅkāra</s>).
