The combination of word and meaning figures, of word and both-figures, and of meaning and both-figures, is in each case classified as a both-figure itself — because the combination, by virtue of the meaning-figure component, is established as partaking of both categories, and this is plausible.
An example of the combination of word-figures alone:
"Having performed the service of King <s>Siṅga</s>, which destroys the disapproval of the righteous (<s>sādhvasaṃmatividhvaṃsi</s>),
the kings, remaining in their own homes, (find that) their understanding is destroyed by fear (<s>sādhvasaṃ matividhvaṃsi</s>)." // Ckc_8.*110 //

children.text:
atra sādhūnāmasaṃmatimasaṃbhāvanāṃ vindato 'labhyamānān sā dhvaṃsayati nāśayatīti sādhvasaṃmatividhvasi durjanatarjanamityarthaḥ /
tādṛśaṃ siṅgabhūpālasevanaṃ kṛtvā nijagṛhe svagṛhe sthitairbhūpairmatividhvaṃsi sādhvasamiti yojanā /
atra nijagṛhe nigṛhītamiti kriyāpadaṃ nijagṛha iti saptamyā gūḍhamiti kriyāgūḍhalakṣaṇo viṣayapadāvṛttiyamakalakṣaṇasva śabdālaṅkārau saṃkīrṇāviti kevalaśabdālaṅkārasaṅkaro 'yam /
children.translated_text: Here, '<s>sādhvasaṃmatividhvaṃsi</s>' means: it destroys the disapproval and disregard of the righteous toward the unattainable — i.e., it silences the reproach of the wicked. Having performed such service of King <s>Siṅgabhūpāla</s>, the kings, remaining in their own homes (<s>nijagṛhe</s>), are seized by fear that destroys their understanding — this is the construal. Here, the verb '<s>nigṛhīta</s>' (restrained) is concealed within '<s>nijagṛhe</s>' (in their own home) in the locative case — hence the word-figure of concealed action (<s>kriyāgūḍha</s>) and the word-figure of <s>yamaka</s> (homophonic repetition) are combined. This is a combination of word-figures alone.
An example of the combination of meaning-figures alone:
"O King <s>Siṅgabhūpa</s>, your mighty-armed thunderbolt without clouds

children.text: kānane nagaravartino ripūna tatpure vipinavāsino mṛgān // Ckc_8.*111 //
children.translated_text: turns the city-dwelling enemies into forest-dwellers, and the forest-dwelling deer into city-residents." // Ckc_8.*111 //

children.text:
atrānaṃbṛdāśaniriti vibhāvanā /
uttarārdhe parivṛttiriti dvayo rarthālaṅkārayossaṃkaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, 'thunderbolt without clouds' is <s>vibhāvanā</s> (causation by an impossible cause); in the second half, <s>parivṛtti</s> (exchange) — thus two meaning-figures are combined.
An example of the combination of both-figures (<s>ubhayālaṅkāra</s>) alone:
"By fortunes as if by goddesses, by good conduct as if by sages,
by policies as if by great ministers — King <s>Siṅgabhūpati</s> is served." // Ckc_8.*112 //

children.text: atrevaśabdena sahārtha iva saṃbhāvamārtho 'pi dyotyata iti ekavācakānupraveśena sahokterutprekṣāyāśva saṅkaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, by the word '<s>iva</s>' (as if), along with the literal meaning, the hypothetical meaning is also suggested — thus, through the single-word subsumption (<s>ekavācakānupraveśa</s>), there is a combination of <s>sahokti</s> (concurrent expression) and <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy).
An example of the combination of word and meaning figures:

children.text: tvayā dīnāriṇā rājan kṛtā dīnāriṇo mama /
children.translated_text: "By you, O king, who gave gold coins (<s>dīnāra</s>), the gold coins of my (poverty) were removed;
O possessor of complete territory (<s>samagrāmavat</s>), (you made) incomplete (<s>asamagrā</s>) the earth (of enemies)." // Ckc_8.*113 //

children.text: atra prathamārdhe dīnāriṇā dīnārīti dvitīyapādamadhyayamakasyottarārdhe samagrāmavatā kṛteti virodhābhāsasya dvayossaṃkaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, in the first half, the <s>yamaka</s> (homophonic repetition) of '<s>dīnāriṇā</s>'/'<s>dīnārī</s>' occurring in the middle of the second foot, and in the second half, the <s>virodhābhāsa</s> (apparent contradiction) of '<s>samagrāmavatā kṛta</s>' — these two are combined.
An example of the combination of word and both-figures:
"Like the moon served by stars — by those women he is served, this King <s>Siṅgabhūmipati</s>, by (his) chamber women;

children.text: citraṃ janasya valayā valayā nitāntaṃ tāsāṃ sitāyatadṛśāmudare kare ca // Ckc_8.*114 //
children.translated_text: wonderfully, (they have) creepers on (their) bellies — steadily, creeper-like bangles on (their) hands." // Ckc_8.*114 //

children.text:
atra udare valayāvalirekhāḥ citram /
avalayan acalayan kare valayaḥ kaṭakamavalayamiti kartṛkriyāpadayorekavacanabahuvacane śliṣṭe iti vacanaśleṣasya tārābhirindurivetyupamāyāśva viveko dṛsyata iti śabdobhayālaṅkārasaṅkaro 'yam /
children.translated_text: Here, the lines of creepers (<s>vali</s>) on the belly are wonderful; and '<s>avalayan</s>' ('did not shake') with '<s>kare valayaḥ</s>' ('bangles on the hand') — singular and plural of the agent and action words are paronomastically joined (<s>śliṣṭa</s>) — thus the verbal-number <s>śleṣa</s> (<s>vacanaśleṣa</s>) and the simile 'like the moon served by stars' are seen to be distinct. This is a combination of word and both-figures.
And as:
"With rubies as if with songstresses (<s>gāṇikya</s>), with chariots as if with sandalwood,
with noblemen as if with noble virtues — King <s>Siṅgabhūpati</s> rejoices." // Ckc_8.*115 //
Here, there is a combination of <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration), <s>upamā</s> (simile), and <s>utprekṣā</s> (poetic fancy).
An example of the combination of meaning and both-figures:

children.text: santrāsaudviṣatāṃ...pratidiśaṃ tvatkīrtirādhāyate tvatkītau paridhāvanaṃ pratipadaṃ gāyanti vairistriyaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Terror of the enemies... in every direction your fame is established; the enemy women sing of your fame fleeing at every step;

children.text: glānirvairibahadhūlatāsu dharaṇī viśrāmyati tvadbhuje viśrāmo bhuvi siṅgabhūpatimaṇeṃ nidrāṃnti vairistriyaḥ // Ckc_8.*116 //
children.translated_text: languor in the creeper-like wives of enemies; the earth rests upon your arm; rest on earth — O jewel among kings, <s>Siṅgabhūpati</s> — the enemy women sleep." // Ckc_8.*116 //
Here, there is a combination of the figure of <s>anāgata</s> (the yet-to-come), the <s>citrahetu</s> (strange-cause) figure, and <s>upamā</s> (simile).
An example of the combination of word, meaning, and both-figures together:

children.text: śrīsiḍgakṣoṇibhartre diśi diśi sumanomānasollāsa kartre sāndrāmindro vibhūtiṃ śuciratiśucitāṃ dharmarājo 'ti dharmam /
children.translated_text: "To King <s>Siṅga</s>, lord of the earth, who in every direction causes the delight of the minds of the virtuous — may <s>Indra</s> (grant) abundant prosperity, <s>Dharmarāja</s> (Yama, grant) surpassing <s>dharma</s> of exceeding purity,

children.text: rakṣāṃ rakṣo 'dhināthaḥ kuṭilavighaṭanodyogicetaḥ pracetā vāyussaṃpūrṇamāyurdhanamapi dhanadaśśaṃṅkaraḥ śaṃ karotu // Ckc_8.*117 //
children.translated_text: the Lord of <s>Rakṣas</s> (Kubera, grant) protection, <s>Pracetas</s> (<s>Varuṇa</s>) — whose mind is intent on removing crookedness — (grant) wind, full lifespan, <s>Dhanada</s> (Kubera, grant) wealth, and <s>Śaṅkara</s> (Śiva, grant) auspiciousness!" // Ckc_8.*117 //

children.text: atra diśi diśīti sumomānaseti śaṅkaraḥ śaṃ kotviti rakṣāṃ rakṣo iti vat chekānuprāsasya sāndrāmidra ityādāvanuprāsasya sumanaśśleṣaḥ pratiśabdotthāpitena dikpāla rūpa...(madhyama?) malokapālasya cānyonyapratīkāralakṣaṇenānyonyārthālaṅkāreṇa pūrvādikpālaparipāṭīkathanalakṣaṇena kramanāmnobhayālaṅkāreṇa saha saṃniveśaḥ prakāśata iti so 'yaṃ trividhālaṅkāra ... ... ... ... laṅkārasaṅkaro 'nusaṃdheyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Here, '<s>diśi diśi</s>' (in every direction), '<s>sumanomānasa</s>' (mind of the virtuous/flowers), '<s>Śaṅkaraḥ śaṃ karotu</s>' (may Śaṅkara grant auspiciousness), '<s>rakṣāṃ rakṣaḥ</s>' (protection from the Rakṣas-lord) — these constitute <s>vṛttānuprāsa</s> (repeating alliteration) and <s>śleṣa</s> (paronomasia); '<s>sāndrām Indraḥ</s>' etc. contain <s>anuprāsa</s> (alliteration); the <s>śleṣa</s> of '<s>sumanas</s>' (virtuous/flowers); and through each word evoking the form of the guardian of each direction — the meaning-figure of <s>anyonya</s> (reciprocal) characterized by mutual resemblance, together with the both-figure of <s>krama</s> (serial order) characterized by the enumeration of directional guardians in sequence — these manifest their co-occurrence. This is a combination of all three types of figures... to be carefully investigated.
"Although these qualities (<s>guṇa</s>) and the like are accomplished by separate individual efforts,
in the poetry of a meritorious poet, they may be accomplished by a single effort." // Ckc_8.62 //
The combination (<s>saṅkara</s>) of qualities and the like has been declared to be itself a figure of speech by <s>Bhoja</s> and other... authoritative (scholars). // Ckc_8.63 //
Of these, the combination of <s>guṇa</s> (quality) and <s>alaṅkāra</s> (figure) — as follows:
The wonder created by <s>Viśveśvara</s> ... ... ... appeared simultaneously with the fame of <s>Siṅga</s>.

As long as the moon, as long as the sun, as long as the lord of mountains (<s>Dharaṇīdharendra</s>), as long as the mother (earth), as long as the sky, as long as <s>Girijā</s> (<s>Pārvatī</s>) — — — // Ckc_8.*118 //

children.text:
(pratha?) mārdhe sahoktiḥ /
uttarārdhe śeṣakīrti -- -- -- meteṣāṃ saṅkaraḥ kāvyacamatkāramakalaṅkamaṅkurayati /
evaṃ saṅkarāntarāṇi yathāsaṃbhavaṃ mahākaviprabandheṣu rasajñairanusandheyāni /
children.translated_text:
In the first half there is <s>sahokti</s> (co-statement). In the second half, <s>śeṣa</s> (remainder) and <s>kīrti</s> (fame) — — — the combination of these produces the aesthetic wonder (<s>camatkāra</s>) of poetry without any blemish.
Thus, other types of combination (<s>saṅkara</s>) should be sought out by the connoisseurs of <s>rasa</s> in the compositions of great poets, according to what is possible.
Thus has been demonstrated the characteristics (of the figures), examined in accordance with tradition.
The poetry adorned by creative imagination shines forth as long as the moon and sun endure. // Ckc_8.64 //
Let this treatise be examined by those whose intellects have been trained in the knowledge of constructing examples and definitions ... ... with (?) // Ckc_8.65 //

children.text: iti sakalamapi kalyāṇam iti sarasasāhityacāturīdhurīṇaviśveśvarakavicandrapraṇītāyāṃ śrīsiṅgabhūpālakīrtisudhāsāra śītalāyāṃ camatkāracandrikāyāmaṣṭamo vilāsaḥ //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the eighth <s>vilāsa</s> (chapter) of the <s>Camatkāracandrikā</s>, composed by <s>Viśveśvara Kavicandra</s>, master of the skill of elegant literary composition — (a work) cool as the essence of the nectar of the fame of King <s>Śrī Siṅgabhūpa</s>. May all be auspicious.
This treatise is complete. //
